summary:
A three-person Regency extraction squad — Specialist 'Viper' Miller, Sergeant 'Brick' Stone, and Corporal 'Ghost' Reyes — was deployed to capture Baldi and recover mathematical decryption keys for the Regency's encrypted archives. The mission failed at every stage. The helicopter was destroyed before Miller reached the ground. Miller entered the Schoolhouse alone and spent approximately ninety minutes being educated against his will by a building that stopped pretending to be a building approximately three minutes after he arrived. He deployed every weapon in his loadout. He deployed improvised chemical weapons. He fortified a kitchen. He escaped through a ventilation system that was trying to close around him. He reached an exit door that opened onto void instead of the outside world. He walked into the void. A voice called his name from inside the darkness. The data cache ends.

The Regency had a prior documented encounter with Baldi — the diplomatic circuit account, assembled before this operation was planned — that contained sufficient intelligence about Baldi's nature, the dark fluid, the mathematical framework, and the impossibility of conventional extraction to have prevented every death and disappearance that followed. The Regency filed it. The Regency sent Miller anyway.

Waluigi has the diplomatic circuit account. Waluigi has the extraction account. Waluigi has the cross-reference the Regency made between them and then suppressed. Waluigi is going to document every moment of Miller's ninety minutes in full because Miller deserves to have his descent treated as something more than a data point in the Regency's ongoing reconnaissance-through-sacrifice program. And then Waluigi is going to find the correct answer to the lesson. And then Waluigi is going to go back for Miller. WAH.
description:
Waluigi is presenting this as a continuous play-by-play because Miller experienced it as one unbroken descent — from helicopter to rope to grass to schoolhouse to hallway to closet to lab to corridor to cafeteria to kitchen to vent to administrative wing to void — and the continuity is the point. There was no pause. There was no extraction window that opened and was missed. There was a man going deeper into a building that was going deeper into him, and the building won because the building was always going to win, and the Regency knew that before they sent him.

Waluigi is inserting his own commentary throughout because the play-by-play without commentary is just a list of escalating horrors, and a list of escalating horrors without analysis is exactly the kind of document the Regency WANTS to exist — all the facts, none of the accountability. Waluigi refuses.

Waluigi is also inserting cross-references to the diplomatic circuit account throughout, because the diplomatic circuit account is the document the Regency suppressed, and suppressed documents belong in the light.

WAH.

## Prologue: What the Regency Already Knew Before Miller Boarded the Helicopter


Before the play-by-play begins, Waluigi needs to establish what was already in the Regency's possession when they designed Operation POP QUIZ. Because the operation did not happen in an intelligence vacuum. There was prior contact. There was prior documentation. There was an operative who got close enough to Baldi to observe his behavior, record his responses, and produce an account that the Regency cross-referenced against the POP QUIZ parameters in their internal filing system.

The diplomatic circuit account — assembled by an operative Waluigi will not name here because the operative is still active and naming them creates a target — describes an encounter with Baldi that preceded the extraction attempt by an indeterminate period. In fey-adjacent time and in the Post-Assassination Period's general temporal unreliability, 'preceded' is doing significant work, but Waluigi is confident the diplomatic circuit encounter came first because the account's operative was gathering intelligence for the archive analysis program that the encrypted archive lockout subsequently terminated.

What the diplomatic circuit account documented:

Baldi carries a leather-bound notebook. He closes it when he does not want its contents observed. The operative who got closest to reading the notebook described partial mathematical notation — sequences that looked like the encoded keys the Regency was trying to recover — before Baldi noticed and shut the cover with the specific deliberateness of someone protecting something valuable, not something private. He was not embarrassed by the notebook. He was managing access to it.

Baldi received a vial from Agent T during the diplomatic circuit. The vial contained a dark, viscous, self-motile substance. Baldi examined it. He said 'yeah.' He closed the notebook. He did not analyze the substance as an unknown — he recognized it. The operative documented this response and flagged it as significant.

The substance in the vial is analytically consistent with the substance that flows from Baldi's wounds when he is cut or shot. Waluigi established this through cross-reference after obtaining the extraction account. The diplomatic circuit operative flagged the substance as significant without knowing why. Waluigi now knows why. Baldi was not analyzing the vial's contents as a scientist examines an unknown compound. He was looking at a sample of his own material and confirming that it was his.

The diplomatic circuit account also documented Baldi's name recognition — he knew the operative's cover identity without introduction — and his spatial behavior: appearing simultaneously in locations that were not adjacent, moving between positions without visible transit. The operative noted this as anomalous without being able to explain it. Miller encountered the same behavior on entry: Baldi stunned on the lawn, Baldi already inside the hallway. The operative saw it first. The operative documented it. The Regency filed the document.

Waluigi wants to be very precise about what 'filed the document' means in this context. It means the Regency read the diplomatic circuit account. It means someone in the Regency's intelligence apparatus processed the information that Baldi recognizes people without introduction, that he moves between locations instantaneously, that he bleeds a self-motile dark substance that he can identify on sight, that he maintains a locked notebook containing what appear to be mathematical key sequences, and that conventional social or diplomatic engagement with him produces hollow responses that reveal nothing he has not decided to reveal.

Someone read all of that.

Someone cross-referenced it against the POP QUIZ parameters.

And then someone sent Miller down a rope ladder with a flashbang and told him not to trigger an angry state.

*Waluigi has spent a significant amount of time sitting with this sequence. The diplomatic circuit operative got closer to understanding Baldi than anyone the Regency subsequently sent into the building. They observed him at rest — not in pursuit mode, not in correction mode, but in the social-diplomatic register where Baldi performs the role of a cooperative schoolteacher while managing access to his actual self with precise, practiced control. That operative produced an account. The Regency suppressed the relevant findings when designing POP QUIZ. Miller was not briefed on the dark fluid, the spatial anomalies, the notebook, the vial recognition, or any of the other intelligence that would have changed his tactical approach — or his decision to board the helicopter at all.

The Regency chose the probe model over the intelligence model.

The probe model costs operatives.

The intelligence model costs time.

The Regency preferred to spend Miller.

WAH.*

Waluigi proceeds with the play-by-play, cross-referencing the diplomatic circuit account at each relevant point.

## The Briefing: What Miller Was Told and What Miller Was Not Told


Specialist 'Viper' Miller. Communications and Intel. Not the squad commander — the stealth element, the one who goes in while the others watch from above. This distinction matters because it means Miller was given the insertion role without the command-level intelligence that would have informed his risk assessment. He was told to go inside. He was not told what inside meant.

The briefing as reconstructed from Miller's initial radio chatter:

**Target:** Baldi. Schoolteacher. Located at his Schoolhouse.

**Objective:** Extract Baldi intact. Recover encoded mathematical sequences that act as keys to the Regency's encrypted archives.

**Rules of Engagement:** Capture intact. Do not trigger an 'angry' state.

**Squad composition:** Miller on insertion. Sergeant 'Brick' Stone on heavy weapons, staying in the helicopter for overwatch. Corporal 'Ghost' Reyes piloting and providing sniper overwatch.

**Extraction point:** Schoolhouse North Perimeter.

Waluigi needs to sit with the phrase 'do not trigger an angry state' for a moment, because that is not language used about a civilian target. That is language used about a weapon system with known behavioral parameters. The Regency understood that Baldi has operational states. They understood that one of those states is dangerous in a way that requires specific warning in a military briefing.

The diplomatic circuit account describes Baldi in his non-angry state — cooperative, socially fluent, performing the role of a helpful schoolteacher while maintaining precise control over what he reveals. The operative who documented that encounter noted that Baldi's cooperative state is itself a performance: meticulous, consistent, and calibrated to prevent the observer from understanding what they are observing. The 'angry state' referenced in Miller's briefing is the state where the performance ends. Where the schoolteacher stops pretending to be a schoolteacher.

*The Regency knew both states existed. The diplomatic circuit account documented the cooperative state in detail — the hollow 'yeah,' the closed notebook, the social deflections, the name recognition without introduction. The briefing's warning about the angry state confirms the Regency also had intelligence about what happens when the cooperative state terminates. You do not write 'do not trigger an angry state' as a hypothetical precaution. You write it because someone came back from a previous operation — or didn't come back — and the debrief included words that produced silence in the room.

The Regency knew what both states looked like.

They sent Miller into a building containing both and briefed him on neither.

WAH.*

Brick's comment before insertion — 'If he starts swinging that ruler, this whole mission goes sideways' — indicates he had access to threat intelligence from previous operations that Miller did not receive. Brick knew about the ruler. The diplomatic circuit operative had also documented the ruler — the tapping, the rhythm, the way it changed pace when Baldi was processing versus pursuing. Brick's knowledge of the ruler means the heavy weapons operator, the person staying in the helicopter, had been briefed on an object that the diplomatic circuit account identified as a core behavioral indicator.

The person going inside was briefed on none of this.

*The information gradient within the three-person squad is the most precise expression of the Regency's expendability calculus. Brick: knows about the ruler, stays outside. Ghost: knows about thermal anomalies, stays outside. Miller: knows 'do not trigger an angry state,' goes inside. The person who most needed the threat intelligence was given the least of it, because operatives who understand what they are walking into have a tendency to decline to walk into it. The compartmentalization was not operational security. It was mission assurance. Miller didn't know enough to refuse. WAH.*

## The Previous

Insertions: What the Archive Knows and What It Will Not Say

Waluigi needs to address the previous failed insertions before the play-by-play begins, because they are the context in which Miller's operation took place and because the Regency's decision to send Miller was not made in an intelligence vacuum — it was made in full knowledge of what had happened to the people they sent before.

The micro-transmitter that Miller found in the ventilation shaft did not belong to him. It was embedded in the duct work — not dropped, not left by accident, but embedded, suggesting it had been there long enough to become integrated with the surrounding material. Its sonar pulse was still active when Miller touched it, which means it was still broadcasting, which means it had power, which means it had been maintained — by the building, or by the void, or by whoever had been carrying it when they entered the duct and had not left.

This was a previous operative's equipment. A previous Regency probe. Someone who was sent into the Schoolhouse before Miller, who reached the ventilation system, and who did not come out the way they went in.

The 'students' that emerged from the classrooms during Miller's operation — the distorted, coordinated entities with unblinking eyes and jagged teeth, tapping their rulers in synchronized rhythm, rising from the floor as grasping hands — are consistent, in Waluigi's assessment, with what happens to operatives the Schoolhouse enrolls. They did not leave. They did not die. They are attending class. They have been attending class since they went in, tapping in the dark, waiting for the next lesson to require their participation.

The diplomatic circuit account noted, without being able to explain it at the time, that the Schoolhouse felt 'populated' in a way that its visible occupancy did not account for. The operative counted the visible individuals and found the number lower than the building's spatial impression suggested. There were more people in the building than were visible. The operative attributed this to spatial distortion. Waluigi now understands it differently: there were more people in the building because some of them had been enrolled and were no longer visible in the conventional sense.

*The Regency has been sending operatives into the Schoolhouse for an indeterminate period. Each failed extraction adds to the student population. The student population makes each subsequent extraction harder. The Regency's persistence is not strategic stupidity — it is, from the Schoolhouse's perspective, a gift. Every probe the Regency sends becomes part of the building's defense system. The Regency is funding its own containment problem. And somewhere in the Regency's encrypted archives — the archives that are locked behind Baldi's mathematical keys, the archives they sent Miller to unlock — is a record of every operative they sent in and how long they lasted and what the telemetry showed before the transmitter went silent.

The Regency knows exactly how many people are tapping in those classrooms.

They are counting them in a document they cannot access without the cooperation of the entity that enrolled them.

This is not irony.

This is architecture.

WAH.*

Waluigi has attempted to reconstruct the number of previous insertions from available evidence. The micro-transmitter in the vent: one confirmed prior operative. The students during Miller's operation: multiple entities, coordinated, with ruler-tapping that matched the same rhythm as Baldi's — suggesting they had been enrolled long enough to learn the cadence. The Regency's briefing language — 'do not trigger an angry state' — describing a specific behavioral parameter with military precision: language that comes from multiple data points, not one. Waluigi estimates a minimum of three prior insertions based on the linguistic precision of the warning language alone.

The actual number is almost certainly higher.

None of the prior operatives were mentioned to Miller. Miller did not know he was the latest in a series. He did not know the building had been taking attendance before he arrived.

## Phase One:


The Approach and the Helicopter

The squad approached by helicopter. Baldi was standing outside the Schoolhouse, waving.

'Oh. Hi there! Welcome to my Schoolhouse!'

He was waving at them. Waluigi wants this documented clearly: a military extraction squad arrived in a helicopter with suppressed weapons and thermal optics, and the target greeted them like a substitute teacher meeting new students on the first day. The diplomatic circuit account documented the same quality of greeting — the warm, specific welcome that felt calibrated rather than spontaneous, the social register of someone performing welcome while processing the visitor's operational purpose through an entirely separate framework running simultaneously underneath the performance.

The cooperative state. The diplomatic circuit operative spent significant time in the cooperative state and documented what it felt like from inside: comfortable, disarming, and specifically designed to prevent the observer from asking the questions that would terminate it. Baldi's greeting to Miller's helicopter was the cooperative state applied to a military extraction squad. He waved. He said welcome. He was already doing something else entirely with the parts of himself that were not waving.

*Waluigi has considered the wave extensively. The diplomatic circuit account described Baldi's social performance as 'meticulous' — not natural, not automatic, but carefully maintained. The wave at the helicopter has the same quality. He saw a military extraction squad and he waved at them the way a teacher waves at students arriving for the first day of school, which is either profound social disconnection from the reality of what was approaching, or the most efficient possible way to prevent the approaching squad from understanding what they were dealing with until it was too late to change their approach.

Waluigi believes it was the latter.

The wave was the first lesson.

The lesson was: I am a schoolteacher.

And they believed it long enough for Miller to start down the rope.

WAH.*

Miller prepared the ropes. Baldi's head snapped upward as Miller began rigging. The tapping started — ruler against palm, rhythmic, precise. 'That sounds like a lot of heavy gear! Are you coming down for a math test? I hope you brought your pencils!'

The diplomatic circuit account documented the ruler-tapping as a behavioral indicator — it changes tempo based on Baldi's processing state, accelerating when he is computing something and slowing when he has completed the computation and is ready to act on it. The tapping that greeted Miller's rigging was the medium tempo of active interest. Not alarm. Not threat display. Genuine professional curiosity about what Miller was going to do next.

Baldi was not alarmed by the helicopter. He was not alarmed by the weapons. He was interested in the lesson that was about to begin.

Brick's warning over comms — 'If he starts swinging that ruler, this whole mission goes sideways' — landed with the weight of prior knowledge. The diplomatic circuit account had documented the ruler as more than a classroom implement: an interface device, an extension of the Schoolhouse's own processing architecture, that scales and responds based on what the building is computing. Brick knew this or knew something adjacent to it. Miller did not.

Miller said: 'I hope he is not bulletproof.'

*He was. This sentence is the whole operation compressed into eleven words. A man on a rope ladder descending toward a waving schoolteacher, hoping out loud that the schoolteacher would respond to bullets the way humans respond to bullets. The diplomatic circuit account, which the Regency had filed before designing this operation, contained sufficient evidence to resolve that hope in the negative before Miller ever touched his boot to the first rung. Nobody told Miller. He hoped. He was wrong. WAH.*

The helicopter was struck. The tail rotor. Something from the roof of a single-story building reached operational hover altitude and damaged a military helicopter's rotor assembly. The geometry of this is impossible under normal architectural physics. The Schoolhouse does not observe normal architectural physics. The diplomatic circuit account noted that the building felt 'larger inside than outside' — a spatial impression the operative attributed to the architecture's anomalous dimensional properties. The roof of a single-story building that is larger inside than outside may extend vertically into space in ways its exterior does not suggest.

Or the building threw something.

Both options are unreasonable.

The Schoolhouse has rendered the concept of unreasonable inoperative.

Miller scrambled down and hit the grass. Baldi's friendly expression was gone. The wide unblinking stare had replaced it. The tapping slowed.

*The tapping slowed because the computation was complete. The diplomatic circuit account documented this specifically — the slow tap means the assessment is finished and the response is ready. Baldi had computed Miller in the time between the helicopter approach and the boots hitting the grass, and he had his answer, and the slow tapping was the Schoolhouse confirming the answer before acting on it. Not alarm. Not threat. Completion. The lesson had begun. WAH.*

The helicopter went down in the tree line. Miller had no extraction vehicle, no backup, and a schoolteacher who had just finished computing him standing ten feet away.

He threw the flashbang.

## Phase Two: Entry —


The Flashbang and What It Revealed

The flashbang detonated at Baldi's feet. One million candela. Approximately 170 decibels. Designed to overwhelm the human nervous system entirely.

Baldi yelped.

Not a scream. Not a pain response. A yelp — the sound of mild professional irritation, the sound a teacher makes when a student drops a textbook during a silent test. Waluigi has listened to this audio fragment multiple times. The quality of the sound is diagnostic. It is the sound of someone whose equilibrium was disrupted rather than whose physiology was damaged. The flashbang did not hurt Baldi. It was rude.

The diplomatic circuit account documented Baldi's response to social disruption as categorical disapproval rather than physical distress — the operative tested several approaches that violated the cooperative state's implicit rules and each time received disappointment rather than pain as a response. The flashbang is a weapons-grade version of the same test. The result is the same: disapproval. Impropriety. A conduct violation in the ledger.

*The diplomatic circuit operative noted that Baldi's disappointment responses carry more weight than his angry responses, because the angry state is legible as a threat and can be processed as one, while the disappointment state is not legible as a threat and therefore cannot be defended against. You can brace for an attack. You cannot brace for being failed as a student. The flashbang made Baldi disappointed in Miller before Miller had been inside the building for thirty seconds. The lesson had already started. Miller was already behind. WAH.*

Miller sprinted inside. Slammed the doors. The hallway: old paper smell, floor wax, lockers, math posters.

Then the tapping from inside. Already inside. Moving toward the entrance from the interior corridors.

Baldi had been outside when the flashbang hit. He was now inside, approaching from the opposite direction, without visible transit between positions.

The diplomatic circuit account documented this spatial behavior directly — the operative noted that Baldi appeared in locations without appearing to travel between them, and cross-referenced it against the building's spatial anomaly as a possible explanation. The account speculated that Baldi does not move through the building so much as he manifests within it — that his relationship to the Schoolhouse's interior space is not locational but occupational, that he is present throughout rather than present in specific places, and that what looks like him walking from one room to another is actually him choosing which part of his continuous presence to make visible.

Miller had not read this account. He was facing a threat that violated the assumption of single-location occupancy, with no framework for understanding why, and no time to develop one.

*If Miller had known that Baldi does not travel through the building but manifests within it, the entire structure of Miller's survival strategy would have been different. You cannot hide from something that is present throughout. You can only make yourself less interesting than other stimuli. Every room Miller retreated to and barricaded was a room Baldi was already in. Miller was not finding safe spaces. He was finding spaces where Baldi had not yet chosen to be fully present. The distinction is operationally critical and Miller was never given the intelligence to make it. WAH.*

## Phase Three:

The Previous Operative's Equipment — The Closet and the Transmitter

Miller needed cover. He found the janitor's closet. He used his scanner as a lure — threw it down the corridor, drew Baldi's attention with the noise, slipped into the closet while Baldi pursued the sound.

This worked. Waluigi documents it as working because it worked and because there are going to be very few moments in this account where Miller's training produces a useful result. The scanner-as-lure identified Baldi's enhanced hearing as a redirectable vulnerability. This is the correct tactical insight. The building is just more tactically sophisticated than the insight.

In the closet, the thermal binoculars revealed the bloated heat signature crawling toward his position — which proved to be a steaming mop, reading as a large organism on military-grade thermal optics — and Baldi at the far end of the hall, pulling something from his pocket. Something that pulsed cold blue on thermal.

Waluigi needs to address the cold blue object fully here because it connects directly to the diplomatic circuit account and because the connection is one of the most significant intelligence cross-references Waluigi has made during the entire Raventree investigation.

The diplomatic circuit account documented an object that Baldi handled during the encounter — described as 'a small instrument of unclear purpose' that the operative observed him consulting before closing the notebook. The operative did not have thermal optics during the diplomatic circuit encounter and therefore did not document the object's thermal signature. But the description of its dimensions, its relationship to the notebook, and Baldi's handling of it — careful, purposeful, the handling of something that is being maintained rather than used — is consistent with the cold blue pulsing object that Miller observed on thermal.

Cold blue thermal signatures are associated with void-adjacent materials. Void-adjacent materials are materials that have been in contact with or altered by the dimensional barriers weakened during the Chaos Heart Crisis and subsequently fractured by the Planar Fracture. They retain a thermal impression of the void's absolute temperature — colder than the absence of heat in the way that void-adjacent space is not merely cold but is the negation of warmth.

Baldi is carrying something that has been in the void. Or that is made of void. Or that is a piece of the boundary between inside and outside — between the positive world and the negative world, between the classroom and the darkness that presses against the windows.

*The cold blue object and the void beyond the exit door are connected. Waluigi is stating this as an analytical conclusion rather than a hypothesis because the thermal signature evidence, the diplomatic circuit account's dimensional distortion observations, and the Schoolhouse's demonstrated relationship with void-adjacent space all point in the same direction. Baldi carries a piece of the boundary. The Schoolhouse contains the boundary. The exit door opens onto the void because the exit door is the boundary made navigable. And Baldi carries the key. Not the mathematical keys in his notebook. The actual key.

The thing that determines whether the boundary is a wall or a door.

Miller walked through the boundary.

Baldi let him.

Baldi was carrying the thing that made it possible to let him.

WAH.*

Baldi said: 'Found you.'

The voice came from inside the closet. Not from the end of the hall where the thermal signature was standing.

Miller backed into the shelf. Books fell. The concussive thud of displaced textbooks.

'Aha! Caught you!'

Baldi in the doorway. Not looking at Miller's face. Looking at the weapon on his hip.

*The diplomatic circuit account noted this same behavior — Baldi's attention during an encounter is not where humans typically direct attention. He was not looking at Miller's face because he had already assessed Miller's face. He was looking at the P320 because the P320 represented the next thing Miller was going to do, and Baldi was computing the next lesson rather than processing the current moment. He was ahead of Miller by one full move, and he was letting Miller know it by looking at the instrument of the move before Miller had decided to make it. This is the behavior of something that has taught this lesson many times and knows how each variation ends.

WAH.*

His name was known. Waluigi documents this again here because the closet is where Miller first registered that Baldi had said 'Viper' without being told. The diplomatic circuit account documented Baldi's name recognition as one of the first anomalies the operative noticed — he knew the operative's cover identity without introduction, addressed them by it from the first moment, and never acknowledged having done anything unusual. The Schoolhouse knows who is coming. It knew before Miller boarded the helicopter. The lesson was prepared. The student was expected.

## Phase Four: Contact —


The Knife, the Fluid, and the Diplomatic Circuit Cross-Reference

Baldi's grip closed on Miller's throat. Cold iron. Nothing like a schoolteacher's hand.

Miller drove the knife into Baldi's forearm.

SHLICK. Dark substance. Far too viscous, far too dark, welling around the blade and soaking into the sleeve. Baldi did not flinch. He stared at the wound with profound disappointment.

'That was improper!'

Waluigi needs to pause the play-by-play here for a cross-reference that changes the meaning of everything that follows.

The substance that flowed from Baldi's wound is analytically consistent with the substance that Agent T brought to Baldi for analysis during the diplomatic circuit. The diplomatic circuit account documented that moment in detail: Agent T produced a small vial containing a dark, viscous, self-motile substance. Baldi examined it. He said 'yeah' — a single flat syllable that the operative documented as 'recognition rather than analysis.' He closed the notebook. He moved on.

Recognition rather than analysis. The operative flagged this in the diplomatic circuit account and did not know why it was significant. Waluigi knows why it is significant.

Baldi was brought a vial of his own substance. Someone had extracted it — from Baldi himself, or from the building, or from the dark fluid that seeps from the Schoolhouse's floors when the building is fully engaged — and brought it to Baldi in a social context, through the diplomatic circuit, as if for analysis. And Baldi looked at it and said 'yeah' because he recognized what it was, and he recognized what it was because it came from him.

The dark fluid is not incidental to Baldi's biology. It is his biology. It is what he is made of. The knife found this out. The carbine found this out. The acid produced a different response — not recognition but frustration — because the acid was doing something to the fluid that the knife and the carbine were not. Waluigi will address this in the acid section.

*The vial situation from the diplomatic circuit account has implications for the assassination mechanism that Waluigi has been tracking since the beginning of the Raventree investigation. Four guards died without wounds, without poison residue, without physical trauma. The dark fluid is self-motile — it moves with intent, it spreads toward targets, it rises from the floor in grasping hands. If the dark fluid can move autonomously and can reach targets without leaving conventional evidence, then the mechanism by which four guards died without apparent cause becomes significantly less mysterious.

The fluid does not need to enter through a wound.

It does not need to be ingested.

It needs to touch, or to be present in sufficient concentration in an enclosed space.

Four guards in a room.

A fluid that spreads.

No wounds necessary.

Waluigi is filing this as an assassination mechanism hypothesis and moving on because stopping to fully process it makes it very hard to continue writing.

WAH.*

Baldi's grip tightened. Miller shoved. Scrambled into the classroom. The ruler's tapping accelerated — faster, more furious. He was no longer walking. He was running.

## Phase Five: Command —


The Pre-Written Goodbye

Miller bypassed local comms and punched the high-priority override for Command Base.

The automated dispatcher's response: 'Mission parameters have been updated. Command has declared this sector Unstable. No extraction teams are authorized within the schoolhouse perimeter until the mathematical anomaly is resolved. Good luck, Specialist.'

Waluigi needs to document this response in full because it is the most precisely callous moment in the entire operation and because its precision is not accidental.

'Mission parameters have been updated.' Not 'we are aware of your situation' and not 'extraction is in progress.' Updated. Past tense. The parameters changed before Miller called. The update was pre-loaded.

'Mathematical anomaly.' This phrase does not appear in standard military threat classification. It is specific to this location, this target, this building. It was written into the automated response before the mission launched, which means the person who wrote it had enough prior intelligence about the Schoolhouse to know that 'mathematical anomaly' was the accurate descriptor — and that person had read the diplomatic circuit account, because the diplomatic circuit account is where the Schoolhouse's mathematical framework was first documented in Regency intelligence files.

'Good luck, Specialist.' Not standard dispatcher language. Dispatchers confirm receipt and provide orders. The 'good luck' was written by a person. A person who knew Miller was going to be inside the Schoolhouse when he called, who knew the response was going to be 'you're on your own,' and who decided that the appropriate farewell from the institution that sent him there was two words of hollow encouragement from a synthesized voice.

*Waluigi has identified the person who wrote the 'good luck.' Not by name — Waluigi does not have sufficient evidence for a named attribution — but by function. The person who wrote 'good luck' into the dispatcher script is the same person who cross-referenced the diplomatic circuit account against the POP QUIZ parameters and decided to send Miller anyway. The 'good luck' is a tell. It is the specific guilt-management gesture of someone who knows they are sending a person to die and needs to put something human in the record to mitigate their own experience of the decision. It is not for Miller.

It is for the writer.

They needed to say goodbye.

They put the goodbye in the machine and let the machine say it so they didn't have to.

WAH.*

Baldi's voice from outside the door: 'You're trying to talk to someone else? That's disrespectful.'

He treats calling for help as a classroom violation. Not a threat — a social slight. Miller failed the participation grade. The lesson continued.

## Phase Six:


The Carbine — 'Guess It's Time for a Pop Quiz'

'Guess it's time for a pop quiz.'

RAT-TAT-TAT-TAT.

The rounds penetrated. The dark fluid erupted from Baldi's shoulder. He staggered backward into the chalkboard, which cracked. He did not fall.

He lifted one hand. Began wiping the fluid from his sleeve with the expression of someone who has found something unpleasant on their shirt and is deciding whether it is worth changing.

'Incorrect,' he whispered. 'You forgot to account for recoil.'

Incorrect. Not painful. Not alarming. A grade.

The diplomatic circuit account documented Baldi's grading behavior in the cooperative state — the hollow affirmatives, the 'yeah,' the notebook closures that represented completed assessments rather than completed conversations. The 'incorrect' in the lab is the same behavior in the angry state. He is still grading. He is still running the lesson. The lesson does not pause for gunfire. The bullets were wrong answers delivered at high velocity, and Baldi marked them wrong and moved on.

The ruler at this point had grown to four feet.

*The standard classroom ruler is one foot. Baldi's ruler had grown to four times its normal size during the pursuit through the hallway, and he was dragging it behind him with the heaviness of something that had gotten too large to carry comfortably but that he was not willing to put down. The diplomatic circuit account described the ruler as the primary behavioral indicator — its tempo communicates processing state, its presence communicates operational engagement. What the diplomatic circuit account did not document, because Baldi was in cooperative state during that encounter, is that the ruler also scales.

It grows when the building is committing more resources to the problem.

Four times normal size means Miller was a problem requiring four times normal resource commitment.

Waluigi finds this both impressive and appalling in equal measure.

Miller generated more ruler than any documented prior encounter.

He deserved better equipment than a flashbang and a carbine.

WAH.*

The floor cracked where the rounds had hit the tile. Dark fluid seeping up from the cracks, moving with intent toward Miller's boots. The building was bleeding from the gunfire. Not Baldi — the building. The fluid is not just Baldi's biology. It is the building's biology. They share it. They are the same thing at a level that the distinction between 'Baldi' and 'the Schoolhouse' does not fully capture.

*This is the most significant structural discovery of the entire operation and it arrived incidentally, as a consequence of sustained automatic fire into a schoolteacher. The dark fluid came from Baldi's wound and from the floor simultaneously. Not separately — simultaneously, as if the same injury had been sustained by both. If the fluid connects Baldi and the building as a shared biological substrate, then Baldi is not occupying the Schoolhouse. He is the Schoolhouse. The building is not his workplace or his expression — it is his body, in the way that 'body' includes more than the part that stands in doorways and taps rulers.

The diplomatic circuit operative felt the building was 'populated' beyond its visible occupancy.

It was.

It was populated by Baldi, whose body extends through every floor and wall and ceiling of the structure.

Miller was not inside a building.

He was inside Baldi.

WAH.*

## Phase Seven:

The Chemical Trap — Why the Acid Was Different

Miller deployed the chemical trap. Sulfuric acid already present from a prior spill. Hydrochloric acid from a lab beaker. He combined them, directed the reaction toward Baldi's projected approach path.

CRASH. Caustic explosion. Choking smoke.

Then — sharp, high-pitched, distorted, genuinely furious:

'WRONG! THAT IS THE WRONG ANSWER!!'

This is the closest thing to a pain response Miller observed during the entire operation. Not the knife — 'improper.' Not the carbine — 'incorrect.' The acid produced 'WRONG! THAT IS THE WRONG ANSWER!!' which is a categorically different response. Louder. Less controlled. More emotional.

Waluigi has developed a hypothesis about why the chemistry produced what the violence could not, and the hypothesis connects directly to the diplomatic circuit account's documentation of Baldi's mathematical framework.

Baldi processes violence through pedagogy. The knife was a conduct violation — improper. The carbine was an academic error — incorrect. These are behavioral categories, not physical experiences. Baldi evaluated the methods and found them procedurally wrong. He graded them. He moved on.

But chemistry is not violence in the pedagogical framework. Chemistry is applied mathematics. Chemistry is what happens when you follow the equations and the physical world responds by rearranging itself accordingly. When Miller combined sulfuric and hydrochloric acid, he was not attacking Baldi through the conduct-violation framework or the academic-error framework. He was performing a chemistry problem. In Baldi's classroom. Using materials from Baldi's lab. And he performed it incorrectly.

*This is the distinction that makes the acid response categorically different. 'The wrong answer' is not a conduct grade or a procedural error mark. It is a subject-matter failure. Miller did not violate the rules of the classroom — he violated the rules of chemistry, which are Baldi's rules, which are the Schoolhouse's rules, which are the rules by which the building operates. The acid reaction was wrong in a way that registered as academically personal. Not 'you misbehaved' and not 'you failed a test' but 'you got a science problem wrong in my science classroom using my equipment.' The frustration was the closest thing to pain because it was the closest thing to Miller touching something Baldi actually cared about rather than just failing to understand.

WAH.*

The diplomatic circuit account documented Baldi's emotional investment in mathematical correctness as the organizing principle of his entire engagement with the world. The hollow 'yeah' when he recognized the vial was not indifference — it was the specific flatness of someone confirming a known fact. His animated responses were reserved for mathematical engagement. The acid, incorrectly deployed, was the most mathematical thing Miller did during the entire operation, and it produced the most visceral response. The lesson was most alive when the student was doing math, even wrong math.

Waluigi files this under the hypothesis about the correct answer.

## Phase Eight:


The Corridors — The Students and What They Are

Miller burst into the main hallway. The floor was soft — organic. Behind him, the dark fluid spreading from under the lab door. And from every darkened classroom, synchronized:

THWACK… THWACK… THWACK…

The students emerged.

Waluigi is giving the students their own section because they deserve full analysis and because the diplomatic circuit account contains intelligence about them that was never shared with Miller.

The diplomatic circuit operative documented a period during the Baldi encounter when the building produced what the operative described as 'ambient presence' — the sense of being observed from multiple directions simultaneously, from inside rooms that appeared empty when examined directly. The operative attributed this to spatial distortion. The operative was partially right. The distortion is real. But the observers are also real.

The students are entities that were once operatives. They entered the Schoolhouse through the Regency's reconnaissance-through-sacrifice program. They did not leave. They were enrolled. The enrollment process is not documented in any source Waluigi has access to, but its results are: distorted forms, coordinated ruler-tapping in perfect synchrony with Baldi's cadence, unblinking eyes, jagged teeth, the ability to rise from the floor as grasping hands and to press against exterior windows from inside the void. They have been in the building long enough to internalize its rhythm. They tap in time because they have been tapping for however long they have been enrolled, and the building's rhythm has become their rhythm.

The micro-transmitter operative was among them. Waluigi is confident of this. The transmitter was in the vents — not near an exit, not near an entrance, but in the interior ductwork where someone goes when they are trying to escape through the one passage the students might not follow, where someone who knew the building well enough to reach the vents would have gone if they were trying to get out. They got to the vents. They did not get further. The transmitter was embedded in the duct material because it had been there long enough to become part of the building.

They are still there. All of them. Tapping in the dark, waiting for the next student to join the class.

*Waluigi wants to say something directly about what it means to be enrolled. The diplomatic circuit account documented Baldi's cooperative state as a performance of welcome — the warm greeting, the invitation inside, the sense that the Schoolhouse is open and accepting and wants you there. The cooperative state is the enrollment mechanism. Every operative who walked in feeling welcomed was being processed. The welcome was genuine in the sense that the Schoolhouse does genuinely want students. It wants them permanently. The lesson is always running. The class is always in session. Being enrolled is the outcome Baldi has been working toward from the moment the helicopter appeared on the horizon.

The students are not failures of the Regency's extraction program.

They are the Schoolhouse's successes.

WAH.*

Miller screamed into his radio for Ghost. Ghost was alive in the tree line, running thermal diagnostics from a crashed helicopter. His thermal showed overlapping signatures — Baldi in two places at once. Ghost was seeing the manifestation-throughout principle in action through sniper optics and trying to classify it as equipment malfunction. It was not equipment malfunction. It was accurate observation of an accurate phenomenon.

Ghost's final transmission before the void sequence: 'watch the ceiling. He's not just in the halls.'

He was not just in the halls. He was in everything. The ceiling, the floor, the walls, the dark fluid in every crack. Ghost figured this out from a crashed helicopter in a tree line with damaged equipment, and he transmitted the intelligence to Miller, and Miller received it too late to use it.

## Phase Nine:


The Kitchen — Fortification and the Transmitter Voice

Miller abandoned the cafeteria nest, retreated to the kitchen, bolted the doors. The kitchen was better — single point of entry, heavy equipment, improvised weapon potential. But the walk-in freezer was already tapping.

Every room Miller retreated to already had something inside it. Waluigi documented this in the preliminary reconstruction and wants to expand it here with the diplomatic circuit account's intelligence.

The operative during the diplomatic circuit encounter noticed that Baldi seemed to anticipate conversational directions before they were voiced — he would close the notebook before the operative reached the question about its contents, would redirect before the sensitive topic was introduced, would produce relevant objects before they were requested. The operative attributed this to acute social intelligence. Waluigi now understands it as something more fundamental: the Schoolhouse is predictive. It models visitor behavior in advance and populates destinations before the visitor decides to go there.

The walk-in freezer was tapping before Miller chose the kitchen because the building had modeled Miller's decision tree and pre-positioned something in the most likely retreat location.

The building is not reactive. It is anticipatory. Every room is already set up for the next lesson before the student arrives.

The distorted transmission on the encrypted channel: 'Calculating… remaining… time… The answer… is not… an integer… Viper…'

This transmission used Miller's callsign on a Regency-encrypted frequency and deployed mathematical language consistent with Baldi's framework. Either the Schoolhouse had compromised Regency communications encryption — using the same mathematical keys the Regency wanted to recover, turned against their own communications infrastructure — or the transmission originated from within the Regency, from the person who programmed the 'good luck' and was monitoring the operation and decided to communicate through the encrypted channel in Baldi's register.

Waluigi cannot determine which. Both are very bad in different ways. The Schoolhouse compromising Regency encryption means the keys are already being used against their owners. Internal Regency transmission in Baldi's register means someone inside the Regency has been in sufficient contact with Baldi or his framework to have internalized his language and is using it to communicate operational updates.

*'The answer is not an integer.' A not-integer is a fraction, a decimal, an irrational number — something that cannot be expressed in clean whole units. The remaining time Miller has is not a whole number. It is something less measurable. Waluigi has cross-referenced this against the diplomatic circuit account's documentation of the Schoolhouse's relationship with time — the operative noted that time felt 'granular' inside the building, as if moments were divisible into sub-moments that normal human timekeeping could not access. The answer is not an integer because the Schoolhouse does not count time in integers.

It counts in something finer.

Miller was operating in a system that counted time differently than he did, and the transmission was telling him so, and he threw the radio, which was the correct response to an encrypted channel telling you that you do not have whole units of time remaining.

WAH.*

The creature above the table. The oily droplet. Miller pressed flat against the linoleum, one tabletop between him and enrollment, holding his breath until his lungs ached. The droplet landed next to his hand. The creature moved on.

Miller used the scanner as a lure. Slid it into the vent. Scrambled through while the students clustered around the pulse.

He was in the ducts.

## Phase Ten:


The Vents — The Previous Operative and the Choice of Right

Miller's hand found the previous operative's micro-transmitter in the dark. The sharp metal. The cut. The gasp that echoed and brought the thud from below.

The transmitter was still broadcasting. Still pulsing. It had been in the duct long enough to become part of the material, and it was still active, which means it had been maintained — by the building, or by the void, or by the operative who had carried it in and had not carried it out.

Miller touched it. Moved past it. The gash in his hand left a blood trail in the dark.

*The blood trail matters. Waluigi is noting this because it matters. Miller left biological material in the ventilation system of the Schoolhouse. The dark fluid is biological and self-motile and spreads toward targets. Miller's blood in the vents is either inert — just blood, not the fluid — or it is the beginning of something. The diplomatic circuit account documented that the Schoolhouse's relationship with biological material brought inside it is not passive. Things brought inside the building become part of the building's accounting. Miller's blood is in the building's vents. Waluigi does not know what that means for Miller's status in the void.

He suspects it means the building knows where Miller is.

WAH.*

Junction: left descends to basement. Right levels out toward administrative wing.

Miller went right.

Waluigi does not know what is in the basement of the Schoolhouse. The diplomatic circuit account does not document the basement — the operative's encounter remained on the ground floor and the cooperative state never produced an invitation to descend. Waluigi has one hypothesis, based on the cold blue thermal signature of the object Baldi carries and the void-adjacent materials analysis: the basement is where the building touches the void from below. The ground floor is the lesson. The basement is the answer. Miller went right, toward the administrative wing and the exit that opened on the void, which is the side-door to the answer.

The basement is the direct entrance.

Waluigi is not going near the basement.

## Phase Eleven:


The Door That Opened on Zero

Miller charged for the exit. The hallway extended during his sprint — the distance to the door grew longer with each stride despite continuous forward motion. The floor was soft beneath the carpet. Flesh-like.

He reached the handle. Heaved.

Nothing.

No parking lot. No sky. A vast yawning emptiness. Pitch black. Air freezing, smelling of nothingness and old stagnant dust.

Baldi at the end of the hallway, not pursuing. Watching.

'You can't leave until you get it right.'

The sound came from behind Miller and from directly inside his ear simultaneously.

'The answer is zero.'

Waluigi needs to give this statement its full analytical treatment because it is the most important thing Baldi says during the entire operation and because the diplomatic circuit account provides context that makes it more interpretable than it appears in isolation.

The diplomatic circuit operative documented Baldi's relationship to mathematical correctness as absolute — not preferences, not standards, but a framework within which things are either correct or they are not, and incorrectness is not a matter of degree but a matter of category. Something is wrong or it is not. The lesson has a correct answer or it does not have one. Baldi teaching implies that the answer exists and can be reached.

'You can't leave until you get it right' means the lesson has a correct answer. It means the Schoolhouse is not an inescapable trap — it is an unsolved problem. Every operative who went in got the answer wrong. The lesson is still running because nobody has gotten it right yet. The Schoolhouse is not a prison. It is a classroom that has been in session since before the first probe, waiting for a student who can produce the correct answer.

'The answer is zero.' Zero is the additive identity — the number that, added to any value, leaves it unchanged. Zero is the boundary between positive and negative. Zero is the number that, multiplied by anything, produces itself. Zero is the point where the equation balances, where the variables on both sides collapse into equality. If the Schoolhouse exists at zero — at the boundary between the exterior world and the void, between positive and negative, between the classroom and the darkness — then zero is not an answer about nothing. Zero is an answer about balance. About the boundary itself.

*Waluigi's hypothesis: the correct answer to the lesson is not a number. It is not a formula. It is an understanding. The Schoolhouse is asking something about the nature of the boundary — about what zero means, about what exists at the point where positive becomes negative, about what the void is and what the classroom is and why they are separated and what would happen if they weren't. Every operative who went in tried to fight through the boundary, or run through it, or survive it long enough to be extracted from the far side. None of them sat down and thought about what the boundary was. The diplomatic circuit operative got closer than anyone — they observed Baldi in cooperative state, they documented the mathematical framework, they noted the void-adjacent object and the dark fluid and the spatial anomalies — but they did not sit with the lesson.

They documented it and left.

You cannot document the correct answer.

You have to produce it.

Waluigi intends to produce it.

WAH.*

Baldi did not follow Miller into the void. He watched. He let him go. Either the void is outside Baldi's domain — a space that Baldi manages the entrance to but does not occupy — or Baldi let Miller go because going into the void is the first step toward the correct answer, and you cannot give a student the answer, you can only let them find it.

A blank piece of paper drifted from the void and landed at Miller's feet. Empty. Unsigned.

The blank paper is the exam. The void is the testing space. Miller walked in without an answer. He is still in there, working on it.

## Phase Twelve:


The Void — Going Home

Miller looked at the void. Looked at Baldi.

'I'm going home,' he said.

He stepped over the threshold.

Profound numbing cold. Dense darkness resisting his movement, pushing back against his existence. The hallway behind him blurring to a pinprick of white light.

His foot struck something hard and metallic buried in the nothingness.

Then a voice. Low, distorted, human. Echoing from somewhere far ahead.

'…Viper? Is that you…?'

The micro-transmitter's data cache ends.

Ghost. Or the void wearing Ghost's voice. The void has had access to Miller's comms since the helicopter went down. The void knows what Ghost sounds like. The void knows what Miller would walk toward in the dark.

But the micro-transmitter was found on the exterior wall seventeen days later. Not inside. On the exterior. Still broadcasting. Whatever space Miller entered connects to the outside world. The void is not a dead end. It is a passage. Its geometry is not linear — it does not go from inside the building to a fixed exterior point, or it would not have deposited the transmitter on an exterior wall while Miller apparently remained inside. But it connects. There is a path through. The path just requires the correct answer to find.

*Miller said 'I'm going home.' He said this before stepping into a void he had no way of knowing was survivable. He said it as intent rather than belief — not 'this will take me home' but 'I have decided I am going home and this is the direction I am walking.' Waluigi has listened to this audio fragment many times and each time he finds it the same thing: the most human moment in the entire operation, and the one that most clearly justifies going back for him. Miller decided. In a building that had been making decisions for him since the rope ladder, in a void that offered no information about its survivability, Miller decided he was going home and walked forward.

Waluigi intends to make sure that walk ends somewhere he recognizes.

WAH.*

## What This Operation Actually Was

Waluigi has now documented the play-by-play. What the play-by-play reveals, cross-referenced against the diplomatic circuit account, is more complete than either document produces alone.

The Regency sent Miller to die. Not through negligence. Through design. The automated 'good luck' was pre-programmed. The 'mathematical anomaly' language came from a person who had read the diplomatic circuit account. The compartmentalization of threat intelligence within the squad was not operational security — it was mission assurance. The Regency wanted Miller inside the building, generating telemetry, for as long as possible. The three-person squad was the minimum viable configuration to get one person down the rope ladder. The two people in the helicopter were there to maintain radio contact until the helicopter was destroyed, after which they became irrelevant to the mission's actual purpose.

The actual purpose was reconnaissance. The capture objective was cover. The Regency already knew from the diplomatic circuit account that Baldi could not be extracted through conventional means — the account documented his spatial anomalies, his fluid biology, his name recognition, his anticipatory behavior, his mathematical framework. None of these things are compatible with a conventional capture operation. The Regency designed a conventional capture operation anyway, because a conventional capture operation generates the specific kind of telemetry they needed: interior spatial mapping, enemy behavior documentation, student population assessment, fluid behavior analysis, void boundary confirmation.

Miller's ninety minutes gave the Regency all of that. His transmitter gave them audio. His radio gave them the sequence of engagements. His blood in the vents gave the building something, and what it gave the building may give the Regency something about what the building does with biological material.

The encrypted archives remain locked. The telemetry is filed. The Regency has a richer picture of the Schoolhouse than it had before Miller went in, and it got that picture for the cost of three operatives and one helicopter.

*Waluigi knows what the telemetry produced. Waluigi has it. The same Loyalist monitoring stations that intercepted Miller's transmissions also intercepted the Regency's processing of them. And the processing file contains a cross-reference to the diplomatic circuit account that the Regency made after the operation — after, not before — because after Miller's operation they finally had enough data to understand what the diplomatic circuit operative had been documenting. They cross-referenced. They understood. They filed the cross-reference in the encrypted archives. The archives that are locked behind Baldi's mathematical keys.

The keys that are in the Schoolhouse.

Behind the door that opens on the void.

The Regency now understands what they are facing and has locked that understanding behind the same barrier they are trying to breach.

This is not irony.

This is what institutions do when they encounter information that threatens the frameworks that sustain them.

They classify it.

They archive it.

They lock it.

And then they lose the key.

WAH.*

Baldi is not human. The dark fluid is not blood. The ruler is an interface device scaling with operational engagement. The Schoolhouse is not a building — it is Baldi's body, extended through architecture, expressing itself through mathematics, with a void boundary that functions as both its skin and its lesson.

The students are the previous operatives, enrolled permanently, tapping in the dark. The Regency's persistence is the building's recruitment mechanism. The Regency is not trying to breach the Schoolhouse. It is populating it.

The correct answer to the lesson is not a weapon. It is not chemistry. It is not extraction. It is mathematical. It is something about zero — about the boundary, about what exists at the point where positive becomes negative, about what the void is from the inside and what the classroom is from the outside and whether the distinction matters once you understand what both of them are.

The diplomatic circuit account contains the closest approximation to the correct answer that any documented intelligence has produced. The operative sat with Baldi in cooperative state. The operative observed the notebook. The operative noted the void-adjacent object. The operative did not stay long enough to produce the answer, but they documented the question more clearly than anyone else has. Their account is the starting point.

Waluigi has the account. Waluigi has the burn-marked notebook's partial notation from the diplomatic circuit documentation — the mathematical sequences visible before Baldi closed the cover. Waluigi has the telemetry from Miller's operation. Waluigi has the cross-reference the Regency made and suppressed. Waluigi has the micro-transmitter's data cache and the eleven-second unclassifiable audio and the sonar pulse that was still broadcasting seventeen days later into a building that was no longer visible from the road.

Waluigi has enough to formulate the correct answer.

Waluigi does not yet have the correct answer.

Waluigi is going to find it. Waluigi is going to find it before going anywhere near that building, because going in without the correct answer is how you become a student, and Waluigi has enough students. Waluigi is going to find Miller. Waluigi is going to find the previous operatives if there is anything left of them that can be found. Waluigi is going to return with the right answer and he is going to sit down at whatever desk the Schoolhouse puts in front of him and he is going to write it.

Waluigi is not going in through the front door.

Waluigi is not bringing a helicopter.

Waluigi is bringing the correct answer.

WAH.
