summary: Waluigi is going to describe the Overgrown Manor Campaign as one continuous, exhausting, temporally incoherent experience because that is what it was. The dates do not make sense. The Feywild calendar jumped from Harvestside to Highsun and back again like a drunk hopping between bar stools, and Waluigi stopped trying to reconcile the timestamps after the third contradiction. What matters is the sequence of events and not the numbers attached to them, because the numbers are lying and the events are not. The campaign began when the Planar Fracture scattered Disaster Inc. across three hostile dimensions and deposited Waluigi, Hjumpik, Toad Lee, and eventually Wario into the Feywild reflection of Raventree Manor. It has not ended. It may never end, because the Feywild does not believe in endings the way civilized dimensions do. The Feywild believes in obligations, and obligations compound. Over the course of this campaign the party dealt with a people-eating shambling mound that the manor called a mascot, a mermaid-hag dispute over a transformed quartz skull, a ghost who remembered being killed by a three-eyed mage, a Revel entity made of mouths and limbs assembled from the bodies of deceased party guests, Wario attempting to bomb a giant dragonfly for treasure, two Rakshasas playing identity games, an Iron Legion sergeant whose entire squad was dead but who somehow was not, Lady Aurelian pretending to be too fragile to fight despite having draconic elemental resistances, Toad Lee getting swallowed by a bathtub plant monster, a hidden diary confirming the Iron Legion watched the Grafting ritual in 988 BF with approval, a five-night deadline that may have already passed depending on which leaf you count, and Waluigi being physically led between Toad Lee and Lady Aurelian like a child between two parents at a shopping center while a dryad commented that it reminded her of kindergarten. WAH.
description:
Waluigi is documenting the Overgrown Manor Campaign as a single continuous record because splitting it into individual nights implies a kind of temporal coherence that the Feywild refuses to provide. The Feywild is not interested in nights as a unit of measurement. The Feywild measures time in obligations, performances, and the number of things you have accidentally agreed to.

## The Play, the Library, and the Rakshasa Who Was Acting Strange


The evening of the 24th Highsun began with Waluigi attending a play, because Waluigi is a person of culture trapped among people who think culture means hitting things with warhammers. The performance was held in the manor small theater alcove where sprites and goblins reenacted stories from the library collection on a stage barely fifteen feet wide, with a reading plinth at its center and stone riser benches on the outer edges for observers. Waluigi found it charming in the specific way that fairy theater is charming, which is to say beautiful on the surface and deeply unsettling if you think about it for more than thirty seconds.

Hjumpik found Waluigi in the theater and whispered with the subtlety of a man who has never successfully whispered in his life. Azure the Rakshasa, who had been watching the performance with genuine delight, became giddy afterward and tugged Hjumpik arm with strength that he could not resist, which is saying something because Hjumpik arms are attached to a dwarf who swings a warhammer for recreation. They ended up in the library, which was one of the most extraordinary rooms in the manor: a massive animated tree served as both librarian and architectural feature, its roots embedded into floors, walls, and bookcases, rearranging the layout at will while golden-red autumn leaves rustled overhead and strange colorful birds carried news between its branches.

Small sprites tended dozens of hanging fruit-shaped books from its boughs while goblin servants ferried volumes back and forth below.

Waluigi grabbed a book to read. The entire shelf collapsed on him. A fairy named Prixie flew overhead and thanked Toad Lee for helping pick up the volumes, suggesting he speak to Woodfellow the tree-librarian. Toad Lee politely declined because Toad Lee has the rare survival instinct of not accepting favors from fairy entities in enchanted libraries, which is one of the more valuable instincts available in this dimension.

Azure walked off with purposeful energy that did not match her earlier performance-induced bliss. Toad Lee tried to stop her but could not match her strength. Hjumpik noted quietly that she was acting unusually powerful, and Waluigi agreed that something about her behavior had shifted since the play, as though the performance had activated or amplified something in her that was not purely recreational enthusiasm. This theory remained unconfirmed because nobody asked her directly and she did not volunteer the information.

## The Foyer, the Statue, and Waluigi Being Correct Again


The grand foyer of the Overgrown Manor was dominated by a massive tree growing from a stone planter barely large enough to contain its trunk, around which a stone statue of a toad with great feathered wings spread its arms protectively over the space. Gnarled roots crawled from the planter like fingers reaching for ankles, and the ceiling above was crisscrossed with ivy and flowering vines from the floor above, blooming with countless bright and strange flowers that Waluigi could not identify and did not trust. The walls were adorned with paintings and tapestries that had been partially consumed by the encroaching plant life, and the whole space smelled of deep forest and something older underneath.

Hjumpik launched himself over the roots with unnecessary acrobatic enthusiasm and then grabbed Toad Lee and flipped him across as well. Waluigi walked over them like a reasonable person and snapped a twig, which he considers an acceptable price for maintaining dignity. Hjumpik had a feeling the statue was connected to someone he had encountered before, something to do with the sleeping dragon from earlier in the campaign, though he could not articulate the connection clearly.

Waluigi sensed magic throughout the foyer, thick and omnipresent, but this was not school-based magic, not the clean arcane categories that the Mages Guild organizes into filing systems. This was natural magic, old and unbothered by classification. Toad Lee said it felt like a fairy tale. Hjumpik said the place was deeper than it appeared. Waluigi agreed with both assessments while filing away internally that neither of them had noticed the specific resonance pattern he had been tracking through the vine-covered walls since their first arrival, which was a different and more deliberate kind of presence than mere ambient enchantment.

## The Lord Chamber and the Lady with Questions


After exploring upward through collapsing ceilings and rotted hallways where the floors had partially given way to reveal steep drops to the library gangways below, the party reached the Lord Chamber, which had been transformed into a makeshift feasting hall and thoroughly trashed by its current occupants. A roaring fire pit dominated the center, spewing smoke and embers upward to blacken the high rafters with soot. Grimy hoof prints circled the pit in thick overlaying paths. Tables around the edge held half-finished meals and laid-out buffets of greens and nuts and fruits and breads and cheeses, while racks and full barrels of wine stood ready to fuel whatever the satyrs considered an appropriate evening.

The woman waiting for them pointed at the Entropy Regulator Ring on Hjumpik wrist and asked for it with the directness of someone who had decided social grace was optional. Hjumpik did not know what it was. She explained it made all things collapse to one, which is the kind of explanation that sounds profound until you realize it provides no actionable information. Hjumpik refused to hand it over on the reasonable grounds that they had just met and he did not give magical artifacts to strangers who pointed at his accessories. She asked if they were there to kill her. Hjumpik said maybe. She said not with that ring he was not.

She reached for the ring and Hjumpik said he would not let someone touch a man on the first date, which combined genuine caution with accidental romantic framing in a way that only Hjumpik achieves.

She explained the satyr situation: a group had arrived expecting a few days stay and had instead taken over entirely. Her guards had been sent to address the problem and had come back hours later, drunk, now drinking buddies with half the satyrs. She wanted the party to evict them. She set a deadline of five nights to get the satyrs out and end the party, which Waluigi noted was the first firm commitment anyone in the Feywild had offered them.

A fireball formed in Waluigi hand during this conversation as he assessed the tactical calculus of whether their assigned mission was actually to kill this woman. He mentioned it to Toad Lee. Toad Lee said no. Waluigi says he was being thorough and not irresponsible, and he maintains this position.

Hjumpik laughed nervously and dragged both of them into a guest room before the situation could develop further.

## Saedia Three Quests and the Music Box That Never Stops


Saedia the dryad Seneschal presented three tasks in exchange for unaging Hjumpik deteriorated papers, doing so with the practiced exhaustion of someone who has been managing a household where half the staff are mythological and the other half are impaired. She rubbed her temple like someone soothing a headache that had become a permanent resident of her skull.

The first task concerned Herniva the mermaid and Stuckina the hag, who had been screaming at each other from opposite sides of a pond in the maze for over a day. Saedia had tried to mediate and failed. She described Herniva as kind with a mean streak and Stuckina as someone she would like to call a friend even if she was a bit off-putting, and concluded by comparing the two of them to harpies shrieking at each other, which is the most diplomatically honest thing Saedia said during the entire campaign.

The second task concerned Shambly, the shambling mound kept for waste disposal, whose keeper Tymnas had disappeared and who had since wandered indoors and begun eating staff. Saedia was emphatic about not killing it. The Revelmaster considered it a prized mascot, which is the most Feywild sentence in this encyclopedia because only in a fairy dimension is a people-eating plant monster considered an institutional treasure.

The third task involved clearing satyrs from the audience hall.

Hjumpik offered a dwarf promise. Saedia wound up a music box that played a melody which lodged itself in Waluigi head and has not left since. She said to come back anytime. The music box kept turning as they left. Waluigi believes it never stops. Waluigi has dreams about the music box. They are not pleasant dreams.

A dead goblin was found in the corridor immediately after, apparently killed while eavesdropping on the quest briefing. Aurelian checked the body and confirmed it dead. A satyr offered to carry it. Aurelian snapped her fingers. The satyr vanished. She snapped again. The body vanished. Three snaps, three disappearances, zero visible concern from anyone except Waluigi, who was the only person in the group who considered casual body disposal through finger-snapping to be worth noting.

## The Shambly Crisis Across Three Days


Toad Lee described Shambly from his previous encounter: green and almost beautiful when dormant, menacing dark purple when active, simultaneously gorgeous and disturbing in the way that dangerous things in the Feywild tend to be simultaneously gorgeous and disturbing. Hjumpik asked if it was friendly. Toad Lee said he did not know.

Toad Lee noticed Waluigi and Aurelian walking away toward a theatrical performance. Waluigi would like to clarify for the historical record that he was conducting intelligence gathering through cultural observation, which happened to involve comfortable seating and distance from a people-eating plant. Toad Lee grabbed Waluigi hand with the grip of someone who had already decided the answer. Aurelian grabbed Waluigi other hand simultaneously. They walked as a group with Waluigi being physically led between them like a child between two parents at a shopping center. Saedia observed from the doorway that it reminded her of kindergarten.

Toad Lee told her she could fight him about it.

She asked how long he wanted the deaging to take and he did not answer.

On the first approach to the creature room, Waluigi opted to sneak forward and peer through the door. He tripped on the carpet. Hjumpik caught him. Waluigi maintains this was the carpet fault. The carpet was ancient, bunched, and hostile. No reasonable court would rule against him.

The creature eventually ate a butler and grew stronger. It ate a guard who screamed for help while Toad Lee mentioned the digestion process was slow. It slammed a door into Waluigi, who deflected it with his tennis racket while shouting the word cheater because door-slamming as a combat technique is low-class and Waluigi will not pretend otherwise. Lady Aurelian cast what she called fairy magic, then the door opened and a bartender and guard charged past shouting about fresh meat.

Hjumpik argued for diplomacy throughout. He wanted to knock the creature out rather than kill it. Toad Lee wanted to kill it and cleanse the house. Waluigi proposed turning the entire room into a freezer and rolling the ice cubes including the creature and Toad Lee outside, then defrosting them later. Hjumpik rejected this. Waluigi then suggested an explosive icicle thrown at Toad Lee. Hjumpik convinced him to wait a few minutes before doing anything drastic.

Lady Aurelian told Toad Lee she was too fragile to fight, used the word suggest with magical emphasis, cast a spell, and walked out. Waluigi caught the emphasis. Toad Lee did not. Waluigi would like to note once again that Lady Aurelian Corvinarus, a woman with draconic bloodline heritage, vertical pupils behind illusions, and confirmed elemental resistances, called herself too fragile. She is not fragile. She is performing fragility because fragility gives her maximum control with minimum accountability. Toad Lee yelled at her to get out. She left looking genuinely hurt, which is either performance or evidence that dragon-blooded aristocrats can be wounded by toad-directed bluntness.

The resolution came from Steely the mechanical dog producing a steam-powered screech at escalating volume that the shambling mound found intolerable. Everyone evacuated: Toad Lee first, then Waluigi, then Aurelian, then the guard, then Steely, then Hjumpik, who told the creature he had not wanted this to happen but it had put up a fight. Shambly entered the grove and became its problem. The quest was technically complete. The butler it had eaten was technically dead. Waluigi considers this outcome asymmetric but acceptable.

## The Wario Encounters (Multiple, Consistent in Character)


Wario appeared throughout the campaign with the reliability of bad weather, each appearance following the same internal logic: everything has a price, everyone is a customer, and empathy is a sales technique that can be learned in classes.

The first encounter happened when the party found Wario surrounded by looted goods. He asked Waluigi immediately whether he had paid his debts. The multiverse is fracturing, reality is in pieces, they are trapped in a temporal pocket of a fairy dimension, and Wario opening question was about accounts receivable. Waluigi loves Wario. Waluigi also wants to strangle Wario. These feelings have coexisted for decades without resolution.

Wario revealed a portal in the back of the estate that could serve as an exit. He offered to sell the information for eight hundred gold. Hjumpik did not have eight hundred gold. Wario said this was horrible and that no information would be forthcoming. He then mentioned empathy classes, described Hjumpik as a very valued customer, and left to make rounds shadeward, which could mean dimensional commerce or theft from sleeping fairies or both.

The second encounter found Wario in Saedia room, looted treasures scattered everywhere, a gemstone being inserted into his pocket with the words ooh shiny as sole justification. Hjumpik dried papers were among the stolen goods. Wario offered to sell them back for ten gold. Hjumpik threatened to inform Aurelian about the theft. Wario reconsidered because it would be bad for business, returned the papers greasy and stained, and kept almost everything else.

Wario handed over a sealed vial of 268-year-old vampire wine from the Raventree cellars, noting he and his pals had gone drinking a few days ago and he had paid for the drinks. The label identified it as a vintage from 687 BF produced in vineyards that no longer exist from grapes cultivated by vampire lords who appreciated fine wine almost as much as fine blood. The bottle was hand-blown glass with intricate etchings and wax bearing the House Raventree crest. Wario had approximately eight bottles stolen from the manor cellars and had already sold three for 500 to 750 gold each to merchants who did not ask questions about provenance.

He was considering raising his prices because he believed he was undervaluing rare vintage vampire wine.

He was correct.

He was also describing a product line built on theft from an interdimensional vampire estate during a planar crisis, which is the kind of business model that Wario considers simply responsive to market conditions.

Wario also handed over a garlic grenade, a portable healing machine, and an aerodynamic cannonball from his bag of holding, which required plunging his arm in to the shoulder while something inside growled faintly and the smell of garlic and old cheese emerged. He did not close the bag properly afterward because he would need it again in thirty seconds anyway.

The debt ledger revealed that Waluigi allegedly owes 14,783 gold in partnership expenses dating to 1015 BF at 15% monthly compound interest. Waluigi disputes this entire debt. Waluigi has never authorized 15% monthly interest on anything, particularly not garlic expenditures classified as operational necessities. Bowser owes 50,000 gold for storage fees that were generated when Wario stole half the treasure and is now charging Bowser to return the remainder. Remi owes 75 gold plus a 25 gold recruitment processing fee. The non-monetary favors section includes a vampire from Raventree who said he owed Wario one after Wario did not stake him, with the note COLLECT THIS written in urgent capitals.

Wario treats this ledger as sacred scripture and has multiple backup copies in different safehouses.

## The Solarium Detonation


Wario attempted to assassinate the Bramblefly with a beautifully gift-wrapped time-bomb because the creature nest contained treasure, and for Wario, treasure justifies methodology. He dusted off his overalls, slipped on brass knuckles with the W letters catching the light, cracked his knuckles with the sound amplified significantly by the reinforcement, and charged in declaring he was there for the gold kind of lore while kicking humanoid bones aside. When the Bramblefly dive-bombed him with an Air Strike, Wario performed a perfect greasy combat roll and stuffed a golden candlestick into his pocket mid-dodge because Wario multitasks greed and violence simultaneously.

Hjumpik revealed himself from concealment and said not everything needed the Wario touch and they could figure it out without explosions. Wario picked his nose and said he did not care. Toad Lee suggested setting the room on fire instead, which Waluigi notes was the first time Toad Lee voluntarily proposed the arson solution.

Hjumpik threw a hand axe at the time-bomb present. The gift tumbled to the floor between Wario and the Bramblefly and kept ticking. Wario froze, eyes wide, and had time to say no no no before the detonation. The explosion blasted him backward through the already weakened Solarium floor. He plummeted screaming his trademark wail, landed in a pile of treasure downstairs, and immediately began scooping gold while bruised and smoking. Still worth it, he declared. The Bramblefly remained unharmed, proving that Feywild insects are constructed to a higher durability standard than Wario expects.

## The Ghost of Usk and the Grafting Vision


Hjumpik touched a statue on the mezzanine and connected with Usk, a fog-elf appearing as a faint twisted shape composed of shifting drifting clouds in perpetual motion as though moved by an unseen wind. His features were angular and tight, his expressions composed with strange quiet dignity accented by deep shadows.

Usk said he had died and was now here. He was uncertain whether here was past, present, or future. He remembered touching a statue and seeing a memory: a Corvinarus in orange robes cutting their own palm over a dragon egg. The egg screamed. The date was 988. The Iron Legion was there. They called it the Grafting.

Hjumpik asked how Usk had died. Someone had cut off his fingers and stabbed him. Not vampires. His own teammate. He described the killer: a mage in robes, purple robes, with three eyes, the third positioned above the other two. His hands were burnt. He had not seen him use magic directly. He began to say the killer name before Toad Lee pulled Hjumpik away from the statue at the same moment the Rakshasa intervened.

Toad Lee touched the statue afterward. Nothing happened. The statue responded only to Hjumpik specifically, which raises questions about what criteria the manor magical infrastructure uses to determine who receives visions and who receives silence. Hjumpik began explaining the Grafting connection to the group. Toad Lee and Waluigi walked away mid-explanation to ask whether Azure was powerful. This is how information-sharing functions inside Disaster Inc.: the person with critical intelligence delivers it to people who are already leaving the room.

The description Usk gave matched Archie Miser closely enough that Toad Lee noted it could be him but could also be clones. This distinction matters and nobody pursued it adequately. Waluigi filed it under ongoing concerns.

## The Vine Room, Hidden Passages, and Aurelian Chalk Circle


The vine storage room was filled with huge green and purple vines covered in razor-sharp thorns, actively guarding various objects and responding to approach with whip-like strikes before the decision to move was even fully formed. Toad Lee entered because he said he saw someone of interest inside. The vines grabbed him and would not let go despite Hjumpik and the others pushing and pulling. Aurelian emerged from a nearby room, explained she had locked that door so nobody would get hurt, and seemed genuinely puzzled about how Toad Lee had gotten in. Toad Lee eventually cleared the full room of vines with his axe and stumbled out on all fours.

The room defensive system accepted three names when Waluigi used magical detection: Corvinarus, Oracle, and Cornelius. This means the room security recognized three specific authority categories. Understanding who qualifies under each designation and how those categories interact with the manor broader architecture is essential intelligence that nobody acted on immediately.

Hidden passages riddled the upper floors. Steely pawed at a wall revealing one. Waluigi discovered a crack behind the thorny vines at the western landing, summoned magical light to illuminate a hidden room beyond, and Hjumpik used his warhammer to clear a path inside. They found the Morning Glory weapon within, a flower bud of densely packed petals that bloomed into a blade of milky gray steel when exposed to daylight.

Aurelian chalk circle in the master bedroom was discovered to be incomplete despite earlier implications that it was finished or near-finished. When confronted, she admitted she was starting now and estimated four days for completion, which placed the ritual finish on the night before the fifth-night satyr deadline. This timing was either coincidental or deliberately engineered. Wario shoulder-bashed through the door mid-conversation, tripped, fell, and smudged the chalk as Aurelian looked on. She was not pleased. Wario offered to sell her better chalk from his counterfeit supplies, producing a chalk box and presenting it with the energy of someone who does not understand they are at fault for the problem they are now proposing to solve for money.

## The Diary, the Bloodline, and the Grafting Confirmed


Toad Lee read aloud from a diary found in the master bedroom. Three entries painted a picture that Waluigi found troubling in ways that multiplied the longer he sat with them.

The first entry described Aurelian walking the halls crowned in living ivy, smiling as if the Revel never ended, but with tired eyes. The satyrs had arrived like locusts and drank the wine cellars dry. The writer told her to send them away. She laughed and said the party must continue until the planes align. Three manors, three lords, three threads, she whispered. Cut one and the tapestry unravels. The flower bed bloomed brighter each night and whispered to her while she slept.

The second entry described Usk ghost drifting through mirrors like smoke, speaking of betrayal and severed fingers and a blade in the dark and a three-eyed mage in purple robes. His anger was cold fire. The vines listened when he named the betrayer and tightened around them. The writer feared he would become part of the manor, another shadow caught in the weave.

The third entry was dated Faystyl 15, Year 722 of the Eternal Bloom, and described the Grafting in first-person observation. The egg screamed as the blade bit deep. It was described as a pure piercing note like winter wind through crystal. Orange robes stained crimson but the bond held. The Legion observers nodded approval, their iron hearts warmed briefly by the promise of control. The writer watched from the branches. The child would be strong, heir to both vine and scale. But something in the scream lingered, a hunger not yet named. The balance tipped toward entropy already.

Toad Lee called the entries background lore. Waluigi would like it on the record that dismissing evidence of blood-magic, draconic binding, Iron Legion involvement in supernatural experiments, and proto-entropic instability as background lore is exactly the kind of historical negligence that gets kingdoms destroyed. Hjumpik recognized the connection to his own statue vision and confirmed the Grafting was real based on personal memory.

A framed image beneath the rug showed Orangus Cornelius and a dragon on the day the bloodline split. Hjumpik asked Aurelian if the Corvinarus bloodline had merged with a dragon. She said eww and gestured to her fairy wings as evidence against the idea. Toad Lee asked if by dragon she meant the giant dragonfly upstairs. She said no, that was a pest she wanted removed. Hjumpik asked if she was not powerful enough to handle it herself. She said she was just a delicate fairy. Waluigi filed this under lies told by women with draconic blood and elemental resistances who prefer the diplomatic leverage of appearing vulnerable.

Under the rug in the master bedroom, rolled beneath the framed image, they found instructions for breaching Darius Planar Sanctum by repairing the damaged magic circle in the Ruined Manor. The ritual required bone, ash, chalk, and iron formed into a paste from powdered components. The process would take eight hours and could be reduced with the right proficiencies. One circle fragment was in the Feyward master bedroom. Another was in the Shadeward master bedroom. Both needed to be studied before the primary circle in the Ruined Manor could be repaired. This was the endgame mechanism. Everything else was preparation.

## The Revelmaster and the Revel Entity


Hjumpik eventually found the Revelmaster in the staff room adjoining the banquet hall, which was filthy and stinking with broken furniture and garbage strewn everywhere and a makeshift throne assembled from damaged furniture jumbled together like a nest. The Revel itself occupied the space: an amalgamation of mouths and limbs, a horrific avatar of gluttony and debauchery, an ephemeral red haze roiling in the air. Looking at it for more than a moment stirred a horrible unnatural hunger in the stomach and revealed a chaos of motion, hands grasping flesh and claws slitting throats and fanged mouths gnawing through their own sinew and crying out in ecstasy.

The Revelmaster operated under multiple names simultaneously: Ralos, Relis, Rellis, Pal, Friend, Leader. He forgot Hjumpik presence mid-conversation, wandered off to chug beer and vomit, then returned having forgotten who Hjumpik was entirely. He knew things he should not have known, singing a song about Hjumpik getting pulled through the vine-room door that was accurate in its specifics. He claimed to have been working on the song since it happened, implying either constant surveillance or some form of temporal awareness.

When asked why people were dying, he said they were drinking too much. When asked if that was bad, he said the Revel never ends so the party does not either. When asked about the bodies, he said they just put them in. This was the true horror of the Overgrown Manor: not a haunting, not a single monster, not a curse in the traditional sense, but a perpetual celebration that consumed its participants and incorporated their remains into itself as fuel. The Revel was self-sustaining through attrition.

The satyrs sang their feelings about the arrangement throughout the campaign:

Oh, have you seen them in the street, a hundred sets of iron feet, they clank-clank-clank in perfect time to prosecute some pointless crime, their backs are straight their faces sour they have not cracked a smile in an hour they eat their rations hard and dry and watch us with a judging eye, the Iron Legion got two left feet.

They also sang about the party itself:

We rolled into Raventree on a Tuesday maybe Thursday, the wine was already flowing and the grapes were getting hazy, the lady said one night only with a smile so very thin, but we satyrs know a party when the party is letting in. The revel never ends, the revel never ends, the glasses never empty and the night has got no friends, we dance until we are breathless we sing until we are hoarse, this party has got no finish it is the satyr only course.

They sang about Hjumpik and Toad Lee specifically:

Hjumpik, oh the dwarf with the hero stride, swinging that hammer like it is three sizes wide, Toad Lee, ax too tall, trip once more and you will dig your own crawl.

Waluigi is choosing not to document what they sang about him. It was accurate and he does not need it preserved.

## Sergeant Coldbrook, the Legion Reach, and the


Invitation

Sergeant Varn Coldbrook of the Iron Legion appeared in a room containing dead bodies, alive and unharmed despite his entire squad being dead around him. He claimed the purple one had destroyed his unit. He described himself as being on a mission and offered a deal: eliminate the Revelmaster and earn the Iron Legion favor. He left without confirming which faction he belonged to, though his phrasing and equipment suggested Legion origin.

Eager noticed he was unharmed and said nothing. Waluigi noticed Eager noticing and said nothing. Nobody said anything, which is sometimes how the most important observations are made in Disaster Inc.: silently, privately, filed away for later.

Waluigi explained afterward that the sergeant had sent guards after him, and Waluigi had used a fireball to destroy all of them, then looted the bodies. He gave Hjumpik a flask labeled Satyr Regret. He gave Toad Lee a sealed envelope. The envelope contained an invitation printed on human skin vellum inviting the holder to the Orange Heir Banquet. The ink smelled of rot. The text read: The Rot is Ripe. The Time is Nigh. Come feed.

Waluigi used the invitation to pick his teeth and then took it back.

The satyrs offered Hjumpik food that he identified on examination as a naturally occurring poison, an alcoholic substance so powerful it would kill on consumption. The satyrs knew about the party plans in detail, singing about them mid-conversation. Information traveled through the Revel network with no apparent delay, which meant privacy within the Overgrown Manor was maintained only by the other parties choosing not to act on what they knew.

## Dyanos, the Gallery of Three, and the Bathtub Monster


Toad Lee, separated from the group after mushroom spores temporarily removed his sense of having a face, encountered Dyanos, a guard who served Chirneros, Lord-champion of Fey, with fifteen years of service. Dyanos introduced Toad Lee to a personal gallery bathed in warm light with gauzy curtains, cases of strange and wonderful items along every wall, and a towering mirror along the southeast wall that reflected the room at night despite it being daytime, so convincingly that the mirror seemed to drink the surrounding light into itself.

Three miniature statues stood in one section: green, red, and blue. Dyanos explained their meanings. Green represented Survival, Adaptation, the Ones Who Endure. Red represented Violence, Consequence, Irreversibility. Blue represented Control, Cold, Memory. These were ancient, predating the Revel and possibly predating the manor itself.

Dyanos asked Toad Lee what he thought they represented. Toad Lee guessed seasons. Dyanos said no. He then handed Toad Lee a purple crystal frog, noting that it was interesting how a toad gravitated toward crystal frogs. Toad Lee said in a way yeah with the understated acceptance of someone receiving a compliment that is also a category observation.

They entered the bathhouse together for what was supposed to be a restorative rest, removed their armor, put on robes, and discussed the nature of the Doughnut World while the waterfall fountain filled the room with flowing water sounds and colorful plants overflowed from corner planters. Then a massive plant arm emerged from a pile of leaves, the rest of the body following until the abomination of plant matter stood fully upright with dangerous-looking talons, and tackled Toad Lee directly into its stomach.

Dyanos stabbed it with his weapon. Toad Lee tried to damage it from the inside and missed. The guard ran out to get help. Toad Lee burst out of the creature and flew across the room, then evacuated the gallery and found Dyanos outside asking what should they do. Toad Lee said he was beaten up and could not kill that thing. He cried. Then he heard an explosion south of the manor and decided to get a drink instead. They went to the bar, where someone had bought everything, all the beer paid for by an unidentified patron. Toad Lee rested. He did not ask who had bought the drinks and Waluigi thinks this was wise.

## Azure Warning, the Midnight Gate, and the Recurring Collapse


Azure the Rakshasa delivered the most significant intelligence of the campaign in fragments scattered across multiple appearances. She said she had seen many planes fall and collapse and had come to see it again. She almost mentioned the Regal Empire before stopping herself. She confirmed the BF calendar marked a previous collapse cycle, implying the current dimensional crisis was not unprecedented but cyclical. She gave three escape options: the Oracle portal plan requiring chalk and circle repair, the Midnight Gate that could be activated independently without the Oracle, or killing mostly everyone except the orange heir.

She immediately regretted mentioning the Midnight Gate and clarified she had not told them its location so it was probably fine that she had disclosed its existence. She said she would go make arrangements. A second Rakshasa appeared moments later, greeting Hjumpik cheerfully and offering him a flower. This was a different Rakshasa than Azure. Hjumpik had been tricked. The first had extracted information by appearing trustworthy while the second confirmed the deception by appearing friendly immediately after.

The Midnight Gate activated briefly when the second Rakshasa entered it and vanished. The portal deactivated. An escape route was discovered and lost inside a single conversation.

Perrius Annmatar spoke directly into Hjumpik mind with a warning: the timelines must not be severed or the plan would collapse. The heir must be killed unless an illegitimate heir could be found. There needed to be an odd number of Oracles because even was balanced and odd was irregular. If only one Oracle remained, probability would become 100% and the outcome would be fixed. Hjumpik gave the ghost a thumbs up, which is the most Hjumpik possible response to receiving existential cosmic intelligence through telepathy while standing in a fairy manor hallway.

## The Ritual Materials and the State of the Deadline


The current ritual materials checklist: chalk acquired from Wario counterfeit supplies, bone still needed and potentially available from satyr remains or fallen enemies, iron potentially available from Wario cannonball though that cannonball keeps getting lost, ash obtainable from burned furniture. The circle construction in the master bedroom is underway but will take four days, finishing precisely on the night before the five-night satyr eviction deadline.

This timing is either coincidental or deliberate. Waluigi does not believe in coincidence when dealing with Corvinarus family members who quote the three threads prophecy while building portals and managing party evictions simultaneously.

The five-night deadline itself may be a flexible construct. The Feywild measures time in obligations rather than sundowns, and the manor calendar has been demonstrably unreliable. Five nights may mean five sequential sundowns, five metaphorical thresholds, or five iterations of whatever event pattern Aurelian is using as her reference. What is clear is that consequences will follow its expiration, and those consequences involve at minimum the Iron Legion presence, the Revelmaster entity, the satyrs relationship with the Revel, and whatever Aurelian ritual is actually constructing in the master bedroom.

Waluigi does not fully trust Aurelian. Waluigi does not fully distrust Aurelian. She is doing something real with that chalk circle and she has agreed to send back more than just three members of the party if conditions are met, which suggests negotiating room exists. But the woman who snaps bodies into nonexistence and claims to be too fragile to fight while having draconic elemental resistances is not operating transparently, and transparent is the minimum Waluigi requires before extending genuine trust to anyone.

The Revelmaster must be dealt with. The ritual materials must be gathered. The satyrs must be evicted or relocated. The Legion presence must be monitored. Azure must be located again because her drunk flirting and dramatically convenient timing suggest she knows more than she is sharing and is choosing her moments carefully.

Waluigi has survived giant spiders, vampire dinner parties, dimensional fractures, a door slamming into him during a plant monster fight, and being led between two people by both hands simultaneously while a dryad compared the scene to kindergarten. Waluigi will survive five nights in a fairy manor with singing satyrs, a body-consuming Revel entity, a dragon-blooded aristocrat performing fragility, and a music box that never stops turning.

Probably.

WAH.

summary: Fawful—the mad tactician who somehow convinced five dragons to follow him—hosted a diplomatic gala that brought together representatives from nearly every significant faction in the region. The guest list read like a 'who's who' of people who want each other dead: Loyalist operatives, Regency diplomats, Rakasha chiefs, Iron Legion observers, independent power brokers, and apparently several individuals whose faction affiliations remain unclear. What happened at this gala has reshaped Waluigi's understanding of the assassination conspiracy, the current crisis, and the relationship between them. Chief Thornpaw confirmed his relationship with Princess Peach. Mistveil extracted intelligence that validated decades of Loyalist theories. Fawful demonstrated capabilities that terrify everyone who wasn't already terrified of him. And Waluigi was NOT INVITED. Waluigi finds this personally offensive. Waluigi's invitation was probably lost in the mail. Waluigi chooses to believe this. WAH.
description:
Waluigi is documenting the gala based on secondhand accounts, intercepted communications, and the testimony of individuals who attended. Waluigi was not present—a fact that Waluigi attributes to postal errors rather than deliberate exclusion—so this entry necessarily relies on sources of varying reliability.

## The Host — Fawful's Rising Threat


Before discussing the gala, Waluigi must establish who Fawful IS, because understanding the host illuminates the event.

Fawful is... complicated. He began as a minor figure—an assistant to a witch named Cackletta who caused problems in the Beanbean Kingdom years ago. After Cackletta's defeat, Fawful seemed to fade into obscurity. Most assumed he was dead, imprisoned, or irrelevant.

They were wrong.

Fawful reemerged in the current crisis as something far more dangerous than anyone anticipated. He has somehow brokered an alliance with FIVE DRAGONS—the survivors of Ignis's death earlier in 1040 BF. He walked through their combined breath attacks unburned. No one knows how. The Star Spirits' prophecy allegedly calls him 'the one who cannot burn,' which is either prophetic significance or coincidental phrasing depending on your interpretive framework.

Fawful's speech patterns are distinctive—a mixture of broken syntax, food metaphors, and unsettling intensity that makes every statement sound simultaneously ridiculous and threatening. He refers to himself in third person. He makes declarations about 'fury' and 'doom' with the same casual tone others use to discuss weather.

He is either genuinely mad, performing madness strategically, or operating on a level of cognition that appears mad to those who cannot follow it. Waluigi cannot determine which.

## The Gala — Purpose and Attendees


Fawful hosted the gala ostensibly as a 'diplomatic summit'—an opportunity for regional factions to discuss the escalating crisis, the Planar Fracture, and the general collapse of everything. The actual purpose was almost certainly intelligence gathering, power demonstration, and whatever else Fawful considers entertaining.

Confirmed attendees included:

- **Chief Thornpaw** of the Rakasha, attending with a small delegation
- **Mistveil** of the Peach Loyalists, operating undercover as a minor noble
- **Regency diplomatic representatives** whose names have not been made public
- **Iron Legion observers** who claimed neutral status
- **Independent power brokers** from various territories
- **Fawful himself**, moving through the event with disconcerting energy
- **Dragons**—at least two of the five allied dragons were present, which Waluigi finds deeply alarming

The guest list suggests Fawful is positioning himself as a power broker—someone capable of bringing hostile factions together under his roof without them killing each other. Whether this represents genuine diplomatic capability or simply everyone being too afraid of the dragons to start violence is unclear.

## The Thornpaw Revelation — Confirming the Conspiracy


The most significant development at the gala was Chief Thornpaw's conversation with Mistveil.

Mistveil—operating undercover—approached Thornpaw during a lull in the formal proceedings. The conversation lasted approximately thirty minutes, according to sources. What was said has been reconstructed from Loyalist intelligence reports and Mistveil's own debriefing.

Thornpaw confirmed:

1. **The secret relationship with Princess Peach.** He described it as genuine love, not political alliance. They met during diplomatic negotiations and developed feelings that both knew were dangerous.

2. **The secret hatch.** Peach showed Thornpaw a hidden passage in her chambers—a route through which he could visit privately. He used this passage regularly during their relationship.

3. **The child.** Their relationship produced a heir—half-Human, half-Rakasha. This child's existence was known only to Peach, Thornpaw, and possibly a small circle of trusted individuals.

4. **The conspiracy motive.** Thornpaw believes the assassination was motivated partly by preventing this child from ever taking the throne. The court conservatives could not tolerate a hybrid heir.

This testimony validates the Loyalist narrative about the assassination—the narrative Captain Toadette has promoted for decades. Either Thornpaw is telling the truth and the Loyalists were right, or Thornpaw is coordinating with the Loyalists to establish a false narrative.

Waluigi has documented his uncertainty about Thornpaw's reliability in the Chief's separate entry. The gala revelation is SIGNIFICANT regardless of whether it's authentic.

## Fawful's Demonstration —


The Dragons Obey

During the gala, Fawful provided a demonstration of his alliance with the dragons. Details vary by account, but the consensus describes:

Fawful stood in the fortress courtyard while two dragons—the fire-breather Cindrus and the acid-spitter Corrosax—were positioned on either side. He spoke to them casually, making jokes about 'fury' and 'burning' that would be suicidal for anyone else.

Then he ordered them to breathe on him. SIMULTANEOUSLY.

Fire and acid struck Fawful from both directions. Guests reportedly screamed, dove for cover, or froze in shock. The breath attacks lasted several seconds—enough to incinerate or dissolve anything mortal.

When the attacks ceased, Fawful was standing exactly where he had been. Unburned. Undissolved. His clothes weren't even singed.

He laughed—that distinctive Fawful cackle—and said something like: 'Fawful has the immunity! The burning and the melting are having no purchase on Fawful's magnificent person! This is being the demonstration of why Fawful is the one you should be listening to, yes?'

The guests listened.

Waluigi does not know HOW Fawful survives dragonfire. Magical immunity? Artifact protection? Some property unique to his physiology? The mystery is as terrifying as the demonstration. If Fawful cannot be burned, conventional military opposition becomes... complicated.

## Intelligence Gathered — What Else Emerged?


Beyond Thornpaw's revelation, several other pieces of intelligence emerged from the gala:

**Iron Legion Expansion:**

Legion observers were overheard discussing 'Phase Three' of operations in the Midlands. The specific content was not captured, but the implication is that the Legion has plans beyond their current territorial control. They are not merely holding ground—they are preparing to expand.

**Regency Weakness:**

Regency diplomats appeared desperate throughout the event. Multiple sources describe them attempting to negotiate with Fawful directly—offering concessions, requesting alliance, seemingly willing to accept almost any terms. This suggests the Regency is weaker than their official communications indicate.

**Rakasha Positioning:**

Thornpaw's delegation included at least one spirit-walker. This individual was observed having conversations with multiple attendees—conversations conducted partly through dimensional means that other guests could not fully perceive. The Rakasha are gathering intelligence aggressively. They are preparing for something.

**Fawful's Knowledge:**

Fawful made comments throughout the evening that suggested disturbing levels of awareness. He referenced events that should have been secret. He mentioned names that should not have been known to outsiders. He implied knowledge of the Planar Fracture that exceeded what any single faction should possess.

Either Fawful has an exceptional intelligence network, or he has access to information through means that defy conventional explanation. Given his other impossible capabilities, the latter seems increasingly plausible.

## Waluigi's Absence — A Personal Grievance


Waluigi was not invited to Fawful's gala.

Waluigi chooses to believe this was an oversight—a postal error, a clerical mistake, an invitation lost in the chaos of current events. The alternative—that Fawful deliberately excluded Waluigi—is too offensive to contemplate.

Waluigi would have been an EXCELLENT guest. Waluigi has diplomatic experience. Waluigi has intelligence value. Waluigi has the kind of magnificent presence that elevates any gathering. Fawful's gala would have been improved by Waluigi's attendance.

Instead, Waluigi must reconstruct the event from secondhand accounts while others made history.

This is TYPICAL. This is the story of Waluigi's life. The important events happen without Waluigi. The critical conversations occur where Waluigi cannot hear them. The revelations emerge in rooms Waluigi was not invited to enter.

Waluigi will continue documenting regardless. Waluigi's exclusion does not diminish the event's significance. But Waluigi NOTES the exclusion. Waluigi will REMEMBER.

WAH.

summary: The Chaos Heart Crisis of 880BF was the closest reality has come to complete annihilation since the Long Dark, and unlike the Long Dark, this was not infrastructure failure but INTENTIONAL destruction orchestrated by Count Bleck using the Chaos Heart artifact. The crisis began with the forced marriage of Princess Peach and Bowser—a union that triggered the Chaos Heart's awakening and began the slow unraveling of dimensional barriers across all existence. Mario, Luigi, Princess Peach, and Bowser were scattered across dimensions. Luigi was captured and transformed into Mr. L. The Void expanded daily, consuming worlds and erasing them from existence. And in the end, Mario did not defeat Count Bleck through combat but through something far stranger—the power of love between Count Bleck and his lieutenant Tippi, formerly a human woman named Timpani whom Bleck had loved and lost. The Chaos Heart was destroyed. The Void collapsed. Reality survived. But the cost was staggering: hundreds dead from Mr. L's campaigns, dimensional barriers permanently weakened, and Luigi carrying fragments of Chaos Heart energy that would not manifest their full danger for another fifteen years. Waluigi was not present for these events, but Waluigi has interviewed survivors, obtained classified reports, and pieced together an account that the official histories mysteriously omit. WAH.
description:
Waluigi approaches this entry with the understanding that the Chaos Heart Crisis has been deliberately minimized in official histories. The Regency does not want people thinking too hard about how close everything came to ending, or about the role certain individuals played in nearly ending it. The Loyalists use the crisis primarily as ammunition against Luigi, ignoring the broader context. The Mages' Guild has classified most of their research into the crisis's dimensional effects. Everyone has reasons to keep the full truth obscured.

Waluigi does not have those reasons. Waluigi documents.

## The Beginning — A Wedding That Should Not Have Happened


The Chaos Heart Crisis began with a wedding. Not a joyful union but a forced ceremony—Count Bleck compelling Princess Peach and Bowser to marry against both their wills, using the dark magic of the Dark Prognosticus to conduct a ritual that should have been impossible. The marriage of a pure-hearted princess to a monster king triggered the awakening of the Chaos Heart, an artifact of such destructive potential that even dimensional entities feared its name.

Waluigi has spent considerable time trying to understand WHY this wedding worked. Marriage is a social construct, a legal arrangement, a ceremony with meaning only because people agree it has meaning. How could forcing two unwilling participants through wedding vows activate anything? The answer, according to sources Waluigi has consulted, lies in dimensional resonance. The ceremony was not about the participants' feelings but about the CONCEPT of union between opposing forces. Peach represented light, hope, the Mushroom Kingdom's royal lineage. Bowser represented darkness, conquest, the Koopa Kingdom's martial tradition.

Forcing them together created a paradox that reality could not resolve—and in that paradox, the Chaos Heart found purchase.

The moment the ceremony concluded, the Void began expanding. A growing sphere of absolute nothingness that consumed everything it touched—not destroying matter but ERASING it, removing existence itself from existence. Worlds began disappearing. Dimensional barriers began failing. The countdown to total annihilation began.

## The Scattered Heroes — Mario's Journey


The wedding ceremony scattered the participants across dimensions. Mario awoke in Lineland with no immediate understanding of what had happened. Peach was imprisoned in Castle Bleck. Bowser was lost somewhere between dimensions. And Luigi...

Luigi was captured.

Mario's journey to stop the Chaos Heart is well-documented in sources that focus on his heroics. He gathered the Pure Hearts—artifacts of crystallized love and hope that could counter the Chaos Heart's destructive energy. He traversed dimensions that should have been unreachable, fought enemies that should have been unbeatable, and demonstrated the legendary capabilities that made him the Mushroom Kingdom's greatest hero.

But Mario's journey was not purely successful. He did not save everyone. He did not stop every tragedy. And he did not reach Luigi before Nastasia's hypnotic restructuring was complete.

Waluigi has found accounts suggesting Mario encountered Mr. L during his journey—not Luigi, but MR. L, already transformed, already hostile. These encounters were not documented in official histories because they complicate the narrative of heroic rescue. Mario fought his own brother. Mario LOST to his own brother on at least one occasion, forced to retreat when the Brobot's firepower exceeded his ability to counter. The hero's journey included failures that no one wanted to remember.

## The Pure Hearts — Love Crystallized


The Pure Hearts were the key to stopping the Chaos Heart, but their nature has never been adequately explained in official accounts. Waluigi has researched extensively and developed a theory that the authorities would probably prefer remained unspoken.

The Pure Hearts were not artifacts in the traditional sense. They were not created by craftsmen or enchanted by mages. They were FORMED from moments of genuine love so powerful that the emotion crystallized into physical reality. Each Pure Heart represented a different relationship, a different form of love, a different connection between beings who cared for each other deeply enough to manifest that caring as dimensional energy.

Mario collected these Hearts by experiencing the love that created them—by witnessing relationships, honoring sacrifices, acknowledging connections that transcended individual existence. The Pure Hearts responded to RECOGNITION of love's power, not to combat prowess or magical ability.

This raises uncomfortable questions about the Chaos Heart's destruction. If Pure Hearts represented crystallized love, what did the Chaos Heart represent? The obvious answer is hate, destruction, entropy. But Waluigi's research suggests something more complex. The Chaos Heart may have represented love CORRUPTED—specifically, Count Bleck's love for Timpani, twisted by grief and rage into a desire to destroy the existence that had taken her from him.

If the Chaos Heart was corrupted love, then its destruction did not eliminate that love but RELEASED it. The energy went somewhere. And Luigi, contaminated by Chaos Heart exposure during his time as Mr. L, may have absorbed some of that released energy.

## Count Bleck —


The Villain Who Wanted to Die

Count Bleck is described in official histories as a dimensional conqueror seeking power. This description is incomplete to the point of dishonesty.

Bleck was originally a being called Lord Blumiere, a dimensional noble who fell in love with a human woman named Timpani. Their love crossed dimensional boundaries that should have been uncrossable. Blumiere's father, horrified by this transgression, used dark magic to scatter Timpani across dimensions—effectively killing her by dispersing her essence so thoroughly that no one could ever find all the pieces.

Blumiere's grief destroyed him. He found the Dark Prognosticus, a book of prophecy that promised the end of all existence. He embraced the prophecy because existence without Timpani was unbearable. He became Count Bleck, gathered servants who shared his nihilistic vision, and began the process of ending everything.

This is not the psychology of a conqueror seeking power. This is the psychology of a suicide determining to take the universe with him. Count Bleck did not want to rule—he wanted to STOP. Stop existing. Stop feeling. Stop remembering what he had lost.

The crisis ended not through Mario's combat victory but through Timpani's return. She had survived Blumiere's father's attack, though scattered and transformed. She had become Tippi, a Pixl guide who assisted Mario throughout his journey without either of them realizing her true identity. When she and Blumiere finally recognized each other, the love that had created the Chaos Heart was able to UNMAKE it—not through destruction but through restoration. They loved each other still. That love was stronger than Bleck's despair.

They sacrificed themselves together, using the Pure Hearts and their reunited love to collapse the Void and save existence. The gesture was beautiful, tragic, and absolutely genuine.

It was also incomplete.

## The


Incomplete Ending — What the Official History Omits

The Void collapsed. Reality survived. Count Bleck and Tippi disappeared, presumably destroyed or transformed into something beyond mortal comprehension. The heroes returned home. Everything was supposed to be fine.

Everything was not fine.

The Chaos Heart was destroyed, but destruction does not mean elimination in dimensional terms. Energy transforms. Power redistributes. The Chaos Heart's energy had to go SOMEWHERE when the artifact collapsed. Official histories are silent on this question because no one wants to answer it.

Waluigi has found evidence that the energy dispersed across three primary vectors:

First, it saturated Castle Bleck and the surrounding dimensional space. The castle still exists somewhere between planes, inaccessible but not destroyed. Mages' Guild expeditions have attempted to reach it and returned with reports of 'impossible geometry' and 'emotional contamination.' Something remains there that the Guild does not want to discuss publicly.

Second, it embedded itself in the dimensional barriers throughout the region. The barriers that separate planes were already weakened by the Void's expansion; the Chaos Heart's energy did not repair them but CHANGED them. This may explain why the Planar Fracture of 1040 BF occurred where and when it did—the barriers were compromised fifteen years earlier and finally failed under additional stress.

Third—and most disturbingly—it contaminated everyone who had direct exposure to the Chaos Heart during the crisis. This includes Peach, Bowser, and most significantly Luigi, who spent weeks in Castle Bleck as Mr. L, directly connected to the Chaos Heart's power through his Brobot and his service to Count Bleck.

Luigi carries fragments of the Chaos Heart within himself. This is Waluigi's conclusion based on extensive research. The authorities know this. The warrant charging Luigi with 'residual Mr. L activities' is not about crimes he committed fifteen years ago—it is about the dimensional contamination he still carries and what that contamination might do as the Planar Fracture destabilizes reality further.

## Casualty


Assessment — The Deaths No One Counts

The official death toll for the Chaos Heart Crisis is listed as 'minimal civilian casualties due to rapid response and dimensional isolation of affected areas.' This is a lie.

Waluigi has compiled evidence of at least 300 confirmed deaths directly attributable to crisis-related violence, primarily from Mr. L's military campaigns against Mushroom Kingdom forces. An additional 150-200 deaths can be attributed to dimensional instability—people who were caught in Void expansion zones, who fell through weakened dimensional barriers, who simply ceased to exist when the fabric of reality tore near them.

Beyond direct casualties, the crisis caused lasting psychological damage to thousands of witnesses. Soldiers who survived Mr. L's attacks suffer ongoing trauma. Civilians who glimpsed the Void describe nightmares that have not stopped in fifteen years. Dimensional researchers who studied the crisis developed conditions that the Mages' Guild refuses to name publicly.

The crisis also caused economic disruption that has never been fully calculated. Trade routes between dimensions were severed. Diplomatic relationships with beings from other planes collapsed. The tentative recovery from the Long Dark was set back by years as resources were diverted to crisis response and reconstruction.

The official narrative treats the Chaos Heart Crisis as a heroic adventure with a happy ending. The reality is a catastrophe that killed hundreds, traumatized thousands, weakened dimensional barriers that protect existence itself, and left Luigi carrying contamination that continues to threaten the kingdom.

WAH.

name: The Sermon of the Third Eye
title: The Day Waluigi Learned That People Have Built a Religion Around Archie Miser
date: Day 31, 1040 BF (Early Morning)
era: Raventree Crisis
location: A town near Raventree Manor — A place of worship
type: Religious Event / Theological Catastrophe / Personal Affront to Waluigi's Worldview
status: Ongoing — the religion still exists; Archie remains unaware; Waluigi has not recovered
summary: Remi ran into a sermon. This is how it started. Not with investigation, not with intelligence gathering, not with any kind of PLAN — Remi bolted past guards into a building and the party chased her and then they were all standing in a religious service dedicated to the worship of ARCHIE MISER as the God of the Third Eye. A living god. A god who is CURRENTLY walking around causing problems, setting things on fire, and getting stuck in collapsed hallways. A god who is, according to reliable reports, currently consorting with the Purple Legion. The congregation is composed of bugbears hiding from vampires. They believe Archie's divine presence protects them from the Corvinarus undead. And Green T — whose location the party has been trying to establish — was apparently HERE, told the bugbears that Archie had teamed up with the Purple Legion AND an aberration, and then LEFT. Waluigi has many feelings and none of them are peaceful.
description:
Context for why the party entered a religious building at four in the morning: Remi ran into it. That is the entire context. The party had arrived at a town near the manor seeking a moment of calm before continuing the search for Green T and Archie, and Remi decided that calmness was for OTHER people and sprinted past guards into a sermon. The party gave chase. The party ended up in a pew. This is what it is to travel with Remi.

## The Congregation (Bugbears, Hiding)


The building was full of bugbears. Not threatening bugbears — hiding bugbears. There is a distinction and it matters. These were not warriors or cultists with a militant theological agenda. These were REFUGEES. The Purple Legion — the Corvinarus vampiric branch that has been consolidating power throughout this crisis — had apparently been hunting them. And the bugbears had discovered, through whatever combination of desperate hope and pattern recognition allows people to find religion in impossible circumstances, that the vampires would not enter a place of worship.

So they stayed. And while they stayed, they needed something to believe in. Something that explained why THEIR place of worship had been protected. Something to give the protection a FACE.

They chose Archie Miser.

Waluigi does not understand why. Waluigi has been trying to understand why for longer than this particular crisis. There is something about Archie — something Waluigi cannot quantify, cannot document, cannot capture in any notation system — that makes people decide he is significant. Not competent. Not reliable. Not particularly wise. But SIGNIFICANT. Like a fire that is also somehow a lighthouse. You don't trust it with anything fragile, but you navigate by it.

The bugbears didn't choose Archie because he was safe. They chose him because he was a FRACTURE — the sermon's own word — and when everything is built on lies, a fracture is exactly what you want on your side.

## The Sermon (Waluigi Has Memorized Parts of It Against His Will)


Waluigi caught enough of the sermon to reconstruct its central arguments. He will document them here with the confidence of someone who both can't stop thinking about what he heard and is extremely unhappy about that.

*'You are not a saint, Archie. You are not a martyr. You are not even particularly kind. You are the fracture. You are the moment the mirror cracks and the reflection refuses to lie anymore.'*

Waluigi sat in that pew and thought: this is the most accurate description of Archie Miser he has ever encountered, delivered as PRAISE, by BUGBEARS, in a building they are hiding in.

The sermon addressed Archie directly. Not as an absent deity to be approached with reverence and distance. As someone who might actually walk in. Someone alive and present and expected. The preacher called him 'the living god who walks among us, whose third eye opened before he could speak his own name.' The third eye — the one that sees through lies, the one that the Regency and every authority structure fears — as the SOURCE of divinity rather than its PRODUCT.

Waluigi has complicated feelings about this theology. On one level, Waluigi finds the elevation of Archie to divine status categorically offensive because Waluigi has SEEN Archie get stuck in a hallway and that is not divine behavior. On another level — a level Waluigi will not publicly acknowledge and is only documenting because future historians deserve honesty — the sermon made a kind of sense. Power structures maintain themselves through consistent and confident lying. If there is a divine function, it might reasonably reside in the person who cannot stop SEEING THROUGH IT.

Waluigi does not believe Archie is a god. Waluigi does believe that Archie makes things impossible to ignore. And that, in a kingdom built on looking away, might function similarly.

## The Green T Problem (He WAS Here)


The bugbears had information. Green T had visited this congregation before the party arrived. This confirms that Green T is mobile, operational, and making choices — he is not captured, not lost, not in immediate danger requiring rescue. He is OUT THERE, making his way through the same crisis landscape as everyone else, and his most recent stop was a bugbear religious service dedicated to his companion.

But Green T's message was not comforting. He told the bugbears that Archie had teamed up with the Purple Legion. And with an aberration — described as 'like a ghost, a monster for sure.'

Eager said it couldn't be true. Markop said never mind, and moved them along. Waluigi noticed that Markop moved them along QUICKLY — the kind of quick that is not disinterest but avoidance. The kind that means the information landed and the implications are too large to process in a room full of religious refugees at four in the morning.

Archie, working with the Purple Legion. Archie, working with an aberration. Archie — the God of the Third Eye, the living fracture, the man the bugbears believe protects them from vampires — potentially working WITH the vampires.

Waluigi does not know if Green T's information is accurate. Green T has demonstrated questionable reliability and a tendency to appear in surveillance positions without announcing himself. But the information fits the warrant facts, it fits the pattern of Archie's trajectory through this crisis, and it fits Waluigi's GENERAL assessment that nothing is as it appears and everything is worse than expected.

The bugbears offered a trade. Bring Archie here, and Archie's physical presence would protect them from the Legion. Markop declined. Remi refused to give Archie up to dangerous people. Waluigi respected both positions even though neither solved anything.

## The Hidden Hatch (Something Is Underneath This Town)


As the party left — as Bowser retreated into his shell in the peaceful sunshine outside and guards walked right past him, which is either a testament to Bowser's disguise or the guards' complete indifference — a door was found open that no one admitted to opening. Beyond it: the sound of water. And a hatch. Secret. Concealed.

Waluigi does not know where the hatch leads. Waluigi does not know who opened the door. Waluigi knows that hidden hatches in towns near haunted manor houses that sit at the intersection of multiple supernatural power struggles are NEVER leading somewhere pleasant. They lead to tunnels. Tunnels lead to crypts. Crypts lead to whatever the Purple Legion has been building underground while everyone else was distracted by auctions and sermons and wardrobe-based combat.

The hatch is a problem that has not become a crisis yet. In Waluigi's experience, this means it will become a crisis at the WORST possible moment. That is the consistent pattern. Waluigi is documenting it NOW so that when the hatch reveals its catastrophic contents, the record will show that Waluigi noticed it FIRST.
