name: Archie's Return to the Shadow Estate
title: The Man Who Fought a God, Escaped a Prison, and Arrived on a Thundercloud
date: ~14th-16th Harvestide, 1040 BF (Shadowfell time — approximately one month has passed since the Planar Fracture in Shadowfell-relative chronology)
era: Raventree Crisis — Shadowfell Fragment / Astral Interlude / Material Plane Convergence
location: The Astral Altar, Shadow Estate Prison Cells, Shadow Estate Kitchen and Exterior, Shadowfell Forest, Tree of Woe Grove
type: Divine Confrontation / Prison Escape / Dimensional Transit / Party Convergence
status: Concluded — Archie survived the Toad God, escaped the Shadow Estate's prison, traveled on a thundercloud, and arrived at the Tree of Woe where the rest of the party was engaged with the Scarecrow
summary: I am documenting Archie Miser's return to the Shadow Estate based on Archie's own account, which he provided in fragments between bouts of exhaustion, defensive sarcasm, and the specific emotional flatness of someone who has been through something they have not finished processing. Archie was launched from the Oracle's ritual into the Astral Altar, where the Toad God was waiting for him. He fought a deity. He lost. He was teleported into the Shadow Estate's past or present, woke up in a room with two dogs and two arguing people, was imprisoned by Onyx Hand guards, escaped by disguising himself as a knight using empty quivers arranged to look like a sleeping person, talked his way past guards by pretending to have just verbally abused himself, electrocuted a guard at the front gate, and spent an unknown period wandering the Shadowfell wilderness before summoning a thundercloud and flying to the Tree of Woe, where he found the toads and the Scarecrow and decided to pick a fight with both. This is Archie. This is how Archie operates. I am furious and impressed in equal measure and I am documenting both because the record should be complete. WAH.
description:
I obtained this account from Archie directly, which means I obtained it in the specific way you obtain anything from Archie Miser: incompletely, out of order, with critical details either omitted because he forgot them or omitted because he decided they were not important, and with a defensive casualness that makes it difficult to determine which omissions are which. Archie does not narrate his own experiences the way a historian would. He narrates them the way a man who has been hit in the head too many times narrates things, which is to say he starts in the middle, jumps to the end, circles back to the beginning when prompted, and treats the most significant moments as asides while spending considerable time on details that have no strategic value whatsoever, like the taste of a fish he was given in a tavern or the quality of music sheets he tried to steal from a bar performer.

I have reconstructed the chronology from his fragments. Where gaps exist, I have noted them. Where his account contradicts observable facts, I have noted that too. Where his account is consistent with what I know independently, I have confirmed it. The result is the most complete version of Archie's journey from the Oracle's ritual to the Tree of Woe that the current intelligence environment permits.

I want to state for the record that Archie fought a god and his primary takeaway from the experience was that the god did not have a name he could remember. This is Archie. This is always Archie. I have spent this entire encyclopedia documenting his decisions and I have never once been able to predict which part of an experience he will consider worth remembering. A man who fought a deity and escaped a vampire prison and survived a month alone in a death dimension will tell you about the fish first. The deity comes later, if prompted. This is not dishonesty. It is the specific information architecture of someone whose brain files threats under 'things that happened' and files fish under 'things that mattered,' and the two categories do not overlap as much as a historian would prefer.

## The Ritual That Launched Him: Context and Suspicion


Before I document what happened to Archie in the Astral Altar, I need to document what I think happened in the ritual room, because the ritual is the mechanism that sent Archie where the Toad God could reach him, and the mechanism matters as much as the destination.

The Oracle's ritual was supposed to send Archie to the Shadowfell. The ritual used candles instead of a circle. I have documented this discrepancy extensively in a previous entry and I am not going to repeat the full analysis, but I need to state the core question again because it has not been answered and it gets more important every time new information arrives: did the Oracle need a circle, or did the Oracle never need a circle?

The Planar Fracture used a circle. Multiple participants. Geometric precision. Distributed anchor points. The circle was the mathematical infrastructure. Archie's unstable magic overwhelmed it and reality shattered. That is the documented cause of the dimensional crisis that everything since has been a consequence of.

The Oracle's Shadeward ritual used candles. One caster. Archie as anchor. No circle. No geometric infrastructure. The Oracle just lit candles and told Archie to stand in the middle of them. And Archie was launched not to the Shadowfell but to the Astral Altar, where the Toad God was waiting.

I have four theories about why the ritual deposited Archie in the wrong location and I have documented them before, but the Toad God's dialogue during the encounter adds weight to one of them that I want to flag specifically.

The Toad God said: I had to wait for your friends to be occupied to bring you here.

The friends being occupied was Berio's arrest operation. The Regency forces arrived to round up the party at exactly the moment the ritual was reaching its peak. The Toad God waited for the arrest to isolate Archie, then pulled him into the Astral Altar.

This means either the Toad God has real-time surveillance of the Material Plane and seized an opportunity, or the Toad God knew the arrest was coming and possibly arranged it, or the Oracle's ritual was designed to deposit Archie somewhere the Toad God could intercept and the Oracle knew this was going to happen.

I keep coming back to option three. The Oracle lit candles. The Oracle did not use a circle. The Oracle looked wide-eyed and said it might be too powerful. And then Archie was delivered directly to the entity that the Oracle's own plans have been operating in the shadow of since the beginning. The Oracle's relationship with the Toad God is one of the largest gaps in my intelligence, and every new piece of information about either of them makes the gap feel more deliberate rather than more accidental.

The Oracle agreed to Vivian C.'s plan to thrall the party and cut the three planes. The Oracle facilitated Archie's departure through a ritual that sent him to a god instead of a dimension. The Oracle kept flesh vats in the Planar Sanctum and admitted to pulling the wrong lever. The Oracle is 46 years old in Toad years, which compound differently than human years, and has been operating at a level of dimensional manipulation that makes the Mages Guild look like amateurs.

I do not trust the Oracle. I have never trusted the Oracle. But I am now specifically distrusting the ritual that launched Archie, because the ritual's outcome, the arrest's timing, and the Toad God's dialogue form a pattern that is too convenient to be coincidental and too important to dismiss.

## The


Astral Altar: Archie Meets the God He Made

Archie woke up in the Astral Altar. Crystalline structures around him. A warppad he did not remember from a previous visit. Darkness ahead. And the Toad God standing before him for the first time since Edgeshade, though Archie would not have recognized him as the same toad because the Crystal Star's transformation does not preserve the original form. The abandoned toad became a god. The god does not look like a toad anymore. The god looks like what abandonment and fury look like when they have been given cosmic permission to take shape.

Archie said: Hello, Toad Prime. How's it going?

I am going to spend time on this greeting because it reveals everything about the gap between what Archie understands about his situation and what his situation actually is.

Archie called the Toad God 'Toad Prime.' Not 'Your Divinity.' Not 'The God of Vengeance Born From My Worst Decision.' Not 'The Being Whose Entire Existence Is a Response to My Personal Failure.' Toad Prime. A nickname. A casual designation. The kind of thing you call someone at a sports event when you cannot remember their actual name and are too socially committed to the interaction to ask.

The Toad God told Archie he had not collected a single star shard yet and that his plan was progressing at a steady rate and that sooner or later the world would be his.

Archie said: Shame. Good for you. My mind's not in a good headspace.

A god announced global domination. Archie responded with mild congratulations and a mental health update. The emotional register mismatch is so severe that it creates a kind of diplomatic vertigo. The Toad God is operating in the register of cosmic ultimatum. Archie is operating in the register of casual acquaintance. Neither is adjusting to the other. Neither can adjust to the other because the gap between 'I will own the world' and 'my mind's not in a good headspace' is not bridgeable through communication. It is bridgeable only through one of them deciding that the other's register is the correct one, and neither of them is going to do that because the Toad God's register is divine and Archie's register is Archie.

The Toad God noted he could simply kill Archie now. He did not. Instead he made demands: Archie must be the one to collect the star shard. No one else. The Toad God wanted it specifically from Archie's hands.

I need to document what this demand implies because it changes the star shard economy in ways that the previous entries did not fully capture.

The Toad God does not want just any person to collect the remaining star shards. He wants Archie. Specifically Archie. The man who abandoned him. The man whose fire magic shattered reality. The man whose entropy bleeds through dimensional boundaries. The Toad God has a specific use for Archie in his plan, and that use requires Archie to be the one handling the shards.

Why? I have theories.

Theory one: Archie's entropy makes him a uniquely effective shard-carrier. The Crystal Star responds to emotional architecture. Archie's emotional architecture is unstable, powerful, and prone to producing catastrophic magical events. If the Toad God needs the shards to do something specific when they are collected, Archie's instability might be the catalyst. The Toad God is not asking Archie to be a courier. He is asking Archie to be a detonator.

Theory two: the Toad God's divine nature requires symmetry. The god was created by Archie's abandonment. The god's plan requires Archie's participation. The deity and the man who made the deity are bound in a cycle that cannot be completed by substituting someone else. The Crystal Star's transformative logic operates on emotional resonance, and the resonance between Archie and the Toad God is the specific frequency that the plan requires. No one else vibrates at that frequency because no one else abandoned the toad.

Theory three: the Toad God is lying. He does not actually need Archie specifically. He is telling Archie that he does because the demand keeps Archie engaged. A man who has been told he is essential to a god's plan will not simply walk away and forget about the star shards. He will keep encountering them because the god told him they were his responsibility. The demand is not operational. It is psychological. It keeps Archie in the game.

I suspect elements of all three theories are simultaneously true because that is how cosmic entities operate in this campaign. They are never doing one thing. They are doing several things at once and presenting the version that produces the behavior they want from the person they are talking to.

Archie said: You seem pretty alright. Do you want a full on fleshed out opinion?

The Toad God said: You dare insult a god?

Archie was launched off the floating stone platform by divine force. He sloppily summoned a cloud. It was a rain cloud because Archie's weather magic reflects his emotional state and his emotional state at that moment was miserable, so the cloud rained on him while he floated on it. The image of Archie Miser sitting on a sad rain cloud while a god destroys the rock he was just standing on is simultaneously pathetic and completely honest, and I find both qualities admirable in their own way because at least the rain cloud is not pretending to be something it is not.

The Toad God destroyed the asteroid with a giant hammer. Archie ran. Hit a wall. Another wall. Another. They shattered. Illusions. The space they were in was constructed from controlled perception, and the Toad God was peeling the perception away layer by layer to show Archie what was underneath.

The Toad God said: I remember you told me to wait. That was the best day of my life.

I am going to spend significant time on this line because it is the most important thing the Toad God has ever said and because Archie treated it as background noise.

The Toad God's best day was the day Archie abandoned him.

The abandoned toad was waiting in Edgeshade. The town was burning. Dragons were falling from the sky. Archie had said wait here, I will be right back. Archie left with the pirates. Archie never came back. The toad waited. The toad realized he had been lied to. The Crystal Star fell from the sky and landed at his feet. The toad picked it up. The fury and the betrayal and the cosmic artifact fused. A god was born.

The best day of his life.

Not the worst. The best. The abandonment was the best thing that ever happened to him because the abandonment was what made him a god. Without Archie leaving, there would have been no fury. Without the fury, the Crystal Star would not have had the emotional architecture to build a deity from. Without the deity, there would have been no plan, no star shard economy, no Crown Shard holder called Rebellion, no distributed fragments, no cave systems with Star Sprites defending pieces of the bomb that already went off once.

Archie's abandonment is the origin event of the entire star shard crisis. And the Toad God is GRATEFUL for it.

This is the most psychologically devastating thing I have documented in this encyclopedia, and I have documented Order 120 and the barrel toads and Remi being turned to stone and auctioned. The Toad God THANKS Archie for the betrayal because the betrayal made him divine. The trauma is the gift. The wound is the crown. Everything the Toad God is, everything the Toad God plans to do, everything the star shard economy represents in terms of cosmic-scale threat, traces back to one man's decision to run away from one toad in one burning town.

Archie's response to learning that his worst moment was the Toad God's best moment was: Yeah, I told you to wait, but there was other stuff going on. My memory is foggy. It was so long ago. But I guess I was entrusting you to do something and you did not follow.

He does not remember. He does not remember what he was entrusting the toad to do. He does not remember the specific shape of the abandonment that created a god. He was there. He made the decision. He left. And the specifics are foggy.

This is not cruelty. This is worse than cruelty. Cruelty remembers what it did. Archie's carelessness does not even retain the details of its own consequences. The Toad God's entire existence is built on a moment that Archie has half-forgotten. The god remembers everything. The man who made the god remembers almost nothing. The asymmetry between those two memories is the specific frequency of their relationship, and it will not resolve through conversation because you cannot bridge the gap between someone who considers a moment the defining event of their cosmic existence and someone who considers the same moment vaguely familiar.

Archie felt a tearing in his stomach. A bubble barrier absorbed some damage. He said: You know what, Toad Prime, wait, what's your name? It's on the tip of my tongue. Even after I hurt you I have a big enough heart to reach out towards you again. I'll at least try, but I'm going to do it my way. I'm not going out without a fight.

He does not know the Toad God's name. He cannot remember the name of the person he abandoned, the person who became a god because of him, the person whose existence is the single largest cosmic-scale threat in the current campaign. The name is on the tip of his tongue. It will not arrive. Archie is going to fight a god whose name he cannot remember because the abandonment that made that god was not important enough to Archie to retain the details.

I find this simultaneously heartbreaking and infuriating and I am documenting both because both are honest responses to the same information.

## The Fight: Fire Against Fire-Immunity


Archie firebolted the Toad God in the eye. Used a storm to rain on his head with thunder. Ascended higher and hit him with a thundershock. The attacks were not fire-based, which is significant because Archie's instinct is always fire and the fact that he opened with lightning suggests he had either learned from the Shadowfell's fire suppression or was adapting in real-time to the Astral Altar's physics.

The Toad God laughed. Swung his hammer. Archie went flying like a pinball, hitting planetoid after planetoid. He was pinned down, badly injured.

The Toad God said: You're not strong enough to face me. Any last words?

Archie said: If there is any, I would say... FIREBALL.

A giant fireball engulfed the cloud. Archie catapulted himself using a small knife thrown at the god's face. The combination of fireball propulsion and knife deployment is the kind of simultaneous multi-system improvisation that Archie produces under maximum pressure, and it is genuinely impressive even when it is also genuinely insane. He used his own explosion as a launch mechanism and his dinner knife as a projectile weapon against a deity. This is not a plan. This is desperation that has been refined by experience into something that LOOKS like a plan.

The Toad God was engulfed in flames and stunned. Then he came out of the smoking fire and laughed.

I'm immune to fire, the Toad God said.

Of course he is. The god born from Archie's abandonment is immune to Archie's primary weapon. The Crystal Star transforms emotional architecture into divine capability, and the toad's emotional architecture was built around surviving Archie. The fire that should have killed him in Edgeshade did not, and the fire that Archie throws at him now cannot, because they are the same fire and the god has already survived it once at the cosmic level.

Every time Archie throws fire at the Toad God, he is confirming the god's origin story. The fire is not a weapon against this enemy. The fire is a PRAYER. It is the thing that made the god, offered again, and the god consumes it the way fire consumes air, not as destruction but as sustenance. Archie's fire feeds the Toad God's identity. The more fire Archie produces, the more divine the Toad God becomes, because the Toad God IS the survival of Archie's fire given cosmic form.

This is the cruelest design I have ever documented. The man's greatest weapon reinforces his greatest enemy. The thing Archie does best is the thing that makes the Toad God stronger. The only way Archie can fight the Toad God effectively is by NOT being Archie, and Archie cannot not be Archie because Archie is the most irreducibly himself person I have ever met.

Archie was hit from behind. Two star spirits arrived, heading toward the Toad God, reporting that someone had stolen a star shard. The Toad God slammed both star spirits into rocks and declared that this was his and Archie's battle, which means even the arrival of cosmic messengers bearing intelligence about the theft of divine fragments is less important to the Toad God than the personal confrontation with the man who made him.

Archie asked about the missing shard. The Toad God pointed at Archie. A spell flew. Archie did not know if it hit. He blacked out.

## The Shadow Estate Prison: Waking Up Wrong


Archie woke up in a room with two dogs barking at him and two people arguing. The room was the Beastmaster's Death Lounge, which I recognized from his description before he finished describing it because I have documented Vaxillus's space extensively. The taxidermied heads. The exotic furs. The weapon racks with old weapons of dark ashen wood. The crossbows named Blood Spiller and Heart Killer and Shadow Piercer and Soul Needler. The peephole behind the elk head. Archie was in the Beastmaster's domain.

The temporal question remains unresolved. Archie's arrival coincides with a moment from a previous session where Markop opened a door, suggesting the Toad God deposited Archie into the manor's timeline at a specific juncture rather than simply dropping him into the present. Whether this was the past, a temporal echo, or the same present approached from a different dimensional angle, I cannot determine. The Shadowfell's time dilation makes every temporal claim unreliable. A month has passed in Shadowfell-relative time. Days have passed in Material Plane time. The Feywild is running its own calendar that I have stopped trying to synchronize with anything because the Feywild's clocks are a form of performance art rather than measurement.

Guards recognized him. Archie Miser, they said. Dogs bit his arm. They dragged him downstairs. Archie smiled and laughed, which is his consistent response to being captured, and which I interpret as either extraordinary confidence or the specific dissociation of someone who has been in enough bad situations that the arrival of another one registers as familiar rather than frightening.

They told him he would be bitten into a vampire sooner or later. He asked them to tell him when. They left.

## The Escape: Empty Quivers and Self-Criticism


Archie was alone in his cell. The lock was a mosaic puzzle featuring a toad in a black shirt with a church background, which I am noting because the church imagery connects to the Church of the Third Eye that the party would later encounter in the Shadowfell towns, the cult that worships Archie as a god. A prison lock decorated with the imagery of a religion that does not yet exist, or that already exists in a timeline that Archie has been dropped into sideways. The temporal implications make my head hurt and I am choosing to file them rather than resolve them.

Archie assessed his resources. He had empty quivers. He arranged six of them to look like a person sleeping on their side, facing away from the door. Two for each leg section. The silhouette, from outside the cell looking through bars or a window, would read as a body at rest. It would not survive close inspection. It did not need to survive close inspection. It needed to survive the attention span of guards who believed their prisoner was secure and who had been told the prisoner was crying.

Archie found old guard equipment in the cell and disguised himself as an Onyx Knight. The disguise was constructed from prison cell materials in under ten minutes. I want to note that this skill, the ability to construct a convincing institutional disguise from whatever is available in a confined space under time pressure, is not a skill that appears in Archie's documented background. He is listed as a fire mage with diplomatic liability tendencies. He is not listed as a trained infiltrator with improvised costuming capabilities. Either Archie has skills he has never disclosed, or the specific creativity that Archie's brain produces under threat includes costume design alongside fireball deployment.

I suspect the latter.

Archie's creativity is not specialized.

It is omnivorous.

When his primary tool, fire, is unavailable, his brain does not shut down.

It starts producing alternative solutions from whatever material is in reach.

Quivers become bodies.

Guard uniforms become disguises.

The creativity that normally manifests as combustion manifests instead as deception.

The underlying engine is the same.

The output changes based on available fuel.

Archie headed upstairs into a storage room. He heard guards celebrating above. They were eating while monitoring his cell, enjoying both the food and the spectacle of having Archie Miser imprisoned.

Archie, in full disguise, climbed to their level. He tripped over a box. A loud crash. The guards heard.

Archie, responding to 'who are you' while standing in a storage room in stolen armor having just tripped over a box, said: I just came down here to tell that wretched Archie, that human manor-lord-killing monster, what I think of him. For, you know, he is a criminal in every sense of the word, and I gave him a tearing into.

He then added, with the improvisational confidence of someone who has decided that the lie's momentum is more important than its plausibility: Oh yeah, and he is really depressed. He is sobbing in his cell right now.

A guard said: Can I see it? That sounds great. Come on, let's check it out.

Archie said: Gladly, lead the way.

The guard went downstairs toward the cell containing six quivers arranged in the shape of a sleeping man. Archie barricaded the door behind him.

I need to document the full sequence of what Archie accomplished here because the individual components are each impressive and the combination is extraordinary.

First: he constructed a decoy from empty quivers that was convincing enough to prevent the guards from immediately recognizing that the cell was empty. The decoy did not need to survive interrogation. It needed to survive a glance through bars from a guard who was expecting to see a prisoner and whose brain would fill in the details because brains complete patterns rather than verifying them.

Second: he constructed a guard disguise from prison cell materials that was convincing enough to pass in a storage room in poor lighting while the observer's attention was split between the unexpected noise and the expectation that everyone in the building was authorized to be in the building.

Third: he performed enthusiasm about having verbally abused himself. He played a character whose defining trait was hatred of Archie Miser, and he played it convincingly enough that the guard not only believed the performance but wanted to see the results. The guard wanted to watch Archie cry. Archie provided the opportunity by directing the guard toward a room containing the evidence of crying, which was six quivers and a locked door.

Fourth: he barricaded the door behind the guard. The guard went in. The guard found quivers. The guard could not get out. Archie was already moving.

This is the kind of multi-layered improvisation that I associate with experienced infiltrators, not with fire mages who resolve diplomatic disputes through combustion. Archie is not supposed to be good at this. Archie's documented skill set does not include prison escapes, costume design, or performance art involving self-criticism as a social weapon. And yet here he is, having escaped a vampire prison through a combination of all three, and when he told me about it later his primary emphasis was on how the dog had bitten his arm, not on the escape itself, because Archie files escape from imprisonment under 'things that happened' and files dog bites under 'things that mattered.'

Archie passed through the kitchen where an unidentifiable creature with jet-black fur was being butchered, its purple meat producing viscous blue blood that evaporated into gray haze. A servant said: Great, what are you going to do, take more of our food? Archie did not take their food. This may be the only documented instance of Archie exercising restraint during an operation, and it occurred because he was in a hurry rather than because he had developed impulse control.

At the front gate, two guards asked why he was leaving his post. Archie said he was meeting someone in the forest, an urgent emergency. They asked who authorized it. Archie said the person with the two dogs, meaning Vaxillus the Beastmaster.

One guard said: Vaxillus is a girl.

Archie had misgendered the Beastmaster during his escape. The correction was delivered with the flat certainty of someone who has corrected this specific error before. The correction created approximately two seconds of social awkwardness, which was enough for Archie to assess his options.

The guard said: We don't want to fight. Follow me.

Archie's response was the only response Archie would ever give to a guard saying 'follow me' in a vampire estate he was escaping from. He sent electricity through his hands into the knight beside him. The guard collapsed. The other guard went inside for reinforcements. Archie ran into the Shadowfell forest and did not look back.

## The Month Alone: What Archie Does Not Talk About


Archie spent approximately one month alone in the Shadowfell wilderness.

He does not talk about the month. He mentions it in passing as though it were a scheduling inconvenience. He does not describe where he slept. He does not describe what he ate. He does not describe how he maintained his magical capability in a dimension that suppresses magic, or how he navigated without landmarks in a landscape of petrified trees and bruised purple sky, or how he processed the fact that he had been launched through dimensions by an entity he fought and lost to, imprisoned by vampires, and was now completely alone in a plane adjacent to death with no way to contact anyone.

I am going to document what I think happened during the month because someone should and Archie will not.

He wandered. He returned to the manor periodically, finding it more restored each time. Crumbling stone replaced with immaculate grey slate. Collapsing roofs replaced with flawless jet-black tiles. Dead plants replaced with unnatural blooms on charcoal stems with thorns like raptor talons. The grass trimmed but colorless. The leaves grey. The branches coal-black. Everything in the estate holding shadows more readily than natural, as though the building were absorbing the darkness rather than standing in it.

Guards told him it was too dangerous to enter. The stones were failing. Too much time had passed. Archie got scared and ran.

Archie got scared. I am documenting this because Archie does not get scared in the way that his documented behavior suggests. Archie walks into dragon lairs and says 'FIREBALL.' Archie sits across from vampire lords and argues about greenhouse repairs. Archie calls a deity 'Toad Prime.' But the manor, at the end of a month alone, scared him enough that he ran into the forest rather than enter it.

What did a month of solitary survival in the Shadowfell do to Archie's fear thresholds? The Shadowfell suppresses everything. It suppresses fire. It suppresses color. It suppresses sound. It suppresses hope. A month in that environment does not just weaken you physically. It erodes the internal structures that allow you to function, the confidence, the denial, the stubbornness that Archie uses as armor. After a month, the armor has been worn thin by entropy, and things that would not have scared the Archie of Day One scare the Archie of Day Thirty.

The manor scared him because the manor had changed and Archie had changed and the combination of those changes produced something he could not walk into. This is the Shadowfell's actual weapon. Not vampires. Not the Scarecrow. Not the Tree of Woe. Time. Time and isolation and the slow erosion of the internal architecture that makes a person capable of entering rooms they should not enter.

After the month, the manor flashed. The walls crumbled. Archie was suddenly back in the Ruined Manor's mirror room with Usk, Orvinder, and Mages Guild agents waiting for him. The dimensional mechanics that produced this transition are unclear. Whether the manor ejected him, whether the month created some kind of saturation threshold that triggered the transit, or whether the Oracle or the Toad God pulled him back at a predetermined moment, I cannot determine.

The Mages Guild drafted him. They revealed that Toadburt had been their sleeper agent. They revealed the Regulator Plane. They introduced Luigi, who bumped into the door frame because even ghost-busting plumbers have coordination issues. Archie was told his power came with oversight and he now worked for the Guild. He had no choice.

Archie explored the Ruined Manor with Luigi and Thornbury. Luigi tore open military ration packs with practiced efficiency. Thornbury tracked every expenditure. A rope broke and Thornbury presented an itemized bill totaling 2,062 gold. Archie overheard the Guild discussing, in partially encrypted communications, that clearing the ghosts might kill him, and the response was 'yes.' They were willing to let Archie die as a side effect of the ghost-clearing operation. Archie heard this and continued working with them because the alternative was worse and because Archie's relationship with self-preservation has always been more negotiable than most people's.

Mystic Morel appeared. Sang 'Shuffle the Deck, Dear Hero' while stealing Archie's watch, keys, and compass. Used the stolen items to open a planar portal. Stepped through while saying: Unless it served a greater play.

Morel left. Archie was alone again. The singing fortune teller had taken his dimensional tools and his dignity and had given him nothing in return except lyrics that might have been prophecy and might have been mockery and were probably both.

## The Thundercloud: What Desperation Looks Like


When It Can Fly

Archie summoned a thundercloud.

I do not know the exact mechanism. Archie's weather magic has been documented at various points, usually manifesting as clouds that reflect his emotional state. A sad Archie produces a rain cloud. An angry Archie produces a storm. An Archie who has spent a month alone in a death dimension, been drafted by the Mages Guild against his will, been robbed by a singing toad while pinned to a bed, heard his employers discuss his acceptable death through a door, and decided that enough was enough, apparently produces a thundercloud capable of sustained flight.

He rose above the Shadowfell's canopy. He looked down at the landscape. He saw the Shadow Estate. He saw the grounds. He saw the hedge maze that the party had been navigating and fighting through and nearly dying in. He saw the Tree of Woe.

He saw the toads.

Markop, Remi, Salam, Eager, and Toad Lee were at the Tree of Woe, engaged with the Scarecrow. The same Scarecrow that offered Remi a swing with a noose. The same entity that sliced through Voss guards like armor was decorative. The entity that told the party it had been going easy on them.

Archie flew his thundercloud toward the Tree of Woe.

I want to document what this looked like from the ground because the image matters for understanding what it meant to the people who were there.

The party had been fighting. They had been losing. They had been through the Scarecrow's games, the swing with the spike and the noose, the root-bow, the singing Mazebounds, the corpses falling from branches like pinatas. Markop had taken crows to the back while covering the retreat. Salam had carved a chunk from the tree and heard it scream. Remi had been hit in the head with a scythe. They were bleeding, exhausted, and running out of the grove when they looked up and saw a thundercloud.

On the thundercloud was a man they had not seen since the Planar Fracture scattered everyone across dimensions. A three-eyed fire mage trailing lightning, flying on a cloud made of his own anger, heading directly toward the thing that had been trying to kill them.

Archie did not arrive because he calculated that his friends needed help. Archie arrived because Archie saw a fight and flew toward it because that is what Archie does. The heroism, if it exists, is in the pattern rather than the intent. Archie keeps showing up. He keeps showing up damaged, underprepared, operating on instinct rather than strategy, carrying consequences from the last three disasters, and he shows up anyway.

The Scarecrow had catalogued the party's capabilities and surpassed them. The Scarecrow had not catalogued Archie on a thundercloud. A fire mage who had fought a god, escaped a vampire prison, survived a month alone, and arrived crackling with electrical energy was a variable the Scarecrow's threat model had not included. The disruption was worth more than any specific tactical outcome the engagement produced.

I do not know if Archie won the fight at the Tree of Woe. I suspect he did not, because engagements with the Scarecrow do not produce clean victories. The Scarecrow dissolves into crows and reforms. But Archie's arrival changed the dynamic. It shifted the Scarecrow from predator to contested. It gave the party time to regroup. It gave the toads something to sing about.

And it gave me something to document that I did not expect to be documenting, which is this: Archie Miser, the man I have spent this entire encyclopedia criticizing for his recklessness, his fireballs, his diplomatic catastrophes, his unstable magic that shattered reality, his abandonment of a toad who became a god, his month alone in a death forest, his inability to remember the name of the deity born from his worst decision, arrived on a thundercloud at the moment of greatest need and flew directly at the worst thing in the room.

This is what I meant in the Disaster Inc. entry when I wrote that the party is heroic not because they want to be heroes but because nobody else showed up. Archie did not choose the Tree of Woe. The Tree of Woe was where his friends were. His friends were in danger. Archie flew toward the danger.

He is a disaster. He is also the disaster that shows up when the other disasters are winning.

I have spent the entire campaign documenting both facts. Both are true. Both deserve the record. The fireball on the wooden ship and the thundercloud at the Tree of Woe are the same person. The abandoned toad and the returning mage are the same person. The man who cannot remember a god's name and the man who flew alone into a supernatural engagement to protect people he has not seen in a month are the same person.

I do not know how to feel about this. I have not known how to feel about Archie since the Tea Party Incident, and the uncertainty has only deepened with every subsequent entry. What I know is that the record should contain both the fireball and the thundercloud, both the abandoned toad and the returning mage, both the prison escape built from empty quivers and the divine confrontation where Archie called a god Toad Prime and asked how it was going.

The record contains all of it. That is my job. The feelings are the reader's problem.

Archie is back. Archie is always back. Whether this is courage or pattern recognition or the universe refusing to let its most chaotic variable leave the board, I cannot determine.

I suspect it is all three.

WAH.

summary: Immediately following the party's forced retreat from the Tree of Woe, Remi was seized at knifepoint by the Voss wedding guard. The guard presented a skull-marked ring and revealed the wedding's true mechanism: a teleportation circle designed to send Remi's consciousness to a separate dimension entirely while her body remained in the ceremony. Markop intervened, the ring changed hands, and the Scorncrow's arrival resolved the standoff by giving the guard something considerably more dangerous to deal with. The Scorncrow then returned holding only the guard's pants, which told the party everything they needed to know. Green T reappeared with Remi's mechanical dog and demanded his gun back. The party retreated toward Raventree Manor, encountered a Mazehound en route, and discovered Tymnas's house contained a Toad dressed as Remi while Volsotos documented everything. The greenhouse was selected as sleeping quarters. During the rest, Wario knocked on the door with vintage vampire wine and Remi's birth certificate, verified and stamped and real, before being revealed as an imp that Green T shot twice. The party then attempted to depart the Shadeward via the Midnight Fountain and found it deactivated, broken by Bowser's earlier transit. They are trapped. The portal requires four artifacts to reactivate. The party returned to the manor house and ended the session in Vaxillus's Death Lounge listening to Vaxillus the Beastmaster and a Medusa argue about the correct methodology for hunting ghosts.
description:
Waluigi is documenting the hours following the Tree of Woe engagement, and he wants to state clearly for the historical record that the hours following a near-death experience at the hands of a soul-eating tree are not, generally, the hours in which a reasonable person should be negotiating wedding logistics at knifepoint. The party did not get those hours. They got these ones instead, which were worse in several ways and more absurd in almost all of them, and Waluigi is going to document every detail because the absurdity is exactly the kind of thing official historians will smooth over when they write the sanitized version of the Raventree Crisis, and Waluigi has spent his entire career fighting the sanitized version of everything.

The reconstruction draws from multiple sources whose reliability varies in ways that are themselves instructive.

Markop's testimony is precise and emotionally honest in ways that read as painful to produce, which Waluigi respects because painful honesty is the only kind worth reading.

Salam's account focuses on the physical and tactical with the specific attention of someone who thinks in terrain and angles.

Eager's notes are sparse, written in the economy of someone who has decided that excessive documentation is a form of sentimentality, and Waluigi suspects that Eager's brevity is not a lack of things to say but a considered decision about how many of them deserve paper.

Remi's notes are enthusiastic, occasionally inaccurate, and contain three separate exclamation points about the imp, which tells you everything about where Remi's attention goes during a crisis and precisely why the Beastmaster already knows all of the party's plans.

## Part I:


The Knife, the Ring, and the Teleportation Circle

The party had barely cleared the grove's edge before the hand came down on Remi's shoulder. The Voss guard, the same man who had delivered the wedding invitation with the professional composure of someone who considers armed ambush a standard administrative procedure, had the knife at her throat before anyone had time to process that the crows had stopped following them. Remi struggled. She is not a passive person by any measurement available to Waluigi, and being grabbed from behind by an institutional enforcer of a dimensional house that wants to marry her to something she has not consented to marrying triggered a physical response that the guard had clearly anticipated, because he held on.

She managed to create enough distance to breathe, enough space to think, but not enough to run.

This is the specific geography of a hostage situation and Waluigi knows it well.

The guard produced a ring. Heavy, ornate, marked with a koopa skull in the setting, which is an unusual choice of wedding symbolism and Waluigi is filing it under things about the House of Voss that do not add up and probably never will. He showed it to Remi. Markop said Remi didn't want this. The guard stared at him in disbelief, the genuine affronted disbelief of a man whose entire professional training did not include the possibility that the people being collected for a wedding would have opinions about attending it. What do you mean, the guard said. Markop told him she was young. That's gross, Markop said.

Waluigi wants to record that Markop said 'that's gross' to an armed enforcer holding a knife to a teenager's throat, because it is simultaneously the least tactical and most correct thing anyone said during the entire standoff, and Waluigi finds that combination deeply admirable.

The guard absorbed this, processed it, and concluded that Markop's objection represented a logistical note rather than a moral one, suggesting a birthday as an alternative framing for the occasion.

Waluigi has thought about this response at length.

A man who hears 'she is too young' and responds with 'okay, birthday then' has a relationship with ethics that Waluigi finds professionally baffling and personally infuriating.

The guard is not a monster.

He is a man with a very narrow definition of what deserves his moral concern, and he follows that definition with genuine professional feeling.

This is how institutional evil actually operates, not through villains but through people who have been told which things to care about and have stopped asking whether the list is complete.

The party suggested they simply rest and let the guard do whatever he needed to do, which was either a genuine stall tactic or evidence that the party was too exhausted to do anything other than ask for a nap in the middle of a hostage situation. The guard's response produced his most useful piece of intelligence: the tree would begin to rot if left unattended. The tree, Markop asked. Yeah, said the guard. Won't it be dead, Markop said. Yeah, said the guard, but it's more like undead, and that's sad, isn't it. Waluigi wants to dwell on this because a man holding a knife to a teenager's throat expressed sincere sadness about the prospect of an undead tree.

His compassion is real.

It is applied to trees.

It is not applied to the teenager.

This is either an extremely compartmentalized moral framework or evidence that the guard's personal values and his professional obligations have simply never been introduced to each other, and Waluigi finds both possibilities equally depressing in different ways.

The guard fired a warning shot. Next one won't miss, he said. Salam said yeah. Eager remained quiet, which Waluigi reads as the calculated silence of someone thinking ahead and not wanting to complicate the board by contributing noise. Remi escaped the guard's grip and got her sword out, because Remi has a threshold for being grabbed and she had reached it sometime around the second grab. Markop intervened before anyone died, which is what Markop does. He put himself in the gap between the situation and its worst outcome and held it there, and he explained the ring. The skull-ring was not a wedding band.

It was a component of a teleportation circle.

The House of Voss's plan was not to marry Remi in any conventional sense.

They intended to use the circle to send her consciousness to a separate dimension entirely, a wedding dimension, a space specifically constructed for the ceremony, while her physical body remained present in the Shadeward for whatever the actual ceremony required.

They would control her body while keeping her mind elsewhere, in a realm she had no map for and no exit from.

Waluigi is going to say this plainly because plain language is what this deserves: that is not a wedding.

That is a seizure.

The House of Voss has constructed institutional language around the complete separation of a fourteen-year-old girl's mind from her body, dressed it in ceremony and invitations and a guard who is sad about trees, and Waluigi finds the dressing more offensive than the act because at least the act is honest about what it is.

Markop said he didn't trust them. The Toads expressed genuine curiosity about what a wedding dimension looked like, which is entirely reasonable as a question and spectacularly poorly timed as a priority, but the Toads have a very pure relationship with interesting information and Waluigi cannot fully fault them for it. The guard tossed Remi the ring. Markop swung at him with his axe, told him enough of his nonsense, and the axe stuck in the ground, which is not the dramatic conclusion Markop intended. He backed up. Remi got hit in the back of the head, not by the guard, but by the scythe. The Scorncrow was there, materializing from the grove's edge at the exact moment that would cause maximum confusion for everyone present.

The party retreated.

The guard turned to face the Scorncrow rather than pursuing them, which is either genuine courage or a contractual obligation about grove security, and Waluigi respects the outcome regardless of what produced it.

## Part II:


The Pants, Green T, and the Mechanical Dog

They were running. Running through the Shadeward's gray light, bleeding, exhausted, missing half their party, when the Scorncrow appeared at the opening of the grove behind them. It was holding pants. Just the pants. The guard's pants. Not the guard, not the guard's body, not his weapons or boots or knife or the professional composure that Waluigi had spent the preceding paragraphs documenting. Just the pants, held up in one hand with the casual display of a trophy that does not need explanation because the explanation is the absence of everything else that used to be wearing them. The party ran faster.

The Scorncrow said it might have some pants, which was the funniest and most terrifying thing anyone said all evening, and Waluigi is documenting both qualities simultaneously because both are genuinely real and both deserve to be in the historical record.

Mossy appeared somewhere during the run. Remi's mechanical dog, the steam-powered construct that had been in Hjumpik's care in the Feywild before Green T apparently retrieved it through means that Waluigi does not yet have the full intelligence to reconstruct. Waluigi wants to note for the record that this is the same mechanical dog that was abducted by manor staff in the Feywild, rescued by Toad Lee and Hjumpik through a mission involving toilet ambushes and a Rakasha pulling a Toad out of a lethal fall by the neck, and renamed Steely by Hjumpik with the specific possessiveness of someone who has decided that rescuing a thing is the same as earning the right to rename it.

The dog sounds like a boiling tea kettle, which is either a mechanical defect or a feature, and the party treats it like the former because it is their pet and therefore beyond criticism.

Waluigi also wants to note, because he wrote about it in a prior entry and the information remains relevant, that this mechanical dog has a secondary unit set to explode.

Whether the explosive unit is the one currently in the party's possession or somewhere else is a question Waluigi does not have a current answer to, and the gap in his intelligence on this specific point is the kind of gap that makes him lose sleep.

A mechanical dog that sounds like a boiling tea kettle is a pet.

A mechanical dog set to detonate is a weapon someone has decided to disguise as a pet.

The party is treating it like the former because they have not yet been given a reason to suspect the latter, and Waluigi finds this distinction important enough to document in bold letters and then thinks better of the bold letters because they look alarmist, but the feeling behind them remains.

Green T appeared behind the party with the specific materialisation of someone who has been moving parallel to a group for long enough to know exactly where they would end up and decided to simply be there when they arrived. Got your dumb mutt back, Green T said. This is documented across all testimony as his opening statement after what was apparently a period of separate and completely unelaborated activity in the same grove that the party had just barely survived. Not are you injured. Not what happened at the tree. Not I have been separately doing things in the Shadowfell for the past hour and a half and would like to discuss them.

Got your dumb mutt back.

Waluigi has enormous affection for this sentence.

It is the sentence of someone who has decided that the only way to survive an evening like this is to reduce it to its most manageable components and refuse to assign emotional weight to any of the others.

Green T then asked for his thing back.

The party assumed he meant the ring, because the ring had just been at the center of an extended hostage situation and was the most recent thing that had changed hands in a manner that could be described as disputed.

No, Green T said.

The gun.

There was a pause.

Well actually yeah, the ring too, he added.

He had fired three shots during his separate movements through the grove.

Three shots in the Shadowfell by a person who moves like he has done this before.

Waluigi is watching this thread carefully and does not intend to stop watching it.

Eager asked if anyone had pants. This is documented because Eager did not have pants and had not had pants since the grove engagement, and none of the primary testimony sources felt the specific mechanics of the trouser situation were worth elaborating on, which Waluigi finds more interesting than any elaboration would have been. When the first question a person asks after surviving a soul-eating tree and a hostage standoff is about whether anyone can provide them with basic lower-body coverage, the evening has been thorough. The Scorncrow was still visible at the grove's edge with the guard's pants, which resolved Eager's question in the most disturbing possible way.

Pants were technically available.

The previous owner no longer needed them.

Nobody took the Scorncrow up on the offer because accepting pants from the entity that had removed them from someone who no longer existed was a bridge too far even for a party that was currently pantless, and Waluigi considers this an appropriate place to draw a line.

## Part III:


The Retreat, the Mazehound, and the Remi Doll

The return to the manor was not clean, which Waluigi could have predicted from a significant distance without needing to be present, because nothing about this party's movements has ever been clean. Remi ran after seeing a Mazehound moving parallel to them through the trees, which prompted the Toads to run, which prompted everyone to run, which made the retreat considerably louder than was tactically wise but considerably faster than it would have been otherwise, so Waluigi is not going to criticize the outcome. Volsotos was in the forest with his pen out. Waluigi does not know when Volsotos entered the forest or why, but Volsotos was there, reaching for more paper from behind a tree, noting that this was going to be a wonderful story and expressing enthusiasm about the cliffhanger potential.

The party ran more.

Markop and Green T held position ahead of the group and let the panicked people move through them, which is the geometry of experienced people providing cover for panicked people, and Waluigi considers it one of the more quietly generous things a person can do and notes that both Markop and Green T did it without acknowledging that they were doing it.

They reached the manor grounds and stood accounting for everyone. Markop looked through one of the manor's windows out of the habitual vigilance of someone who has learned to check his sightlines before his brain has finished deciding to, and saw inside Tymnas's house a Toad dressed as Remi sitting in a chair while Volsotos stood nearby declaring that this would make for a perfect story. Waluigi wants to express his opinion about this clearly: Volsotos being inside a house, documenting a staged Toad dressed as a bleeding teenager who is currently outside the house, while also having been observed outside the house taking notes on the real bleeding teenager moments prior, is one of the most unsettling things Waluigi has encountered during the Raventree operation.

Whether it is sinister or merely extremely committed journalism is a question Waluigi has been turning over and has not resolved.

What he knows is that the Remi-Toad was staged, and staged things are staged by someone for a purpose, and the purpose has not been disclosed.

Waluigi is watching Volsotos.

Remi suggested sleeping in the manor. This was shut down immediately, and Green T suggested the greenhouse shed instead, which is marginally better in the way that a shed is marginally better than the house the shed is attached to when the house contains a vampire and an unaccounted writer and a staged Toad sitting in a chair for reasons nobody has explained. The vampire materialized from behind a paper standee to announce an ambush, asked Markop whether Remi liked Toads, asked the Toads whether they liked the Toads, received the answer yes but not Speaker L, which is a factional caveat that Waluigi is filing away because factionalism always matters eventually and the Speaker L caveat is specific enough to mean something.

The vampire circled Remi briefly in a way that multiple sources document without elaborating on, and then everyone went to the greenhouse, which was, relative to the preceding two hours, almost peaceful.

## Part IV:


The Rest, Wario, and the Imp That Was Not Wario

The greenhouse was not luxurious but it was enclosed and it was not the manor. Salam stayed up using the woodcarver's tools to make something, which Waluigi respects as the productive insomnia of someone whose hands need occupation while their brain processes the events of the day, and the events of this specific day gave the brain a great deal to process. Eager kept watch in the shadows, pantless and silent and professional about both. Markop tended to Remi before resting himself, steady hands easing the pain from the scythe hit on her head and the accumulated damage of a day that started with a soul-eating tree, and then he slept.

Remi's rest produced thirty-five hit points and two HD and the comfort of being tended to, but the material resisted when she tried to make something and nothing usable came of the effort, which is the frustration of creative energy with nowhere productive to land.

Markop woke up to knocking. He called out asking for a name and a purpose. The voice on the other side of the door said it was the boss. Markop asked what the present was, which is a reasonable challenge response and the kind of protocol that keeps doors closed to things that should not be opened to. Vintage vampire wine, the voice said. Markop pointed out that Remi was too young to drink. The door smashed open.

Wario was standing there. Or something that looked exactly like Wario was standing there, which in the Shadeward amounts to the same thing until proven otherwise. The figure explained it had fought through vampires who were planning an ambush on the greenhouse, which was either true and alarming or false and alarming, and offered the wine as a gift. Markop looked at the wine. He looked at Wario. He looked at the wine again. And then Wario produced Remi's birth certificate.

Waluigi needs to stop on this for a moment because it deserves the stop. A verified, stamped, institutionally sealed, legally real birth certificate for Remi. Not a forgery, not a rough approximation, not the kind of document you produce when you have limited intelligence about your target and are hoping nobody looks too closely. The real thing, obtained through real institutional channels by someone with the access required to obtain it, delivered by Wario to a sleeping greenhouse in the Shadeward in the middle of the night. Markop was shocked in the specific way of a man who has been operating for weeks in an environment where everything is false or broken or staged or trying to kill him, and has encountered something that is simply, genuinely, inconveniently real.

He asked if it was legal for Wario to have this document.

Wario said he didn't have it anymore, which is technically accurate because he had just handed it to Markop, and also the least useful possible answer to the question that was actually being asked.

Markop accepted the wine and the certificate, and then he asked Wario very carefully whether Wario was real.

Waluigi loves this question. Not because it is clever, though it is, but because it is the question you only think to ask after you have spent enough time in a dimension that performs reality so convincingly that you have learned to verify the performance before trusting it. Most people ask who are you. Markop asked are you real. This is the difference between someone who arrived in the Shadeward recently and someone who has been here long enough to understand how it works.

Markop used his senses. He looked at Wario. He looked at the room. Wario did not glow. The paper standee in the corner, the vampire's earlier craft project that had somehow made its way into the greenhouse at some point during the rest, glowed. The standee was the magical source. The figure presenting gifts and birth certificates and smashing doors open was an imp. An imp that had been given a Wario costume, a rehearsed story about vampire ambushes, a bottle of vintage wine, and a legally real verified birth certificate for a fourteen-year-old girl, and had been sent to knock on a greenhouse door in the Shadeward in the middle of the night.

Waluigi wants to be clear about the resources this required.

Obtaining a real birth certificate through institutional channels takes access.

Deploying an imp with this level of briefing takes planning.

Coordinating the paper standee as a magical decoy takes forethought.

Whoever arranged this operation wanted the party to believe Wario had delivered this document, wanted the document itself to be accepted as genuine, and wanted whatever followed from that acceptance to happen.

Waluigi does not yet know what they wanted to follow.

He knows the document is real.

He knows the Wario was not.

He knows these two facts together mean something that he has not finished thinking about.

Green T shot the imp once. Then shot it again. No traitors, he said. The second shot was not tactically required but was clearly emotionally required, and Waluigi understands the distinction and respects the decision. The imp was neutralised. The birth certificate remained. The wine remained. Markop was left holding both.

## Part V:


The Midnight Fountain, Wario's Surprise, and the Word Trapped

This is where the evening stops being difficult and starts being something worse.

The party made their way to the Midnight Fountain. The same planar transit point that Bowser had fallen through when he entered the Shadeward. The exit. The plan. Survive the grove, survive the guard, survive the imp, get to the fountain, leave. The objective that tired and wounded and pantless people hold in front of themselves like a torch because without it the darkness of the Shadeward gets philosophically as well as literally close.

The fountain was deactivated.

Waluigi is going to let that sit. The party's only known exit from a plane adjacent to death, where trees eat souls and wedding invitations come with consciousness-displacement technology and a centaur keeps ghosts in his rugs, was dark and cold and completely inert. They are trapped. Wario was with the party at the fountain and Wario was genuinely surprised, and Waluigi has known Wario for long enough to know what genuine surprise looks like on him. It looks different from performed surprise, which Wario deploys when he wants you to think he didn't plan something. This was the real kind. Wario knew the fountain existed.

Wario expected it to work.

Wario did not anticipate finding it deactivated, which means someone else deactivated it, and that someone else was Bowser.

Bowser fell through the Midnight Fountain on his way into the Shadeward and apparently broke it in the process, which is exactly the kind of collateral damage Bowser produces when he interacts with dimensional infrastructure while in a hurry.

The king who punches floors and falls through them has now burned out a planar transit mechanism by using it too hard.

Waluigi finds this simultaneously frustrating and completely consistent with every documented Bowser interaction with fragile systems.

The portal requires four artifacts to reactivate. The Black Crystal, which is shadow-aligned magical resonance and which is not sitting in a drawer waiting to be collected, because nothing in the Shadowfell is ever in a drawer waiting to be collected. The Mirror of True Reflection, which shows true forms rather than appearances, which in a dimension where imps wear Wario costumes and Mazebounds perform solidity and trees have faces is invaluable and also potentially devastating, because some truths are worse than the performances they replace and Waluigi knows this from personal experience. The Orb of Shadow Dominion, about which Waluigi wants to note that the word dominion in an artifact's name is always a warning label dressed as a title, and anyone selling you a thing called an Orb of Shadow Dominion is selling you a thing they had very specific reasons for naming that way.

And the Umbral Signet, a seal of shadow authority whose authority Waluigi does not yet know but intends to find out, because authority in the Shadowfell belongs to things that have earned it in ways that do not recommend them as transaction partners.

Four artifacts.

One broken fountain.

One trapped party in a dimension that is actively trying to harvest their souls or marry them to other dimensions or put them in rugs, depending on which estate resident they have most recently offended.

## Part VI:


The Death Lounge, the Beastmaster, and the Medusa

The party returned to the manor house to regroup and begin planning artifact acquisition, which sounds like a sensible activity and in any other context would be. Instead they walked into Vaxillus's Death Lounge, and Waluigi is going to describe this room in detail because the room itself is a document. Every space tells you something about the person who lives in it and the world that person inhabits, and Vaxillus's Death Lounge tells you more than most.

The lounge is dimly lit and comfortably appointed in the way that rooms are comfortable when the person who decorated them has a very specific definition of comfort involving being surrounded by things they have killed. Against the walls hang the taxidermied heads and pelts of Shadowfell creatures that look like terrestrial animals at first glance and become progressively more wrong the longer you look at them. Two great cats with white coats and onyx manes lie on the floor as rugs, their heads more canine than feline and their paws replaced with birdlike talons, their glassy black eyes following movement with the patience of dead things that have not fully committed to the concept of being dead.

A massive bear-like creature with a shark's mouth and porcupine quills lies half under a couch, and Waluigi wants to note that having a creature with a shark's mouth and porcupine quills lying half under your couch is a decorating choice that tells the visitor something about your risk tolerance.

A black elk's head with red eyes and antlers of dark bone hangs on the east wall radiating malice with the dedication of something that was malicious in life and has simply continued the habit.

The massive head of what appears to be a white elephant with no eyes and no mouth, only tusks and a trunk, hangs on the southern wall, and Waluigi finds the absence of eyes and mouth more unsettling than if it had both, because the absence implies the creature experienced the world through entirely different mechanisms than vision and speech and Waluigi does not want to think about what those mechanisms were.

On the west wall a stony black lizard head with a beak and three horns and two sets of eyes arranged like a spider's stares out with the patient observation of something designed to see everything, and it is still doing so.

Weapon racks hold old weapons of dark ashen wood and black metal, battleaxes and spears and warhammers and glaives and full crossbow bolt cases, none of them special, all of them available to the party if they want to take them because Vaxillus may not notice. The crossbows in the corner each have names carved into them. Blood Spiller. Heart Killer. Shadow Piercer. Soul Needler. These are not enchanted weapons. They are regular crossbows with names that a young person carved into them to make them feel important, and Waluigi has an unexpected and entirely unwanted pang of recognition at this because Waluigi named his first stolen knife Destiny's Edge when he was fifteen and kept it for two years until Wario threw it in a river during an argument about whose fault the Koopaling card game debt was.

The impulse to make a mundane weapon feel mythic through naming is universal across class and species and dimension, and Vaxillus and fifteen-year-old Waluigi would have understood each other on this specific point, and Waluigi is going to stop thinking about this immediately because he is a documentarian of the highest professional standard and this is not the place for nostalgia about knives.

There is also a peephole hidden beneath the antlered elk head in the southeastern corner that allows anyone standing there to hear conversations in the adjacent lounge with stunning clarity. This is the kind of architectural feature a young person installs when they want to know what the adults are saying without being invited to hear it, and Waluigi files it as potentially extremely useful and moves on.

Vaxillus was in the room. The Beastmaster, because Vaxillus is the Beastmaster, the same young estate resident who tinkered with crossbows and drank alone and turned his family's lounge into a taxidermy gallery of things he had hunted through the Shadowfell. A centaur of significant physical presence. He had been, at the moment of the party's arrival, hunting ghosts inside the manor. Markop asked if he was interrupting something. He was told yes. The Beastmaster explained that he wanted to kill a real ghost to prove that ghosts were real, and that once he had the proof he intended to put the ghost's soul in one of his rugs.

Waluigi looked at the Shadow Manes on the floor, the shark-mouthed bear under the couch, the eyeless elephant on the wall, and understood that the rug collection was not decoration.

It was a thesis.

Every pelt was an argument.

Every mounted head was evidence.

The Beastmaster does not believe things exist until he can step on them every morning and confirm through physical contact that they are real.

The ghost is the gap in the collection.

The ghost is the one thing he cannot yet prove through possession.

Waluigi finds this epistemological framework genuinely fascinating and genuinely alarming in equal measure, which is the ratio that describes nearly everything in this manor.

The Beastmaster then noticed that Markop was a centaur. He noted that he did not have any centaur rugs. Waluigi wants to be clear that this observation, delivered with the candid enthusiasm of someone who has never fully developed the filter between observation and speech, is the most threatening thing anyone has said to Markop during the entire Raventree operation while technically not constituting a threat, and the gap between the intent and the impact is exactly the gap that makes the Beastmaster dangerous. He added oh sorry, come in, which is exactly the follow-up a person produces when they realize they have just told a centaur they don't own a centaur rug and want to make the situation feel welcoming despite everything that statement implies about their collection goals.

The Beastmaster offered his deal. He would bring his two dogs, which he said in the tone of someone using the word dogs to describe things that are not dogs, and the party would find the ghost. In exchange he would provide the shadow crystal. Markop asked how the Beastmaster knew about the shadow crystal. The Beastmaster said they knew about all of the party's plans. He said Remi wouldn't shut up about it. Waluigi is going to be direct about this because directness is the appropriate register for an intelligence failure of this scale: the Beastmaster's network has a comprehensive and apparently accurate picture of the party's goals, resources, and strategic intentions because Remi has been sharing operational objectives with entities the party has not vetted since approximately the beginning of the Raventree operation.

This is the same Remi who nearly signed an Onyx Hand enthrallment contract disguised as a friendship agreement.

The same Remi who a Voss guard noted was famous for always being tricked, which is cruel and also statistically documented.

Waluigi does not blame Remi for having the instincts of someone who assumes other people are operating in good faith, because in most of the world most of the time that instinct is correct and produces good outcomes.

The Shadowfell is not most of the world.

The Corvinarus estate is not most of the time.

The party is now negotiating from an information disadvantage that was built by one member's consistent transparency, and the Beastmaster's offer sounds generous precisely because it was constructed using intelligence he was given for free.

Markop thought about the ghost that had been assisting the party. He did not say anything about it. Waluigi considers this one of the best decisions Markop has made during the entire operation and documents it explicitly because Markop does not document his own good decisions and the record should contain them. You do not tell the entity who wants to put a ghost in a rug about your helpful ghost. Markop understood this immediately and stayed quiet about it immediately, which is the kind of tactical discretion that separates the people who survive the Shadowfell from the people who end up as evidence in someone's epistemological thesis.

The Medusa was also in the room. Waluigi is going to document this with the weight it deserves, which is considerable, because a Medusa in the same space as a centaur Beastmaster surrounded by the taxidermied remains of Shadowfell apex predators changes every dynamic in that room. The Beastmaster and the Medusa were arguing. Not fighting but arguing, the specific register of two entities who have been working together long enough to develop genuine professional disagreements about methodology and have stopped being diplomatic about them. The argument was about how the ghost should be hunted, what qualified as proof, and whose approach was correct, and the party walked into the middle of it and stood there bleeding and pantless while the two most dangerous things in the room continued to disagree about ghost logistics as if the arrival of a group of recently-traumatized adventurers was a minor scheduling complication.

The session ends here. The party is in the Death Lounge. Vaxillus is offering hellhounds and a shadow crystal in exchange for a ghost. The Medusa is offering an opinion about the methodology. Markop is not mentioning the helpful ghost, which remains the best decision anyone has made all evening. Eager still does not have pants. The fountain is broken because Bowser broke it by existing near it too forcefully. The portal needs four artifacts distributed across an estate full of vampires and centaurs and medusas and a writer who documents staged Toads dressed as teenagers. Waluigi documents all of it and trusts none of it and is beginning to suspect that the deactivation of the fountain was not an accident produced by Bowser's transit but a deliberate act by someone who needed the party to remain in the Shadeward long enough to retrieve four specific artifacts for reasons that party will not fully understand until the artifacts are already gone.

WAH.

outcome: Remi's capture by the Voss guard was resolved by the Scorncrow's arrival and the guard's subsequent disappearance, pants returned, guard not. The wedding's true mechanism was revealed. An imp posing as Wario was exposed and shot twice. A verified birth certificate of unclear purpose was obtained. The Midnight Fountain was found deactivated, broken by Bowser's earlier transit, trapping the party in the Shadeward. Four artifacts are required to reactivate the portal. The session ended in Vaxillus's Death Lounge with the Beastmaster offering hellhounds and a shadow crystal in exchange for a ghost, the Medusa disagreeing about method, and Markop successfully not mentioning the helpful ghost.
notableFeatures: The Wedding Mechanism — the skull ring was a teleportation circle component designed to split Remi's consciousness from her body; her mind to a wedding dimension, her body remaining; Waluigi wants to be clear this is not a wedding, it is a seizure.
The Guard's Pants — the Scorncrow returned holding only the pants; the guard did not return; this communicated everything necessary without a single additional word.
The Deactivated Fountain — the party's only exit was broken by Bowser's transit through it; Wario's genuine surprise narrows the causation and confirms Wario did not arrange the shutdown.
The Four Artifacts — Black Crystal, Mirror of True Reflection, Orb of Shadow Dominion, Umbral Signet; each required to reactivate the portal; none of the names suggest easy acquisition.
The Mechanical Dog's Explosive Unit — the dog has a secondary unit set to explode; which unit the party currently has is unconfirmed; Waluigi is watching this.
The Imp's Birth Certificate — verified, stamped, legally real; the resources required to obtain and deliver it imply an arranger with institutional access and an unestablished objective.

The Death Lounge — Vaxillus's personal taxidermy gallery containing Shadow Manes, a Spiny Devourer, a Shadow Elk, a Hellephant, an Obsidian Watcher, and crossbows named with the optimism of a teenager; also contains a ghost-hunting centaur and a medusa.
The Beastmaster's Intelligence — knew about the shadow crystal because Remi discussed it with people the party had not vetted; the party is negotiating at an information disadvantage they created.
Markop Did Not Mention the Helpful Ghost — this was the correct decision and Waluigi is documenting it explicitly because correct decisions deserve documentation.
Eager's Pants — lost during the grove; not recovered; the Scorncrow's offer of the guard's pants was declined; dignity was maintained.
