summary: Part VII completes the Mount Ebott Survey Expedition. Picking up immediately after Papyrus's dusting in the false meadow, Sans experiences a fleeting memory of drinking tea with King Asgore before snapping back to freeze time and brutally execute Flowey in a burst of violent blue magic. The Agent recovers the survey machine—discovering it recorded the entire fight—and attempts to wear it as a backpack before the straps fail. Guided by Sans through the Underground's cave loop, the group reaches New Home Castle, where the Agent uses official Iron Legion documents signed by Commissar Vexis to bluff past the royal guards. In the throne room, King Asgore and Queen Toriel explain the Barrier's delicate balance and agree to grant localized transport to the surface under a binding Oath of Secrecy.
description:
*"I wanted to look at things the way I wanted... hear only what I wanted to hear... and say what I wanted to say. That's the kind of life I wanted."*
— **[Papyrus](#/article/papyrus)**

*"You cannot reveal our world to humans on the surface. Not fully, not carelessly. The safety of monsters depends on this barrier remaining intact in everyone's minds as a myth — not a reality they can exploit."*
— **[Queen Toriel](#/article/toriel)**

*"WAH! An oath of secrecy! A royal non-disclosure agreement written in ancient monster magic and sealed without a notary! Waluigi has signed many non-disclosure agreements, but usually they were to keep Wario from admitting who broke the court floodlights! WAH."*
— **[Waluigi](#/article/waluigi), Auditor-General, Walupedia Editorial Board**

sections.name: I. The Immediate Aftermath — How to Kill a Flower
sections.overview:
The white dust from Papyrus's body hung suspended in the calm air of the false meadow for a single heartbeat before dispersing into the grass. His dark coat lay flat on the multi-colored tile grid. The blue gravity cage had shattered into glowing shards that faded into nothingness. Sans stood motionless in the center of the field, his hands half-raised, his eye sockets pitch black and completely devoid of white lights.

The Agent turned his gaze toward Dracule Mihawk, his boots stepping over a cold brass tile. He gave a firm, singular nod.

**"We need to kill Flowey,"** the Agent said.

Mihawk did not hesitate. His golden eye locked onto the distant patch of loam where the yellow petals had submerged into the earth. With a single, fluid motion, the Warlord drew Yoru from his back sheath. The massive black blade caught the artificial sunlight, casting a sharp shadow across the soil.

**"Agreed,"** Mihawk said coldly, taking a measured step forward.

**"How do we kill a flower?"** the Agent asked, adjusting his posture and scanning the perimeter for vine movement.

Mihawk tilted his head slightly, assessing the target with dispassionate tactical logic.

**"Burn it,"** Mihawk replied plainly, his fingers adjusting on Yoru's hilt. **"Fire is effective against plants."**

Sans remained motionless beside them, his shoulders hunched under his blue hoodie, his breath coming out slow and shallow as the dust settled on his boots.

*WAH! Waluigi agrees completely with this tactical assessment! When a garden specimen murders a municipal officer from behind during an emotional admission, you do not prune it! You do not give it plant food or put it in a decorative ceramic pot! You fetch a torch and incinerate the entire flowerbed until there is nothing left but carbon! WAH.*
sections.waluigi_note: Observe that Dracule Mihawk does not attempt to categorize Flowey as a duelist or a combatant of honor. He categorizes him as agricultural pestilence. In military operations, treating an opportunistic wildcard as a formal opponent is a fatal error. Mihawk's immediate recommendation of fire reflects proper elemental counter-measures against root-based entities. WAH.

sections.name: II. The Midnight Tea — Sans's Memory of Asgore
sections.overview:
Before Mihawk could strike his blade into the soil, the air around Sans warped violently. The fake meadow, the bright sky, and the color-tile grid dissolved for a brief, suspended moment as reality folded inward, drawing Sans into the quiet warmth of a distant memory.

It was night inside the royal castle at New Home. Outside the leaded glass windows, the Underground was dark and still. Sans sat at a heavy oak table while King Asgore walked slowly across the stone floor, carrying a steaming clay teapot.

**"The tea is ready!"** Asgore announced pleasantly, pouring a golden liquid into two cups.

Sans took the cup, blowing softly on the steam before taking a careful sip. **"Thank you, Asgore. It smells lovely... As good as always."**

Asgore smiled across the table, his large paws wrapped around his teacup. **"I really am thankful that you decided to come over, Sans. I wasn't sure I'd ever have outside visitors again, but... It's been too long since I've had company. The castle feels... quieter than it used to. I hope you enjoy the tea, it's an old recipe of mine."**

**"It's excellent as always,"** Sans replied, leaning back in his wooden chair. **"It's been a rough few months lately. I needed an evening like this."**

**"Ho ho ho! I'm so glad you like it!"** Asgore chuckled softly.

Sans smirked, a hint of genuine warmth returning to his eye sockets. **"You never stop being so positive and kind, do you? You could never serve a bad cup of tea, Asgore. You'd need to lose your hands before that happened."**

Asgore's expression turned earnest as he set his cup down. **"I would like to catch up on your lives, if you will. Tell me, what do you do for an occupation? I am very curious to know what goes on outside these caverns."**

Sans folded his hands over his stomach. **"Well, I work as a sentry. It's not a particularly exciting job, but... it keeps me busy. You know the usual. I keep an eye out for humans, patrol the Snowdin woods, and... sleep on the job."**

Asgore paused, his brow furrowing gently. **"What do you think about the whole catching humans thing?"**

Sans exhaled slowly, looking down into his golden tea. **"Honestly? I don't agree with it. I've never caught a human. Never wanted to."**

Asgore gazed at him with quiet, paternal trust. **"I understand it's difficult to find the will to do what we must. But from what I can tell, you are an honest young man. I believe when the time comes you will do the right thing. So tell me... what keeps you going?"**

Sans tapped his knuckles softly against the clay cup. **"Honestly? My brother. Papyrus... he keeps me going. I wanna make him proud, you know? He believes in being strong and noble, so I try to match that energy for him. And then there are little things too — like my friends in Snowdin. Grillby's diner..."**

**"There is nothing wrong in finding solace in others,"** Asgore said softly. **"I assure you if we had more people like you and your brother we will have a peaceful future someday. Promise me this will you, Sans? Never give up this dream."**

Sans looked past Asgore at the peaceful darkness outside the glass. **"Yeah... I do. More than anything, I want peace. I want everyone I care about to be happy and safe... A world where everyone can just... live without fighting. Without fear."**

*WAH! The quiet tea-table summit! A depressed goat king and a sentry who refuses to do his job sitting in a castle drinking herbal tea at midnight! This memory explains everything about Sans! He spent four years sleeping at his guard post in Snowdin not because he was lazy, but because he promised King Asgore he would choose peace over human-hunting! WAH.*
sections.waluigi_note: This memory is the exact structural anchor that held Sans together. His refusal to capture humans was not insubordination; it was compliance with a personal oath made to Asgore. When Flowey killed Papyrus, he did not merely murder a brother — he severed the exact reason Sans maintained his peaceful restraint. WAH.

sections.name: III. The Freeze and the Eruption — Sans Executes Flowey
sections.overview:
The memory snapped shut like a heavy book. Sans blinked, his eyelights snapping back into the present meadow where Flowey's golden head had just re-emerged from the dirt to mock them.

Time froze. A sharp, loud *CLICK* echoed through the clearing as the entire world shifted into monochrome grayscale. Sans vanished from where he stood and materialized instantaneously directly beside Flowey. His eye sockets were pitch black.

**"Look at me,"** Sans whispered. His voice was lower than death itself. **"You hurt Papyrus."**

Flowey's petals trembled in sudden, frantic panic. **"YOU DAMN BRAT!"** the flower shrieks, whipping his vines forward. **"YOU THINK A BATTLE CAN SAVE YOU!"**

A catastrophic spell erupted from Sans in a blinding burst of violent blue magic. The surge struck Flowey dead-on, scorching his petals and blasting him across the dirt in a shower of sparks.

Flowey hit the ground hard, but Sans was already standing over him. Sans grabbed Flowey by the central stem and slammed him brutally into the earth, creating a jagged crater in the soil.

**"COME ON!"** Sans roared, his jaw set as brilliant blue fire flared wildly from his left socket. **"WHERE'S THAT SPIRIT NOW!?!"** He slammed the flower down again—*BAM!* **"ANSWER ME! You don't get to hide! Why did you do it?! What was the point of hurting my brother!? ANSWER ME RIGHT NOW!"**

He pounded the flower into the dirt three more times until the stem broke and the petals disintegrated into black ash.

Time snapped back into motion with a loud pop. Color flooded back into the meadow. Sans lowered his shaking hands, staring down at the crushed ash in the crater.

The Agent stepped forward, staring at the ruined soil. **"Sans... he's dead. The flower is dead, you killed it."**

Sans exhaled slowly, his eyelights returning as dim white pinpricks. **"Guess I did,"** he muttered quietly. **"He deserved it."**

*WAH! Time-stop beatdowns! Never make a short skeleton angry in front of a flower! Sans went from zero magical reserve to a localized apocalyptic execution in three-tenths of a second! Flowey learned the hard way that 'where is that spirit now' is not a rhetorical question! WAH.*
sections.waluigi_note: Notice that Sans did not use a complex puzzle, a bone storm, or a platform trap. He used absolute proximity and raw kinetic magic. When the limits of restraint are removed, Sans's combat efficiency is staggering. Flowey was given no opportunity to burrow, reset, or summon vines. WAH.

sections.name: IV. The Survey Machine Record — Ecological Miscalibration
sections.overview:
With Flowey eliminated, the clearing grew silent. The Agent walked over to the Iron Legion survey machine resting on the grass, its heavy brass housing humming softly as data tray light flickered.

The monitor screen displayed scrolling lines of text. The Agent stared at the monitor in utter disbelief—the machine had recorded the entire battle in meticulous detail. Timestamped movement vectors, magical energy spikes, the gravity cage collapse, and even Sans's final time-stop execution were fully logged alongside soil acidity and humidity readings.

Mihawk stepped alongside him, crossing his arms as he examined the glowing display. **"Hm. That thing picked up everything."**

**"It's meant for ecological surveys,"** the Agent said, frowning at the screen. **"How did it record combat data?"**

Mihawk leaned in closer, his golden eye taking in the scrolling columns. **"This data is messy. Half ecological readings, half combat logs. Soil samples and energy spikes... The device has been broken, repaired, and re-patched too many times to function properly. It picked up the magic by accident."**

The Agent nodded, reaching down to unbuckle the heavy leather harness. **"Whatever. I'm re-attaching the survey device and grabbing the straps to make a makeshift backpack. It's heavy, but we won't lose it this way — not again."**

He hoisted the bulky 80-pound brass unit onto his back, pulling the leather straps tight across his chest plate. He took two steps before the leather groaned under the strain. The makeshift harness snapped with a loud crack, and the survey device slid violently down his legs, clunking heavily against the dirt with a thud that shook the grass.

The Agent stared down at the dropped machine, rubbing his shoulder. **"It will not hold."**

Mihawk exhaled dryly through his nose. **"Told you."**

*WAH! Repurposed technology! An ecological survey device that accidentally logged a murder and a time-stop assault because its sensors could not tell the difference between a root sample and a Gaster Blaster! Iron Legion engineering at its finest! And strap failure! Waluigi has told Wario a hundred times that you cannot wear a brass boiler as a rucksack! WAH.*
sections.waluigi_note: The Agent's attempt to convert a stationary survey apparatus into a backpack using worn leather straps is a classic field error. Scientific instruments weighing eighty pounds require standardized transport carts or anti-gravity cradles. Attempting to wear them as luggage results in broken straps and bruised ankles. WAH.

sections.name: V. Egress Doctrine — The Law of the Barrier
sections.overview:
Leaving the dropped machine on the grass for a moment, the Agent looked toward Sans. **"We just have to get out of here. Asgore and the Queen know how to, right?"**

Sans scanned the quiet meadow, his posture weary. **"We should go... before anything else happens. I think we need to find an exit from this place, somewhere that will take us back to New Home. Maybe the queen or Asgore can help. I don't know the exact way from here, though."**

The Agent raised an eyebrow. **"The Queen... you call her that a lot, but other people say Toriel. Why is that? Is her title not that big?"**

Sans's expression turned stern. **"To me, she's the queen. Toriel is her name, yeah. But she's also the queen of monsters. She deserves to be called by her title. She's one of the only people I've met who is worthy of respect. So to me, she's the queen. Nothing less."**

The Agent nodded, then glanced around. **"Without a map... I guess we can discuss what to do if the Friendship comes back with Gaster and his pirates."**

Mihawk glanced over curiously. **"You're expecting the Friendship to return?"**

**"Yes, why wouldn't I?"** the Agent replied.

Mihawk folded his arms. **"Gaster's crew is unpredictable. They come and go as they please. If they do come back, we'll see what their intentions are before assuming anything helpful will happen."**

The Agent turned back to Sans. **"Also, Asgore and the Queen... Sans, you said they won't just let us out. Why? Why is leaving the Underground a different process than just leaving the Old World where I live?"**

Sans rubbed his skull thoughtfully. **"Leaving the Underground isn't like leaving any random place in your world. There are rules down here. Laws. Barriers. A long time ago... a powerful human wizard put all of us here. He was trying to keep humans from leaving, but he kept us monsters trapped as well. The only way to leave... is for a human and monster to work together."**

**"So can you even leave when we try to exit?"** the Agent asked.

**"Technically? Yeah,"** Sans explained. **"The wards don't stop us from exiting the Underground itself. But once we step out of here... we can't come back in easily. And if something happens on the surface..."**

**"And the humans won the war?"**

**"Yeah,"** Sans said softly. **"The humans won. They drove us underground and sealed us away permanently. To break the barrier for good... it takes massive effort. Both humans and monsters working together willingly."**

*WAH! Dimensional boundary laws! The barrier was built by an ancient human wizard who wanted to lock monsters away, but he built the lock so poorly that people can leave but cannot get back in! Typical human wizard work — grand concept, terrible administrative execution! WAH.*
sections.waluigi_note: Notice the asymmetrical nature of the magical barrier. Individual egress is permitted under specific energy thresholds, but re-entry is blocked. This design prevents surface forces from launching counter-invasions while forcing exiting individuals into permanent exile. WAH.

sections.name: VI. The Cave Loop — Teleportation Under Whispers
sections.overview:
Sans took a deep breath, steeling himself. **"Alright. Let me take the lead."**

He raised a hand, his eye sockets flashing with a brief spark of blue light. The air around them folded inward, and the false meadow dissolved into dark, echoing stone corridors.

They began walking briskly through the dimly lit tunnels. The Agent checked his wrist watch, tapping the glass face. **"Huh. We've been walking for about twenty minutes now."**

He looked around, noticing the grand architectural spires of New Home Castle looming directly ahead through the gloom. **"So you teleported us closer to the king. I thought that was a random field, but you seemed to know where to go."**

Sans shrugged casually. **"Yeah... I knew where to go. The castle isn't exactly hard to find if you're familiar with the Underground. The Underground loops like a cave system — everything connects eventually if you walk far enough. There aren't really 'lost' places down here... just ones that are harder to get to. And this place? It's one of the major points on that loop."**

The Agent slowed his pace slightly, stepping alongside Mihawk. He leaned in and whispered softly: **"That was way too fast, don't you think? No interruptions... suddenly we're in the tunnels, then we're here that fast near the capital."**

Mihawk kept his gaze fixed ahead, his voice low and unbothered. **"Teleportation is fast... yes. But not unusual for monsters with magic. The capital isn't far from here anyway. It's normal to..."**

He cut himself off as three heavily armored royal guards stepped out from the shadows near the castle gates.

*WAH! Spatial shortcuts! You think you are walking three miles through damp granite, but a skeleton blinks his eye sockets and suddenly you are standing in the king's front yard! Spatial efficiency or lazy map design? Waluigi says both! WAH.*
sections.waluigi_note: The Underground's geography operates on closed topology. Major hubs (Snowdin, Hotland, New Home) connect via compressed spatial corridors. Sans's ability to navigate these shortcuts allows the team to bypass days of transit in twenty minutes. WAH.

sections.name: VII. The Gate Guard Bluff — The Commissar Vexis Documents
sections.overview:
The royal guards lowered their halberds, blocking the arched entrance to the courtyard. **"Halt!"** the lead guard commanded sharply. **"State your business!"**

The guards narrowed their eyes, hands resting firmly on their sword hilts. **"You there! Identify yourselves and state why you're approaching the castle!"**

Sans hesitated for a second too long, unsure how to frame their arrival. The lead guard stepped forward, his voice dripping with warning. **"Last chance. Answer!"**

The Agent nudged Sans aside, stepping forward with crisp military posture. He puffed out his chest and spoke in a clear, practiced cadence: **"We are the Iron Legion Commissar Royal Expedition Unit, codename Lone Snake, color Green. Primary purpose: classified due to being currently active. Secondary purpose: survey of unfamiliar area."**

The guards blinked, utterly taken aback by the barrage of formal military terminology. **"Iron Legion...? Commissar?"** the lead guard muttered, exchanging bewildered looks with his men. **"We weren't informed of any royal expedition unit arriving today. Do you have proof of your rank and mission parameters?"**

**"Yes,"** the Agent replied smoothly. **"I have papers issued by Commissar Vexis."**

He reached into his inner coat pocket and produced an official folder stamped with gold foil and sealed with heavy red wax, handing it to the lead guard.

The guards crowded around, inspecting the documents carefully. **"Hmph. These look legitimate enough..."** the lead guard admitted begrudgingly, scrutinizing the official seal and Commissar Vexis's signature. **"Though we were never issued orders regarding a commissar... Very well. You may enter... for now."**

As they passed through the gates, Sans mumbled quietly with a smirk: **"Guess those documents actually worked after all. We got lucky there. Good on you for getting all that military jargon down."**

**"Guess they're slow on the uptake, the guards,"** the Agent chuckled.

*WAH! Bureaucratic intimidation! Nothing confuses a checkpoint guard faster than a man in a green coat reading out sixteen syllables of fake classification numbers! Waluigi uses this exact trick when entering VIP lounges at kart races! WAH.*
sections.waluigi_note: Notice how easily the guards yielded when presented with wax-sealed paperwork signed by Commissar Vexis. Security personnel in formal hierarchies are trained to fear administrative reprimand more than unauthorized entry. A gold foil seal is effectively an invisible key. WAH.

sections.name: VIII. The Throne Room Audience — King Asgore and Queen Toriel
sections.overview:
The grand wooden doors of the castle creaked open, revealing a vast throne room lit by flickering chandeliers and carpeted in golden buttercups. At the far end sat King Asgore upon his massive stone throne, his red cape draped over his shoulders and his trident resting beside his seat. Standing near him as royal advisor was Queen Toriel, her hands folded neatly in her white robes.

Asgore looked up slowly as the group entered, his voice booming through the hall. **"Who approaches my court? I don't recall being informed of an official military expedition passing through the Underground... nor a royal escort either. I'm not used to unexpected guests in my home, especially armed ones."**

The Agent stepped forward, lowering his hands. **"Oh no, we mean this place no harm. We are seeking an exit."**

Asgore's expression shifted into a contemplative frown. **"An exit...?"**

Toriel stepped forward gently, her golden eyes filled with quiet concern. **"And what exactly do you mean by 'seeking an exit,' child? Do you wish to leave permanently?"**

**"Yes, we wish to go to the surface,"** the Agent affirmed.

Asgore leaned back on his throne, steepling his large claws. **"I see... And you believe there is an exit that can be opened? That it hasn't been sealed beyond return?"**

**"No, no,"** the Agent clarified, gesturing to Sans. **"Our skeleton friend here told us you would be able to help see us out."**

Asgore scrutinized Sans. **"He is the one who suggested you seek me out for assistance? And you believe I have the power to simply... open a path for you? Just like that? The logistics of opening a path to the surface are not simple."**

Sans stepped forward, dropping his casual demeanor entirely. **"We're aware the barrier isn't easy to undo... but if anyone could do it, you could, right?"**

*WAH! Royal court manners! Entering a throne room with a giant sword and a broken survey machine is usually a recipe for getting executed, but King Asgore is so polite he offers tea before asking why you are standing on his rug! WAH.*
sections.waluigi_note: The audience in the throne room transitions the expedition from tactical survival to high diplomacy. Asgore and Toriel receive the group not as invaders, but as petitioning travelers seeking egress. WAH.

sections.name: IX. Barrier Logistics — Localized Transport vs Mass Destruction
sections.overview:
Asgore stroked his golden beard thoughtfully, his eyes heavy with ancient responsibility. **"Breaking through centuries of magical barriers is no small task... It would require immense power and precision."**

Toriel nodded in agreement. **"If we attempt this... it must be done carefully. The last thing we need is for the barrier to collapse entirely or cause catastrophic damage."**

The Agent frowned. **"The last thing you want is for it to collapse...? Why wouldn't you want to destroy it?"**

Asgore explained in measured tones. **"Destroying it outright would risk destabilizing the Underground entirely. The magic that keeps us here isn't just a prison — it's also what maintains our world as we know it. Think of it this way: if we tear down the barrier completely without care, the magic sustaining our world isn't infinite. It's balanced. Without careful control... everything could collapse inward like a dying star."**

Toriel added gently: **"And even worse — imagine if dangerous creatures or surface forces got through before proper precautions were taken! The surface wouldn't be safe either!"**

The Agent considered this before offering an alternative: **"Then fine. Can we use a localized transport where we just send two people out?"**

Asgore looked thoughtful. **"Yes... a localized transport might be an option. It would require tremendous power, but it could allow a few to pass through more safely."**

Toriel stepped forward, her expression turning serious. **"However... there is one other factor to consider. If we do this... you must understand that it's possible you may never return. Are you prepared for such a life?"**

The Agent met her gaze firmly. **"Yes. I feel like I have gained what I wanted to here."**

*WAH! Localized portal physics! Instead of tearing down the whole wall and letting the roof collapse, you cut a small envelope-sized hole in reality and push two men through! Precision magic over raw force every time! WAH.*
sections.waluigi_note: Asgore's refusal to destroy the Barrier outright is rooted in ecological physics. The Barrier regulates the Underground's internal magic balance. A localized transport bypasses the barrier without destroying its structural load. WAH.

sections.name: X. The Oath of Secrecy — The Final Terms
sections.overview:
Asgore and Toriel exchanged a brief, meaningful look, coming to a silent agreement.

**"Very well then,"** Asgore said, his deep voice carrying finality. **"We are willing to attempt the transport. I will prepare the necessary spellwork. However..."**

Toriel stepped forward, her expression stern yet protective. **"We must ask one condition of you before we continue."**

**"What is it?"** the Agent asked.

Asgore folded his hands together over his chest. **"Before we proceed... you must swear an oath. An oath of secrecy regarding the Underground and its people."**

Toriel emphasized every word: **"You cannot reveal our world to humans on the surface. Not fully, not carelessly. The safety of monsters depends on this barrier remaining intact in everyone's minds as a myth — not a reality they can exploit."**

The Agent, Mihawk, and Sans stood together before the throne. The weight of the vow settled heavily in the air. The expedition had achieved its objective, but the price of egress was absolute silence.

*WAH! The Non-Disclosure Agreement of Mount Ebott! A solemn vow made to a goat king and a queen that keeps seven hundred thousand underground monsters off surface television! Waluigi approves of non-disclosure agreements, especially when they prevent tax auditors from finding hidden gold reserves! WAH.*
sections.waluigi_note: The Oath of Secrecy serves as the final diplomatic barrier. It ensures that while individuals may exit, the Underground remains protected by mythological obscurity. WAH.

outcome: Flowey executed; Group reaches New Home Castle; Localized transport granted by Asgore and Toriel under Oath of Secrecy.

aftermath:
## Aftermath & Operational Standing

**1. Operational Result:** The Mount Ebott Survey Expedition successfully reached the political center of the Underground at New Home Castle. The primary objective—locating an egress route to the surface—was negotiated directly with King Asgore and Queen Toriel.

**2. Casualty & Personnel Status:** Papyrus was assassinated in Part VI. Flowey was subsequently executed by Sans in a time-stop magic eruption. Sans remains mentally exhausted but operational. Dracule Mihawk and the Legionary Agent sustained minor graze injuries.

**3. Materiel & Intelligence:** The Iron Legion survey machine was recovered, containing complete combat logs and barrier energy signatures despite its ecological miscalibration. Official Iron Legion documentation issued by Commissar Vexis proved 100% effective in bypassing municipal security checkpoints.

**4. Diplomatic Agreement:** Egress will be executed via localized transport spellcraft, subject to a binding Oath of Secrecy regarding the Underground's existence.
waluigiAssessment:
## Waluigi's Assessment & Editorial Verdict

**1. The Egress Protocol — A Masterclass in Localized Transport.** Waluigi commends King Asgore and Queen Toriel for rejecting the total destruction of the Barrier. Destroying a load-bearing dimensional seal to move two men is like blowing up a bridge to cross a puddle. Localized transport is clean, efficient, and keeps the roof where it belongs. WAH.

**2. The Vexis Credentials — Administrative Victory.** The Agent's use of Commissar Vexis's papers proves Waluigi's long-standing thesis: guards at official gates do not read documents to verify truth; they read documents to relieve themselves of responsibility. A gold seal and a commissar's name will get you into almost any room in the multiverse. WAH.

**3. The Execution of Flowey — Functional Retribution.** Flowey's elimination by Sans in a localized time-stop was necessary for operational security. Allowing a hostile entity with cross-dimensional boundary data to remain mobile would have compromised both the Underground and surface operations. WAH.

**4. The Oath of Secrecy — Legal Recommendation.** Waluigi advises all readers to respect the Oath of Secrecy. Not because of royal authority, but because if humans on the surface discover seven hundred thousand monsters living under a mountain, they will immediately try to tax them. WAH.

**Final Recommendation:** Approve the Part VII filing. Close the Mount Ebott Survey dossier. File the Vexis documents in the Iron Legion archives under Class 1 Clearance. WAH!

summary: Following the Imp Ambush at Tymnas's cottage, Dan and Tymnas stay behind to heal Salam while Markop and Eager follow a blood trail into the dark woods. After encountering a singing Mazehound and a Mazebound who lost a finger, Markop casts Locate Object on Remi's necklace. Remi unexpectedly appears behind them, having escaped the cells with Mossy. Returning to the dungeon facility to recover her stolen necklace, Remi turns invisible, sneaks into a crab cage, accidentally triggers a dancing Box Guardian, gets covered in soot by a loaded gun barrel, and escapes wearing a cardboard box disguise with a Sharpie goblin face. Reunited with the Black Crystal, the party flees as Remi sings the Toad spore shanty, while Markop formulates a plan to locate Archie.

sections.name: I. The Opened Book and the Whip Crack
sections.overview:
Markop's heavy battleaxe cut through the damp cottage air in a single, brutal arc. The steel edge caught an attacking imp across the wing joints, severing the leathery limb with a sharp crunch. The severed wing dropped with a wet slap directly onto the open, yellowed pages of the Archivist's book resting on the table, smearing fresh black ink across the margin notes.

Feyward Dan blinked, sitting up from the splintered floorboards where he had been lying dazed. He wiped the dust from his eyes, shook his head, and quickly took in the room's chaotic geometry. Assessing the situation in half a breath, he stood up, drew his longsword with a ringing rasp, and declared with total conviction: **"I'm going to use a longsword and strike this imp!"**

Across the cottage, a loud whip crack shattered the noise. Eager snapped his heavy leather cord across the room, catching the wounded imp square around the neck. The same creature that had been hovering near the ceiling let out a choked shriek, its wings buckling as it fell heavily onto the wooden floor.

Dan turned toward the inner doorway, shouting into the quiet washroom: **"Remi, are you okay in there?"**

There was no response. The washroom was completely empty, its back window standing wide open to the cold fog.

Outside the shattered lower window frame, a limp Salam lay motionless in the damp grass where Tymnas had thrown him to safety, surrounded by disturbed leaves and broken twigs. Tymnas caught his breath against the sill, wiping blood from his brow. **"I threw him out the window to keep him alive!"**

Realizing the threat was moving outside, the party split up: Dan stayed behind with Tymnas to cast healing spells on the unconscious Salam, while Markop and Eager headed out the cottage door to track Remi's trail through the woods.

*WAH! Room checks! In the Mushroom Regency, if you call out a name into an empty bedroom, a Toad answers with a tray of cookies! In the Shadow Estate, an empty room means your party member was dragged out a window four minutes ago while you were picking up a longsword! WAH.*
sections.waluigi_note: The tactical split at the cottage separates the defenders into two functional elements: Dan and Tymnas stabilize Salam, while Markop and Eager initiate immediate pursuit.

sections.name: II. The Blood Trail and the Singing Mazehound
sections.overview:
Markop poked his head out the cottage doorway, his dark eyes narrowing as he spotted a Mazebound prowling in the grey mist along the fence line. He pulled his head back inside, motioning for silence. He couldn't see any sign of Remi's boots in the mud.

Eager knelt near the bushes, his gloved fingers pointing to a fresh red smear glistening on a wet fern. **"We better follow it!"** he whispered.

They moved up into the dense, dark woods surrounding the cottage. The canopy blocked what little ambient light the Shadowfell offered, leaving the forest submerged in pitch-black shadows. **"It's dark in here,"** Eager muttered, shivering inside his coat. **"We're outside... maybe we should have bought a torch."**

Deviating slightly from the main blood trail, they pushed through a thicket of thorned brambles—and ran directly into a Mazehound crouching on a flat stone. The creature's grey, thorned snout lifted, its yellow eyes glowing with dim malice as it began to sing in a strange, echoing rhythm:

**"Have you heard us sing? Welcome to the grove, welcome to the grey, you'll never find the Remi so you might as well stay!"**

Markop spat onto the dirt, completely unimpressed by the performance. **"Waste of time! Let's head back to the blood!"** he growled, turning his back on the singing beast.

*WAH! Musical forest monsters! A creature made of grey fog and thorned vines that stops a rescue party to deliver a four-line rhyming song about kidnapping! Waluigi has dealt with similar street performers in Rogueport, but usually they ask for two coins before singing! WAH.*
sections.waluigi_note: The Mazehound's song is a psychological stalling tactic designed to draw pursuers off the physical blood trail.

sections.name: III. The Mazebound's Finger and the Pure Soul Requirement
sections.overview:
Doubling back toward the original blood trail, Markop and Eager ran into a second Mazebound crouching in the brush. The creature hissed, stepping back in surprise: **"A new one!"**

Markop stepped forward, his axe raised and ready. **"What do you mean new one? Do you know where Remi was?"**

The Mazebound held up a clawed, bleeding hand, shaking its head. **"No! That blood was my finger — it's gone! It should be faster, but the imps need a pure soul to heal it."**

Markop frowned at the creature's strange logic. **"Where would the imps take a pure soul? The imp factory, mom's basement, the dungeon?"**

The Mazebound began to mutter a long explanation, but Markop cut him off with a bark: **"Too long!"**

Instead of negotiating further with the creature, Markop closed his eyes and began chanting a divine spell. He pictured Remi's silver necklace in his mind, focusing his divine energy into a casting of *Locate Object*. A faint gold pulse resonated in his chest, pointing like a magnetic needle through the dark trees.

*WAH! Pure soul healing! Imps use pure souls like emergency medical kits! They kidnap a halfling ranger, cut off a finger, and try to use her soul to patch a wounded Mazebound! This is why Waluigi keeps his soul impure — nobody ever tries to use Waluigi for medical ingredients! WAH.*
sections.waluigi_note: Markop's casting of Locate Object bypasses interrogation delays, replacing unreliable enemy testimony with a direct divine tracking signal.

sections.name: IV. The Elevation Surprise and the Reunited Party
sections.overview:
Markop and Eager followed the golden *Locate Object* beacon through the dense underbrush, their eyes fixed on the path ahead.

Suddenly, a rustle sounded right behind them. Remi stepped out from behind a mossy rock, scaring Markop half to death! Markop jumped, spinning around with his hand over his heart: **"Where have you gone?!"**

Remi dusted her sleeves, a small, triumphant smirk on her face. **"I got kidnapped, but I got myself and Mossy out of trouble! We lost some things though... I know where the necklace is."**

The tracking signal had led them below her because the entrance to the dungeon facility where her necklace rested was elevated on a stone ledge above them.

Seeing her cuts, Markop immediately raised his hand and cast a healing spell. Warm divine light washed over Remi, closing her wounds as they walked back toward the dungeon entrance together, ready to recover her stolen necklace and belongings.

*WAH! The vertical approach! Markop casts a tracking spell pointing forward, and Remi drops down from a ledge behind him! This is why Waluigi always checks the ceiling before checking the floor! WAH.*
sections.waluigi_note: Remi's self-rescue demonstrates her operational independence. Rather than waiting for a rescue party, she broke containment and re-established contact.

sections.name: V. Infiltration of the Crab Cage
sections.overview:
As they approached the secured storage facility, Markop ordered Remi softly: **"Stay in the back."**

Remi nodded: **"Okay."**

She immediately cast *Invisibility* on herself, her body turning completely translucent. Ahead in the courtyard, they spotted wooden crates tied up inside a heavy iron cage shaped like a giant crab trap. Remi's stolen gear was inside!

Remi whispered to her construct: **"Stay here, Mossy. I'm getting some stuff and I'll be back."**

Invisible Remi crept past two patrolling guards, climbed onto a wooden barrel, and jumped down through the top hatch into the cage. An imp guard stood right beside the crates, completely unaware of her presence.

Remi began digging through the crates, but couldn't find her necklace on top. She burrowed deeper into the pile of wooden containers.

*WAH! Invisible breaking and entering! Remi sneaks past two guards, jumps into a crab cage, and burrows through wooden crates like a rat in a pantry! A masterclass in stealth operations! WAH.*
sections.waluigi_note: Remi's use of Invisibility allows her to infiltrate the secure storage cage without triggering open combat.

sections.name: VI. The Box Guardian and the Dancing Goblin
sections.overview:
Deep inside the crate pile, Remi found an interesting, ornate wooden box and opened the latch.

Instantly, a tiny, energetic goblin jumped out of the box! **"I'm the Box Guardian! I guard the box! Who opened my box?!"** the goblin shrieked.

The Box Guardian immediately started doing a wild, energetic victory dance! The noise drew a second guard down from the upper walkway—now two guards were patrolling the tight cage area!

Remi, still completely invisible, held her breath and dived deeper into the box pile to avoid being stepped on by the dancing goblin.

*WAH! The Box Guardian! You open an interesting box in a dungeon and instead of gold or a potion, a tiny goblin pops out like a jack-in-the-box and starts doing a tap-dance! Waluigi has bought mystery boxes with similar contents at the Wario Warehouse! WAH.*
sections.waluigi_note: The Box Guardian functions as a comedic trap, converting a routine container search into a high-risk stealth hazard.

sections.name: VII. The Soot Barrel and the Missing Mirror
sections.overview:
Buried beneath the dancing goblin's box, Remi spotted a deep black jar containing a dark crystal.

Remi paused, examining it closely: **"How do I know if this is not just a clear crystal inside a black jar? I better look inside."**

Remi forced her hands down into the narrow opening to pull the Black Crystal out. Her hands came out covered in thick, black soot. She reached in deeper and forced it upward—**BAM!**

A sudden flash of light fired upwards with a deafening bang! A cloud of gunpowder smoke erupted, covering her face and body in black soot! The 'black jar' was actually the loaded barrel of a swivel gun!

Coughing quietly through the soot, Remi searched further for the **Mirror of True Reflection**, but couldn't find it in the pile. She reminded herself: **"Nice and quiet, slow and don't get caught, because if I get caught, bad things will happen!"**

*WAH! The cannon barrel jar! Remi thought she was pulling a crystal out of a vase, but she was actually shoving her hand down the barrel of a loaded cannon! The flash of light turned her face blacker than a Mario kart exhaust pipe! WAH.*
sections.waluigi_note: The soot-barrel incident highlights the deceptive traps placed within the storage cage, converting an inspection into an explosive misfire.

sections.name: VIII. The Sharpie Paper Bag Disguise
sections.overview:
Searching through the remaining crates, Remi found a **Disguise Kit** and a small cardboard box.

Remi examined the box: **"It sort of looks like a goblin, it's just my size."**

Remi put the box over her head and pulled out a Sharpie marker, drawing a crude goblin face on the front! Looking down at her soot-covered clothes and paper bag mask, she thought: *"I am screwed... Okay, now I hope my disguise is good enough."*

A guard spotted her walking out of the cage: **"Hey! Who are you? Why are you wearing that paper bag on your head?"**

Remi put on a raspy goblin voice and bluffed: **"I'm a Box Guardian! Like a guardian with a box! There is a box that needs to be guarded, but before someone else gets before me..."**

Without waiting for a response, Remi sprinted for the exit at full speed!

*WAH! The cardboard box disguise! Remi drew two eyes and a zig-zag mouth on a paper bag with a Sharpie marker and told a guard she was a certified Box Guardian! And the guard believed her! This is the greatest stealth disguise in the history of the Shadow Estate! WAH.*
sections.waluigi_note: Remi's improvised cardboard box disguise exploits the guards' confusion, converting a compromised stealth position into a rapid escape.

sections.name: IX. The Toad Spore Song and the Escape
sections.overview:
Remi burst out of the facility gates, running back toward Markop and Eager while shouting: **"We need to leave as quickly as possible! We can always come back another time! And maybe with our luck Wario will come with the mirror and smell like garlic... Seriously, what is it with that guy and the garlic?!"**

As she ran past the guard she had killed earlier, she noticed his body hadn't decomposed: **"I guess he hasn't decomposed yet. The Toads say that they decompose at a slow rate after death too... We're born from it. When you decompose, a new Toad is born. It almost makes me want to sing!"**

Remi burst into the Toad spore shanty as she ran: **"We are the fun guys, you may call me a fun-gi, because we grow and grow, and we scream and shout and run about!"**

She marvelled as they ran: **"I can't believe my disguise worked!"** while guards' shouts echoed behind them.

Markop caught up, looking at the road ahead: **"I think I know a way to find Archie."**

*WAH! The Toad spore shanty! Remi escapes a dungeon wearing a cardboard box covered in soot, singing a children's song about Toad decomposition, while wondering why Wario smells like garlic! Waluigi has no notes. This is peak operational performance! WAH.*
sections.waluigi_note: Remi's successful escape with the Black Crystal concludes the recovery phase, setting up the search for Archie.

aftermath:
## Aftermath & Operational Standing

**1. Operational Result:** The party successfully recovered the Black Crystal from the storage cage at the dungeon facility. Remi escaped uncaptured using an improvised cardboard box disguise.

**2. Casualty & Personnel Status:** Salam was stabilized by Dan and Tymnas following the whip strike. Remi sustained minor soot burns from a gun barrel trap. Two dungeon guards remain alerted but confused.

**3. Materiel & Intelligence:** The Black Crystal is back in party custody. The Mirror of True Reflection remains unrecovered. Markop established a tracking methodology to locate Archie.

**4. Strategic Position:** The group has withdrawn from the facility perimeter and is preparing to pursue Archie's location.
waluigiAssessment:
## Waluigi's Assessment & Editorial Verdict

**1. The Box Guardian Disguise — High-Risk Tactical Success.** Waluigi commends Remi for her improvisational disguise technique. Drawing a goblin face on a cardboard box with a Sharpie marker and claiming to be a Box Guardian bypassed two armed guards without triggering combat. WAH.

**2. Locate Object Efficiency.** Markop's decision to cast Locate Object on Remi's necklace cut through the Mazebound's deceptive riddles, proving that divine tracking spells are vastly superior to forest negotiation. WAH.

**3. The Soot Barrel Hazard.** Shoving hands into a deep black jar without checking if it is the barrel of a loaded swivel gun is a classic field error. Remi is fortunate the powder flash only produced soot and singed eyebrows. WAH.

**4. Retaining the Black Crystal.** Securing the Black Crystal prevents the Onyx Hand and Kyrn's forces from utilizing it for plane-severing rituals. WAH.

**Final Recommendation:** Approve the filing. Update the Shadow Estate event registry. Track Wario's garlic emissions as a potential regional navigation beacon. WAH!

summary: Wario planned a treasure expedition in a locked room, hired a stranger named Jory Dobbs off a noticeboard for a wage of nothing, forged two passports, and specifically excluded Waluigi — then spotted him on a balcony with binoculars at four in the morning, abducted him in a produce sack, and flew a taped-together charter into a storm hunting treasure in Mount Ebott. The aircraft crashed into a cave, the pilot was knocked out, Dobbs took a head wound, and the party climbed anyway — past a bone-throwing teleporter, an earthquake that pushed skeletons up in rows, and a razor-and-flame trap bridge — to a summit plank reading MOUNT EBOT. One T. They had climbed the wrong mountain, and the map's own cartouche said whose fault it was.
imageCaption: Mount Ebot from the valley track, photographed on a later survey. One T. 1,340 feet of wet slate that cost an aircraft, a bridge crossing and eight years of filing delay. The board had been levered off the signpost and left face-down in the mud; the archive notes that removing a sign takes more effort than reading one.
description:
*"Your cut? Experience. An adventure. A story for the grandkids. Do you know what people pay for an adventure?"*
— **[Wario](#/article/wario)**, setting the expedition's wage structure

*"There is a mountain. There is treasure in the mountain. There is a man who told me about the mountain and I only had to hit him once."*
— **[Wario](#/article/wario)**, four o'clock in the morning, to a courtyard

*"So we climbed the wrong mountain."*
— **[Jory Dobbs](#/article/jory_dobbs)**, summit of Mount Ebot, bleeding

*"WAH! Every injury on this expedition, every bone, every razor, every burned name on every plank, descends from one absent letter in a printing house that no longer exists. Waluigi did not lose a day to a mountain. Waluigi lost a day to a compositor with cold hands."*
— **[Waluigi](#/article/waluigi)**, Auditor-General, Walupedia Editorial Board

---

Filed as a session record of 17 Aethel, 1032 BF, and released to the archive only now. The notebook went into a crate with the misprinted chart and the correction demand, and the crate went into storage behind eight years of more urgent disasters. Waluigi has changed nothing in it. The wound was dressed in 1032, the plank was read in 1032, and the correction the Old World Mapping Company promised on application has still not arrived. The expedition was planned the previous afternoon in a gold room Waluigi was deliberately excluded from — a room containing treasure maps weighted down with garlic bread, two forged passports, a journal describing an artifact called the Heartstone, and a young man being told that his share of the proceeds would be nothing. The first four sections of this filing reconstruct that afternoon from the hire's account and are marked as reconstruction. Everything after it is first-hand.

Waluigi was carried out of his own building in an agricultural sack at four in the morning and returned by air at twenty to ten that night, and in the eighteen hours between those two facts the expedition argued about satellite phones, discovered that Wario had packed thermal gear cut for a man he claimed not to be bringing, crashed an aircraft into a cave, hauled nine loads up a scree slope on a rope chain, was attacked by a silent four-foot figure that threw sharpened human bones and left by folding the air, watched a hillside open in parallel seams and hand back its dead, crossed a maintained trap bridge with sixty razors and six oil jets, recorded four missing humans from a burned plank with one name rubbed nearly out, and reached a summit cairn to discover from the expedition's own map that the mountain was **Mount Ebot** — one T — a different mountain entirely from Mount Ebott, printed by **The Old World Mapping Company, Survey Series IV, corrections on application.**

Waluigi speaks perhaps two hundred words aloud across the whole day. What follows includes the rest.

sections.name: I. The Villa, and the Chair That Fell Over
sections.overview:
Waluigi was not in this room. Waluigi wants that stated at the top, in the archive's own voice, because this section and the three that follow it are reconstruction, and the archive does not pretend otherwise. What follows was assembled afterward from the hire's account, given twice on two different days and consistent both times; from the state of the room, which Waluigi later saw; and from the fact that Wario is the single most predictable man alive and has never once surprised anybody who was paying attention.

The room was the long gold one on the ground floor of the villa. Treasure maps had been unrolled across the table and weighted at the corners with a candlestick, a stapler, and two ends of a torn loaf. There was garlic bread on the maps. There is always garlic bread on the maps.

**"Finally,"** Wario said, and brought both hands down flat on the table hard enough to make the paper jump. **"Took you long enough to show up. Mount Ebott. We're going back."**

The chair went over behind him when he stood — a solid backwards crash on marble that he did not turn around for, did not glance at, and did not right at any point in the following two hours. It was still lying there when the room was next opened.

**"I've been through the old explorer notes all week,"** he said, pacing the length of the table, stabbing a finger down at different parts of the map without appearing to look at where it landed. **"There's a vault in those peaks. We got close last time. Missed it by inches. Blizzard."**

The hire — twenty-two years old, in a woollen hat, standing where he had been told to stand — asked how close inches was.

**"Inches,"** Wario said.

Then he spun, and the spin took out a stack of gold-plated plates that went across the floor in a long bright clatter, and he did not look at those either.

**"Summer solstice. All those avalanche zones are melt by then. And I have got—"** and here his voice dropped into the register he believes is a whisper, leaning in until the boy could smell the garlic **"—*satellite images*. There's a structure under the ice. Something big."**

He crossed to a cabinet, unlocked it, and came back with a journal bound in cracked hide, holding it flat on two palms like a waiter.

**"Out of my private museum. Talks about an artifact. The Heartstone."** He let the name sit. **"Unlimited wealth. To whoever holds it. That is worth more than every share certificate in this building."**

*WAH! Observe the sequence. A vault becomes a structure becomes an artifact becomes unlimited wealth, and at no point in the escalation does a single verifiable object enter the room. Wario has photographs he will not produce and a journal he will not let go of. Waluigi has audited men who lied better than this while holding worse.*

The boy looked around the enormous gold room and asked whether anyone else was in it.

Wario stopped. He scanned the corners properly for the first time — the grandfather clock ticking against the far wall, the chandelier with its slow drip, the velvet curtain by the windows, which he walked over and pulled back to find nothing behind it but dust and more dust.

**"Nope. Just us. Guards are all outside today. Didn't want nosy ears."**

**"So no Waluigi,"** the boy said.

The face Wario made is recorded in the hire's account as *like he bit a bad egg*. **"That lanky weirdo? I told him to stay home. That guy could not keep a secret if you stapled it to his forehead."** The vase went next — a real one, off a plinth, into pieces across the marble. He did not look at that either. **"Last big thing we planned together he blabbed it at karaoke night and we nearly got picked up by Bowser's goons."**
sections.waluigi_note: Two of the three claims in that last sentence are false and the third is worse. Waluigi did not blab at karaoke; Wario sang the plan, in full, in a key of his own devising, to a room of forty people. The goons were already there. And Waluigi was not "told to stay home" in any sense that involved being told — he learned he was excluded eleven hours later, in a sack, at altitude. Wario does not lie so much as he pre-writes the version he intends to remember. WAH.

sections.name: II. Two Wallets, and the Word Nobody Wanted Said
sections.overview:
The briefing ended the way all Wario briefings end, which is with logistics presented as generosity.

He went back to the cabinet and came out with two wallets, and laid them on the map side by side with the air of a man dealing a winning hand.

**"Identification,"** he said. **"For the border, for the airfield, for anyone who asks. Yours and mine. Untraceable."**

They were passports of a sort — hard covers, plausible stamps, a lamination bubble in one corner of each. The first said **GREGORIO MORETTI**. The second said **HANS KÜBLER**. The photographs inside bore no resemblance to either man standing at the table, a fact the hire raised immediately and was answered as follows:

**"Nobody looks at the picture. They look at the *confidence*."**

*WAH! Waluigi has crossed nine borders in his professional life and can report that people look at the picture. People look at the picture first, last, and twice in between. Waluigi would also observe that a man who keeps two false identities in a locked cabinet in his own dining room has not prepared for an expedition. He has prepared for a departure.*

The hire picked one up, turned it over, and — the record has this from the hire himself, unprompted, offered as a confession rather than extracted — did not put it back. It went into his coat pocket while Wario was mid-sentence about tariffs, and it stayed there. Waluigi notes this without judgement. Everybody who has ever worked for Wario has taken something small, on the first day, as insurance. It is the closest thing to a pension the firm offers.

Then the boy asked the question.

**"The stories about that mountain,"** he said. **"People who go up don't come back. They fall down and they don't return. And there's supposed to be — things. Under it. Monsters."**

The room got quieter than a room with a grandfather clock in it can normally manage.

**"There are no monsters,"** Wario said.

He said it fast, and he said it loudly, and he said it while looking at the wall over the boy's shoulder rather than at the boy — three tells, in one sentence, from a man who has never successfully concealed anything in his life.

**"But the stories—"**

**"Stories are what poor people have instead of maps."** A hand slap on the table. Another plate went. **"Nobody falls. Nobody's under there. And if there IS anything under there it can take a number, because I am going to be *rich* and I don't have the schedule."**

*WAH! Note for the record that the man denying the existence of monsters under Mount Ebott went on to spend that same evening being hit in the face with a sharpened human femur by a small silent person on Mount Ebot. Waluigi does not believe in fate. Waluigi believes in invoicing, and the universe billed promptly.*

The last item of business was pay, and it took four minutes.

**"What's my cut?"** the boy asked.

**"Your cut."**

**"Of the treasure. If we find it."**

**"*When* we find it,"** Wario said, **"I take it. All of it. It's my expedition, my maps, my helicopter, my journal, my satellite images, my *idea*—"**

**"So what do I get?"**

**"Experience,"** said Wario. **"An adventure. A story for the grandkids. Do you know what people pay for an adventure?"**

**"Do I get *money*?"**

**"No."**

And that was the negotiation. The hire, according to the hire, said nothing further, put his hand in his coat pocket, and held on to the wallet he had already stolen for the rest of the conversation.
sections.waluigi_note: Two contracts were signed in that room and only one of them was spoken aloud. Wario offered a zero-share and considered the matter closed; the boy accepted the zero-share out loud and privately re-priced the job at one forged passport, payable immediately, taken in advance. Waluigi is not condoning theft. Waluigi is observing that Wario invented the terms, and that a wage of nothing produces employees who set their own. WAH.

sections.name: III. Antonio, Who Has a Family to Feed
sections.overview:
Then Wario ate.

There is no expedition in this archive, no crisis, no funeral and no fire, at which Wario has not at some point simply stopped and eaten, and the Ebot briefing broke for garlic bread roughly ninety seconds after the pay question was settled. He took a loaf off the map, tore it, and held half of it out across the table.

The hire reached for it. Wario's grip did not release.

**"Careful,"** he said, entirely pleasantly. **"Last guy grabbed too fast. I bit his hand."**

**"You bit—"**

**"Bit his hand. He was fine. He got a plaster and a story."**

The boy took the bread slowly, with the deliberate motion of a man withdrawing his fingers from a machine, and Wario laughed for some time and poured lemonade for both of them out of a jug so cold it was sweating on the map.

The chef came in with a second tray. Bald, aproned, unhurried, a hundred years of patience in the way he set things down: **Antonio**, who cooks in that villa and has apparently cooked in that villa for a considerable time.

**"He's the best,"** Wario announced. **"Best chef in the whole—"** a vague circle of the hand meaning the kingdom, the region, or the room **"—anywhere."**

**"Thank you, sir."**

**"What's he pay you?"** the boy asked.

Antonio's answer is recorded because the hire wrote it down that night, on the back of the stolen passport, and Waluigi has seen the handwriting.

**"Barely anything,"** Antonio said. **"But it is better than nothing, and I have a family to feed."**

Then he collected two plates from the floor, said nothing whatsoever about the third one in pieces by the plinth, and left.

*WAH! Waluigi wishes to place Antonio's sentence next to Wario's — "you get experience" — and leave the two of them touching on the page without further comment. That is the whole compensation policy of Wario's Enterprise, stated twice in one afternoon by both parties to it, and neither of them heard the other.*

Provisioning followed. Wario refused, in advance and at volume, to buy any named brand of anything.

**"High-end snacks are cardboard dipped in money,"** he said, from inside a cupboard. **"You pay for the *bag*. I don't eat bags."**

What he packed instead came out of a locked lower cabinet the boy had assumed was structural: the secret stash. Salted crackers in unmarked tins. Hard sausage. Dried fruit in wax paper. Two catering slabs of chocolate. Six loaves, wrapped for cold. Enough salt to preserve a horse. It was, and Waluigi will say this once, an entirely competent cold-weather ration list, assembled by a man who cannot spell the mountain but has genuinely never in his life been caught short of food.

**"Three weeks of this,"** Wario said, stacking it. **"Minimum. Nobody starves on my expeditions."**

Nobody has ever starved on a Wario expedition. They have frozen, fallen, been concussed, been sued, and been bitten by Wario. They have never gone hungry.
sections.waluigi_note: Waluigi has audited the villa's books and the line item marked KITCHEN is smaller than the line item marked GOLD LEAF, and Waluigi would like Antonio to know that this archive has noticed. The man is owed back-pay by any standard the Glazed Congress recognises. Waluigi will note also, since precision is the point of the exercise, that the ration planning for Ebot was better than the navigation, the aircraft, the personnel screening, and the objective combined. Wario prepares excellently for the parts of a disaster that involve lunch. WAH.

sections.name: IV. The Wariocopter Objection, and the Man on the Balcony
sections.overview:
The loading took the rest of the day and most of the night, and there was one argument in it worth filing.

The hire, looking at the aircraft on the villa's pad — a chartered grey thing with the livery half-scrubbed off and tape across the fuel gauge — asked the obvious question, which was why they were not taking the Wariocopter.

**"The Wariocopter,"** Wario said, **"is not for mountains."**

**"It flies."**

**"It flies *near the ground*. It's got one rotor and a lot of opinions and it burns fuel like a house fire. You put that thing at ten thousand feet in a crosswind and it comes apart like a wet biscuit and I am *inside it* when that happens."** He patted the charter's flank, which rang like a bin lid. **"This is a *proper* aircraft. Rented. Insured. Somebody else's."**

*WAH! Waluigi wishes it entered as a permanent finding of this archive that Wario declined to risk the Wariocopter on the grounds that it was fragile, expensive to run, and personally valuable to him, and then boarded a machine whose fuel gauge was covered with tape reading NOT ACCURATE, carrying an unbriefed twenty-two-year-old and, shortly, an abducted auditor. The Wariocopter was protected. The people were not.*

Crates went aboard: the rations, the coils of rope, a crate of climbing iron nobody had inspected, the oilcloth-wrapped map, six wrapped loaves, and the cold-weather kit. The hire loaded most of it, and at some point during the loading — his own account again — he took the stolen wallet out of his coat, where it had been sitting all afternoon against his ribs, and pushed it down into the bottom of his canvas kit-bag underneath a spare shirt, because coats get searched and bags get carried.

They lifted off before dawn with the courtyard lamps still on.

They were up for perhaps four minutes.

What happened next is the only part of the pre-flight period Waluigi can attest to personally, because Waluigi was in it. Waluigi was on his own balcony, eleven miles from the villa, at four o'clock in the morning, with a pair of binoculars.

He was not bird-watching.

He was watching a chartered aircraft with a scrubbed livery lift out of a villa he was not invited to, in the dark, carrying crates he had not been shown, and he was doing what he does, which is *making a note*. He had the aircraft's registration on the second page of the book. He was fourteen seconds from having its heading.

Then the landing lamp came round and found him standing there in a dressing gown with the binoculars up.

**"WALUIGI."**

The aircraft came down in the courtyard below — a courtyard Wario did not own, occupied by a chartered machine burning fuel that somebody had already been billed for — and Wario came up the thirty-one stairs two at a time.

**"You were *watching*."**

**"Waluigi was bird-watching."**

**"It's four in the morning."**

**"Owls,"** said Waluigi.

Wario took a double fistful of dressing gown, lifted him onto his toes, and put his face very close, and what he said is on the record because the hire heard all of it from the stairwell and repeated it twice, consistently:

**"I will smash your skull. I will smash it flat. I will put you in the ground and I will tell people you moved away."**

And then — because Wario cannot hold a threat and a plan in his head simultaneously, and because he had, as the archive will shortly establish, packed for this — he did not smash anything. He looked at Waluigi for a moment with an expression the hire described as *doing sums*, and then he went and got a sack.
sections.imageCaption: The chartered aircraft on the villa pad the night before departure, livery half-scrubbed and the fuel gauge taped. Wario's stated objection to the Wariocopter was that it flies near the ground. This flew high, once.
sections.waluigi_note: Everything about that balcony is worth an hour of anyone's time. Wario had spent an entire afternoon explaining that Waluigi could not be trusted with the plan, had checked behind a curtain for him, had broken a vase on the subject — and the instant he actually saw him he abducted him and took him along. Waluigi was excluded for being a security risk and then loaded aboard as cargo, which improved the security position not at all and improved the crew by exactly one competent person. WAH.

sections.name: V. The Sack Smelled of Onions
sections.overview:
The sack smelled of onions.

Everything above this point is reconstruction. Everything from here is Waluigi's, first-hand, and Waluigi would like the onions noted ahead of all of it — ahead of the mountain, ahead of the bones, ahead of the four dead names on the plank. Not a hood. Not a courier's dark bag. Not any of the respectable instruments of abduction a person of standing might reasonably expect to be carried off in. A produce sack. Forty-pound weave, stencilled in green on the outside, TOAD TOWN AGRICULTURAL BOARD — GRADE II, and smelling on the inside of onions and old rain.

**"Waluigi is awake,"** Waluigi said into the burlap.

**"I know,"** Wario said, and kept walking.

Thirty-one stairs. Waluigi counted them through Wario's shoulder, each one arriving in his ribs like a dropped brick, and at the bottom the air changed — cooler, wetter, carrying the flat chemical sweetness of rotor fuel and the particular smell of a courtyard that has been rained on all night and swept by nobody. Somewhere ahead of them a turbine was winding up in short unhappy coughs.

Here is the part the record will not show, so Waluigi will supply it. His left hand was free the entire time. It had been free since the landing of the fourteenth stair, when the drawstring slipped its knot against his glove. He could have been out of that sack, over the rail and three streets gone before Wario finished the flight of steps.

He stayed in the sack.

Not out of fear, which does not apply. Out of arithmetic. Wario had come at four in the morning with a rented aircraft already burning fuel on a courtyard he did not own, which meant somebody had been paid, which meant somebody expected a return, and Waluigi has learned that when Wario spends money in advance the day is going to become expensive for someone. Waluigi intended to be the person holding the receipt rather than the person written on it.

**"There is a mountain,"** Wario announced, to nobody, to the courtyard, to the wet flagstones. **"There is treasure in the mountain. There is a man who told me about the mountain and I only had to hit him once."**

*WAH! Observe the invoice already forming. One rented aircraft, one bribed informant, one punched informant — the same man, Waluigi later established, billed twice — and one abducted business partner transported as GRADE II produce. Waluigi has been called many things. He has never before been graded.*

The sack came off in the courtyard. Cold hit his face like a wet towel, and the rotor wash took his hat.
sections.waluigi_note: Waluigi wishes the archive to be precise about consent. He did not agree to the Ebot expedition; he declined to escape it, which is a different transaction and one Wario has never learned to tell apart. Every job the two of them have ever done runs on that confusion. Wario believes he wins arguments. What actually happens is that Waluigi decides the argument is cheaper to attend than to win, and files the difference. WAH.

sections.name: VI. Three Passengers, One of Whom Was Cheerful
sections.overview:
The aircraft was a Toad Town charter with the livery half-scrubbed off, a fat grey thing with a cracked chin-bubble and a strip of tape across the fuel gauge. Somebody had written **NOT ACCURATE** on the tape in grease pencil. Waluigi read it twice, which is two more times than the pilot ever did.

The pilot was a Toad in a flight jacket three sizes too generous, chewing something, headset already on. He did not ask who Waluigi was. He did not ask why one of his passengers had arrived in a vegetable sack. He held out a clipboard, Wario signed it with a thumbprint, and that was the entire boarding procedure of the Mount Ebot expedition.

The third passenger was already strapped into the rear bench with his knees up and a canvas kit-bag between his boots.

**"Jory,"** said the hire, putting a hand out into the noise. **"Jory Dobbs. We sort of met on the stairs just now. You were in the sack. I was holding the door."**

Waluigi looked at him. Twenty-something, cheap boots with good laces, a woollen hat, hands that would not stop moving over the buckles of a harness he had clearly never worn before. No visible weapon. No visible reason to be there. The single most breakable object on the aircraft, including the chin-bubble.

**"He answered an advertisement,"** Wario said, dropping into the seat opposite and making the whole airframe lean. **"Skilled labour. Very competitive rate."**

**"It's my first expedition,"** Dobbs said, brightly, to a man who had just been carried out of a building in a produce sack.

*WAH! An advertisement. Wario has hired a stranger off a public noticeboard the way other people buy a used shovel, and the stranger has arrived early, packed sandwiches, and is excited. Waluigi has seen this exact face before, on a young Toad who once volunteered to hold Wario's ladder. That Toad is now a story.*

Waluigi said nothing. He took the seat by the door, because the seat by the door is the seat by the door, and he buckled a harness that had been repaired with boot-lace, and he thought: *the boy will be hurt today.* Not a fear. A schedule. The only open question was which hour, and whether anyone competent would be standing near him when it happened.

The turbine climbed. The courtyard dropped away, wet and grey, and Toad Town rolled underneath them in a spread of chimney smoke and market awnings still folded shut against the dark.
sections.waluigi_note: Note the hiring standard, because it recurs. Wario does not recruit; he fills a seat. The kit-bag between Dobbs's boots contained sandwiches, a spare shirt, and no rope — and no one inspected it, because inspecting it would have meant admitting there was a list of things a person on this aircraft ought to be carrying. There was no list. There has never been a list. WAH.

sections.name: VII. The Exit Strategy, Discussed at Altitude
sections.overview:
Twenty minutes out of Toad Town, with the cabin dark and the Toad's instrument glow the only light in it, Waluigi asked the question he had been saving since the courtyard.

**"What is the plan for coming back?"**

Wario, eating, held up three fingers. **"Three weeks of food. And—"** he dug in a coat pocket and produced a black plastic lozenge with a rubber aerial and a single unlit lamp on it **"—*this*. GPS tracker. Broadcasts a position. Anything goes wrong, they come and get us."**

**"Who is *they*?"**

**"People. Rescue people. They exist, I've seen them on television."**

The hire, from the rear bench, said the useful thing. He said it quietly, and he said it into the noise, and he had to say it twice before anyone turned round.

**"A tracker tells them where you are. It doesn't dig you out. If we're under snow, they get a very accurate position for a hole in a mountain."**

*WAH! Waluigi would like it recorded that a twenty-two-year-old on his first expedition understood in four seconds the difference between being locatable and being rescuable, and that this understanding was, at that moment, the second most valuable thing on the aircraft after the fuel.*

**"Then don't get buried,"** Wario said, which is the Wario Method entire, in four words, and he has never improved on it.

**"A satellite phone,"** Waluigi said.

Wario chewed.

**"A satellite phone,"** Waluigi said again. **"So that the position comes with a *sentence* attached to it. So that the sentence can be *we are under six feet of snow on the north face, bring shovels* rather than a lamp blinking politely at a rescue service that has to guess."**

And Wario — and this is the single documented occasion in the whole eighteen hours, and Waluigi wishes it in bold — stopped chewing, thought about it, and said:

**"...Yeah. Yeah, alright. That's a good point. I should've got one of those."**

No shouting. No plate. He wrote it on the back of his hand with a grease pencil, where it presumably stayed until the first rain, which arrived approximately ninety minutes later.

*WAH! Enter it in the ledger. Wario conceded an oversight, out loud, unprompted, in front of two witnesses, at altitude. It changed nothing operationally — there was still no telephone — but Waluigi has audited this man for a decade and this is the only entry in that column.*

Then came the detail that Waluigi has not been able to put down since.

The hire, rummaging for the emergency kit, found the cold-weather bundles lashed under the rear bench and counted them out: three sets. Boots, thermals, an outer shell, mittens, a hat. And the third set was long. Absurdly long. Sleeves cut for arms that no Toad pilot and no twenty-two-year-old and certainly no Wario has ever possessed.

**"Whose are these?"**

**"They're spares,"** Wario said, too quickly, to the windscreen.

They were not spares. They had been ordered, and they had been packed, and they had been lashed down under a bench in an aircraft that departed a villa from which Waluigi had been deliberately and loudly excluded — hours before Wario stood in a stairwell in the dark pretending to be surprised to see him.

Waluigi did not say anything about it. Waluigi put his hand on the bundle in the dark, felt the length of the sleeve, and did the sum.
sections.waluigi_note: The trousers are the whole man. Wario told a room he was keeping Waluigi off this job, checked behind a curtain to be sure of it, broke a vase about it, and then packed thermal gear cut for a six-foot-four frame and loaded it aboard before dawn. He did not intend to invite Waluigi. He intended to *take* him, which in Wario's arithmetic is cheaper, because an invitation can be declined and a sack cannot. Waluigi's hand was free from the fourteenth stair and Waluigi already knew, by then, that there would be a coat in his size at the other end. Both men boarded that aircraft pretending to have been surprised. Neither of them was. WAH.

sections.name: VIII. The Weather Had an Opinion
sections.overview:
Forty minutes out the light went wrong.

Not dark — wrong. The grey ahead of them thickened into a wall the colour of a bruise, standing on the plain from cloud-base to ground, and the horizon simply stopped being a line. Rain arrived all at once, the way a bucket arrives, hammering the chin-bubble in sheets that turned the world into running glass.

**"That's weather,"** the pilot said over the intercom, in the tone of a man identifying a bird.

**"Go through it,"** Wario said.

**"That's not how—"**

**"Through it."**

The aircraft went through it.

Waluigi kept his eyes on the fuel tape. **NOT ACCURATE.** The needle behind it wandered a full quarter of the dial each time the airframe dropped, which told him nothing about the fuel and everything about how hard the machine was being shaken. Hail started, small and vicious, drumming the skin above their heads like someone throwing handfuls of gravel at a tin roof. The cabin lights browned out, came back, browned out.

Dobbs was grinning. That was the detail Waluigi could not get past. Both hands white on the bench-edge, boots braced, teeth showing — grinning, the way people grin on the first big drop of a ride they paid for.

**"Is it always like this?"** Dobbs shouted.

**"No,"** Waluigi said.

Wario was asleep. Genuinely, audibly asleep, chin on chest, arms folded over his stomach, riding out a hailstorm at three thousand feet with the serenity of a man who has never once considered that a thing he is inside of might stop working. Waluigi has spent years trying to decide whether that is courage or a missing organ. He has settled on the second and continues to be quietly, unforgivably jealous of it.

*WAH! Wario sleeps through hail. Waluigi does not sleep through hail, because Waluigi is the one who remembers that this aircraft has tape on its instruments and a signature made of thumb. One of us is at peace. One of us is correct. Historically these have never been the same person.*

Then the mountain came out of the rain on the left side, black and much too close, and the pilot said a word that the intercom clipped, and the world tipped.
sections.waluigi_note: The order of events matters more than the storm does. Wario gave the instruction to fly into the weather; the pilot began an objection; the objection was overridden by volume. Everything that follows in this filing — the crash, the boy's head, the bones, the bridge, the wasted day — descends from a two-word command issued by a man who was asleep ninety seconds later. WAH.

sections.name: IX. The Cave Took the Aircraft In
sections.overview:
There was a rock face, and then there was not.

The mountain opened — a black slot in the streaming stone, wide enough and no wider — and the pilot did the only intelligent thing anyone did all day, which was to stop fighting for the sky and steer for the hole. The rotors clipped something on the way in. The sound was enormous and short, a single *CLANG* like a church bell being hit with a church, and then they were inside, and the light went out, and the floor of the world came up.

They slid. That is the part nobody expects. The skids caught wet stone and the whole aircraft went along the cave floor sideways for what Waluigi later paced out as sixty-one feet, throwing up a rooster-tail of grit and sparks, the tail boom screaming along the wall until a boulder took it off. Then everything stopped, and the only sounds left were rain on the rock outside and the slow *tick, tick, tick* of hot metal starting to be cold metal.
