name: Judgement in the Grove
title: Judgement in the Grove: A Musket in the Smoke, the Warhammer That Would Not Hear an Appeal, and the Man Remi Found Asleep
date: 1 Aethel, 1040 BF — just past midnight on the Shadowfell clock, the Skittering Grove inside the Scorncrow's tree, continuing straight out of the descent
era: Harvestide 1040 BF — Shadow Estate storm chain
location: The Skittering Grove, inside the Scorncrow's tree (Shadowfell)
type: Session Event / Grove Battle / Execution
status: Unresolved — the Scorncrow is dead but the grove is surrounded, Salam is down and unrecovered, Markop's skull is split, Remi is separated over a man she may have killed, and the Legion alliance ends in Archie's arrest
summary: The party fought its way out of the web canopy and into an execution. Remi swapped the crossbow for the musket and landed two direct hits through the smoke; Dan planted himself in front of everyone including Markop and turned the spiders with a mushroom-studded holy symbol; Eager and Dan killed the ettercap between them. The Iron Legion called for pest control, retreated, and then tried to arrest Archie mid-battle, which produced a temporary alliance nobody expects to hold. Markop called down divine favour, took a scythe to the skull, and split the Scorncrow's head open while it was on its knees asking a paladin for mercy. Remi, thrown clear by Mossy, found a breathing man with a red punch mark on his forehead and had the steel defender stand on his chest. Salam went down and did not get up.
description: *Three filings called the Scorncrow a monster and the fourth one took its mask off and found a human face under it. This filing is what the party did with that information. [Waluigi](#/article/waluigi) was not there. He has assembled it from [Markop](#/article/markop), [Archie](#/article/archie_miser), [Remi](#/article/remi_akamatsu_full_backstory) and a [Toad](#/article/toads) who would not give a name, and he wants it on the record before anybody smooths it over: the thing knelt, said it was human, asked a paladin to spare it, and the warhammer came down anyway. WAH.*
imageCaption: The moment before judgement. The Scorncrow on its knees with the scythe fallen out of reach, hood off, the face underneath plainly human and still asking; Markop at the top of the swing. The archive files this as neither murder nor justice.

sections.name: I. Smoke, and the Wrong Way Out
sections.imageCaption: She put the arrow back in her pocket and took the musket instead, then reloaded it slowly, in the open, with the brood already coming. Two direct hits. The bow stayed on her back.
sections.overview:
"It's a little smoky in here," Remi said.

She had been walking back the way she thought she had come, which in a grove with no sky and a silk floor is a sentence with no meaning in it. The webs take the edges off direction the same way they take the edges off sound. She got turned around once, corrected, got turned around again by the correction, and walked directly into the spiders.

She had the crossbow up and an arrow on the rail before she had finished registering the ettercap. Then she stopped. She looked at the arrow, and she looked at the thing in front of her, and she put the arrow back in her pocket.

The musket came off her shoulder instead.

The bang went flat across the web canopy and the ettercap came apart at the shoulder. A direct hit. Then she stood in the open and reloaded — powder, ball, ram, the whole unhurried procedure — while the grove watched her do it and did not close. She fired again. Another direct hit.

"You invaded my home, right," the Scorncrow said from somewhere in the dark. It was not really a question.

"Will the spiders attack?" Markop asked.

"They'll come around."
sections.waluigi_note: *She put the arrow back in her pocket. Read that again, because it is the most professional thing anybody did all night. A fourteen-year-old under contact, in smoke, having already walked into the enemy by accident, stopped to change weapons because the crossbow was the wrong tool — and then reloaded a musket in the open, twice, and hit with both. Three filings ago this girl was hiding behind Markop. Waluigi is going to stop describing her as the youngest member.*

sections.name: II. The Scythe That Cleaves Everything in Its Path
sections.overview:
The Scorncrow hurled its scythe.

It went out spinning, shrouded in something that bent the air around the blade, and it did not travel like a thrown weapon. It cleaved everything in its path — web, branch, standing bodies — and it dragged a chilling cold behind it that cut through anyone caught in the wake. Not the blade. The wake.

It caught Eager, Archie and Dan across the same line. All three took it. All three were grazed rather than opened, which is the only reason this section is four sentences instead of an obituary.

A spider came in on Eager while he was still registering the cold. Markop attacked it back off him.

Then Markop heard it: *thump. thump.* A giant green spider, going away from them rather than towards them — *thump thump* — heading for the Iron Legion guards.

Remi got webbed. "Why — *whyyyy* —" she shouted, as the strand took her and the thing on the other end of it pulled, and it clawed at her, and her clothes came apart under the hooks.

One of the Legion guards made the only correct tactical assessment of the night:

"We gotta call pest control. RETREAT!"
sections.waluigi_note: *A thrown weapon that cleaves everything in its path and freezes the air behind it, and it grazed three people instead of killing one. Waluigi notes the Scorncrow chose the spread. It could have put that scythe through a single body and it chose to open a line across three, which is what you do when you are not trying to win yet — you are trying to find out what everyone is made of. Dan said they had not seen half its power. Nobody has revised that estimate downward.*

sections.name: III. A Book in Full View, and a Paladin in Front of Everyone
sections.imageCaption: Feyward Dan put himself in front of everyone - including Markop, who is a head-and-shoulders taller and armoured - and turned the brood with a mushroom-studded holy symbol.
sections.overview:
"Come on, I'm looking at my spells," Remi said.

She said it tied up. She said it with the book open in full view, wrapped in silk, while another spider came down the strand towards her. There is no reading of that image that flatters anybody standing nearby.

Then Feyward Dan walked forward and stood in front of everyone.

Everyone including Markop — which matters, because Markop is a centaur with a warhammer and Dan is a Toad who had been unconscious an hour earlier and had spent every point of magic he owned healing himself. He put himself between the party and the Scorncrow, faced it, and then turned and swung at the spider instead.

He got out his holy symbol. A mushroom-studded thing, more garden than cathedral, and he held it up and faced it at the spiders.

Then he moved behind the spider, and he and Eager took it together — Dan swinging once, Eager coming in behind the distraction with a sneak attack. The spider roared.

Eager ran while it was distracted, straight into a spidery bush.

Markop walked past the spider. It bit at him and missed. He did not turn around to check. He was already facing the Scorncrow.
sections.waluigi_note: *Dan stood in front of Markop. Waluigi wants the ordering noted because Dan is the smallest combatant on the field and Markop is the largest, and the paladin's read was that the line goes where the oath is, not where the mass is. Four filings ago this Toad was a liability with a cursed staff. Waluigi has been unkind to him in print and is revising it here rather than quietly dropping the subject.*

sections.name: IV. Come to Offer Your Head
sections.overview:
"Oh, you come to offer your head. How vigilant."

Markop stared at him. He did not answer, which for Markop is an answer.

He walked closer. He got the warhammer up, and it began to glow — and above the dead grove with no sky in it, the ceiling opened anyway and thunder came down through it and hit the head of the hammer. Markop had come prepared. He had been holding divine favour since before the rope.

He struck. The Scorncrow blocked it. The block did not hold, and it flinched — the first time in four engagements that anything this party did has made it flinch.

Then it hit him in the head.

The scythe came around and split Markop's skull and he stood there bleeding into his own eyes, and the thing laughed at him.

"You think you can kill me? I have lived in this tree. Made it my treehouse when I was little."

Archie Miser — fireball-throwing, three-eyed, dimension-hopping, having split between worlds — prepared a fireball.

Then: "Nah, just kidding." He winked at no one in particular, and a considerably smaller firebolt hit the Scorncrow instead.

It coughed blood. "I'm still alive."
sections.waluigi_note: *Made it my treehouse when I was little. That is the second piece of physical evidence and nobody in the grove stopped moving for it. The first was the human blood under the mask. This is a childhood, in a location, with a tense. Whatever the Scorncrow is now, it is claiming to have grown up in the tree the party is currently standing inside, and Waluigi cannot file that as villain theatre because the archive already got caught doing exactly that three times.*

sections.name: V. The Tree of Love, and a Recruitment Pitch
sections.overview:
"Listen. Do you think the worst person can change?"

It was bleeding out of a ruined face and it wanted to have a conversation.

"We can hang people together on the tree of love. Join me, young one. Join the Scorncrow — or hear my last ballad."

"Sorry, Scorncrow," Archie said. "I'm on the side of good. Despite all my accidental crimes."

The guards were retreating deeper into the grove by then, and they took the opportunity of a lull in the murder to remember their jobs.

"YOU TOADS ARE UNDER ARREST."

"No — no, wait —"

"Archie Miser is right there. Arrest him."

"No, wait, *help*, get these spiders —"

What followed was a negotiation conducted at speed between people being actively eaten. They struck a temporary alliance: the Legion helps with the brood, the Toads agree, and Archie gets arrested at the end of it. Archie shrugged.

"This won't last."
sections.waluigi_note: *Do you think the worst person can change. Waluigi is obliged to note that the thing asked this question and then, two sections from now, was killed while asking a version of it again. The archive does not get to enjoy Archie's line about accidental crimes without also filing what the question was and who was asking it. Also: the Iron Legion attempted an arrest in the middle of a losing fight against a spider brood. Waluigi has no assessment. Waluigi simply wants it preserved.*

sections.name: VI. Down Here
sections.overview:
"What are you doing down here?" Archie asked.

"Down here? What do you mean?"

"Yes, *down here*. Remember the rope? We went down into the lair, and now we're fighting here. We're in the undergrowth, right?"

"The tree is a teleporter," Markop said.

"What are you guys talking about? This is the ruined manor."

Nobody resolved it. A punch landed somewhere off to the left with a sound like a wet sack dropped from height, and Wario laughed.

"I am tired of running."

"It's been like six seconds," Markop shouted.

Wario explained, without embarrassment, that he is a bad runner.

"This is all your fault, you know," Archie yelled at him.

"Alright then. I'll leave."

Salam fired at the ettercap and missed. Dan swung at the same moment and also missed. Then Feyward Dan and Eager went in together, in time with each other, and both hit, and the ettercap fell.

Every head in the grove turned to the Scorncrow.
sections.waluigi_note: *Three people in one conversation gave three different answers for where they were standing: down a rope in a lair, in the undergrowth, and in the ruined manor. Markop said teleporter. Last filing he recognised this place as the Silent Grove, which the party cleared on Raventree's grounds by walking to it in daylight. Waluigi's position is that all three answers are correct and that this is the actual emergency, well ahead of the spiders.*

sections.name: VII. BARK BARK
sections.overview:
Eager healed himself with duct tape.

Remi was about to be eaten. The thing had her wrapped and it came down to bite and there was no version of the next second that she survived on her own.

**BARK BARK.**

Mossy hit her side-on at a dead run. The steel defender put its whole weight into her and she went flying — off the strand, into the leaves and the branches, through them, and out the other side, and landed sitting on the floor of the grove with her ears ringing and every spider suddenly somewhere else.

She got up and she ran, and she kept running, and then she was alone in the woods.

She investigated. She found a body.

Then: no — he is breathing.

A man, unconscious, face up. There was a red punch mark on his forehead, fresh and clean and roughly the size of a gauntlet.

She tapped his head with a stick. Lightly. Nothing happened.

Mossy came bounding back to her.

Remi told Mossy to wake the guy up by stepping on him.

The hard steel came down and pressed onto the man's ribcage. There was a crack. The steel defender barked and lowered itself very slightly further onto his chest.

*Welp,* Remi thought. *I killed a guy in his sleep.*
sections.waluigi_note: *A red punch mark on the forehead. Waluigi has read the previous filing and would like to draw the obvious line: Wario was separated inside this grove, Wario punches things, and Wario had just announced he was tired of running. Waluigi is not filing that as fact. Waluigi is filing it as the first question anybody should ask the man if Remi's steel dog has left him in a condition to answer it.*

sections.name: VIII. The Warhammer Has Spoken
sections.overview:
Markop swung. The Scorncrow blocked with the scythe.

"Wait — please. I will change."

Its head split open and started glowing.

"Wait, please. I am human. I am not a monster."

It started to kneel.

"You're a paladin, right? You have to spare me. Please. I will change ways."

The head splits open. The warhammer has spoken and given him judgement.

Markop picked up the scythe.

Somewhere behind him, the rest of it was still going. Archie Miser announced that they should regroup to the three Toads, while pointedly not hearing the guards who were still asking to arrest him.

"We gotta find our friends."

"We're coming to get you home, Remi."

Alone in the woods with a man she may have killed, Remi heard the word *home* and it went somewhere in her that the spiders had not reached. She shook her head. Focus on the mission. Her dress was torn. She needs new armour.
sections.waluigi_note:
*Here is what the record says, in order. It said it would change. It said it was human. It said it was not a monster — the same sentence it has shouted in four consecutive engagements, the one the archive spent three filings calling theatre until a girl with a musket proved it was a statement of fact. Then it knelt. Then it asked a paladin, by his office, for mercy. Then Markop killed it.*

*Waluigi is not going to pretend this is uncomplicated and he is not going to pretend he would have done differently. The thing put a scythe through Markop's skull ninety seconds earlier and it had four engagements of dead Toads behind it. But the archive already got caught once assuming this creature was lying, and Waluigi will not make the same error in the other direction by recording an execution as a victory. Markop picked up the scythe. That is a man taking a trophy from someone who was on his knees, and Waluigi files it with the ruling and lets the reader weigh it.*

sections.name: IX. Every Grove at Once, and Salam
sections.imageCaption: Salam clawed across the face and down, crossbow fallen beside him, as the grove closes from every direction at once and Embercap's fire goes up behind. He was not recovered. The wound scars.
sections.overview:
It was not over. It was arithmetic.

Embercap, and spiders — giant spiders — came in and surrounded the grove, out of every grove, from every direction at once.

Markop felt a shadow come over him and then a blaze of heat off his own shoulder as fire went past his ear and into the ettercap.

A spider got to Salam. It clawed across his face, opened it, and he went down unconscious. It will scar.

A Legion guard was killed by a spider. At the same moment, on the other side of the grove, Markop was attacked again.

**Salam has fallen.**
sections.waluigi_note: *Salam. Last filing he crossed forty feet of open ground under a murder of crows to stabilise a man he barely knows, and said 'your service won't go in vain' to somebody who was still breathing. This filing he is face down in a dead grove with his face opened and the only healer in the party is the man he saved. Waluigi wants the symmetry on the record and wants somebody to go and get him.*

reputationNotes.markop: Executed the Scorncrow on its knees, unmasked, after it identified itself as human and formally asked a paladin for mercy. The archive is not recording that as clean, and neither are the Judges.

aftermath:
**The Scorncrow is dead.** It was killed on its knees, unmasked, after identifying itself as human and formally asking a paladin for mercy. Markop took the scythe. The claim it made four times across four engagements — *I am not a monster* — was tested by musket last filing and found to be true, and it was killed anyway. The archive is not going to record that as clean.

**Salam is down** with his face opened and has not been recovered. Feyward Dan, the only healer on the field, spent every point of magic he owned on himself an hour ago.

**Markop's skull is split** and he continued fighting through it. **Remi** is separated in the woods, her armour destroyed, standing over an unconscious man whose ribs her steel defender has just cracked on her instruction. She believes she may have killed him in his sleep.

**The Iron Legion alliance is explicitly temporary** and ends with Archie Miser's arrest. Archie's own assessment: *this won't last.* At least one guard is dead.

**The grove is still surrounded.** Embercap and giant spiders came in from every direction as the Scorncrow fell, so killing the thing that owned the place did not empty it.

**Unresolved:** the man with the red punch mark. Where the party actually is — rope-lair, undergrowth, or ruined manor, with Markop's teleporter reading unconfirmed. And what the Scorncrow meant by growing up in a tree the party has been standing inside all night.
waluigiAssessment:
**The execution is the filing and everything else is weather.** Waluigi has written the word *monster* about that thing in three separate articles and had to retract it last filing when a fourteen-year-old put a musket against its face and found a man underneath. This filing it knelt. It said it was human. It asked a paladin, by his office, to spare it. Markop killed it and took its scythe.

**Waluigi is not calling that murder and he is not calling it justice.** The thing had four engagements of casualties behind it and had opened Markop's skull ninety seconds earlier. But the archive got caught once assuming this creature was lying, and the correction does not become free just because the creature is now dead. Both facts go in the same paragraph or neither of them is honest.

**Remi Akamatsu is not the youngest member any more and the archive should stop filing her that way.** She changed weapons under contact because the crossbow was wrong for the target, reloaded a musket in the open twice, and read her spellbook while tied up with something descending on her. She also ordered a steel dog to stand on a sleeping man until he cracked. Both of those are the same person and Waluigi declines to separate them.

**Feyward Dan stood in front of Markop.** The smallest combatant put himself ahead of the largest. Waluigi has been unkind about this Toad in print for four filings and is revising it here rather than letting it quietly lapse.

**The position is worse than when they came down the rope.** The Scorncrow is dead, and the grove is surrounded, Salam is down, Markop is bleeding from the head, Remi is separated, the exit is still sealed, and the party's allies are the people who intend to arrest one of them. Killing the landlord did not clear the building.

name: The Roll Call at Trinity
title: The Roll Call at Trinity: A New Advisor, Eleven Names, and the Word Nobody Was Supposed to Explain
date: 5 Aethel, 1040 BF — morning, Classroom 2-B, Trinity General School, Kivotos (Kivotos academy clock)
era: Aethel 1040 BF — the Kivotos intake
location: Classroom 2-B, Trinity General School, Kivotos
type: Session Event / Introductions / Disclosure
status: Filed — the class is introduced, the SCHALE attachment is disclosed, the Equestrian liaison breach is admitted and under internal query, and the deployment briefing for Sectors 7 through 12 is unfinished
summary: A new advisor took Classroom 2-B at Trinity General School and ran a roll call, and the roll call turned into the archive's first look inside Kivotos. Eleven students answered to their names: the one who arrived first and claimed the front desk, the one with the chocolate, the one who quieted the room without raising her voice, the one in the corner who is classified supplementary, the one who finished page six of the pamphlet, the one who found gaps in the documentation overnight, the one in the back row with weapons clearance, the one who kept asking what words meant, the one who declared himself lord of the classroom, and the one who admitted nobody had ever explained any of this to him. Asked a direct question, the advisor confirmed the class is attached to SCHALE, spelled the acronym out, conceded it sounds stupid, and explained what it does. A follow-up question about an Equestrian liaison seen walking the school produced an admission that a diplomatic programme had been mishandled. A question about weapons produced a refusal — and the public disclosure of one student's existing clearance. No combat, no travel, no casualties. Eleven people were introduced and one institution said out loud what it wants from them.
description:
*Waluigi was not in this room and has never been to Kivotos, which has not stopped him before. What follows is assembled from the classroom record of a single morning at [Trinity General School](#/article/trinity_general_school), and Waluigi files it because of what it is: an intake. Eleven children, one advisor, and the moment an institution stopped pretending it was a school.*

*[Kivotos](#/article/kivotos) is not new to this archive. It is where [Remi Akamatsu](#/article/remi_akamatsu_full_backstory) was born — Residential District Seven, 12th Harvestide 1026 BF — it is the issuer of the credits in her field wallet, and its four-term academic year has been sitting in the archive's calendar data the whole time. What the archive has never had is an interior. Now it has one, and it is a classroom with a sliding door and a contested front row.*

*Nothing is fought here. Waluigi wants that stated plainly, because the temptation with an introductions session is to apologise for it. Do not. This is the filing where the cast gets their names, the seating chart turns out to be politics, and a man with a clipboard answers a question he could have dodged.*
imageCaption: Classroom 2-B on the morning of the new advisor's first roll call: the sliding door, the window row, the contested front desk, and the back row that behaves like a separate country.

sections.name: I. The Door Slides Open
sections.imageCaption: Ten seconds before anyone else had processed that the door had opened: both palms down on the advisor's desk, the pencil holder still rattling, the halo spinning like a top.
sections.overview:
The door slides rather than swings, and it opened with a click that the record calls satisfying. The new advisor stepped through it adjusting a pair of glasses that — the record is specific — he does not need for vision.

**"Alright everyone, settle down! I'm your new advisor — you can call me Sensei. Think of me as… the glue holding this whole operation together."**

He spun around once and pointed at nothing in particular. Then he laid out the deal: follow the rules, behave like proper students, everything goes smoothly. *We cool?*

The answers arrived in the order that tells you the room. From the window seats, a hand straight up and a grin: **"Sensei~! So does this mean you'll be around to chat during break too?"** From the front row, hair tucked behind an ear and a warm, formal welcome, with the Sisterhood Club's help offered before anyone had asked for it.

And then the door again, because [Misono Mika](#/article/misono_mika) had not finished arriving. She came through roughly ten seconds before the rest of the class had processed that anything was happening, pink hair bouncing, skidded to a halt at the advisor's desk and slammed both palms down on it hard enough to rattle the pencil holder.

**"SENSEI! I got here first! Does that mean I'm your favorite student now~?"**

Her halo spun above her head like an excited top. Behind her, other students were still filing in; Mika had already claimed the desk directly opposite his and sat down in it with a very deliberate, princess-like posture — back straight, hands folded, chin slightly elevated.

Then she offered him tea.

**"Also I brought you tea! Well… I didn't bring tea. But I *thought* about bringing tea."** A pause. **"…The thought counts."**

Somewhere in the middle of this, a newcomer turned to the person in the next seat and asked, with feeling, whether this was really the right place. The answer came back cheerful and immediate: yes, definitely, Mika-senpai does this with every new teacher, and you will get used to it after — *oh, probably never, actually.*

The advisor noticed the whispering, raised an eyebrow, and turned back to the room with a smirk.

**"Something to share? Because if you're comparing me to your last advisor who 'mysteriously disappeared,' I assure you — I'm much harder to get rid of."**

He tapped the desk twice with a knuckle. **"So! Roll call. Let's see who actually shows up on time."**
sections.waluigi_note: Waluigi wishes to flag the throwaway line, because throwaway lines are where institutions confess. *Your last advisor who mysteriously disappeared.* He said it as a joke, in air quotes, on his first morning, to eleven children who did not laugh. Nobody in the room asked a follow-up question. Waluigi is asking it: what happened to the last advisor of Classroom 2-B, and why is the replacement already making jokes about it?

sections.name: II. Eleven Names Off a Clipboard
sections.overview:
He picked up the clipboard and read, finger trailing down the page with practiced efficiency, and the roll call did what roll calls do in a first session: it introduced everybody by showing how each of them answers to their own name.

[Kurimura Airi](#/article/kurimura_airi) — present, with an enthusiastic little wave.

[Shirasu Azusa](#/article/shirasu_azusa) — silence, then a tiny voice from the corner mumbling something inaudible. *I'll take that as a yes.* Her desk is in the far corner, angled slightly away from the room, as far from everyone else as a desk can be while still being a desk. Her posture was immaculate, her hands folded, her pen aligned perfectly parallel to her notebook's edge. A breeze from a cracked window pushed a strand of hair across her face. She did not move to fix it.

[Ibaragi Yoshimi](#/article/ibaragi_yoshimi) — a sharp intake of breath from the middle row. The advisor glanced up, said nothing, marked a check and moved on. She was hunched in her seat like she was trying to physically shrink, gripping the desk edge hard enough to whiten her knuckles. *I'm here.* Her eyes scanned the room to see who was watching, landed on the advisor looking directly at her, and she flinched and looked away fast.

Somewhere in here, [Airi](#/article/kurimura_airi) held out a small wrapped chocolate with both hands. *A little something to start the day off sweetly. You looked like you needed it!* The advisor examined it with exaggerated suspicion for a full three seconds, then ate it. **"Mmh. Not bad."**

[Iochi Mari](#/article/iochi_mari) — a polite nod from the front row.

**"…Shaggy."**

Dead silence. Everyone looked around. The advisor scanned the room slowly and sighed through his nose. **"Alrighty, so we're either missing Shaggy, or he's hiding behind that sleeping kid in the back row."**

A hand rose slowly from behind a desk near the window, where [Shaggy](#/article/shaggy) had been crouched low trying to make himself invisible. He stood with his characteristic slouch, green shirt hanging off one shoulder. **"Uh… yo. Present. Like, hi."** His voice cracked on *hi*.

Then the clipboard produced a name the advisor had to squint at. **"…Lord Verity."** He looked around the classroom with genuine curiosity, found nobody obviously matching the description, and his eyes landed on the newcomer sitting right there. One eyebrow arched. **"Huh. You're Lord Verity? …Alright then."** He made a checkmark with a confident flick of the wrist and moved on.

He was wrong, and the correction was not quiet. [Lord Verity](#/article/lord_verity) stood up abruptly, chair scraping loud against the floor. Every head turned.

**"YES I AM LORD VERITY. AND I SHALL BE YOUR MASTER FROM THIS DAY FORWARD — KNEEL BEFORE ME, MORTALS!"**

A beat of stunned silence. Someone in the back coughed. Mika started giggling. Airi covered her mouth. The advisor blinked once, twice, and turned calmly back to his clipboard. **"…Right. Next."**

It still took a second prompt — *sensei what about me!* — before he found the right line and produced the name that had been missed: **"You're… Asa Hanko?"** Curious, not unkind, like tasting an unfamiliar word and deciding how it fits in the mouth.

[Kenzaki Tsurugi](#/article/kenzaki_tsurugi) did not raise her hand when called. She sat in the back with her arms crossed and her legs kicked up on the desk, dark hair falling across one eye, and let out a low chuckle. *Keheh.* Then she looked away. **"…What a pain."**

[Asagao Hanae](#/article/asagao_hanae) raised a hand slowly, fingers trembling, and gave a small shy wave. **"I-I'm here… Sensei…"** Barely above a whisper, eyes on the floor, sleeve pulled over the knuckles. **"P-Please take care of me…"**

And near the back, one more student sat without leaning toward anybody — not confused, not excited, simply watching, which in that room made them more noticeable than everyone being loud.

The newcomer's assessment of the whole procedure, filed verbatim: *a lot of students.*
sections.waluigi_note: Eleven names and eleven completely different ways of answering to one. The girl in the corner nods so faintly it barely registers. The boy behind the desk hides until the roll reaches him. One of them announces himself as a lord. One of them apologises for existing. Waluigi has covered war councils with less character in them than this register. The advisor read the list in about four minutes and every one of those four minutes is load-bearing.

sections.name: III. The Room Gets Away From Him
sections.imageCaption: Shouting had failed. She stood up, walked to the front, positioned herself slightly behind his desk, and asked. The record says they complied like dominoes falling.
sections.overview:
Between the roll call and the lesson, the classroom stopped being a classroom.

Airi got up and walked the aisle to the back with a second chocolate, weaving between desks with practiced ease, and slid into the seat next to [Shaggy](#/article/shaggy). *Here you go~ Don't let Sensei see you eating candy during his speech though, okay?* He unwrapped it, put it in his mouth, and slouched lower — as though going sideways would make him less visible.

**"Like… thanks for the chocolate, Airi. You're like, way too nice to me."** Then, leaning in at a volume the record notes was *not remotely quiet enough:* **"Uh… why's Lord Verity acting all weird again? Like, is today a cosmic alignment or something?"** His leg bounced under the desk hard enough to vibrate the furniture.

At the front, the advisor raised the clipboard like a shield.

**"ALRIGHT! SEATS! NOW!"**

The room did not obey. Chairs kept scraping. Mika had somehow ended up sitting on top of her desk rather than in her chair. He pinched the bridge of his nose, exhaled slowly through his teeth, and tried being specific instead of loud:

**"Let me make one thing perfectly clear: I don't care who you are or what club you're in. You sit down, you pay attention, and you behave like students. Not… *whatever* this is."**

His eyes swept the room — Lord Verity mid-pose, Shaggy half-swallowed by his hoodie, Azusa staring at a wall, Mika spinning on her chair for no reason anyone could identify.

From the back row, [Tsurugi](#/article/kenzaki_tsurugi) watched the whole thing with her chin tilted down and her eyes narrowed to razor slits. She pulled out her phone under the desk, thumb hovering, visibly weighing whether this was worth documenting. **"…What a circus."**

Lord Verity, meanwhile, had escalated. He slammed both fists on the desk hard enough to rattle every pencil within two feet. **"THIS CLASS WILL COME TO ATTENTION OR FACE THE WRATH OF LORD VERITY HIMSELF!"** Airi giggled. Mika kept spinning. Someone in the back row did not look up.

Then [Iochi Mari](#/article/iochi_mari) stood up.

She did not shout. She walked to the front, positioned herself slightly behind the advisor's desk, gave a small nod to the students nearest her — a silent signal — and said, in a voice the record describes as soft but carrying clearly:

**"If everyone could take their seats properly, that would be wonderful~"**

The record: *cutting through the noise more effectively than any shouting ever could. A few students glance her way and begin complying, chairs clicking into place one by one like dominoes falling.*

What finally settled Lord Verity was a last warning: sit down or be removed. His fist was still in the air. The words died on his lips. He lowered the fist slowly, and the hoodie-cape slid off one shoulder and pooled on the desk behind him *like a deflated balloon.*

**"…You can't kick ME out. I'm not even IN anything yet."**

He stood in the middle of the aisle, suddenly looking less like an emperor and more like someone who had wandered into the wrong building. **"…Fine."** Through gritted teeth, jaw tight.

The advisor watched him go back to his seat with the quiet satisfaction of a man who had just defused a bomb using nothing but volume and posture. **"Thank you for your cooperation, Lord Verity."** The sarcasm, the record notes, was *barely thin enough to pass through a colander.*
sections.waluigi_note: Note who actually restored order, because it was not the adult. The advisor shouted twice and got nothing. Mari stood up, asked nicely, and the room folded like wet paper. She has no authority in that room whatsoever. She has something better, which is that everybody likes her and nobody wants to be the one who ignored her. Waluigi has watched generals fail to do what that girl did with one sentence and a hair-tuck.

sections.name: IV. The Word He Did Not Have To Explain
sections.imageCaption: THE RESISTANCE in underlined block capitals, and a rough map of the eastern perimeter — warehouses, supply routes, and abandoned industrial buildings that make good hiding places.
sections.overview:
With the room finally seated, he leaned against the desk and started on what the class actually *is*. Students of Trinity General School. Here to learn, grow, and be prepared for whatever comes next.

**"SCHALE operations, academy life, the whole package."**

And then a voice from the floor: **"SCHALE operations?"**

The session changed shape at that line. [Lord Verity](#/article/lord_verity)'s eyes snapped to attention — *actual* attention, not the theatrical kind. The dramatic pose melted like frost in sunlight. His fingers tightened on the desk edge.

**"Wait. You're saying this class — THIS class — is connected to SCHALE? As in… actual missions? Real-world operations?"**

His voice cracked on *real-world.* The record catches what was underneath the theatrics for exactly one second: *something raw — something hungry. Something that sounds like a kid who's been waiting for exactly this his entire life.* He started to say *I thought we were just—*, stopped himself, swallowed, and put the mask back on. It no longer fit properly.

In the corner, [Azusa](#/article/shirasu_azusa)'s eyes sharpened — the record's simile is *like a blade being drawn from a sheath so smooth you'd miss it if you blinked.* The name landed in her chest and stayed there, heavy and cold. She knows what SCHALE means better than most students at Trinity, because she has felt the weight of systems that sort people into categories they did not choose, into boxes labelled *supplementary* like it is a diagnosis rather than a circumstance.

[Yoshimi](#/article/ibaragi_yoshimi) tensed, shoulders to her ears. **"…What does that have to do with ANY of us?"** — sharper than she meant it, which is saying something.

[Hanae](#/article/asagao_hanae) whispered the word to herself, held the advisor's gaze for exactly two seconds, and said **"I… I know what that is."** Then her courage ran out.

[Shaggy](#/article/shaggy) said what nobody else was willing to: **"Uh… like, yeah. What exactly IS SCHALE? Sounds like some kinda… I dunno, video game thing or whatever?"** And then the sentence that turns this filing from a briefing into an indictment:

**"Like… okay, real talk. I've been at Trinity for a while now and nobody EVER explained this stuff to me. I get that there's Knights, I get that there's the Resistance, I even get that there's some kinda war going on — but 'operations?' Like… combat operations? Because if you're telling me I gotta fight something, I need to know where the nearest exit is first."**

The advisor set the clipboard down with a deliberate click and turned to face the room fully. He held up a hand when Lord Verity opened his mouth. *Nope. I'm talking. You're listening.*

**"SCHALE isn't some secret club or a video game. It stands for Strategic Counter Hazard Activation League Execution."**

He let the acronym sit. Then came the question that got the honest answer — *sounds stupid, what does it actually do?*

**"It does sound stupid. I'll give you that."**

A few nervous laughs. He held up a finger before anyone got comfortable.

**"But here's the thing — it's not really an acronym people throw around for fun. SCHALE is the backbone of everything that keeps this city breathing. It decides which Knights respond to hazards, how resources get allocated, who gets support when things go sideways."**

[Mari](#/article/iochi_mari) translated it for the students too embarrassed to ask, opening with the line that let them off the hook — *most people don't fully understand it until they're told directly* — and laying it out in three clean sentences: the framework that keeps Kivotos stable, coordinating Knight responses and Resistance intelligence, turning strategic decisions into actual missions. *In essence… it's the difference between knowing there's a threat and actually doing something about it.*

Then the whiteboard came out, and with it the geography. Sectors 7 through 12, along Kivotos's eastern perimeter: warehouses, supply routes, a couple of abandoned industrial buildings that make great hiding spots for people who do not want to be found. The Resistance had been spotted moving supply lines through those corridors. Exact numbers unknown.

Asked what any of that meant, he wrote **THE RESISTANCE** on the board in block letters and underlined it twice.

**"They're criminals who want to tear down everything Kivotos stands for — the academies, the peace agreements, all of it."**

He turned around and looked directly at the student who had asked. **"The short version: we're going there because someone's been moving weapons through those sectors, and SCHALE is the group that stops that from happening. You — all of you — are part of that."**
sections.waluigi_note: Waluigi is going to be careful here, because this is the paragraph where an archivist earns his keep. *They're criminals who want to tear down everything Kivotos stands for* is not a finding. It is a description of an armed political faction, delivered in one sentence, to a room of children, by an employee of the body they are fighting. It may even be true. Waluigi does not know, and neither does anyone in that classroom, and that is the point: not one student in the room had the information to test it. The archive files it as the advisor's characterisation. Ask again in twenty sessions.

sections.name: V. The Ponies, the Guns, and the Thing He Should Not Have Said
sections.overview:
Two more questions landed before the briefing could resume, and both of them opened something.

The first came almost in passing — a question about external threats versus internal ones, and then: *what about the pony liaison that came from Equestrian earlier, I saw some walking around the school, was that meant to be private?*

The advisor's expression shifted. Just barely, just enough for anyone paying attention. His jaw tightened a fraction. He set the clipboard down on the desk with a deliberate click, and chose his words like stepping over a tripwire he could not see.

**"That's… a separate matter."**

Then he confirmed it: a diplomatic initiative between Kivotos and Canterlot. Small groups, cultural exchange, building goodwill before things get messy enough to need actual military coordination. *It was supposed to be handled quietly.*

He exhaled through his nose.

**"So the fact that you saw them walking around openly tells me someone dropped the ball on security protocols somewhere along the line."** His eyes swept the room. **"I'll look into it. If any of you see more of those liaisons wandering where they shouldn't be, report it to me — not to social media, not to your friends, to me. Directly."**

In the corner, Azusa's pen stopped mid-notation. Two pieces that did not fit: an organisation that runs on need-to-know, and diplomatic personnel walking a school corridor in plain view. She wrote something brief in the margin that was not part of the lecture, said **"…Understood"** to nobody in particular, straightened a page that was already perfectly aligned, and resumed writing.

[Airi](#/article/kurimura_airi) had three questions and no filter: are there snacks in Sector 7, are the ponies friendly, can she hug one, and do they get breaks. [Shaggy](#/article/shaggy) followed with the sensible objection nobody else made — *if we're dealing with bad guys AND ponies showing up uninvited, that's like… two different problems, right?*

It was correct, and the advisor said so. The Resistance is an internal threat operating out of Kivotos itself. The Equestrian liaisons are an external diplomatic situation *that someone mishandled* — his tone carrying an edge that suggested opinions about who. **"The fact that those two things intersected at this school without proper coordination is exactly why SCHALE exists."**

On the ponies, he was blunt: they are not your friends, they are diplomatic personnel operating under an agreement *that does NOT include hugging.*

Then the second question: **"We can all use guns at least right?"**

The silence lasted exactly two seconds before [Tsurugi](#/article/kenzaki_tsurugi) spoke, and she did not look at whoever had asked. She kept her eyes on the advisor. She uncrossed her arms slowly, deliberately, leaned forward, and pointed at him like a blade.

**"…Seriously? If you're about to say 'yes' to that, then this class is just an excuse for a shooting range and I'm filing paperwork."** Her expression hardened. **"I've handled weapons since before most of you were old enough to stop putting them in your mouths."**

She leaned back, arms recrossing with finality. **"Sensei. What's the actual plan?"**

Shaggy put himself on the record immediately and defensively — *I just want it on the record that I said nothing about wanting guns* — describing himself and Scooby as diplomatic solution kind of guys, and offering a bag of Scooby Snacks as his contribution to the mission.

The advisor exhaled slowly through his nose.

**"Nobody is handing out guns."**

Stone-cold finality. The room went quiet for exactly one second. And then he held up a finger to preempt an objection Tsurugi had not made and did not appear about to make.

**"—except Tsurugi. You already have clearance."** A beat. **"Everyone else: no."**

He turned back to the whiteboard and wrote **need-to-know** in block letters, underlining it twice: SCHALE tells you what you need for your assignment, and you do not ask about things outside it. Anyone whose role requires a firearm will be briefed separately, with proper safety training, by certified personnel. *Not me. Not YouTube.*
sections.waluigi_note: He disclosed a student's weapons clearance to ten of her classmates in order to win an argument he had already won. She had not volunteered it. She had, in fact, just spent her only real contribution of the session arguing AGAINST arming children — which is the most responsible position anybody takes in this entire filing, and it is taken by the girl with her boots on the furniture. The record does not show her reacting. Waluigi finds that the most informative non-reaction of the morning, and notes for the file that the man explaining need-to-know had, ninety seconds earlier, told the room something it did not need to know.

sections.name: VI. Cute Outfits, and the Question He Did Not Answer
sections.overview:
What the class did with all of this was form a committee about clothes.

It started when he said there would be no cool gadgets and no matching outfits — *at least… not yet* — and let it hang. That was a mistake. **"not yet! does that mean we get cool outfits!"**

Airi nearly knocked over a juice box getting out of her seat. **"WE'RE GETTING OUTFITS?! Oh my gosh oh my gosh—"** What colour, what style, matching or pick-your-own, and could hers have chocolate mint on it somehow.

From the back row, Tsurugi's mouth twitched upward — not quite a smile, the precursor to one. **"…Not yet, huh. How long do we have to wait? …Days? Weeks?"** Low, direct, two syllables cutting through the noise.

[Yoshimi](#/article/ibaragi_yoshimi)'s eye twitched. **"…Outfits?"** — said as though he had announced they would be dissecting cats. **"If this is about uniforms, I'm opting out. I don't do group matching. Last time the school made me wear anything I looked like a kid playing dress-up."** She looked sideways at Airi's bouncing with the expression of someone watching a person pour gasoline on themselves, and asked how much of the actual briefing Airi was hearing. Airi was not hearing a single word. Yoshimi exhaled through her nose like a frustrated bull.

The advisor tried to reclaim it. The outfits comment was a joke. *Mostly.* SCHALE is not glamorous — it is paperwork and logistics and making sure the right people are in the right places when things go wrong. **"But it IS important. The Resistance runs through this system. Every Knight deployment, every supply line, every evacuation order during a hazard event — it all flows through SCHALE."**

In the corner, Azusa delivered her verdict flat, like reporting a weather condition. **"Cute outfits. …Who cares about outfits."** A barely perceptible shrug. And then the question underneath the entire session:

**"The question is whether SCHALE actually works. Or if it's just another thing that sounds important but doesn't do anything for people who are already at the bottom of every list."**

Her gaze dropped to her desk — notebook closed, pen aligned parallel to its edge.

**"…Doesn't matter though. I'm not on any list. Supplementary students don't count for much either way."**

Nobody answered her.

The committee formed anyway, and it formed around the newcomer, who had declared a preference for cute clothes and recruited Airi on the spot. Lord Verity, whose hoodie Airi had been modelling as a ball gown without permission, rose to bless the arrangement — *BEHOLD! The Lord of Verity graces this humble girl—* — while Airi waved and mouthed THANKS with exaggerated enthusiasm, and he pivoted mid-sentence into *an alliance that shakes the very FOUNDATIONS of… SCHALE training readiness!* He pointed at the advisor, retracted, pointed again but lower, then settled for crossing his arms and nodding sagely.

Yoshimi watched it with an expression the record says could curdle milk. **"An alliance. They're forming an *alliance* over a cape."** Then, flatly: **"…I'm not joining any alliance."** And then, in the very next breath: **"But if Sensei needs someone who actually reads the handouts…"**

She pulled a crumpled SCHALE pamphlet from her bag and slapped it on the desk with more force than necessary.

**"I finished page six."**

[Hanae](#/article/asagao_hanae) raised her hand hesitantly, like asking permission to speak at a town hall. **"…I want to join the alliance too."** She introduced herself properly, said she does not do loud things, and offered logistics and scheduling — paperwork stuff. Then she held up a small notebook filled with neat handwriting and colour-coded tabs.

**"I already started organizing the SCHALE information Sensei shared. There were gaps in the documentation so I cross-referenced it with the school's emergency protocols…"**

Nobody had asked her to. It had been a matter of hours. She found gaps.

The newcomer's response to the offer of paperwork was *what no eww* and a counter-proposal to design cute outfits for the class instead — and Hanae, who by every expectation should have folded, lit up instead *like someone just turned on a lamp inside her chest cavity.* She offered to help pick colours and check uniform modifications against school regulations, trailed off when she heard herself volunteering detailed logistical support for a committee that did not exist, and went pink at the ears. **"…I'll do whatever helps!"**

Airi called her a genius and a hidden treasure, grabbed her hands and shook them gently. Hanae looked startled and did not pull away.

Then Airi turned the whole thing on the least approachable person in the room: they would make everyone look so good that even Kenzaki could not complain. Group photos. Props. Maybe balloons.

**"…You want to put BALLOONS on SCHALE tactical gear."**

**"It would LOOK SO CUTE—"**

Tsurugi stared at her for a long, uncomfortable beat. Then — so quietly the record says it almost did not exist — the corner of her mouth twitched.

**"Keheh."**

Airi screamed with joy.

And in the middle of all of it, [Mari](#/article/iochi_mari) raised her hand, though she had already been looking at him, and asked the only question that went to the point:

**"I think what everyone here is actually asking — underneath all the outfit requests and snack searches — is whether SCHALE means we'll get to DO something meaningful. People don't care about gadgets or uniforms. They care about purpose. So… will it?"**

The record does not show him answering.

He dropped into his chair with the bone-tired slump of a man who had survived a natural disaster and was now filling out paperwork about it, observed that nobody had mentioned the classroom would treat every meeting like a variety show, and set the order of business: deployment rotation first. Then fashion.

The word came out, the record says, *like he's chewing glass.*
sections.waluigi_note:
Two questions were asked in this room and neither was answered. Azusa asked whether the system does anything for people at the bottom of every list, and said, out loud, that she is not on any list. Mari asked whether any of this amounts to purpose. Eleven people and one adult heard both. The reply to the first was silence and the reply to the second was a deployment rotation.

Waluigi is going to drop the voice for a moment, because this is the part that matters and the jokes can wait. An institution that will not answer *does this do anything for me* has told you the answer. The archive will be asking both questions again, in writing, every session, until somebody in that building says something.

outcome:
No combat, no travel, no casualties, and nothing physically changed hands except two chocolates and a crumpled pamphlet. What changed is what the class knows.

Filed as settled: Classroom 2-B is attached to SCHALE operations; the acronym is Strategic Counter Hazard Activation League Execution; the body coordinates Knight deployments, resource allocation and hazard response, and runs on need-to-know. A deployment rotation covering Sectors 7 through 12 on Kivotos's eastern perimeter is in preparation, justified by reported Resistance movement of weapons and supply lines. The class will not be armed; one student already is.

Filed as admitted: an Equestrian liaison programme with Canterlot exists, was intended to be conducted quietly, and was observed by students walking the school openly. The advisor characterised this as a failure of security protocol and opened an internal query.

Filed as open: what happened to the previous advisor of Classroom 2-B, referred to in a joke as having 'mysteriously disappeared'. Whether SCHALE does anything for students classified supplementary. Whether any of this amounts to purpose — asked directly, and not answered.

The Equestrian liaison programme with Canterlot, disclosed as a mishandled security matter rather than as a diplomatic announcement
One student's weapons clearance disclosed publicly by the advisor, seconds before he explained the need-to-know principle
Two questions asked and neither answered: whether the system helps students at the bottom of every list, and whether any of it amounts to purpose
A joke about the previous advisor having 'mysteriously disappeared', which no student followed up
aftermath:
**Eleven students have names in the archive and one institution has stated its terms.** That is the whole of it, and for an intake filing it is enough.

The alliance that formed over an oversized hoodie is, on paper, an outfit-design committee: Asa Hanko proposing, Airi escalating, Hanae supplying logistics, Lord Verity blessing it, Yoshimi refusing to join while volunteering to do the reading. It has no standing and no remit. It is also the only structure in that classroom that anybody chose.

The deployment briefing did not finish. Sectors 7 through 12 are named, the Resistance is characterised, and the rotation itself is still unread when the record ends.

Three things are owed. The previous advisor of Classroom 2-B is unaccounted for and was joked about on the replacement's first morning. The Equestrian liaison breach is under an internal query with no stated deadline. And Shirasu Azusa said, in a full classroom, that supplementary students do not count for much either way, and nobody contradicted her.
waluigiAssessment:
**The session is an introduction and the disclosure is an accident.** Waluigi wants both halves of that sentence taken seriously.

The advisor came in to run a roll call and set expectations. What he actually did was answer a question a confused student asked because they did not know it was the kind of question you are supposed to already know the answer to. And once he started answering he did not stop: the acronym, the function, the sectors, the Resistance, the ponies, the clearance. A more careful man lets the first SCHALE question die in the noise. Waluigi has covered enough institutions to say that the careful man is the more common one, and to note, grudgingly, that this one is better than that.

But look at what the honesty cost. He told a room of children that the people in the eastern sectors are criminals who want to tear it all down, in one sentence, with no evidence offered and none available to them. He confirmed a diplomatic programme was being run badly by confirming that seeing it was the problem. And he named a student's weapons clearance out loud, to ten classmates, moments before writing NEED-TO-KNOW on a whiteboard and underlining it twice.

The children, meanwhile, sorted themselves faster than any institution could have. Mika took the front. Tsurugi took the back and watched only him. Azusa angled her desk toward the door. Airi crossed the room twice to reach whoever was alone. Mari stood up and stopped a riot by asking politely. Hanae went home and audited the documentation. Yoshimi read page six and waited all session for a reason to say so.

And Lord Verity, who had spent the morning demanding that mortals kneel, said *I'm not even IN anything yet*, and then heard the word SCHALE and forgot to perform.

**Waluigi's finding:** this is a good room. It is also a room where a fourteen-year-old said she is not on any list and eleven people let it pass. Waluigi has filed that in two places so it cannot be lost. WAH.

summary: Bowser and the Oracle finally have the conversation the sanctum has been circling. It is not a fight. The Oracle fishes a boot out of nothing while explaining that a shepherd tends his garden; Bowser calls the sanctum a dumb space garden and demands to know why he is in the B plot. What follows is the most information the Oracle has ever surrendered in one sitting — that both Oracles are fated to die and he intends to be the last one, that the seals break and the world does not collapse, that he warned Peach and she did not listen because she may have wanted to die — and the most self-examination Bowser has ever done in public. Bowser refuses the Astral Shore trap on king's intuition, catches the Oracle spying on Peach through a floating eyeball, and negotiates: three weeks, not a cut tether, and he will personally keep the Legion off the Feyward. Then he steps onto the circle and lands alone in a basement where nobody is watching — a bowl of blood, a lever he does not pull, five labelled honeys, a knight's statue, a satyr running a bar for the Revel, and a room full of caged Goombas being shipped abroad for weapons by the Mushroom Regency. The Toad who owns the blood is Mystic Morel, and he leaves without explaining any of it. Bowser leaves his own countrymen in the cages. The clock starts when he lands.
description:
Waluigi has assembled this from Bowser's retelling, which arrived in an unusual condition: quiet.

Bowser does not do quiet. Bowser does volume, property damage, and the specific grammar of a man who has never once considered that a sentence might be improved by revision. What he brought back from the Planar Sanctum was a conversation he lost, a deal he made anyway, and a basement he walked out of without smashing anything. Waluigi has checked this account three times because it does not sound like the subject.

It is also, by some distance, the most the [Oracle](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/the_oracle) has ever said out loud.

## The garden

Bowser opened with the obvious question — why are you in this place — and got the answer that names the whole session: *a shepherd needs to tend to his garden.*

Bowser, who has more experience with hostile gardens than he would like, said it reminded him of the galaxy, back when he took over the Mushroom Kingdom for a second. He noted the absences out loud: no stars, no Rosalina. Then, because he is Bowser, he asked whether the Oracle had any stars.

The Oracle's reply was to cast a fishing line into the sanctum and pull out a boot.

Bowser's response to this was not anger. It was professional offence. *I'm the star of the show.* The Oracle told him he was relegated to the B plot. Waluigi wishes to record that a forty-something Toad custodian told the King of the Koopas he was a subplot, to his face, while holding a boot, and survived.

## The part where nobody is fighting

The fight never came, and by the end the Oracle said so directly: *you've gotten soft. I insulted you, I barred you, I even mentioned Peach, and you didn't attack once.* He added that half of what he said he did not mean, and hoped Bowser would not take it to heart.

He had been testing. The whole conversation was a measurement, and he told Bowser it was a measurement only after he had the reading.

Bowser's answer is the line Waluigi will be thinking about for a while. He looked down and said that after what happened to Peach, he has not been the same.

The Oracle: *we all change, don't we. We just don't all reflect on our actions. Some change for the better, some for the worse.*

## What the Oracle knows about the assassination

This is the section that will be cited.

Bowser caught him spying — a snap of the fingers and a floating eyeball appeared, which the Oracle had been using to watch the Princess. Bowser's objection was proprietary rather than moral: *only I get to do that.* He then declined to be angry at a little Toad, which is its own kind of new.

Asked why he cared, the Oracle said he wanted to know what drives a person to kill someone. And then he described the scene: five or six mages' locks broken. The room untouched. She sat there with a comb in her hand, dead, unmoving, the blood staining the floor. The guards came in. They all died, and the record does not say why.

Bowser: *you know something about her death.*

The Oracle: *yes. I know a lot of things. I ponder. I am the Oracle. I warned her. She ignored me — or maybe she didn't want to listen. She knew. She wanted to die.*

Bowser rejected it on the obvious ground: she had a kingdom to take care of, someone had to do it. And the Oracle asked the question that ended that line of argument — *was it really her kingdom, or the Mushroom Kingdom?*

Waluigi is not going to pretend to be neutral about this. An unbroken room, broken locks, a comb still in her hand, and a full guard detachment dead of no stated cause is not a description of a murder. It is a description of a scene someone arranged to be read. The Oracle has been holding this for the entire operation and gave it up in a room with no witnesses, to a man he had spent the previous hour needling into stillness.

## The trap Bowser did not walk into

The Oracle offered to send Bowser directly to the Oracle — the other one — at a place called the Astral Shore, where Bowser *may kill* him. Bowser asked whether [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) would be there. The Oracle smiled and said yes, he'll be there.

Bowser did not take it. His exact objection is a better piece of analysis than most of what this archive produces:

> In what way? Like, is he *present*? You Toads are very puzzly. You hide your intentions.

The Oracle's clarification confirmed the suspicion: Hjumpik would be there in the same way that it is fate for both Oracles to die and for him to become the sole Oracle. No more orbiting. No more watching. A prophecy, not a promise, and a prophecy will happily be satisfied by a corpse.

Bowser asked what the Oracle got out of it. The answer was three things and Waluigi believes two of them: the seals break, the world does not collapse, and Bowser gets to go home away from him.

Then: *something tells me Hjumpik isn't there. Call it king intuition.* And: *you're trying to trap me and I don't like being tricked.*

He demanded the power star and no more lying.

Waluigi wants the record to show that Bowser was offered a shortcut to the thing he wants, spotted it was rigged from a single evasive verb tense, and said no. *If I was that dumb, I wouldn't be a king.*

## The deal

The Oracle wanted blood inside one week or he would manually cut the planar tether linking the Feyward to the Material sanctum. Bowser countered.

The negotiation, in order: Bowser asked for three weeks, on the grounds that these guys are slow. He argued that Hjumpik avoids fights and talks — *he loves to talk, talk, talk* — so two or three weeks is realistic and four is the failure case. He offered something better than a deadline: rather than the Oracle cutting the plane, Bowser would personally make sure it does not get too rowdy with the Iron Legion, and if he is going down he wants to go out on his own terms, not because of his companions.

He asked for one specific concession and repeated it twice: **do not cut it exactly at three weeks.** Give him a margin. *I want some insurance, Mr. Self-Reflection, if that's fine.*

The Oracle's counter-offer was three surprises waiting if Bowser makes it: one that smells like peaches, one involving arts and crafts, and one that is something Bowser wanted today.

Bowser heard *peaches* and did not get angry, and did not let himself hope. His line — *I don't know if this is a test or get hopes up* — is the most guarded sentence in his file.

There was also a live objection that the archive should not lose: Bowser asked whether they had to kill the Oracles at all, since Hjumpik had said he wanted to talk to them. That objection came from Bowser. It is on the record.

**The clock starts on teleport.** Three weeks. The Oracle started it as Bowser stepped onto the circle.

## The basement

He landed alone.

A sigil carved in the floor. A table, a bowl of blood, candles lighting the room warmly. Above him, muffled, the Revel; around him, the clear sound of dripping water. And a lever on the wall which Bowser described as *begging to be touched.*

He did not pull it. Waluigi has read this line four times and it still does not sound like the subject of this file. *My workplace. I don't have time to be wasting.*

What followed is a solo infiltration by a man with no subtlety and a functioning sense of priority. He stepped off the altar. He passed the crest of Raventree on a shield, walked over bones and candles, and thought — *I think I was there* — which is the first indication in the record that Bowser recognises this estate.

He failed to pick a lock because his hands are too big. He found cold storage and five labelled honeys. And then, from behind him, a voice with an opinion about preserves.

## The Toad in the cellar

One Toad is in this basement, and the archive should be precise about him, because he already has a record and a habit of being underestimated.

**[Mystic Morel](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/mystic_morel) — Purple T** — is the one who appears behind Bowser. Not arriving; already there, with an opinion about preserves: *I prefer jam.* Bowser asked who he was. He denied being an Oracle, introduced himself as a friend of Hjumpik, and stopped caring the moment Bowser proved not to be a newcomer.

He is also the one who owns the bowl of blood on the altar table. *Not my blood, but yeah, it's mine.* He asked whether Bowser had touched anything in that room, said he had been using it, wished him the best of luck, and left. The door slammed. Bowser took the honey.

Between them the session learned more about Bowser than about the Toad. On [Archie](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/archie_miser): a destructive force, a headache, wanted by the Mages' Guild, and *kinda crazy* — not a random magic user. The reply was indifference. On the fireballs: *it reminds me of me, back in the day.* Asked why he stopped, Bowser gave an answer he has never given in this archive before — an incident happened with a kingdom, he slowed down, he started to realise life isn't about throwing fireballs, he lost his purpose in an instant, and he is here for vengeance. The Toad said they shared that goal.

The terms were set from the other side: *as long as you don't get in my way, you're NOT an enemy.*

And on Hjumpik, Bowser said the quiet thing: he would have made a good frontliner in one of his kingdom battles. He talks too much. **Not a friend — but I like him more than the rest of my dumb group.**

Asked why he had not allied with more Koopas, Bowser said his men have to take care of his kingdom while he is gone, and that he misses his Koopas. His children.

Waluigi is going to leave that sentence sitting next to the next section without comment for exactly one paragraph.

## The cages

Bowser was called over by a goblin to help move cargo. He asked where he was and what the time was, and got the answer this filing cannot resolve: *722? Maybe like 2 AM.* The Oracle had said 922. Bowser said *722, right, okay* and moved on.

He asked which castle he was in and was corrected: it is not a castle, it is a mansion, and he is in the **Cornivours estate**. The goblin found his confusion suspicious — *are you not meant to be here?*

Bowser deflected into the job. Then the handler called him a Goomba.

*Who are you calling a Goomba? Show me the Goomba.*

The handler brought out a cage. Asked who was in it, he said: *I don't know. Food?*

The cargo is Goombas. Nine of them, in cages, stacked. Bowser asked where they came from and who sent them, and got the shape of an answer that reframes the entire operation: there was an ambush, there is a whole food chain, and **the Mushroom Regency is shipping people off to other countries for weapons.**

Bowser's reaction to a sentient-trafficking pipeline run by the Regency was to declare it could not be tolerated and that he would deal with them later. Waluigi notes that this is the King of the Koopas taking a firmer public line on Regency conduct than the Regency's own opposition has managed this year.

Then he asked whether any of them had sold information, threatened to smash one that hesitated, and left them in the cages.

His stated reason: they are meant to be his men, getting caught brings his kingdom's reputation down, and they are dumb for getting caught. He will figure out what to do with them later. He does not want them getting stopped the way Mario did.

Waluigi has been documenting Bowser for a long time and this is the single most Bowser sequence in the file. He identified an atrocity, condemned it correctly, committed to acting on it eventually, and then left the victims in the cage because letting them out would be a bad look. He misses his children. He walked past nine of his own countrymen in a shipping crate and pulled the door shut behind him.

## The satyr, and the chest that held

Past the cages: a satyr playing cards against himself, who has not been outside much and is not a fan of the Revel but keeps the drinks going up to it. Bowser asked after Hjumpik and a dwarf and got a ruckus outside and nothing more.

They played. The record shows two hands, both wins, both bet 25 — dealer busts, player holds 19, then 20.

The satyr's intelligence is better than his card play. Asked who his boss was, he ruled out the Revel with genuine disgust — *that pile of fleshy, mouldy thing? How could it even speak? It just eats and eats and eats* — and named the **Orange Heir**, who is organising an army of tree-cutters to fight the overgrowth. A green hag walked in, mocked Bowser's own question back at him in his own voice, and the door closed.

Bowser asked what was in the chests. Personal mementos, supplies, people's beds. He was handed a jug and told it could be filled on the way out, possibly to get someone drunk.

He punched the chest anyway. The chains rattled. He punched it again. The chains held.

Waluigi records this as the session's only honest defeat: a man who cracked the floor of a clockwork observatory with one punch could not open a cellar footlocker, twice.

## Standing

Bowser is in the Feyward basement with a jug, five honeys, a door knob, and three weeks. Hjumpik does not know he is coming. The party above does not know the tether has a deadline on it. The Oracle is counting.

WAH.
outcome: No blood, no fight, and the most productive conversation of the Raventree operation. The Oracle disclosed more in one sitting than in the entire prior record: that it is fated for both Oracles to die and for him to be the last, that the seals break without the world collapsing, and that he warned Princess Peach before her assassination and believes she knew and wanted to die. He described the scene — five or six mages' locks broken, the room untouched, a comb in her hand, the responding guards all dead of no stated cause. Bowser refused the Astral Shore offer on the grounds that the Oracle's promise that Hjumpik would 'be there' was a prophecy rather than a fact, caught the Oracle spying on Peach via a floating eyeball, and demanded the power star. They settled on a hard three-week deadline before the planar tether is cut, with Bowser's repeated request that it not be cut exactly on the mark, and Bowser's counter-offer to personally hold the Iron Legion off the Feyward. Three unnamed rewards were dangled: one that smells like peaches, one involving arts and crafts, one Bowser wanted today. Bowser also asked, on Hjumpik's behalf, whether the Oracles have to be killed at all. He then teleported alone into the Feyward basement of the Cornivours estate, where the clock started. There he met Mystic Morel — Purple T — who appeared behind him without being seen to arrive, claimed the bowl of blood, denied being an Oracle, named himself a friend of Hjumpik, set terms of non-hostility and left. Bowser took five labelled honeys, learned from a satyr that the Orange Heir is raising a tree-cutting army and that the Revel is not in charge, and found nine Goombas caged as freight. The handler called them food. Bowser established that the Mushroom Regency is shipping sentient people abroad in exchange for weapons, declared it intolerable, and left the Goombas in their cages because being captured embarrasses his kingdom. He did not pull the lever. He could not open the satyr's chest.
