Bowser's repeated request not to have the tether cut exactly at three weeks — he asked twice for a margin
Bowser's counter-offer: he personally keeps the Iron Legion off the Feyward instead of the Oracle cutting the plane
Three unnamed rewards promised for making the deadline: one smells like peaches, one involves arts and crafts, one is something Bowser wanted today
Bowser asks whether the Oracles have to be killed at all, on Hjumpik's behalf — the objection is on the record
'After what happened to Peach I haven't been the same' — said quietly, unprompted, to a man who had spent an hour goading him
The Oracle admits the entire conversation was a test and that half his insults were not meant
Bowser does not pull the lever in the teleport room
Five labelled honeys taken from cold storage: Warrior, Norn-Blessed, Hearth Fire, Hive Warden, Sacred Bear
Mystic Morel — Purple T — appears behind Bowser in the cold storage without being seen to arrive; the same Toad owns the bowl of blood and leaves without explaining it
'Not my blood, but yeah, it's mine' — Mystic Morel on the bowl in the teleport room
'As long as you don't get in my way, you're NOT an enemy' — the terms, stated precisely and not offered as friendship
Bowser on Hjumpik: not a friend, talks too much, would have made a good frontliner — 'I like him more than the rest of my dumb group'
Bowser's origin admission: an incident with a kingdom, a purpose lost in an instant, and vengeance as the reason he is still moving
THE CAGES: nine Goombas held as freight; the handler, asked who they are, answers 'I don't know. Food?'
The Mushroom Regency is shipping sentient people to other countries in exchange for weapons
Bowser condemns the trafficking pipeline as intolerable and leaves the Goombas in their cages anyway — being captured embarrasses his kingdom
Bowser misses his Koopas and calls them his children, in the same scene in which he abandons nine of them
The satyr rules out the Revel as his boss — 'it just eats and eats and eats' — and names the Orange Heir
The Orange Heir is organising an army of tree-cutters against the overgrowth
A green hag mocks Bowser's question back at him in his own voice
Two hands of cards, both bet 25, both wins — dealer busts against 19, then 20
Bowser punches the satyr's chest twice; the chains hold both times
THE YEAR IS DISPUTED: the Oracle says 922, the goblin says '722? maybe like 2 AM', and Bowser accepts 722 without resolving it
The estate is named on site as the Cornivours estate; the shield in the hall carries the crest of Raventree

participants.name: Bowser
participants.role: King of the Koopa Troop — negotiated the three-week clock instead of taking the one-week ultimatum — refused the Astral Shore offer on king's intuition after catching the Oracle's promise about Hjumpik as a prophecy rather than a fact — caught the Oracle spying on Peach with a floating eyeball — demanded the power star and an end to the lying — asked, on Hjumpik's behalf, whether the Oracles have to die at all — admitted he has not been the same since Peach — teleported alone into the Feyward basement — did not pull the lever — took five honeys — established that the Mushroom Regency is trafficking sentient people for weapons, declared it intolerable, and left nine caged Goombas where they were because being captured embarrasses his kingdom — failed twice to break a chained chest

participants.name: The Oracle
participants.role: Custodian of the Planar Sanctum — 'a shepherd needs to tend to his garden' — fished a boot out of the sanctum — told Bowser he is relegated to the B plot — disclosed that it is fated for both Oracles to die and for him to become the sole Oracle — offered the Astral Shore as a route to that death and was refused — revealed he warned Peach before the assassination and believes she wanted to die — described the sealed room, the broken locks, the comb, and the dead guards — admitted to spying on the Princess via a conjured eyeball — admitted the whole conversation was a test and that half his insults were not meant — set the three-week countdown on the planar tether and promised three unnamed rewards

participants.name: Mystic Morel (Purple T)
participants.role: Appeared behind Bowser in the cold storage without being seen to arrive — asked whether Bowser had come to stop him — denied being an Oracle and introduced himself as a friend of Hjumpik — lost interest once Bowser proved not to be a newcomer — indifferent to Archie Miser and the Mages' Guild's interest in him — claimed the bowl of blood in the teleport room, 'not my blood, but yeah, it's mine' — asked whether Bowser had touched anything in that room — set the terms: 'as long as you don't get in my way, you're NOT an enemy' — wished him luck and left; the door slammed behind him

participants.name: Hjumpik Deldkur
participants.role: Absent and discussed — the Oracle promised he would 'be there' at the Astral Shore in the same way it is fated for the Oracles to die, which Bowser read as a trap — Bowser relayed his stated wish to talk to the Oracles rather than kill them — assessed by Bowser as a good frontliner who talks too much, and as the only member of the group he actually likes

reputationNotes.bowser: Negotiated a planar deadline up from one week to three without conceding the kill, refused a rigged shortcut, and took a public position against the Mushroom Regency's trafficking pipeline — then left nine of his own countrymen in the cages, which the archive records alongside the position rather than behind it.
reputationNotes.the_oracle: Disclosed more than at any prior point in the operation, including the assassination scene and his own intention to become the sole Oracle, and admitted the conversation was a test.
reputationNotes._record: The Mushroom Regency is now on the record, via a goblin freight handler in another plane, as shipping sentient people abroad in exchange for weapons. The claim is uncorroborated and comes from a hostile source under no obligation to be accurate, but it is specific and it names a mechanism.

aftermath:
**Standing.** A hard three-week countdown is running on the planar tether between the Feyward and the Material sanctum; it started the moment Bowser teleported. Bowser is in the Feyward basement alone, carrying five honeys, a jug, and a door knob. Hjumpik and the Feyward party do not know the clock exists, do not know Bowser is beneath them, and are three sessions into their own operation upstairs. The Oracle is counting and has promised three unnamed rewards if the deadline holds. Nine Goombas remain caged as freight. The Orange Heir is raising a tree-cutting army. The satyr's chest is still shut.

**Unresolved.** The basement's year: the Oracle said 922, the goblin said 722, and nobody settled it. The archive files both readings rather than pick one.
waluigiAssessment:
Waluigi wants to isolate the thing that actually happened here, because the session looks like a negotiation and is in fact an audit of Bowser conducted by a Toad with a fishing rod.

The Oracle insulted him, barred him, dangled a shortcut, and named Peach — the one subject that has reliably produced property damage for eighty-five years. Bowser did not swing. At the end the Oracle said so out loud, which means the entire exchange was instrumentation and the reading was taken before Bowser knew he was being read. He was measured, and he passed a test whose passing condition was restraint.

And Bowser knew he was being handled and made the deal anyway, because the deal was better than the ultimatum. One week became three. A cut tether became a margin he asked for twice. That is not a man being outplayed. That is a man who understands he is the weaker party at the table and is negotiating competently from there.

Then there is the assassination. Waluigi has been building this file for a long time and has never had a witness say *I warned her.* An untouched room behind five or six broken mages' locks, a comb still in her hand, and every responding guard dead with no cause recorded. That is not a killing. That is a composition. Someone wanted the room to be read a particular way, and the Oracle — who watches, who ponders, who admits to a floating eyeball over the Princess — is now the closest thing this archive has to a source who was paying attention at the time.

Waluigi does not believe the Oracle is telling the truth. Waluigi believes he is telling *a* truth, selected, on purpose, to a man he had just finished measuring.

And then the cages.

Waluigi is not going to be delicate about this section. In the same hour, Bowser said he misses his Koopas and called them his children; identified a Regency pipeline shipping sentient people abroad for weapons; correctly called it intolerable; and walked away from nine of them in a crate because being captured makes his kingdom look bad. All four of those are true at once. That is the character. Not a hypocrite discovering himself — a man whose loyalty runs exactly as deep as his reputation requires and stops precisely there.

He did not pull the lever. He could not open the chest. He left his countrymen in the cages, and he has three weeks.

WAH.

imageCaption: The Planar Sanctum, mid-negotiation. Bowser with both arms out demanding to know why he is in a dumb space garden; the Oracle seated on a floating slab with a fishing rod, having just pulled a sodden boot out of the void. The size difference is the whole conversation: the small calm one set the terms.

sections.name: The Garden and the Boot
sections.subtitle: a shepherd tends his garden, and the star of the show is informed he is a subplot
sections.overview:
Bowser asked the obvious question and got the answer that names the session: *a shepherd needs to tend to his garden.*

He said it reminded him of the galaxy, back when he took over the Mushroom Kingdom for a second, and noted the absences out loud — no stars, no Rosalina. Then he asked whether the Oracle had any stars.

The Oracle cast a fishing line into the sanctum and pulled out a boot.

Bowser's response was not anger. It was professional offence: *I'm the star of the show.* The Oracle told him he was relegated to the B plot.
sections.waluigi_note: *WAH.* A forty-something Toad custodian told the King of the Koopas he was a subplot, to his face, while holding a wet boot, and is still alive. Waluigi has seen people lose limbs for less and wants that on the record.
sections.imageCaption: The negotiation, accurately staged. Bowser with both arms out demanding to know why he is in a dumb space garden; the Oracle seated on a floating slab with a rod, having just landed a boot. The size difference is the whole conversation — the small calm one set the terms.

sections.name: The Test Nobody Told Him About
sections.subtitle: an hour of deliberate provocation, and the one time Bowser did not swing
sections.overview:
The fight never came, and at the end the Oracle said why: *you've gotten soft. I insulted you, I barred you, I even mentioned Peach, and you didn't attack once.* He added that half of what he said he did not mean.

He had been measuring. The entire exchange was instrumentation, and Bowser was told only after the reading was taken.

Bowser's answer is the quietest line in his file. He looked down and said that after what happened to Peach, he has not been the same.

The Oracle: *we all change, don't we. We just don't all reflect on our actions. Some change for the better, some for the worse.*
sections.waluigi_note: *WAH.* Waluigi has documented this subject through four dimensional crises and has never once seen him absorb the name Peach without breaking something. He absorbed it here, from a man who said it on purpose to see what would happen.

sections.name: What the Oracle Knows About the Assassination
sections.subtitle: five or six broken locks, an untouched room, and a comb still in her hand
sections.overview:
Bowser caught him spying. A snap of the fingers and a floating eyeball appeared — the Oracle had been watching the Princess with it. Bowser's objection was proprietary rather than moral: *only I get to do that.*

Asked why he cared, the Oracle said he wanted to know what drives a person to kill someone. Then he described the scene.

Five or six mages' locks broken. The room untouched. She sat there with a comb in her hand, dead, unmoving, the blood staining the floor. The guards came in. They all died, and the record does not say why.

> *Yes. I know a lot of things. I ponder. I am the Oracle. I warned her. She ignored me — or maybe she didn't want to listen. She knew. She wanted to die.*

Bowser rejected it: she had a kingdom to take care of, someone had to do it. The Oracle ended that line with a question — *was it really her kingdom, or the Mushroom Kingdom?*
sections.waluigi_note: *WAH.* Waluigi is not neutral here. Broken locks, an unbroken room, a comb still in her hand and a full guard detachment dead of no stated cause is not a description of a murder. It is a description of a scene arranged to be read. And the only witness willing to discuss it is a man who admits to keeping an eyeball over her.

sections.name: The Astral Shore, Declined
sections.subtitle: a shortcut to the thing he wants, refused over one evasive verb
sections.overview:
The Oracle offered to send Bowser straight to the other Oracle, at a place called the Astral Shore, where he *may kill* him. Bowser asked whether Hjumpik would be there. The Oracle smiled: yes, he'll be there.

Bowser did not take it.

> In what way? Like, is he *present*? You Toads are very puzzly. You hide your intentions.

The clarification confirmed it: Hjumpik would be there in the same way that it is fate for both Oracles to die and for this one to become the sole Oracle. No more orbiting. No more watching. A prophecy, not a promise — and a prophecy is satisfied just as well by a corpse.

Asked what he got out of it, the Oracle named three things: the seals break, the world does not collapse, and Bowser gets to go home away from him.

> Something tells me Hjumpik isn't there. Call it king intuition.

He demanded the power star and an end to the lying. *If I was that dumb, I wouldn't be a king.*
sections.waluigi_note: *WAH.* Waluigi wants this filed prominently, because the archive has spent years describing this man as a blunt instrument. He was handed the shortest route to his own objective, detected the trap in a verb tense, and walked away from it.

sections.name: Three Weeks
sections.subtitle: the clock starts on teleport, and he asked twice for a margin
sections.overview:
The Oracle wanted blood inside one week, or he would manually cut the planar tether joining the Feyward to the Material sanctum. Bowser countered.

He asked for three weeks, on the grounds that these guys are slow. He argued Hjumpik avoids fights and talks — *he loves to talk, talk, talk* — so two or three weeks is realistic and four is the failure case. Then he offered something better than a deadline: instead of the Oracle cutting the plane, Bowser personally keeps the Iron Legion off the Feyward, and if he goes down he goes out on his own terms rather than through his companions.

He asked for one concession, twice: **do not cut it exactly at three weeks.** Give him a margin.

The counter-offer was three surprises if he makes it — one that smells like peaches, one involving arts and crafts, and one that is something Bowser wanted today.

He heard *peaches* and did not get angry, and did not let himself hope: *I don't know if this is a test or get hopes up.*

One more thing belongs in the record. Bowser asked whether they have to kill the Oracles at all, since Hjumpik had said he wanted to talk to them. **That objection came from Bowser.**
sections.waluigi_note: *WAH.* One week became three. A severed plane became a margin he had to ask for twice. That is not a man being outplayed — that is a man who knows he is the weaker party and negotiates properly from there. The clock starts on the teleport, not on the handshake.

sections.name: The Basement Nobody Was Watching
sections.subtitle: a bowl of blood, a lever, and the honey
sections.overview:
He landed alone. A sigil carved in the floor, a table, a bowl of blood, candles lighting the room warmly. Above him the muffled Revel; around him the clear sound of dripping water. And a lever on the wall which Bowser described as *begging to be touched.*

He did not pull it. *My workplace. I don't have time to be wasting.*

He stepped off the altar, passed the crest of Raventree on a shield, walked over bones and candles, and thought — *I think I was there* — the first sign in the record that he recognises this estate. He failed to pick a lock because his hands are too big. He found cold storage and five labelled honeys: Warrior, Norn-Blessed, Hearth Fire, Hive Warden, Sacred Bear.

Then, from behind him, a voice with an opinion about preserves.
sections.waluigi_note: *WAH.* Waluigi has read the lever sentence four times. A wall lever, unlabelled, in a room he had just been deposited in by a man he does not trust, and he left it alone. Growth is a horrible thing to witness.

sections.name: The Toad Who Was Already Behind Him
sections.subtitle: Purple T claims the blood, denies being an Oracle, and answers nothing
sections.overview:
There is one Toad in this basement, and he is already behind you.

**Mystic Morel — Purple T** — spoke from behind Bowser while Bowser was inspecting the cold storage. His opening contribution was a correction about preserves: *I prefer jam.* Bowser asked who he was. He denied being an Oracle, introduced himself as a friend of Hjumpik, and lost interest the moment Bowser proved not to be a newcomer — *oh, thought you were a newcomer. What are you doing down here, come to stop me?*

He is also the one who owns the bowl of blood on the altar table. *Not my blood, but yeah, it's mine.* He asked whether Bowser had touched anything in that room, was told no, said he had been using it, wished him the best of luck and left. The door slammed. Bowser took the honey.

Between the two of them the session learned far more about Bowser than about the Toad. On Archie: a destructive force, a headache, wanted by the Mages' Guild, *kinda crazy* — not a random magic user. The reply was indifference. On the fireballs: *it reminds me of me, back in the day.* Asked why he stopped, Bowser gave an answer he has never given in this archive before — an incident with a kingdom, he slowed, he started to realise life isn't about throwing fireballs, he lost his purpose in an instant, and he is here for vengeance. The Toad recognised a shared goal and said so.

Then the terms, from his side: *as long as you don't get in my way, you're NOT an enemy.*

And on Hjumpik, Bowser said the quiet thing: he would have made a good frontliner in one of his kingdom battles. He talks too much. **Not a friend — but I like him more than the rest of my dumb group.**
sections.waluigi_note: *WAH.* Note the precision of the Toad's sentence. Not 'you are a friend.' Not even 'we are allies.' A conditional absence of hostility, with the condition stated first. Waluigi has read contracts with more warmth. And note what he never answered: what the blood is for, what he was using the room for, or why a fortune teller who robs people is standing in the Feyward with a bowl of it.

sections.name: The Cages
sections.subtitle: nine Goombas, a weapons trade, and the door he pulled shut behind him
sections.overview:
A goblin called him over to move cargo. He asked where he was and what the time was, and got the answer this filing cannot resolve: *722? Maybe like 2 AM.* The Oracle had said 922. Bowser said *722, right, okay* and moved on.

He asked which castle he was in and was corrected: not a castle, a mansion — the **Cornivours estate**. The goblin found his confusion suspicious.

Then the handler called him a Goomba. *Who are you calling a Goomba? Show me the Goomba.*

The handler brought out a cage. Asked who was inside, he said: *I don't know. Food?*

The cargo is Goombas. Nine of them, stacked. Bowser asked where they came from and who sent them, and got the shape of an answer that reframes the whole operation: there was an ambush, there is a whole food chain, and **the Mushroom Regency is shipping people off to other countries for weapons.**

Bowser declared it could not be tolerated and that he would deal with them later. He asked whether any of them had sold information, threatened to smash one that hesitated — and left them in the cages.

His reasons: they are meant to be his men, getting caught brings his kingdom's reputation down, they are dumb for getting caught, and he does not want them getting stopped the way Mario did.
sections.waluigi_note: *WAH.* In the same hour he said he misses his Koopas and called them his children. Then he identified a Regency pipeline trading sentient people for weapons, called it correctly, and walked past nine of his own countrymen in a crate because letting them out would look bad. All of that is true at once. That is not a hypocrite discovering himself — that is a man whose loyalty runs exactly as deep as his reputation requires and stops precisely there.
sections.imageCaption: The last look. Nine Goombas held as freight in a Feyward cellar, and the King of the Koopas leaving — head turned back over his shoulder, jaw set, already walking. He called the trade intolerable on his way out.

sections.name: The Satyr, and the Chest That Held
sections.subtitle: cards, the Orange Heir, and the session's only honest defeat
sections.overview:
Past the cages: a satyr playing cards against himself, who does not go out much and is not a fan of the Revel but keeps the drinks going up to it. Bowser asked after Hjumpik and a dwarf, and got a ruckus outside and nothing more.

They played two hands, both bet 25, both wins — dealer busts against 19, then 20.

The satyr's intelligence is better than his card play. Asked who his boss was, he ruled out the Revel with real disgust — *that pile of fleshy, mouldy thing? How could it even speak? It just eats and eats and eats* — and named the **Orange Heir**, who is organising an army of tree-cutters against the overgrowth. A green hag walked in, mocked Bowser's own question back at him in his own voice, and the door closed.

The chests hold personal mementos, supplies, people's beds. Bowser was handed a jug and told it could be filled on the way out, possibly to get someone drunk.

He punched the chest anyway. The chains rattled. He punched it again. The chains held.
sections.waluigi_note: *WAH.* A man who cracked the floor of a clockwork observatory with one punch could not open a cellar footlocker in two. Waluigi is choosing to find this funny because the alternative is thinking about the cages again.

name: The Snowdin Bone-Line Registry
title: The Snowdin Bone-Line Registry: The Interview That Twenty-Eight Records Were Already Citing
date: Harvestide 30, 1045 BF — the day after High Command disabled the Mount Ebott logger; the interview itself runs roughly forty minutes inside the Gamma Agent's one monitored hour
era: The Old World Crisis — Mount Ebott Survey Arc / Monster Underground Contact / Post-Logger Custody Dispute
location: Snowdin Town — Sans's room, reached down a monitored Iron Legion line from the Gamma Agent's quarters
type: Interview / Archival Verification / Contested Record
status: Filed — the registry is now a document; whether it is a true one is a separate question
summary: Twenty-eight filed dossiers list their subject as 'recorded in the Snowdin household registry.' The registry itself had never been written. Waluigi spent the Gamma Agent's monitored monthly hour getting it on the record from the one witness who would not perform for him, and what he got was an interview in which the witness denied almost everything. Sans rejected the family tree name by name — Gee Lady, Cursive, the Boneless branch, Grabache Brother, Hellvitica — and then, confronted with footage of himself saying 'dirty brother' and 'has a very special attack', conceded the words were his and the context was not. Times New Roman arrived mid-call claiming brotherhood by archival lineage code, produced a sibling-designation document with citations, and had Sans sign a blank box. The contract burned with blue fire. Every name on it then walked into the room. Wing Gaster's shadow resolved at the back of it. And then the whole set vanished, leaving Sans alone in a room full of socks with Papyrus shouting down the hall about the ceiling fan. Waluigi holds a recording of all of it and cannot say what he recorded.
description:
Waluigi is going to open this filing with the administrative problem, because the administrative problem is the reason the filing exists.

**Twenty-eight records in this archive describe their subject as 'recorded in the Snowdin household registry.'** Papyrus. [Grandpa Semi](#/article/grandpa_semi). [Lazybones](#/article/lazybones). [Baby Bones](#/article/baby_bones). [Cursive](#/article/cursive). [Times New Roman](#/article/times_new_roman). [Gee Lady](#/article/gee_lady). [Pet Rock](#/article/pet_rock). Twenty-eight of them, each pointing at a registry as the thing that establishes them.

**The registry did not exist.** Not lost, not sealed, not restricted — never written. Twenty-eight citations to a document with no document under it. That is the single largest structural hole in this archive and Waluigi has been walking past it for a year.
outcome: The registry that twenty-eight dossiers cite as their authority is now a filed record — obtained during the Gamma Agent's monitored monthly hour, a privilege the Iron Legion granted the day before without specifying who could be called. Sans rejected the family tree name by name, confirmed only Pet Rock and Wing Gaster, and correctly identified that two of the listed relatives — Dirty Brother and Has A Very Special Attack — correspond to sentences he once said about Papyrus and had cut out of context. Times New Roman asserted brotherhood by archival lineage code #TNR-01, produced a footnoted sibling-designation document listing Gee Lady as a designated family member confirmed by lipstick signature analysis, and obtained Sans's signature in a blank box. The contract burned with silent blue fire; the names on it then manifested in the room, culminating in Wing Gaster stepping forward and unfurling a wing. The manifestation then ceased entirely, leaving Sans alone with the laundry and an approaching argument about socks. The archive holds the recording. The archive cannot say what the recording is of.
notableFeatures: TWENTY-EIGHT filed dossiers cite the Snowdin household registry as their authority; until this filing the registry had never been written
Obtained through the Gamma Agent's one-hour monthly monitored call privilege — granted by the Iron Legion the previous day, with no restriction on who could be called
Filed one day after High Command disabled the Mount Ebott logger: the Legion establishes what may be recorded, then its own reward scheme hands the archive forty unsupervised minutes
The witness REJECTED the document — Sans denied the family tree name by name rather than cooperating with it
Gee Lady is not Sans's mother; Sans names Toriel and has never met a G-shaped skeleton
Sans dismissed the 'Boneless' branch as absurd on the grounds that the family is made of bones
Only two entries confirmed outright: Pet Rock (he carries it) and Wing Gaster (at which point he stopped joking and checked the room)
'My brother has a very special attack' — confirmed as Sans's own line about Papyrus; the archive holds a dossier for Has A Very Special Attack
'If you cheat, you'll end up a dirty brother' — confirmed as Sans's own warning to Papyrus; the archive holds a dossier for Dirty Brother, who repairs chimneys and is covered in soot
Footage shown to Sans cut him off mid-sentence at 'my brother will—', which is what fabricated context looks like and also what a hard edit looks like
Times New Roman asserted brotherhood as 'designation: brother, confirmed by archival lineage code #TNR-01' — kinship by reference number, with no warmth offered
The Official Archival Record of Sibling Designation carries footnotes and an appendix reference for skeletal alignment
Gee Lady listed as a designated family member 'confirmed via lipstick signature analysis and emotional resonance frequency matching'
The document included duplicate entries, question-marked titles, and an unverified branch pending DNA
Wingding Gaster appeared alone at the foot of the document, underlined twice in red, with no title and no question mark
Sans signed the blank box in plain letters with no flourish — the archive notes he did not treat it as a joke
THE CONTRACT BURNED — silent blue heatless fire, names curling to ash, smoke shaped like small bones
Times New Roman watched the burn without reacting, in the manner of someone observing an expected step
Every name on the burned document then manifested in the room, Gee Lady opening a gold light to admit the rest
Wing Gaster's shadow — indistinct in every previous frame — resolved, stepped forward, and unfurled a single wing
Wing Gaster's own dossier describes the family's caution 'around impossible doors'; a door opened and he came through it
The entire manifestation then ceased without fading, leaving Sans alone in a room of scattered socks
Papyrus arrived immediately afterwards, angry exclusively about socks in the ceiling fan, having noticed nothing
Sans's closing assessment, to nobody: the family tree stuff had felt real
Sans volunteered unprompted that his parents are 'not around anymore' and that Toriel raised him 'after everything happened with dad'
Shown a second spelling — Bonefull, double L — Sans conceded it was 'actually not terrible' and almost majestic, the only thing on the document he liked
'Lazy Bones' circled in red: conceded immediately, with naps under laundry, skipped guard shifts, and falling asleep mid-sentence talking to Toriel about taxes
Pet Rock is 'little buddy' — Toriel used to water it like a plant and Asgore once tried to use magic on it; Sans did not know it was filed beside Gaster
WING DINGS appeared on screen with soft chimes — Sans: 'that's not a special effect you can just add with editing software'
The power cut and a distorted voice said 'dark... darker... yet darker...' — not through the speakers, by Sans's account
Two silhouettes on screen: Sans clear, the second blurred with a possible hunch or wings, which Sans called 'an echo from before time started'
THE REWIND: replayed with the lights on, the blurred figure was gone and Gee Lady stood in its place, hands over Sans — same footage, different occupant, and nobody explained it
A robed half-shadowed figure with no name card, which Sans read as 'quiet powerful' and as someone who had actually existed once
A floating eyeball with Sans posed beside it grinning — a portrait he has no memory of sitting for; the archive files Prunsel as a colossal eye-shaped relative
Title card: 'EXACTLY WHEN SANS'S PUNS BECAME A HOUSEHOLD HAZARD', attributed to Waluigi, alleging he reads the section when nobody is watching
Archive log entry #472 — 'sans uses pun in public for the 10,001st time'
Asked whether it was a brotherly reunion, Times New Roman answered 'affirmative' and offered nothing further
Sans's own summary of the method: 'you took pieces of truth and built an entire fake world around them'
Papyrus's closing count: seven socks in places they do not belong, delivered in disciplinary calm

participants.name: Sans
participants.role: Interview subject and hostile witness to his own family record — rejected the tree name by name, denied Gee Lady as his mother in favour of Toriel, dismissed the Boneless branch as absurd, confirmed only Pet Rock and Wing Gaster — identified that 'dirty brother' and 'has a very special attack' were his own remarks about Papyrus cut from context — signed the sibling-designation document in plain letters without joking — watched the contract burn and the family walk out of the ash — was alone in a room of socks thirty seconds later and said it had felt real

participants.name: Times New Roman

reputationNotes.waluigi: Used a Legion-authorised communication privilege for archival work the Legion did not sanction and would not have sanctioned, one day after High Command demonstrated its willingness to switch a recorder off mid-sentence.
reputationNotes.sans: Spoke at length to an outside archivist about Underground family matters on a monitored line, one day after swearing an oath of silence regarding the Mount Ebott extraction. Waluigi notes he disclosed nothing about the extraction and everything about his socks.
reputationNotes._record: The registry is now filed, but the filing does not resolve what it is. The document was rejected by its own subject, asserted by reference number, destroyed by fire, and then apparently proven correct by every name on it walking into the room — after which nothing remained. The archive holds a recording and no conclusion.

aftermath:
**Standing.** Twenty-eight dossiers now cite a registry that has a filed record behind it. The record is a contested interview rather than a genealogy, which is the honest outcome and not a tidy one.

**Open.** Nobody has explained what the burn was for, why a document needed a signature before it could produce the people it described, or how Times New Roman holds a lineage code that predates any mother Sans can name. Papyrus has not been interviewed. Papyrus is the subject of both verified quotations and has never been asked about either.

**Unresolved by design.** Whether Sans experienced an event, a recruitment, or a very long nap.
waluigiAssessment:
Waluigi is going to be honest about the three possibilities, rank them, and then refuse to pick, because picking would be the dishonest part.

**One: it was a dream.** Sans was asleep under laundry when the call began and alone with socks when it ended, and the whole thing has the internal logic of a nap — bureaucracy turning into ceremony turning into family turning into nothing. In favour: the ending. Nothing real stops that cleanly. Against: **Waluigi has the recording, and Waluigi was awake.**

**Two: it was a fabrication that worked.** Somebody assembled a genealogy out of cut footage and overheard sentences, and Sans caught it in real time — he identified the hard cut at 'my brother will—' unprompted. In favour: two of the relatives are demonstrably Sans's own words with people built around them. Against: a fabrication does not typically ignite, and the fabricated relatives do not typically walk in.

**Three: the registry is a mechanism, not a record.** A document that requires a signature, consumes itself, and then produces its contents is not describing a family. It is constituting one. Under this reading Dirty Brother exists *because* Sans once said the words, and Has A Very Special Attack exists *because* Sans once described Papyrus that way — the archive is not documenting the Bone-Line, the archive **is** the Bone-Line, and Times New Roman is not its historian but its author.

Waluigi finds the third reading the most frightening and the best supported, and would like to state plainly that wanting a reading to be false is not evidence.

Because here is the part Waluigi keeps returning to. Times New Roman logs Sans's puns. Entry #472. He claims no permission is required because it is 'an archival initiative.' Waluigi has said almost exactly that sentence, in almost exactly that tone, to people who asked why they were in this encyclopedia.

Waluigi documents a household and calls it completeness. Times New Roman documents a household and the household **appears**. Waluigi does not know whether the difference is one of kind or merely of degree, and Waluigi has elected not to run the experiment.

One last thing for the record. Twenty-eight people are filed as members of this family. Twenty-seven of those entries were written without anyone asking Sans, who is listed on every version of the tree and agreed to none of it. The one member who has consistently refused the paperwork is the one member every piece of paperwork depends on.

Papyrus, meanwhile, was down the hall the entire time, and the only thing he wanted to know was why there were socks in the ceiling fan. Waluigi envies him enormously. **WAH.**

imageCaption: The signature. Sans at the table in a room he has not tidied, writing his name in plain letters at the foot of a document that keeps unrolling; Times New Roman standing over him with the clipboard, waiting. On the back wall, the shadow that was indistinct in every earlier frame has begun to resolve, and it has a wing.

sections.name: I. How Waluigi Got the Call
sections.overview:
Through a channel the Iron Legion built and then forgot to think about.

At the close of [the Mount Ebott Survey](#/article/mount_ebott_survey_final_log), the Gamma Agent converted a full intelligence haul into the only reward he wanted: **one Legion-issued secure device, one hour per month, external calls permitted, monitored by the duty officer, revocable on conduct.** The authorization slip is painfully precise because the Legion is precise about permissions and careless about consequences.

Nobody wrote down who the Agent was allowed to call.

So on Harvestide 30, the day after High Command reached over and switched off a logger mid-briefing, the monitored hour was spent on a skeleton in Snowdin, and Waluigi was on the line. Waluigi notes the symmetry without enjoying it: the Legion spent Day 6 establishing that it decides what may be recorded, and on Day 7 its own reward scheme handed the archive forty minutes of unsupervised Underground testimony. A duty officer logged the call. Waluigi doubts the duty officer understood one word of it.
sections.waluigi_note: Through an unmonitored Legion frequency during an authorized audit window. The Gamma Agent knew who kept the filing cabinets in working order.

sections.name: II. The Interview, and the Witness Who Would Not Cooperate
sections.overview:
Sans took the call the way Sans takes everything. He had been asleep under laundry. He thanked Waluigi for coming on short notice and then apologised for his own punctuality by blaming Papyrus for having standards.

Then Waluigi put the family tree in front of him, and Sans started saying no.

This is the part Waluigi wants understood before anything else: **the witness rejected the document.** Not cagily, not evasively — flatly, and name by name, over roughly twenty minutes of the monitored hour.

**On his parents.** Asked about family, he answered plainly and without being prompted: Papyrus is his brother, and *mom and dad are not around anymore.* Told that [Gee Lady](#/article/gee_lady) was his mother, he rejected it outright — his mother was [Toriel](#/article/toriel), a goat, who baked and *raised me after everything happened with dad.* Waluigi did not press on the word *everything* and has regretted it since.

**On the names, in order.** [Garbage Brother](#/article/garbage_brother) — nothing. [Will](#/article/will) — nothing, unless you meant Papyrus's willpower. [Quantity](#/article/quantity) — nothing. [Pretty Soon](#/article/pretty_soon) — nothing. [Cursive](#/article/cursive) is handwriting; Papyrus once wrote him a puzzle clue in it and he squinted for ten minutes. [Helvetica](#/article/helvetica) sounded to him like an ancient curse or an expired ketchup brand. [Baby Bones](#/article/baby_bones) he took to mean Papyrus as a child, because there were no other baby skeletons. [Grandpa Semi](#/article/grandpa_semi) — never met him; no skeleton grandparents on record.

**On the impossible branch.** Shown a *Boneless* family, Sans stopped and pointed out the obvious: they are skeletons, that is the entire thing they are. Shown a second spelling — **Bonefull**, with the double L — he paused, allowed that it was *actually not terrible*, called it almost majestic, and then said it was still invented.

Waluigi records that concession because it is the only moment in the interview where Sans liked something on the document.

**On the two he confirmed.** A name circled in red turned out to be *Lazy Bones*, and he conceded it immediately and with visible reluctance — *that's me, pal* — volunteering that he naps under laundry, skips guard shifts, and once fell asleep mid-sentence while talking to Toriel about taxes.

Then Waluigi dusted off a name filed next to Gaster in the archive: a **pet rock**. Sans went completely still. *Little buddy.* [Pet Rock](#/article/pet_rock) is his — a boulder he has had for as long as he can account for, which Papyrus finds strange, which Toriel used to water like a plant, and which [Asgore](#/article/asgore) once tried to use magic on. His only question was how his own pet rock came to be filed beside the most dangerous name in the Underground without anybody telling him.

**On [Prunsel](#/article/prunsel) and Gaster.** Waluigi read out Prunsel the giant eyeball, then Wing Gaster, then Wingding Gaster. The register of the conversation changed on the spot. Sans stopped joking, looked around the room as though somebody might be listening, and said that is not a name you throw around casually. He tied it to *W.G.* and to Asgore and to something older than himself, Papyrus, or Snowdin. He added that Papyrus will not discuss it either: some things are better left buried with time and silence.

Told the archive had connected Gaster to old paperwork, Sans lowered his voice without appearing to notice he was doing it and called that paperwork **forbidden** — sealed-in-a-vault old, belonging to a man who *was not supposed to be remembered.* He then delivered the assessment Waluigi has had framed: this is either the dumbest or the bravest research project he has ever seen.

Waluigi has conducted a great many interviews with people eager to be in the archive. This was the first with somebody actively trying to get out of it.
sections.waluigi_note: Sans asleep under two loads of mismatched laundry, apologizing for his punctuality while dodging every single concrete genealogical query.

sections.name: III. The Footage, and the Two Words That Were His
sections.overview:
Waluigi played tape. This is where the file turns, and it turns twice.

**Clip one.** Sans, on record: *'my brother has a very special attack.'* He confirmed it instantly — Papyrus does, it is the bone rush, he trains for it. No hesitation at all.

**Clip two.** Sans warning Papyrus off a shortcut during puzzle practice: *'if you cheat, you'll end up a dirty brother.'* Also his. Also, he insisted, a joke — sibling banter about not taking the easy path, not the name of a person.

And the archive holds a dossier for [Has A Very Special Attack](#/article/has_a_very_special_attack), a purple-clad cousin who announces every entrance like the last act of an opera. And a dossier for [Dirty Brother](#/article/dirty_brother), a soot-covered relation who repairs boiler shafts, chimneys and old puzzle mechanisms.

**Two of Sans's own sentences have people filed under them.**

**Clip three** is the one that gave him his theory. Footage of Sans mid-sentence — *'my brother will—'* — cut hard, before the verb. Sans's reaction was immediate and, Waluigi concedes, correct in method: somebody has been taking things he said about Papyrus, cutting them out of their sentences, and building relatives around the fragments. He guessed the ending himself — *eat his spaghetti*, or *solve another puzzle* — and called the edit sneaky.

**Clip four** he rejected wholesale. Footage of Sans apparently talking to Toriel, except the figure on screen was Gee Lady, and Sans was saying *'you really know how to tell jokes'* with the ease of someone addressing a relative. He has no memory of the exchange and stated flatly that Toriel would have scolded him for introducing a strange magical skeleton as an aunt without asking.

Asked to summarise, Sans gave the cleanest account of the method anyone has managed: *you took pieces of truth and built an entire fake world around them.* Clever, he allowed. Realistic, no.

Waluigi notes the other reading and will not choose between them: a family whose members are *named for the circumstances in which they are first spoken about* would produce exactly this evidence too. Dirty Brother repairs chimneys. Soot is not a slander. It is a job description.
sections.waluigi_note: Sans confirming his brother's special attack on video playback, then flatly refusing to authenticate the signatures on the household rolls.

sections.name: IV. Dark, Darker, Yet Darker
sections.overview:
Then the screen cut out, and the file stops being about editing.

**Wing dings appeared on the screen** — small winged glyphs, soft chimes under them. Sans tensed immediately. Those symbols are tied to [Wing Gaster](#/article/wing_gaster) specifically; by his account they surface when the name is spoken, when somebody remembers him, or when something of his legacy activates. His verdict was the first time in the call he gave ground on the whole exercise: **that is not an effect you add with editing software** — and if the dings are real, the video may not be fake after all.

Then the power cut. Not a flicker; the room went fully dark, and the screen went to a black that Sans described as wrong rather than off. A distorted voice arrived — not from the speakers, he was clear about that, but from the walls or from inside the head:

> **dark... darker... yet darker...**

Sans did not move. He said the phrase and its rhythm are how *he* talks when things go bad down there, and repeated something Papyrus once told him: when everything gets too quiet and too dark at once, something old is waking up.

**The two silhouettes.** The screen resolved into two figures. One unmistakably Sans — lanky, slumped, hood up. The other blurred: no features, only shape, possibly a hunch, possibly wings, possibly static pretending to be a form. Sans said his bones were telling him it was wrong, and that the second figure felt familiar *like an echo from before time started.*

**The rewind is the part Waluigi cannot explain.** The lights came back. Asked whether he remembered standing there, Sans dropped the jokes entirely and said yes — clear as day, realer than most memories he has.

Then the same footage was replayed with the lights on and no fog, and **the blurred figure was gone.** In its place stood [Gee Lady](#/article/gee_lady), hands over Sans, the whole scene brighter. Same footage. Different occupant. Sans's question — why did the video change between viewings — is the single best question asked by anybody in this filing, and nobody answered it.

**The gallery continued.** [Cursive](#/article/cursive) in a tuxedo with a cane marked C, which Sans found oddly classy for a world of spaghetti and laundry. Then a robed figure, half-shadowed under bright light, with no name card and no title — Sans read that one as different from the rest: not flashy, *quiet powerful*, and someone who had actually existed once. Then a single floating eyeball with Sans posed beside it, grinning, stiff, thumbs-up — a portrait he has no memory of sitting for. The archive files [Prunsel](#/article/prunsel) as a colossal eye-shaped relative or omen recorded in the margins.
sections.waluigi_note: Wing dings appearing on the terminal screen with chime audio. Sans tensing in the chair, dropping the jokes, and watching the monitor feed like a hawk.

sections.name: V. Times New Roman, and a Signature Box
sections.overview:
Mid-call, [Times New Roman](#/article/times_new_roman) walked in.

He arrived holding a clipboard, in spectacles, moving — in Sans's description — too cleanly, like text that had not been touched by real life. He opened with *hey, what's up, brother.*

Before any of the paperwork, there was the title card: **EXACTLY WHEN SANS'S PUNS BECAME A HOUSEHOLD HAZARD**, with a Waluipedia attribution line noting that the entries are kept for completeness, that Sans has never let anyone borrow that section, and that he reads it when he thinks nobody is watching.

Times New Roman then cited **archive log entry #472 — 'sans uses pun in public for the 10,001st time.'** Asked who authorised the documentation, he did not flinch: *no permission required. this is an archival initiative.*

Sans's reply — *i didn't think anyone cared that much about my terrible jokes* — is filed here because it is the only moment in the call where he sounds pleased about being in a record.

Asked directly whether this was a brotherly reunion, Times New Roman answered **'affirmative'** and nothing else. No embrace, no shared memory. Sans's assessment: the most awkward reunion in history, like meeting a twin from a universe where emotions had been deleted.

He is the Bone-Line's archivist — the family typesetter, keeper of an indexed chronicle, a man who by his own filed description distrusts any story that opens with *you had to be there.* He greeted Sans as **brother** and supported the claim the way he supports everything: **'designation: brother. confirmed by archival lineage code #TNR-01.'**

No warmth. No shared childhood. A code.

He produced an [[prop:prop_sibling_designation_tnr01|Official Archival Record of Sibling Designation]] — Sans listed as Primary Brother (Documented), himself as Secondary Brother (Archival Confirmation), with footnotes and an appendix reference for skeletal alignment. Gee Lady appeared on it as a *designated family member*, confirmed via lipstick signature analysis and emotional resonance frequency matching.

Then the page kept unrolling. Dozens of names, down the table and onto the floor. Titles, question marks, duplicate entries, an unverified branch pending DNA. And at the bottom, alone, underlined twice in red: **Wingding Gaster.** No title. No question mark.

And a blank signature box.

Sans signed it. Not as a joke — Waluigi wants that in the record, because Sans does almost everything as a joke. He wrote his name in plain letters with no flourish.
sections.waluigi_note: Times New Roman walking in with wire-rim spectacles and an iron clipboard, moving like type that had never been folded or smudged.

sections.name: VI. The Contract Burned
sections.overview:
The paper caught **blue fire** — silent, heatless, every name curling to ash that rose as smoke shaped like small bones. Times New Roman watched it burn without moving, which Waluigi reads as the reaction of a man watching an expected step complete rather than a man watching a document destroyed.

Then they arrived. Cursive first, adjusting a cuff. Times New Roman, no longer an assistant. A tall angular relation. [Gee Lady](#/article/gee_lady), who did not glitch, did not pose, and simply smiled, then gestured at the wall and opened a soft gold light that let the rest through.

And at the back, the shadow that had been indistinct in every frame until now resolved, stepped forward, and unfurled a single wing.

Sans's own filed dossier already describes Wing Gaster as a shadowed elder whose absence shapes the family's caution *around impossible doors.* A door opened. The elder came through it.
sections.waluigi_note: Heatless blue flames turning thirty names into smoke shaped like vertebrae. A legal document immolating itself without leaving soot on the carpet.

sections.name: VII. And Then the Set Was Gone
sections.overview:
No fade. No collapse. The gold light, the family, the wing — absent, in the manner of something that had never been switched on.

Sans was alone in his room. Socks on the floor, socks on the chairs, one somehow in the ceiling fan. Papyrus shouting from down the hall, furious about the socks and nothing else, on his way to conduct a disciplinary interview about hygiene.

Sans lay down on the bed and said the family tree stuff had felt real.

The line stayed open. Waluigi said nothing, which is not a thing Waluigi does.
sections.waluigi_note: The background set dissolving instantly without a fade. Just an empty room with dirty socks on the floor and a dial tone on the receiver.

sections.name: VIII. What Waluigi Actually Holds
sections.overview:
A recording made on Legion equipment, during a Legion-authorised hour, of an interview in which:

- the subject **denied** the document he was shown, comprehensively and by name
- **two of his own recorded sentences** turned out to have people filed under them
- a self-described archivist asserted kinship **by reference number**
- a contract **burned**
- the burned contract's contents **walked into the room**
- an elder who is not supposed to be remembered **stepped through**
- and all of it **stopped existing**, leaving a witness who was not sure it had happened

Twenty-eight records cite this registry. Waluigi can now confirm the registry exists, because Waluigi watched it burn and watched what came out of the ash.

What Waluigi cannot confirm is whether it is a record of a family, or a mechanism that produces one. **WAH.**
sections.waluigi_note: An interview where the subject denied the document, the witness was erased, the paper burned, and the archive holds only the master tape. WAH.

name: The Airlift That Never Came
title: The Airlift That Never Came: A Legion Code, Two Fires, and the Card Remi Traded to Get Out
date: 1 Aethel, 1040 BF — continuing without a break from the Scorncrow's execution; the grove is already surrounded when this begins
era: Raventree Crisis — Shadeward Operations / The Skittering Grove / Post-Scorncrow Collapse
location: The Skittering Grove, the burning undergrowth, and Anamatar's Den
type: Retreat Under Contact / Rescue Dispute / Extraction
status: Filed — the grove is on fire, the party is split four ways, and nobody was airlifted
summary: The Scorncrow is dead and the position is worse. A Legion guard hoists the unconscious Salam onto his shoulder and announces he is taking him to an Iron Legion hospital; Feyward Dan and Markop both tell him not to break the line, and he goes anyway, on the code — no man left behind. The guards promise a helicopter. Dan asks what a helicopter is. Remi strips her ruined dress, pulls a chain shirt off a body, heals herself twice and still is not right, takes a battle axe and walks out of the grove alone. Archie erases the crossed-out lines in his spellbook, circles his last high-level spell — and casts Fireball at a bush, setting the grove alight a second time. Markop, surrounded and bitten, is pulled out by Dan's javelin and a barrier, and ends the night sitting on Wario's motorbike with no idea how to ride it. Wario, Remi and Mossy blunder into Anamatar's den, where passage out is sold for a possession: Pierce Anamatar asks for the siglet, declines an expired coupon, and takes Remi's student ID instead. No helicopter arrives. The three Toads are left in the dirt watching everyone else leave.
description:
Waluigi is going to open with the sentence that decides this filing, because everything after it is consequence.

**A man picked up a wounded Toad and walked off with him, and he was right by his own rules and wrong by everybody else's, and no two people in that grove agreed about which mattered.**
outcome: The Scorncrow is dead and the party is in a worse position than before it died. An Iron Legion guard took the unconscious Salam on his shoulder and left against the objections of Archie, Feyward Dan and Markop, citing the Legion code — no man left behind — and stating plainly that he trusts himself more than them and will not leave a casualty with the people who produced one. The promised helicopter never arrived; the guards left on foot, fireman-carrying Salam after one of them tripped and Salam was briefly dragged by a spider. Archie erased the crossed-out lines in his spellbook, circled his last high-level spell, and cast Fireball at a bush, setting the grove alight for the second time in two filings with the party still inside it. Markop stopped his own bleeding, was surrounded, stepped on spider eggs mid-declaration, and was extracted by Dan's javelin and a barrier cast across the grove before he threw it; he ended the night sitting on Wario's motorbike with no idea how to ride it. Remi stripped her destroyed dress, took a chain shirt and a battle axe off a body, healed herself twice without getting right, and walked out of the grove under her own power — then ran into a room of wrights with Wario and Mossy. Pierce Anamatar offered passage out of Guild-controlled ground in exchange for a possession, asked for the siglet, declined an expired coupon, and accepted Remi's Gehenna Academy student ID because it is durable. The three Toads were left in the dirt watching everyone else leave.

participants.name: Iron Legion guards

reputationNotes.markop: Told a Legion guard he had no standing to remove a casualty and was told his incompetence was beyond measure. The alliance struck one filing ago is now a dispute over a body.
reputationNotes.archie_miser: Spent his last high-level spell setting fire to the ground everybody was standing on, while under a standing Legion arrest warrant.
reputationNotes.remi_akamatsu_full_backstory: Bought passage out of Guild-controlled ground from a man who openly dislikes the Guild, paying with her own student ID.
reputationNotes._record: The temporary alliance from the previous filing did not survive contact with a wounded man. The Legion kept the casualties and the party kept the grievance.

aftermath:
**The grove is burning again.** Archie lit it with his last high-level spell, aimed at a bush, with everyone still inside.

**The party is in four pieces.** Markop is on a motorbike he cannot ride. Feyward Dan and Eager are surrounded. Remi, Wario and Mossy are in Anamatar's den with passage bought. The three Toads are in the dirt watching everyone leave.

**The Legion has Salam.** Salam left in a fireman's carry, bound for Legionhold — the same facility the guards promised would host Archie's arrest.

**No helicopter came.** It was promised twice and never appeared.

**Remi has no student ID.** Pierce Anamatar has it, and it is the last document proving she was ever enrolled at Gehenna Academy.

**Unresolved:** what Anamatar wants with a student card; whether the Legion will return Salam; and whether anyone told the three Toads what happened.
waluigiAssessment:
**The argument over Eager is the filing and the fire is the punchline.**

Waluigi has read the exchange between Markop and the guard a dozen times looking for the party's side to be obviously right, and it is not. The guard said he would not leave half a dead person with people who gallivant around and get killed, and he said it standing over a grove containing one fallen Toad, one man fighting while badly hurt, and a Toad unconscious on his shoulder. **The evidence was on his side.** He was rude, he was unilateral, and he was not wrong.

What makes it a dispute rather than a rescue is the second half of his sentence: *I trust myself more than you guys.* That is not the code talking. The code was the justification he reached for; the distrust was the reason. And Eager — awake enough to ask — told him to put him down, and he did not.

**Then Archie set the grove on fire.** Waluigi wants to be careful here, because Markop had just shouted for exactly that and the spiders were closing. But the sequence in the record is: erase the crossed-out lines, find the last high-level spell, circle it, aim at a **bush**. One spell of that grade left in the book, spent on shrubbery, in a grove that was already burned once, while nine people were standing in it.

Everybody who was surrounded before the fireball was still surrounded after it. The only thing that changed is that the room is now on fire.

**And then there is the card.**

Pierce Anamatar could have asked for gold. He asked for a possession, twice now — a contract paid in passage home on a rooftop, and tonight a piece of laminate belonging to a fourteen-year-old. He declined an expired coupon, which means he was choosing, not taking whatever was offered.

Remi left Gehenna Academy without a formal withdrawal. That card was the only document in the world still asserting she had been a student somewhere. She traded it to get three people out of a burning wood, and she did it without visible hesitation, and Waluigi does not think she has worked out yet what she handed over.

**What the night actually cost:** a promised helicopter that never came, a wizard's last big spell spent on a bush, Salam in Legion custody, a paladin surrounded, a centaur on a motorbike he cannot ride, three Toads abandoned in the dirt, and a girl's name coming off the only paper that carried it.

They killed the Scorncrow last filing. Waluigi would like somebody to explain what they won.

WAH.
