sections.name: I. The Worst First Ride in the Archive
sections.overview:
The filing opens where [the last one](#/article/the_airlift_that_never_came) ended: [Markop](#/article/markop) on [Wario](#/article/wario)'s motorbike, engine running, no idea what any of the controls do. What follows is the archive's first recorded centaur riding lesson, and it goes the way everything in the [Skittering Grove](#/article/skittering_grove) goes. He drove it poorly and rammed it into the trees; he bumped — the record's word, and Waluigi is keeping it — into [Salam](#/article/salam).

Consider what had to be true for that last part to happen. The Legion guards left this grove on foot, at a sprint, fireman-carrying an unconscious Toad through a burning wood. A man on a shoulder is not fast. A grove on fire rearranges its own paths. Somewhere between the exit they had promised themselves and the exit that exists, they were still there when a motorbike came off its line and found them — and the casualty they were carrying became the thing the motorbike hit.
sections.waluigi_note: A centaur on a goblin-built motorbike with no clutch experience is an aviation disaster waiting to ignite. Waluigi records that the throttle survived the oak tree.

sections.name: II. Let Him Go — He Is Awake
sections.overview:
The words came first: *let him go, he is awake.* Then [Salam](#/article/salam) made them true and woke up — his first recorded moment since the airlift carried him out of the frame. Two filings down. Face scarred from the clawing. On the ground between a guard's shoulder and a burning wood.

[Markop](#/article/markop) asked the question the whole arrangement now turned on: *can we go?*

The guard's answer began — *if you leave* — and the record cuts it there. Waluigi has spent longer than is professional on the rest of that sentence. If you leave, you are on your own. If you leave, we are not coming back. If you leave, the code stops applying. It does not matter, because Markop did not wait for it:

**"You said leave no one behind, right?"**

One filing ago that sentence was a hand on Salam's shoulder, walking him toward Legionhold over everyone's objection including Salam's. Tonight it was four words long and pointed back at the men who own them, and it worked. The guard let him go. An awake man is not a casualty, and a code that will not abandon a body has no clause for a person standing up and walking somewhere else.
sections.waluigi_note: Quoting an army's official field manual back to a sentry holding a weapon is dangerous literature. Markop made the code work by standing between the guard and the trees.

sections.name: III. Salam, You Rest
sections.overview:
What happened next was an order, and the order is the hinge of the filing. *Salam, you rest,* [Markop](#/article/markop) said. *Oh — okay. I got it,* said [Salam](#/article/salam), and took it.

Waluigi notes the transaction, because the archive has filed this party arguing about everything for two nights — about fire, about routes, about custody, about the definition of a helicopter — and the first command given and accepted all session was *rest*.

Then the plan, assembled out loud at the edge of the fire:

- [Salam](#/article/salam) waits at the motorbike, and a Legion guard waits with him. *You could just wait here, Salam. And you, guard.*
- [Markop](#/article/markop) goes to get his friends.
- If things get rough, the party is going back through the tree — the tree of the grove, the same throat the party roped down through when the grove first took them in.
- And Salam's options if it turns, named honestly, to his face: he might end up with these guards — *or on your own, but it won't be safe in this place.* *I hear you. Well, alright.*

And then the sentence this filing will be quoted by forever, delivered with its pause intact:

**"Don't leave. You just stay put. If we have to leave, I'll… scream for you."**

Waluigi has filed battle plans written by generals and evacuation protocols written by institutions, and he has never filed a signal that was an unfinished sentence. It is perfect: a scream carries through fire and web where orders do not, and nobody who hears one mistakes it for anything else.
sections.waluigi_note: An order to rest is the rarest command in this archive, and Salam took it without an argument because his ribs were whistling like an open flute.

sections.name: IV. The Toads Go Up
sections.overview:
The three [Toads](#/article/toads) made their own arithmetic on the far side of the grove. They would run upwards, deeper in. If it turned south, they may have to fully disengage.

*What if there is a guy up there?*

*I'll hope they're friendly… if not… I'll find a way out.*

The archive files both sentences without comment, in the same paragraph, next to each other, because that is the entire strategic doctrine of this party in two lines: hope first, exit second, no plan third.
sections.waluigi_note: The Toads made their own arithmetic in the dark. In this archive, scouts who plan their disengagement before the shouting begins are usually the ones who survive to be audited.

sections.name: V. A Legion Man Runs
sections.overview:
And then the filing's cold beat, the one Waluigi cannot explain and will not invent:

**An [Iron Legion](#/article/iron_legion) man ran past [Markop](#/article/markop) in panic.**

Not walked. Not withdrew. Ran, in the open, past an armed stranger, in the direction of out. The record does not say what he saw. The last time this archive watched the Legion in this grove, they were promising helicopters and grading everyone else's competence. Something in the deeper grove — the same deeper grove the three Toads have just decided to run toward — moved a professional soldier like that.

The archive does not know what it was, and notes only that it did not chase the man. Whatever it is, it let him go.
sections.waluigi_note: A trained legionary does not run from bad weather. Whatever was coming through the branches behind him had stripped six months of drill right out of his boots.

sections.name: VI. One Spell
sections.overview:
[Archie](#/article/archie_miser) ran toward the Toads on the other side of the grove. [Markop](#/article/markop) watched him go and shouted after him, and the distance between the two of them — two men calling across a burning wood — is this filing's geography.

*Great,* Archie called back. *I only have enough mana to use a single spell.*

One filing ago Archie erased the crossed-out lines in his spellbook and spent the last high-level spell in it on a bush. The well has a floor, and the floor is one spell of any size. And into the smoke, from someone — the record does not say who, and every one of them had earned the right to ask it — came the night's only honest question:

*How could this have happened?*

The arithmetic that answers it was called across the grove like a ledger being read out: [Markop](#/article/markop), sixteen. [Archie](#/article/archie_miser), eight. [Eager](#/article/eager), sixteen. [Dan](#/article/dan_the_toad), eleven — nobody dead, nobody fit. Four numbers, none of them far enough from zero to matter, held by a party that is about to split — *I hate having to split up,* Markop said — inside a grove that just frightened the Iron Legion.

The split itself was argued properly. [Archie](#/article/archie_miser) was fine with leaving [Wario](#/article/wario) behind — Wario having already bought his way out through [Anamatar](#/article/pierce_anamatar)'s den at the price of [Remi](#/article/remi_akamatsu_full_backstory)'s student ID, a transaction Waluigi still cannot believe he gets to keep filing — but Salam, at least, should follow Markop. *If I go get Salam it will be too slow,* Markop answered. *Spiders will surround us.* And across the grove, Archie, in absolute earnest, shouted the question this archive has been waiting the whole campaign to hear:

**"Can Salam hold onto you?"**

A cavalry question, about a centaur, shouted across a burning wood — and the archive files it with joy.
sections.waluigi_note: Holding one spell in reserve while surrounded by things with mandibles is a severe test of character. Archie held the book shut until the grove demanded the fire.

sections.name: VII. Blades for a Doorway
sections.overview:
[Eager](#/article/eager) attacked with his blades — holding the spiders off, clearing a way for [Archie](#/article/archie_miser): a doorway made of one Toad swinging. [Dan](#/article/dan_the_toad) swung too, then looked around, put his head down, and put a shield around Archie, and told him to run.

The order of operations is the man. One filing ago Dan pointed one finger at Markop and sent the barrier across the grove before the javelin left his hand. Tonight he put his whole head down and put a shield around the wizard before he thought about himself at all. The archive has filed paladins who talk about protection. It keeps filing one who does it.

And from the motorbike — from the sentry post, from the rest Markop ordered — [Salam](#/article/salam) shot a spider. The man who left this grove unconscious on a Legion shoulder spent his first waking hour in two filings putting an arrow into the fight for his friends.
sections.waluigi_note: Eager made a doorway out of swinging steel. One Toad carving twenty seconds of free air for a wizard who was still trying to remember where he parked his boots.

sections.name: VIII. The Green One
sections.overview:
The way did not hold: [Archie](#/article/archie_miser), [Dan](#/article/dan_the_toad) and [Eager](#/article/eager) were surrounded.

[Eager](#/article/eager) got bitten and slashed; [Dan](#/article/dan_the_toad) dodged the attacks — all of them, and the filing notes a Toad paladin in a closing ring, unhittable, and unable to be everywhere at once. [Archie](#/article/archie_miser) was attacked by the giant green spider — the same green one that closed on Markop at the end of the last filing, patient as an institution — and it bit him, and Dan's temporary shield broke.

That spider has now attended two filings, menaced a centaur, and bitten a wizard through a shield made by a paladin who does not miss. It is the best fighter in the grove and it is owed a file of its own.
sections.waluigi_note: The giant green spider did not negotiate. It closed the perimeter like an experienced bailiff with eight legs and an overactive venom gland.

sections.name: IX. Stand Still, You Worm
sections.overview:
At the motorbike, a guard decided the sentry arrangement had run its course and tried to grab [Salam](#/article/salam) off the bike.

*Stand still, you worm.*

**"No!"**

Two filings ago Salam was carried out of this grove unconscious, on a shoulder, over an objection he was not awake to make. Tonight, awake, under orders, one arrow into the fight, he refused the hands. And the next thing the record shows him doing is drawing the bow again.

Spiders approached [Markop](#/article/markop), and a spear was rammed into the ettercap. The record does not say whose spear, in a grove containing Legion guards who carry them and a party whose javelin left in the last filing. Waluigi files his suspicion nowhere.
sections.waluigi_note: Calling a wounded Toad a worm while trying to repossess him for a military hospital tab is standard Legion bedside manner. Salam's refusal was his best line all night.

sections.name: X. The Syringe
sections.overview:
And then the Legion closed the night by closing its own loop.

The guards said they would heal [Eager](#/article/eager). *Stand still.* One got out a syringe.

One filing ago, over Markop's offer to heal his own man, a guard said: *he is scared, we can fix that right away.* Waluigi filed it then as the most Legion sentence in the record. He files the syringe now as that sentence made physical: an institution that processes fear, and wounds, and objections, through procedure. The same organisation that carried a man out on the code one filing ago put a man back together on the same night, with the same certainty, while its own soldier was running past in the other direction.

The code, paid in both directions within the hour. Waluigi did not expect to file that.
sections.waluigi_note: The Legion's idea of roadside first aid is an iron needle the size of a knitting needle shoved through combat fatigues without an antiseptic wipe.

sections.name: XI. Standing
sections.overview:
The position as this filing closes:

[Archie](#/article/archie_miser), [Dan](#/article/dan_the_toad) and [Eager](#/article/eager) surrounded — Archie bitten through a broken shield with one spell of mana left in the book; Eager bitten and slashed and being held still for a syringe; Dan untouched and unable to fix either of those things. [Markop](#/article/markop) at the motorbike with spiders approaching. [Salam](#/article/salam) on the motorbike, awake, under orders, refusing hands, one arrow spent and one missed. A Legion guard beside him who has been told to wait. The three [Toads](#/article/toads) somewhere above, running deeper into the thing that made a soldier run.

And strung between the bike and the surrounded, unspent, the arrangement: *if we have to leave, I'll… scream for you.*

Nobody has screamed yet. Waluigi has attended a great many battles, and he reports that the sound everybody is listening for is the one nobody wants to make.

WAH.
sections.waluigi_note: The code came back the other way, the scream was still trapped in Archie's throat, and the grove was about to demand the rest of the bill. WAH.

name: The Cut and the Puppet Master
title: CUT!: A Coffee Machine That Was Not an Exit, a Plumber Man Who Fought to the Music, and the Director Behind the Curtain
date: 5 Aethel, 1040 BF — continuing the studio encounter without a break; the same archive day as the amended promo account — the Day Log files where the archivist actually was
era: 1040 BF — Mario disappearance file
location: The Nintendo Mania studio — the break room, the ceiling ducts, the maintenance room, and the collapsing set
type: Escape Attempt / Musical Skirmish / Studio Revelation
status: Filed — the show has a director, the director has a remote, and the only complete witness is a lord the archive met two filings ago
summary: Darian presses the EMERGENCY EXIT button and gets coffee — until the steam pops a ceiling vent open, and the escape goes up instead of out. In the ducts: rats, noise, and a blue light. Under it, Luigi — alive, alone, working security feeds and notes headed Wario's corruption. Darian's rolling-pin ambush is stopped by Alistair's hand and answered with a flashlight. Then Evil Mario comes through the door wearing a cape of pixelated shadow feathers, and the studio turns the music on: Plumber Man, the real Mario's own song, fought to and dodged by a corrupted copy. The floor collapses; three studio-uniform paratroopas catch them; Darian orders a V formation and Luigi yanks the cape off. A tanuki leaf, a second Wario head, a flaming pipe through a window, fire, a fire alarm crawl, sprinklers, ice — and then Darian says CUT, the one word the building obeys. Curtains. Reset break room. Wario walks in to applause from an empty room, and behind everyone comes a man in a director's cap Wario calls Boss: Director Mario, who knocks Wario out for ruining his show. Evil Mario points at the door he left through — and in a dark hallway Darian watches the Director pass, carrying a folder and a small remote control wired like it runs the studio.
description:
Waluigi is going to open this filing with the only sentence in the whole account that behaves like an exit, because nothing else in the building did.

**A button beside a coffee machine said EMERGENCY EXIT, and pressing it made coffee. Everything after that — the vent, the song, the fire, the ice, the word, the curtains, the man with the remote — followed from a lord deciding to climb anyway.**
outcome: The escape attempt became a raid on the show itself. The studio's exits are still traps, but the ceiling was real, the paratroopas are real crew, and Luigi — reported missing since the promo account — was found alive at the maintenance computer with notes on Wario's corruption. The cape of pixelated feathers was destroyed by a V-formation pass and Luigi's hands; the corrupted Mario burned through a tanuki leaf, a second Wario head, fire, and ice before the word CUT froze the entire production and the curtains came down. The reset break room hosted the second reveal: Wario ran the show, the applause was a recording for an empty studio, and Wario answers to a Director Mario — who beat Wario unconscious for betraying him and left without a word. Evil Mario survived everything and pointed the survivors at the Director's exit. In the hallway, hidden, Darian saw the Director carry past him a folder and a small wired remote — a control unit for Evil Mario, or the studio, or both. Nobody has the remote. The archive now knows the show has an off switch and an owner.
notableFeatures: A button labelled EMERGENCY EXIT, next to the coffee machine — pressing it made coffee
The scalding coffee and steam popped a ceiling vent open: the exit was the appliance's fault
Armed from the break room: a heavy metal rolling pin and a broken coffee-pot handle
'Careful — noise might draw attention' — Alistair, as a rolling pin echoes through the duct system
LUIGI FOUND ALIVE — alone in a maintenance room, running security feeds, a studio map, and notes headed 'Wario's corruption'
Darian's rolling-pin drop on Luigi, stopped by Alistair's hand mid-swing; Luigi answered with a flashlight to the shoulder
'Innocence doesn't get you far' — Evil Mario, entering through a destroyed door
'A king cannot let his subjects fall!' — Darian, before putting Evil Mario through the computer desk with Alistair
THE CAPE — shadowy, pixelated feathers, moving like a living thing; the power source
The floor collapses and three studio-uniform paratroopas with parachutes catch all three out of the air
PLUMBER MAN — the studio plays the real Mario's own song and Evil Mario fights to the beat, dancing through the tranq barrage
Luigi hums along unwillingly; the song is the real Mario's — the corrupted copy wields it as a weapon
The real Mario appears at the song's final note, bruised, having crawled out of the wreckage
Evil Mario freezes mid-charge — eyes glitching, feathers fraying — then decks the real Mario
'As a king, I order the troops into formation — a V, like a bird' — and the V cuts the cape wind
LUIGI YANKS THE CAPE OFF in the formation's dive
A tanuki leaf; a fox tail; Wario's hair; and a second grinning WARIO HEAD on Evil Mario's shoulder
Alistair returns through a window with a flaming pipe — 'this is really stupid', Darian tells him, correctly
The Wario head pops off like a balloon and bursts into smoke; the flaming pipe sets the leaf burning
Fire Evil Mario; Darian's fire-alarm crawl through debris — 'it's too risky but I must keep going'
Sprinklers douse the fire; Evil Mario points and the room freezes into ICE — the real Mario's fist freezes stuck in him
'How many forms does this thing have… this must be all an act' — and the ice smirks
CUT — one word from Darian and the entire production stops; the paratroopas lower weapons 'like he just remembered something'
Theatrical curtains fall; crew voices; 'cut the feed'; the studio resets to the original break room with a single static TV
Wario walks in to recorded applause: 'Best show on TV!' — 'some of you didn't sign up for it'
DARIAN CHECKS THE AUDIENCE: every seat empty; the whole facility silent — 'we're alone'
DIRECTOR MARIO — director's cap, script, and a cigar he snaps in half: 'you tried to f*** me'
He puts Wario through a wall, knocks him unconscious, straightens his suit, and leaves without a word
Evil Mario — still alive — smiles and POINTS at the Director's exit
In the hallway, hidden, Darian watches the Director pass with a folder and a small wired REMOTE — 'a control unit… for Evil Mario? Or maybe the whole studio?'

participants.name: Lord Darian Marsh of the Dark Shores
participants.role: Pressed the button, took the rolling pin, dropped on Luigi, ordered the V formation, crawled for the fire alarm, said CUT, checked the audience, spotted Evil Mario watching, and hid in the alcove to watch the Director pass with the remote. Burned hands, a numb shoulder, and the only complete picture of the studio.

participants.name: Alistair of the Marshkeepers
participants.role: Inventoried the break room, boosted his lord into the duct, stopped the rolling pin mid-swing, was hurled down a hallway by the cape wind, and returned through a window with a flaming pipe to burn the tanuki leaf. 'This is really stupid', his lord told him, correctly.

participants.name: Luigi
participants.role: Found alive at the maintenance computer running security feeds and notes on Wario's corruption, having come to the studio to find his brother. Fought off a rolling pin with a flashlight, kicked Evil Mario's legs, hummed his brother's song without meaning to, and yanked the cape off in the V-formation dive.

participants.name: Mario
participants.role: The real one — beaten in the corridors, appeared at the song's final note, punched through a wall by the unfrozen Evil Mario, punched the ice and got his fist frozen stuck, and watched a man in his own face discipline Wario.

participants.name: Evil Mario
participants.role: The corrupted Mario from the television. Fought through cape, tanuki leaf, a second Wario head, fire, and ice — all of it, the filing concludes, an act. Froze at the word CUT, survived the curtains, watched the Director leave, and pointed at his exit.

participants.name: Director Mario
participants.role: The man Wario bows to. Director's cap, script, cigar. Declared the show had gone over better than Wario knew, accused him of betrayal, knocked him unconscious with one punch, and left down the hallway carrying a folder and a small wired remote.

participants.name: Wario
participants.role: Walked into the reset break room clapping, claimed the whole ordeal as his show — 'Best show on TV!' — and was knocked unconscious by his own Director for ruining it. His face appeared as a second head on Evil Mario's shoulder and popped like a balloon.

participants.name: Waluigi
participants.role: Archivist; not a witness. Filed the account the same night as the amendment it answers, and opened a lead on a remote control device.

reputationNotes._record: No standing moved: the studio is not a faction, its paratroopas take no orders the archive can bill, and the only institution on the stage answers to a man the archive met four paragraphs ago.

aftermath:
**The show has a director.** Director Mario — a cold copy of the most famous face in the world — outranks Wario inside the studio, and Wario found out by going through a wall.

**The applause was for nobody.** Every seat was empty; the whole facility was silent. Whatever audience the show plays to, it was never in the room.

**Evil Mario is an actor with a power source** — pixelated feather cape, destroyed; tanuki leaf, burned; fire, sprinkled; ice, CUT. He survived all of it, and pointed the survivors at the Director's exit.

**Luigi is alive**, at a studio computer, holding notes on Wario's corruption — the best evidence the file has ever been handed.

**The remote exists.** Small, buttoned, wired, carried like a habit by a man who no longer knows he was seen with it. A control unit for Evil Mario, or the whole studio.

**Unresolved:** who Director Mario answers to; what the folder holds; whether the paratroopas take orders from the remote or the Director; what Evil Mario wants; and how a lord of the Dark Shores gets a wired remote off the most dangerous man in the building.
waluigiAssessment:
**1. The word did what the weapons could not.** Two filings of violence — fireballs, javelins, warhammers, rolling pins — and the thing that stopped the corrupted Mario dead was a production command delivered by a provincial lord who had worked out the building's grammar. CUT is not a spell. It is a word the studio's owner could not afford to have said in front of the cast. Waluigi has re-shelved half of this file accordingly: the question is no longer how to beat Evil Mario. The question is who is afraid of the word CUT, and why.

**2. The remote is the whole case.** A folder and a small wired device, carried past a hidden witness by a man who had just demonstrated what he does to employees who exceed their brief. If it runs Evil Mario, it explains the cape, the leaf, the fire, the ice — a costume rack with a controller. If it runs the STUDIO, it explains the resetting break room, the curtains, the applause with no audience, and the exits that lie. Either way, the Mario disappearance file now has an object to hunt instead of a vibe.

**3. Luigi was doing the archive's job better than the archive.** Security feeds, a studio map, notes on Wario's corruption, and a mission statement — find Mario, fix this — while Waluigi was filing newspapers. The maintenance computer is the best evidence in this case and it is sitting in a building that resets itself. Somebody should go back for it.

**4. The empty seats are the part Waluigi cannot file yet.** A show needs an audience. The applause track says one exists. The room says it does not. Either the audience is somewhere the windows do not show, or the performance is being recorded for a viewer the building is not prepared to name. Both readings have a person at the end of them, and Waluigi has a name he is not writing down until he has to.

**Recommendation:** the remote, before the Director notices it was seen. And somebody collect Luigi's notes on the way out.

WAH.

timeline.note: The studio half of this timeline is reconstructed, not witnessed — Waluigi was not in that building. The Feyward half is witnessed — he was in that one, as leverage. The studio keeps no clock the archive would trust (the wall clocks are PROPS), so the times below are the archive's, laid over the account in order on the Material calendar the file already uses; the manor's clock is stuck at 922, which is not better.
timeline.method: Duration anchors: one complete performance of Plumber Man — three minutes forty-one seconds by the archive's own copy, timed twice; the account's own two minutes of surveillance; and the honest assumption that a king climbs slower than a rat. The Feyward rows need no anchors — they were witnessed, and no clock in that manor agrees with itself anyway.

worlds.label: The main world — where the archive keeps its desk
worlds.timeOfDay: A dated-true, written-late day. The desk stamped three filings to the fifth — teaser, correction, sequel — and typed none of them at this desk on the fifth: the teaser went up from behind a barricade in the Feyward, the correction arrived there by wire, and the sequel and this timeline were written in the writing-late period, under the lamp, by a man who had finally stopped being chased.
worlds.weather: Low grey cloud all morning; a dry east wind that took the dust off the roads by midday; rain after dark — steady, unhurried rain, the kind that makes a lamp and a closed door feel like a policy decision.
worlds.source: Waluigi went looking for what the sky was doing while a studio in another world played a song. The RNN morning bulletin gave two lines and a shrug, so he dug the morning editions out of the WAH Media Collective's back-issue boxes — three newsstands and one argument with a print vendor later, the archive can state the weather on the day the building obeyed a lord. Nobody asked it to. That is what archives are FOR.

weatherWidget.line: Low grey cloud; no rain yet
Dry east wind — the dust came off the roads

worlds.label: The Nintendo Mania studio — the promo world
worlds.timeOfDay: Morning by the archive's clock. Indoors there is no time of day — only stage light, static glow, and whatever the scene calls for.
worlds.weather: No weather on record, and the archive means that as a FINDING. The studio's weather is internal: a cold coffee machine that turns volcanic; sprinkler rain in one scene; frost in the next; a velvet night that falls on command when somebody says the word. Beyond the seats the windows show the whole facility silent, under a sky that did not perform. No wind. No birds. The applause track is the closest thing to weather the building has.
worlds.source: The account itself. The archive has no correspondent in that world, the windows were not talking, and the one clock on the wall was a prop.

weatherWidget.line: Scalding steam — the coffee machine's idea of weather
Room heat refused; sprinkler rain deployed
Frost climbing the walls; icicles off the sprinkler heads
No weather on record — a silent sky that did not perform

worlds.label: The Feyward — the Overgrown Manor, where the archivist actually was
worlds.timeOfDay: No hour anyone trusts. The manor's clock is stuck at 922; the goblin downstairs says 722; the Material says 1040. The session ran from the doorway to the open floor without a break, and ended at a locked bathroom door.
worlds.weather: No weather on record — the session never once looked at the sky. The manor's weather is internal: the Revel fighting itself through the ceiling, trees testing the walls, a corridor of polished marble, and one floor that opened.
worlds.source: Witnessed — the only world card in this filing that is. The archivist was in the building, in Colour Division custody, cuffed by choice, for the whole of the studio's morning. The doorway filing (I Can't Afford Not to Care Anymore) is the record; this card is its weather.

weatherWidget.line: The trees testing the walls — knock, scrape, silence
The Revel, audible all day, fighting itself
Vines on every door; the beauty of nature is slow
The floor opened — the manor's one honest weather event

entries.beat: The fall onto the pilot set
entries.detail: Darian and Alistair drop out of their own sky onto a soundstage mid-shoot: the tour, the product demonstration, the tape, the game show, the flashlight. Filed as the promo account — the teaser this timeline's day began with.
Alistair surveys like the steward he is: back door to the kitchen, an air vent, five monitors, a cold coffee machine — and a small button labelled EMERGENCY EXIT that was not there before.
Darian presses it with calibrated pessimism. Scalding coffee, a room filling with steam — and the rising heat pops a ceiling vent open. The exit was the appliance's fault.
A rolling pin, a broken coffee-pot handle, the machine shut off, and a steward's cuped hands: the king goes into the duct first.

entries.beat: The crawl, the rat, the CLANG
entries.detail: Hands and knees in the dark; an ordinary rat (reassuring, by this building's standards); a rolling pin clangs off the duct walls and rolls through the whole system; Alistair whispers the sentence of the year — careful, noise might draw attention.

entries.span: two minutes of surveillance — the account counts them
entries.beat: The man at the blue light
entries.detail: Luigi. Alive, alone, face lit blue, typing fast: security feeds, a studio map, notes headed Wario's corruption. Darian watches from the vent and shushes his steward.

entries.beat: The drop, the arm, the flashlight
entries.detail: Darian drops swinging; Alistair's hand closes on the arm mid-swing; Luigi answers like a cornered man — one flashlight, one numb shoulder.

entries.beat: The door comes off its hinges
entries.detail: Evil Mario, fresh from beating the real Mario, reads the seating chart: innocence doesn't get you far. The room loses the arithmetic — until a rolling pin finds a shoulder, CLANG, the first honest hit in two filings, and a king declares he cannot let his subjects fall.

entries.beat: The cape, the floor, the squad
entries.detail: The pixelated feather cape is the power source; the floor falls in; three studio-uniform paratroopas catch them out of the air — a rescue squad on payroll, and Waluigi has questions about the budget.

entries.span: one complete performance — 3:41 by the archive's copy
entries.detail: The studio turns the music on and the actor fights to the beat: dodges on the downbeat, backflips on the chorus, a tranq barrage that cannot find its timing. Luigi covers his ears, then stops. He knows the song. It belongs to his brother.
Bruised, hat askew, crawled out of the wreckage on his own. Sir, you're alive. The real and the corrupted stand face to face while the song runs out.

entries.span: one gust; then minutes filed as MISSING
entries.detail: The copy stops mid-motion, the cape frays, and the gust knocks Alistair clean off his feet and away down a dark hallway. The paratroopas anchor the others to a broken pipe.
A king cannot let his subjects fall, so he orders the troops into a V, like a bird. The V cuts the wind; Luigi rides the dive and yanks the cape off with both hands. The actor screams.

entries.span: a minute, and a really stupid plan
entries.beat: A leaf, a second head, a window
entries.detail: A tanuki leaf: fox tail, Wario's hair, a second grinning Wario head on one shoulder. Through the broken window comes Alistair — covered in dust, carrying a flaming pipe — and the leaf catches fire.

entries.span: the length of one belly crawl
entries.detail: The actor erupts into flame; Darian goes for the smashed-glass alarm on his belly through the heat, debris under his hands, a flame whip missing by inches. He pulls the handle.

Water everywhere; the fire hisses down; Darian inventories his hands — soot, scratches, small burns, alive. Then the room turns cold: frost, icicles, an ice body with glowing eyes, and a fist frozen stuck in the surface.
The lord of the Dark Shores out-reasons an entire television studio: everything stops. Ice mid-advance, weapons half-lowered, and whatever runs the show FLINCHES.
Velvet from the whole ceiling; crew voices; cut the feed. When the curtains open the studio has reset itself to the break room — no flames, no ice, one television showing static.

Wario walks in clapping and applause comes out of the dark — Oscar-worthy, he says, brilliant special effects — until a lord who checks the building's work looks at the seats and finds every one of them EMPTY.

entries.span: under a minute, including the suit
entries.detail: A figure in a director's cap says let's see how you like the real deal; Wario goes pale, bows, calls him Boss — and goes through a wall for ruining his show. One punch. The Director straightens his suit like a man who has swatted a fly.
Evil Mario, still there, half in shadow, red eyes tracking the Director to the door — smiles slowly, and points one finger at the door the Director left through.

entries.span: as long as a man takes to pass close enough to touch
entries.detail: Darian, hidden in a dark alcove, watches Director Mario stride past with a folder under one arm and a small wired remote in the other, carried like a habit. The account ends on it: that remote could be the key to stopping everything — if they can get it.

entries.time: Evening — the Overgrown Manor, by no clock it trusts
entries.beat: The correction, received in the field
entries.detail: The full account of the promo morning catches the archivist mid-emergency and the teaser is amended on the spot, in pencil, in the field posture: PORTAL FAILED, Luigi missing, a Mario-shaped thing out of a television. The word teaser enters the archive's vocabulary that evening, in a building with no honest clock, and it is not leaving.

entries.span: ten bought minutes, and two paragraphs read under duress
entries.detail: Four Iron Legion operatives introduce themselves by colour and take Toad Lee and Waluigi as leverage against one overdue Aegis Magi contract — cuffs, not cages, and the archivist is out of his before anybody notices and keeps wearing them anyway. Hjumpik buys ten minutes and reads [[prop:prop_accords_900_20_containment|six pages of the Autumnwood Accords]] standing up. The question that keeps the pocket book busy all night opens here: who sends a Colour Division across a planar boundary to collect one dwarf?

The thing wearing Lady Aurelian states its whole plan — collapse the manor, grow trees in the ruin, the beauty of nature is slow — and answers to the name Carnivorous. Red's poisoned dinner goes into its chest, the glamour comes apart, and the floor opens. Witnessed, not reconstructed: the archivist was in this building. Filed in full in the doorway filing.

entries.span: the rest of the night; no lamp was involved
entries.detail: In custody, cuffed by choice, the archivist works the question. The archive already holds the answer's shape: the arrangement — payments between the Iron Legion and Regency officials with the Chancellor's own signature on them — and the Mages' Guild's privileged access to Regency facilities, the same Guild whose failed contract the colours just collected like a household errand. Three names, one machine. The pocket book's next question writes itself: where does a machine like that keep its money?

entries.time: Night — the archive's maps, from memory
entries.detail: The maps say Yale Shores is an actual place, and an archivist who cannot recall his own maps in a building with no lamp deserves what the building does to him: Port Yale, the largest port on the western coast — seven thousand souls, a melting pot and a den of pirates and smugglers — under Fort Yale's guns; the Crimson Fleet's Smuggler's Cove running goods past the Regency's own tariffs; a graveyard reef that has claimed hundreds of hulls; a lighthouse nobody relit; pearl-divers, a crab kingdom with a foreign policy, star-fall on a ley-line beach; and one sea serpent, sole occupant of a trench the maps rate stronger than the fort. Rich, Guild-aligned, not militarized, no Legion garrison — the province where the money enters the kingdom, guarded by nobody because everyone is already paid. The Mages' Guild's own Astral Spire stands over all of it.

entries.time: Night — the dossier, read again from memory
entries.span: one file the archive has never once been able to close
entries.detail: The head of the Regency is Chancellor Toadsworth, the son who inherited everything — his father's journals allegedly confess to enabling Peach's assassination, and the inheritance is filed verbatim: 'My son inherits what I built. He inherits the secrets with it.' Villain, or victim of the wrong father: the archive holds both readings and cannot close the file. What it CAN file: the arrangement carries his own signature, and the archive can now add that he sits under Loyalist house arrest while the machine's paperwork stayed current without him. The leader's true nature, as far as this archive will file it: not the engine — the HEIR. The next day proved the trade sails from his own coast whether he signs it or not. WAH.

sections.name: I. The Break Room, Inventoried
sections.overview:
This filing continues [the promo filing](#/article/promo_mario_newspaper) without a break: [Darian](#/article/lord_darian_marsh) and [Alistair](#/article/alistair_marshkeeper) in the employee break room, four monitors showing static and one showing a lie, the coffee machine gone cold, and the sound of a corrupted [Mario](#/article/mario) beating the real one somewhere out in the corridors. How do we get out of here, though — we have no other leads but this place. Right.

[Alistair](#/article/alistair_marshkeeper) surveyed the room like the steward he is. A back door leading to the kitchen. An air vent big enough to crawl through. The monitors, showing possible exits. And something new: a small button by the coffee machine, labelled **EMERGENCY EXIT**.

*WAH! New. A button that was not there before, in a building that keeps adding rooms to its own script. Waluigi has filed entire investigations that began with less.*
sections.waluigi_note: The break room had four screens showing static and one showing a forged Mario beating the real one. Waluigi notes that broadcast production values have cratered across the provinces.

sections.name: II. The Button That Made Coffee
sections.overview:
[Darian](#/article/lord_darian_marsh) pressed it, with the specific pessimism of a man testing whether the exit is another trap — *brilliant, let's see how it's not an exit to the coffee machine.*

The coffee machine came to life. Aggressively. Scalding coffee poured out uncontrollably; the room filled with steam; [Alistair](#/article/alistair_marshkeeper) coughed out the sentence *it's… not an exit* — and then the steam did what steam does. It rose. And a ceiling vent popped open from the heat.

The exit was the coffee machine's fault. The building had hidden an escape route behind an appliance, or the appliance had staged a rescue — in this studio those are the same sentence with different fonts.
sections.waluigi_note: An emergency exit button wired to a drip percolator is the ultimate corporate trap. Darian tested it with the grim fatalism of a man who expects the radiator to shoot at him.

sections.name: III. Into the Ceiling
sections.overview:
They armed themselves from the break room like men who have learned what this place does to the unarmed: [Darian](#/article/lord_darian_marsh) took a heavy metal rolling pin and the broken coffee-pot handle with its sharp edge. [Alistair](#/article/alistair_marshkeeper) shut off the machine, the steam cleared, and he boosted his lord up into the duct first.

The vent was dark, dusty, cramped — hands and knees, faint emergency light from below, small cracks letting in glow. Something scurried past [Darian](#/article/lord_darian_marsh)'s face. A rat. An ordinary rat, which after the black-eyed thing on Camera Three was almost reassuring. [Darian](#/article/lord_darian_marsh) fumbled for the rolling pin; the metal clanged against the duct walls, one long echo rolling through the whole system, and [Alistair](#/article/alistair_marshkeeper) whispered the sentence this archive would like bronzed: *careful — noise might draw attention.*

Ahead: a faint blue light.
sections.waluigi_note: Arming yourself with an industrial rolling pin and a flashlight before crawling into sheet-metal air ducts is sound estate management when dealing with rogue media personnel.

sections.name: IV. The Man at the Blue Light
sections.overview:
The vent opened over a maintenance room with a working computer screen, and below it, someone typing fast, muttering *come on… come ON…*

It was [Luigi](#/article/luigi). Alive. Alone. His face lit blue, exhausted but unharmed. On the screen: security camera feeds, a map of the studio, and notes headed **Wario's corruption**. He typed that he had to find Mario, that he had to fix this — a scared brother running his own investigation two rooms away from the fight, with better tools than the archive has ever had and nobody to tell.

[Darian](#/article/lord_darian_marsh) watched from the vent and shushed [Alistair](#/article/alistair_marshkeeper) — *let's see if he does anything rash; we don't know how dangerous he is.* It is the correct instinct in this building and Waluigi has said so in ink. The archive has already filed one [Luigi](#/article/luigi) that was not [Luigi](#/article/luigi). The man at the blue light zoomed cameras, checked door sensors, typed notes, seemed normal — and then grabbed a flashlight and stood up to leave.
sections.waluigi_note: Luigi frantically typing in the dark at a maintenance terminal, trying to hack an access gate while muttering to himself. The first confirmed sighting of the real plumber in the complex.

sections.name: V. The Rolling Pin, and the Arm That Stopped It
sections.overview:
[Darian](#/article/lord_darian_marsh) went for the drop — out of the vent, rolling pin coming down on the head of a man he had decided not to trust.

[Alistair](#/article/alistair_marshkeeper)'s hand closed on his arm mid-swing. The steward stopped his own lord's kill shot on a hunch, and the hunch was right, and it was also nearly fatal for everybody: [Luigi](#/article/luigi) turned, saw an armed stranger descending from his ceiling, and did exactly what a cornered man does. He dodged the second swing and put the flashlight into [Darian](#/article/lord_darian_marsh)'s shoulder hard enough to numb it. [Alistair](#/article/alistair_marshkeeper) shouted that they were not here to hurt him. [Luigi](#/article/luigi) was not listening. He was in full panic, ready to fight or flee or scream.

*WAH! Two minutes of surveillance undone by one rolling pin. In the margin of the account Waluigi has written: the steward earns his keep twice in this filing, and the second time is not this.*
sections.waluigi_note: Darian dropping from the rafters to brain an unfamiliar plumber with kitchen hardware, only for Alistair to catch the swing. Restraint in an air shaft is hard to come by.

sections.name: VI. Innocence Doesn't Get You Far
sections.overview:
The door went off its hinges.

[Evil Mario](#/article/evil_mario) stood in it — bruised, grinning, glowing red-eyed, fresh from beating the real [Mario](#/article/mario) somewhere out in the corridors. *Innocence doesn't get you far,* he said, surveying the room like a man reading a seating chart. Three against one, [Darian](#/article/lord_darian_marsh) counted. *We can take him… I think.*

They could not. [Evil Mario](#/article/evil_mario) moved like a special effect — dodged the flashlight, dodged the rolling pin, shoved [Alistair](#/article/alistair_marshkeeper) into a desk, laughed the whole time, and hurled [Luigi](#/article/luigi) into a shelf by the collar. What actually landed was [Darian](#/article/lord_darian_marsh)'s rolling pin: a full swing, **CLANG**, into the shoulder, the first honest hit anyone has put on this thing in two filings. [Evil Mario](#/article/evil_mario) grunted, stumbled back — surprised — and for one second the room believed.

They pressed it. [Luigi](#/article/luigi) kicked his legs. [Alistair](#/article/alistair_marshkeeper), battered upright, called *GO FOR HIS FACE!* — and [Darian](#/article/lord_darian_marsh), somewhere in the noise, produced the sentence that Waluigi will now have to live with:

**"A king cannot let his subjects fall!"**

The lord of the Dark Shores and his steward hit the corrupted Mario together and put him through the computer desk. Monitors shattered. And then the floor began to shake, and [Evil Mario](#/article/evil_mario) started to laugh again, and standing up out of the wreckage he wore a cape.
sections.waluigi_note: The corrupted Mario kicking the door off its hinges with glowing red pupils and bruised knuckles. That voice had too much bass and bad intent for a licensed plumber.

sections.name: VII. The Cape
sections.overview:
Not a costume cape. A cape of **shadowy, pixelated feathers**, moving unnaturally, like a living thing — and the shaking, the flickering lights, the cracking walls were coming from it. The cape was the power source. [Luigi](#/article/luigi) said it out loud: his weakness, it has to be. Destroy the cape.

Then the floor fell in.

All three of them dropped into the collapse — and three **paratroopas in studio uniforms with parachutes** caught them by the arms out of the air. Studio crew. Parachute rigs. One yelled *HOLD ON TIGHT.* [Evil Mario](#/article/evil_mario) screamed below, cheated of three victims at once.

*WAH! Waluigi has questions and he is going to put all of them in the investigation file, starting with: since when does a television studio keep a paratroopa rescue squad, and who wrote them into the budget?*
sections.waluigi_note: Shadowy pixelated feathers moving like live leeches. The studio walls cracking and stage lights buzzing to the frequency of corrupt broadcast signals.

sections.name: VIII. Plumber Man
sections.overview:
The paratroopas did not fly the party out. They flew it **at** [Evil Mario](#/article/evil_mario) — a flying squad in formation, weapons drawn, non-lethal rounds aimed at the cape. *NEUTRALIZE THE THREAT.*

And the studio turned the music on.

**Plumber Man** is filed in full in the [songbook](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/songs) with the lyrics as sung, because what happened next cannot be filed without it: [Evil Mario](#/article/evil_mario) began to fight to the beat. Dodging on the downbeat. Backflips on the chorus. A villain in a feather cape, dancing through a tranq barrage in perfect time while the paratroopas — who train for many things — could not get their timing to land.

[Luigi](#/article/luigi) covered his ears, then stopped covering them. He knew the song. He hummed it, weakly, unwillingly, drawn to it — and the account reaches the conclusion the archive also reached: **the song belongs to the real Mario.** Four feet ten, the stache, the star that powers him, the pipes, the lass, the kingdom. It is a love song disguised as a jingle, and the corrupted copy of the man was using it as a weapon.

At the final note, [Mario](#/article/mario) appeared behind him. Bruised. Hat askew. Crawled out of the wreckage on his own. The paratroopas gasped *Sir, you're alive*; [Luigi](#/article/luigi) nearly wept; and the real and the corrupted stood face to face while the song faded.
sections.waluigi_note: Paratroopas flying in formation with combat ordnance to the rhythm of an unlicensed theme song. A choreographed television hit squad operating on camera cues.

sections.name: IX. The Freeze, and the Yank
sections.overview:
Four against one now — *still not scared*, [Evil Mario](#/article/evil_mario) said, and cracked his neck, and the fight resumed. [Darian](#/article/lord_darian_marsh) ordered the charge — and [Evil Mario](#/article/evil_mario) stopped. Mid-motion. Head tilted, eyes flickering like a screen losing signal, the cape's dark feathers starting to fray. A gust came off it that knocked papers, equipment, and finally [Alistair](#/article/alistair_marshkeeper) clean off his feet and away down a dark hallway like a ragdoll. The paratroopas caught [Luigi](#/article/luigi) and [Darian](#/article/lord_darian_marsh) by the arms and anchored to a broken pipe.

Then the statue came back to life and hit the real [Mario](#/article/mario) across the face hard enough to put him through a wall, and it was clear the fight was lost — until the lord of the Dark Shores remembered what he is for.

**"As a king, I order the troops into formation — a V, like a bird."**

The squad snapped into a V. The V cut the wind. And on the next order — *grab Luigi, fly him into that cape* — the lead paratroopa took [Luigi](#/article/luigi) into the formation's dive, straight at the fraying feathers, and [Luigi](#/article/luigi), who came to this studio to find his brother, reached out with both hands and **yanked the cape off.**

[Evil Mario](#/article/evil_mario) screamed.
sections.waluigi_note: Darian commanding the frost spray, freezing the floor under the creature's boots and tearing the feathered mantle away with a grappling hook.

sections.name: X. A Leaf, a Second Head, and a Very Stupid Return
sections.overview:
The scream became a smile. In his hand: a **tanuki leaf**. The transformation ran through him — fox tail, [Wario](#/article/wario)'s wild hair, and then, grotesque on his shoulder, **a second head: [Wario](#/article/wario)'s**, grinning.

And through the broken window behind them came [Alistair](#/article/alistair_marshkeeper) — blown away minutes ago, presumed lost — crashing back in covered in dust, carrying a **flaming pipe**, with visible rage and, in [Darian](#/article/lord_darian_marsh)'s own words, a plan this filing can only describe as *really stupid.* The Wario head popped off like a balloon and burst into smoke, as if it agreed.

The flaming pipe met the tanuki tail. The leaf caught fire. [Mario](#/article/mario) tackled the thing off its feet, and [Luigi](#/article/luigi) snatched the burning leaf out of the air just as it fully ignited.
sections.waluigi_note: A Tanuki leaf producing a fox tail and a grotesque second head muttering about broadcast ratings. Waluigi declines to audit the biological feasibility of studio props.

sections.name: XI. Fire, Water, Ice
sections.overview:
The corrupted Mario ran out of forms to wear and put on the last one: he **erupted into fire** — no shape left, a living blaze, the room catching around him. [Darian](#/article/lord_darian_marsh) looked for a fire alarm, found one red and smashed-glassed by the shattered door, and went for it through the heat on his belly — *it's too risky, but I must keep going* — debris under his hands, a flame whip missing him by inches. He smashed the glass and pulled the handle.

Sprinklers. Water everywhere. The fire form hissed, shrank, flickered. [Darian](#/article/lord_darian_marsh) looked at his hands — soot, scratches, small burns. Alive.

And [Evil Mario](#/article/evil_mario) pointed at the dying fire, and the room turned **cold**. Frost climbed the walls, breath turned visible, the sprinkler water became icicles, and the corrupted Mario stood remade as a body of shimmering blue ice with glowing eyes. The real [Mario](#/article/mario) punched it and his fist froze stuck in the surface.

*How many forms does this thing have?* [Darian](#/article/lord_darian_marsh) said — and answered himself: **this must be all an act.**

The ice sculpture smirked. Which is how they knew he was right.
sections.waluigi_note: The creature shedding all anatomy to become an open pillar of kerosene flame, setting the acoustic ceiling tiles and set dressing ablaze.

sections.name: XII. CUT
sections.overview:
Here is the moment the filing exists for, and Waluigi wants it quoted exactly, because it is the moment a provincial lord out-reasoned an entire television studio with one word.

**"CUT!"**

Everything stopped. The ice stopped spreading. The paratroopas lowered their weapons mid-breath. The real [Mario](#/article/mario) lowered his fists *like he just remembered something* — and [Evil Mario](#/article/evil_mario)'s frozen expression flickered, pixelated, broke apart like a bad signal. The word had reached whatever was running the show, and whatever was running the show **flinched.**

Theatrical curtains — heavy velvet, whole-ceiling — came down from above. Crew voices. Equipment moving. Someone shouting *cut the feed.* The curtains closed with a THUD, and when they opened again the studio had reset itself: the original break room, no flames, no ice, no evil copies — [Darian](#/article/lord_darian_marsh), [Alistair](#/article/alistair_marshkeeper), the real [Mario](#/article/mario), and a single television showing static. *What just happened?* [Mario](#/article/mario) asked. Nobody had it.

*WAH! He said the word the building lives in fear of. Not a spell, not a weapon — a PRODUCTION COMMAND. Waluigi has been filing this place as a trap for two filings and it may in fact be a stage that cannot bear to be told the take is over.*
sections.waluigi_note: Darian shouting CUT at the top of his lungs and freezing the entire soundstage in place. One provincial lord out-reasoning a television crew with industry jargon.

sections.name: XIII. Best Show on TV
sections.overview:
[Wario](#/article/wario) walked in clapping, and applause came out of the dark.

*Bravo! What an entertaining performance!* Oscar-worthy, he said — the ice scene, brilliant special effects — and an audience that was not there roared approval while a television replayed the fight as security footage. He admitted all of it with his arms spread: *Best show on TV!* Some of you didn't sign up for it. The real [Mario](#/article/mario) asked the only question that mattered — *you used me? Like some kind of puppet?* — and [Wario](#/article/wario) waved it off as a bit of fun.

And [Darian](#/article/lord_darian_marsh), who has spent two filings learning to check this building's work, looked at the audience.

**Every seat was empty.**

Beyond the seats, through the windows, the whole studio facility: silent. No crew, no life, nobody. The applause was a recording for a room of chairs. *We're alone,* [Mario](#/article/mario) said, and [Wario](#/article/wario)'s smirk finally faltered, and four men who had just survived his variety hour began to close on him with their sleeves rolled.
sections.waluigi_note: Wario emerging from the dark clapping his fat paws together, praising the special effects and trying to charge admission fees for an unlicenced brawl.

sections.name: XIV. The Man Wario Bows To
sections.overview:
They never got to him. A voice behind them said, *since this was all for show, let's see how you like the real deal* — and there stood a figure in a **director's cap**, holding a script.

[Wario](#/article/wario)'s face went pale and he bowed. *Boss.*

**[Director Mario](#/article/director_mario)** — and Waluigi is filing that name exactly as the account gives it, cold, calculating, no warmth in him anywhere. The corrupted Mario was an actor. The song was a number. [Wario](#/article/wario) was the producer. The Director said the show had gone over better than [Wario](#/article/wario) knew, that he knew about the results, and then said the quiet part with his cigar snapping in half in his fingers: *you tried to f*** me.*

He took [Wario](#/article/wario) by the collar, put him through a wall hard enough to shake the building, told him *you betrayed me — you ruined MY show,* and knocked him unconscious with one punch. Then he straightened his suit like a man who had swatted a fly, looked once — unreadably — at [Darian](#/article/lord_darian_marsh), [Alistair](#/article/alistair_marshkeeper), [Luigi](#/article/luigi) and the real [Mario](#/article/mario), and walked out without a word.
sections.waluigi_note: A shadowy figure in a director's cap holding a television remote control, commanding the set and the budget. The one authority Wario does not dare invoice.

sections.name: XV. The Watcher, the Hall, and the Remote
sections.overview:
[Darian](#/article/lord_darian_marsh) — alone — noticed that [Evil Mario](#/article/evil_mario) was still there. Half in shadow, perfectly still, red eyes tracking the Director to the door. He told nobody. He moved for the exit slowly, signalled [Alistair](#/article/alistair_marshkeeper) to look, and let the whole room arrive at its own stillness around the thing in the corner.

And [Evil Mario](#/article/evil_mario) smiled. Slowly. And raised one finger, and pointed — not at any of them — at the door the Director had left through.

[Darian](#/article/lord_darian_marsh) stepped out into the dim hallway and waited, and heavy deliberate footsteps came on, and he hid in a dark alcove, and **[Director Mario](#/article/director_mario) walked past him close enough to touch.** In one hand: a folder. In the other, carried with the ease of long habit, a **small remote device with buttons and wires running from it.**

A control unit. For [Evil Mario](#/article/evil_mario). Or for the whole studio. The account ends on the thought the archive now cannot put down: *that remote could be the key to stopping everything — if they can get it.*
sections.waluigi_note: Evil Mario lingering in the shadows with red eyes fixed on the Director. The mechanical chain of command behind the broadcast exposed.

sections.name: XVI. Standing
sections.overview:
[Darian](#/article/lord_darian_marsh): burned hands, a numb shoulder, a working rolling pin, and the only complete picture of what this studio actually is. [Alistair](#/article/alistair_marshkeeper): blown the length of a hallway and back through a window with a flaming pipe, unkillable and unconsulted. [Luigi](#/article/luigi): found alive, his notes on Wario's corruption on a studio computer, his brother's song stuck in his head. The real [Mario](#/article/mario): beaten, frozen, unfrozen, and standing. [Wario](#/article/wario): unconscious on his own soundstage, disciplined by his own employer. [Evil Mario](#/article/evil_mario): alive, unwearied, and pointing at the man with the remote. And the Director: gone round a corner with a folder, a control unit, and every answer this file has wanted since a newspaper said PROMO MARIO.

The applause was for nobody. The show is not over. Somebody is holding the off switch.

WAH.
sections.waluigi_note: Burned fingers, a bent rolling pin, a studio that refuses to stay dead, and a lord who understands that television is just debt in high definition. WAH.

name: The Debt Siege and the Sixty-Thirty Split
title: The Debt Siege and the Sixty-Thirty Split: Wario's Claw, the Ice Wall, and the Contract of Accord
date: 2 Aethel, 1035 BF — late evening, two weeks after the Star Hill rescue
timeWindow: 2 Aethel, 1035 BF — one evening: the balcony reading, the helicopter siege of the outpost, the ice-wall defence, the negotiation, and the departure for Star Hill
era: The Mushroom Kingdom Regency Era (1030s BF) — Mario's Disappearance Arc
