sections.name: I. The One O'Clock Post
sections.overview:
One in the morning at Peach's Castle, and the castle was awake. The account is specific about why: the kart races were on. Somewhere in the building a hall of Toads was watching a broadcast, and the noise of it came down the corridors in waves — a cheer, a groan, the particular silence of a last lap — so that a guard standing a lantern post on the ceremonial route could follow the race without seeing it.

John Lee [[prop:prop_john_lee_night_posting|stood the post]]. Ceremonial guard: a lantern in one hand, a sword at the hip that the kingdom had issued for the look of it, livery pressed, the instruction to stand where the lamp made the castle look guarded. He had a small son asleep somewhere in the household wing, or so he believed at one o'clock. The account does not say how long he had held the post. It says he was good at standing.

Two things were being talked about by every Toad who passed him, and he collected both. The first was the prisoner. There was a prisoner in the dungeon — captured, held, *tense* was the word that travelled with him — and nobody who said the word prisoner would say what the prisoner was. The second was the meeting. Mario and Luigi were expected. They were coming to the castle that night to mediate a meeting with *this toad guy*, and the account never names the Toad, because the guards who said it did not know either.

John Lee jumped. The account counts it: four times, straight up, lantern and all, at the news that the brothers were coming to the building he was standing in. The head guard came down the route to find out what a ceremonial post was doing bouncing, and questioned him. The account records the questions as a formality and the jumping as the only honest thing anybody did before midnight became one.

*WAH. A kingdom a month from losing its princess, and the palace is up late for a kart race, talking about a prisoner nobody will describe to a guard they have put next to a lamp. I have read a great many accounts of the last weeks of the reign. This is the first one in which the building sounds like a building.*
sections.waluigi_note: The race is a time anchor, and the only one the account gives above ground. A broadcast at one in the morning is a repeat or a late card, and the castle watching it at that hour tells me the court kept the hours of people who did not expect to be assassinated. The prisoner's species was withheld from the guards on purpose — every Toad who passed John Lee knew there was a prisoner and not one knew it was a Koopa. That is not secrecy about a prisoner. That is secrecy about a guest.

sections.name: II. The Keys to Every Door
sections.overview:
Toadsworth came down the route after the head guard had gone. The account calls him the chancellor and describes the suit first: new, cut for him, worn the way a Toad wears a thing he has just been given and has decided he deserved. He did not question John Lee about the jumping. He explained the building to him.

*"I have the keys to every door,"* he said. Not as a threat; as an inventory. A chamberlain's sentence — the account did not know that, and said chancellor, and I have left the word where the guard put it and the man where I believe he stands.

Then, to a ceremonial guard with a lantern who had jumped four times because the Mario brothers were coming: *"Bask in your inferiority."* And on down the corridor, in the new suit, with the keys.

*I have read the son. The son would not say that to a guard — the son would write a memorandum about the guard. The father, by every account that is not the Regency's, was a Toad who had recently been given something and wanted to be seen holding it. A month before Highsun 1 he had the keys to every door and told a guard so. The journals, if they are his, say the positions were cleared. The keys clear positions.*
sections.waluigi_note: The attribution problem, stated once and plainly. The account says 'the chancellor'. In 955 BF both Toadsworths were in the palace and the son was already styled Chancellor; it is the son the Highsun 1 record shows finding the figure in the chimney and taking a beam from Fawful for it. The man who told a guard he had the keys to every door and, later this night, told the Mages' Guild whom to dispatch of is a man with the household's keys and the Guild's ear — which is the Chamberlain, Toadsworth the Elder, and which is also precisely what his disputed journals confess to. I file him as the Elder. If a second account names the son, I will amend this note and apologise to nobody, because a reading stated as a reading is not a lie.

sections.name: III. Lost, in Order
sections.overview:
After the suit went by, John Lee left the post. The account does not say he was relieved and does not say he deserted; it says he went to find where the brothers would be, and then it says, in order, where he was instead.

The ballroom first. Trumpets — a fanfare being rehearsed or performed at one in the morning, the account cannot tell which — and Toads marching, in step, across the ballroom floor, in a formation that had nothing to do with a kart race and that nobody explained to a guard with a lantern. He backed out.

A corridor of heavy Toads next: big ones, armoured, standing shoulder to shoulder in a wall formation across a passage, facing outward, not moving, not speaking. He did not try to pass them. He went another way.

The dining hall. And here the account slows down, because at the long table, past midnight, with the kart race audible through the wall, sat a small Toad boy with a plate in front of him and a maid beside him — *Marilyn*, the account names her, the only servant it names — and the boy was his. Toad Lee, awake, at the table, being minded. John Lee saw his son and his son's minder and the account records that he did not stop, because he was a guard who had left his post and was in a room he had no business in, and because a boy at a table with a maid is a boy who is fine.

A hooded figure passed him in the next corridor. Robed, head covered, walking with purpose toward the part of the castle he had just come from. The account notes it and moves on, because at that hour, in that building, a hood was a thing that went past you.

Then a tower, and a storage room at the top of it — crates, dust, the race very faint through the stone — and that is where the guards found him.

*Five rooms. I have read the plans of Peach's Castle; it is a building that gets people lost on purpose. But read the order back. A ballroom rehearsing a procession. A wall of heavy Toads holding a corridor. A hood going toward the dungeon. The guard thought he was lost. He was walking through the Arrangement being set up, room by room, and every room was a thing that would be explained the next morning as perfectly normal.*
sections.waluigi_note: The dining hall is the paragraph I would least like to be wrong about, so I will be exact about what it supports. It places Toad Lee — the Disaster Inc. Toad Lee, by John Lee's own identification of his son — in Peach's Castle, as a small child, in the care of a chambermaid, on a night in Efferd 955 BF. It does not place him anywhere on Highsun 1. It does not make him kin to the magistrate Toad Lee the Elder, who signed the evacuation order that day; it only makes the question unavoidable. What it does establish is who had the boy last before the Guild did: Marilyn. The account never sees her again.

sections.name: IV. Escorted
sections.overview:
Two guards. The account does not give them names and does not give them anger; they found a ceremonial post in a storage tower and did what the night's orders apparently said to do with a ceremonial post that was somewhere it should not be, which was to walk it down to the dungeon.

The account is not clear on whether the dungeon was a punishment, a reassignment, or simply the place where spare guards were being put that night, and I have decided the ambiguity is the guard's and not mine. He went. The lantern went with him. Down past the kitchens, down a stair, down a second stair, into stone that did not carry the race any more.

*Everybody who touched this Toad tonight moved him toward the cell. The suit lectured him off his post. The building funnelled him. Two guards escorted him the last of the way. I am not saying the castle conspired to put one ceremonial guard in front of the handshake — I am saying that if it had, the account would read exactly like this.*
sections.waluigi_note: I have tried to make the escort mean something and it will not. Two guards, unnamed, with an order. The one thing I can say is that the dungeon was staffed thinly enough that a lantern post could be sent down to it, which fits a cell that was never meant to hold anyone.

sections.name: V. The Unlocked Cell
sections.overview:
The cell door was not locked. The account is emphatic: not forced, not open — unlocked, standing as a door stands when the lock has been turned by somebody with a key and left that way. One of the escort put a hand on it and it moved.

The prisoner was a Koopa.

He was not surprised by the door. He was surprised by the faces. The account gives his first words in full, and they are the hinge of the night: *"So you finally came to free me —"* and then, looking at a ceremonial guard with a lantern and two Toads in corridor livery, *"— oh. It's you."*

He had been expecting somebody. The door had been unlocked for that somebody. John Lee, a guard who had not known the prisoner was a Koopa until the lantern found him, had walked in on an appointment.

And the escort fell. One of the two Toads who had walked him down — the account says only that he fell, dead, between one breath and the next, with no blade in him that John Lee saw and no sound that he heard. The lantern shook. The other escort is not mentioned again, and I have read the passage a dozen times trying to find him.

*"Oh. It's you." A prisoner who knows what free looks like and knows that this is not it. I have been handed a hundred pieces of paper about the Arrangement and not one of them had a voice. This one has a voice and the voice is bored.*
sections.waluigi_note: The escort's death is unexplained in the account and I am not going to explain it for him. What the record supports: he died beside an unlocked cell in the half-minute before a bean and three Guild hoods walked in, with no visible wound, and the hood John Lee passed in the corridor was walking this way. A reader may put those together. I have, and I have put it in the leads, not the prose.

sections.name: VI. The Handshake
sections.overview:
Fawful came in. The account describes him as a Toad would who had never seen one: small, green, the glasses, the teeth, the voice that arrives before the body does. He went to the Koopa and the Koopa put out a hand and Fawful took it.

*"I HAVE VICTORY,"* Fawful said, which the account records in capitals because that is how it was said.

*"Never thought I'd work with a bean,"* the Koopa said, which the account records as the only thing anybody in that corridor said in a normal voice.

Three hooded figures came in behind Fawful. Mages' Guild — the account knows the robes, every Toad in the palace knew the robes — and they did not greet the Koopa and did not greet the bean. One of them said what they had come to say. *The guild is already in place.* And then: *we won't act yet.*

John Lee was still holding the lantern. The account is honest that nobody had yet looked at him, that a ceremonial guard with a dead escort at his feet had been, for the length of a handshake, furniture.

Then he ran.

*Three sentences and the whole file turns over. 'I have victory' — the bean already counts it won, a month out. 'Never thought I'd work with a bean' — the Koopa is working, not conspiring; he has an employer. 'The Guild is already in place; we won't act yet' — the Guild is not joining a plot. The Guild is the schedule. The journals say the Guild provided the method. Here is the Guild explaining that the method is installed and the date is not tonight.*
sections.waluigi_note: Compare the Guild's sentence to the Highsun 1 record, where the Guild is 'already positioned' — scrubbing the chambers, snapping fingers at a Chancellor, in the vault during the killing. The same adverb, a month apart, from the Guild's own mouth. I did not expect the archive to be handed the word 'already' twice. The image on this filing is the corridor at this instant; the artist has drawn the hoods with their hands lit, which the account does not say, and I have left it because something put the escort on the floor.
sections.imageCaption: The handshake. The cell door open behind the Koopa, Fawful's teeth, the three hoods, the escort down, and the lantern. The account says nobody had looked at the guard yet.

sections.name: VII. SURPRISE, IT'S ME
sections.overview:
He ran up the stairs toward the only authority he had been questioned by that night, and found the captain, and told him: the cell is unlocked, the prisoner is a Koopa, there is a bean, there are hoods, the escort is dead. The account does not record the captain's answer, because the captain did not get to give it.

The wall came in.

*"SURPRISE, IT'S ME,"* said Bowser, through the dust, at a hall of Toads who had been watching a kart race. He had come to the meeting. He said so: *"I wasn't invited to the meeting."* He looked for the brothers and announced that they were not here, which was true, and seemed to disappoint him more than the Toads did.

Then he breathed fire down the hall.

The captain stood in it. The account is brief about the captain's death in the way that accounts by people who were standing next to the person are brief: the fire went down the corridor, the captain was between the fire and the stair up to the royal apartments, and then there was no captain. John Lee was behind him and lived.

*"Take me to Peach,"* Bowser said, to whoever was left.

And this is the line the file has been waiting fifteen years for without knowing it: when the bean's name came up — the account is not clear who said it, somebody in the smoke — Bowser did not know it. *He didn't know Fawful.* The Koopa King, a month before the Highsun 1 narrative made him Fawful's partner in the murder, stood in the ruins of a wall asking who that was.

*Two intruders in one castle in one night and they had never met. Bowser came for Peach the way he always came for Peach — loud, through a wall, asking for her by name — and was annoyed the brothers were not there to make it a proper evening. Fawful came through the dungeon with the Guild. Thirty days after Highsun 1 the kingdom decided these were the same visit. The guard who was in both rooms says they were not.*
sections.waluigi_note: The captain's death is the night's second body and the first one with a cause: Bowser's fire, in a corridor, at a Toad who did not move. I want to be fair to Bowser about the next part — the account does not say the captain was the target; it says the captain was between the fire and the stair. The Highsun 1 record has Luigi beating Bowser in a corridor of this castle a month later. The archive is accumulating corridors.

sections.name: VIII. The Sash and the Letter
sections.overview:
What a ceremonial guard does when the captain is gone and the hall is burning is, by this account, inventory. There was a dead Toad near him — a guard, not the captain, one of the ones the fire had reached first — and John Lee took three things from the floor.

The shortsword. His own was ceremonial; this one was not, and the account records that he knew the difference by the weight.

A letter, from the dead Toad's livery, which he read by the fire: [[prop:prop_bean_shop_letter|*meet me in Fawful's bean shop.*]] No signature the account mentions. An address, in effect, on the body of a palace guard who had been standing in a hall waiting for the Mario brothers.

And the captain's sash — scorched, the account says, but whole — which he wound around both forearms, the way a Toad binds his arms for a fight he does not expect to win or to ask permission for. He was a ceremonial guard. He knew what a captain's sash was for and he knew it was not for this, and he put it on anyway.

Around him, through the dust, the Goombas were coming in behind Bowser and taking Toads. The account uses the word kidnapping; it does not count them. It records that it was happening and that nobody was stopping it, because everybody who might have was dead, on fire, or watching the Koopa King.

*A dead palace guard with directions to a bean shop in his coat. Think about what that means for the hall. The Guild was in the dungeon; the Koopa was in the dungeon; Fawful was in the dungeon; and up here, among the Toads waiting for Mario, at least one guard already had the address. The Arrangement was not a thing happening beneath the castle. It was a thing the castle was already full of.*
sections.waluigi_note: The letter is filed as an exhibit and argued over in the capital file. On the record here: it was found on a palace guard, not on a conspirator, and it was found before the bean shop had been mentioned to John Lee by anyone. He went to the shop because a dead Toad's pocket told him to. The sash is also filed, as the account describes it, so that the next person who sees a Toad with a captain's sash on both arms knows whose it was.

sections.name: IX. One Small Orb
sections.overview:
A Mages' Guild member ended it. The account is clear that it was one hood, one object — *a small orb*, held up, not thrown — and that Bowser went down. Not staggered; down, at once, the way a thing goes down when the thing that was holding it up has been switched off. One shot. The Koopa King on the floor of Peach's Castle with his fire still smoking in the walls.

And the Toads cheered. The account says it without comment, which is the comment: the hall that had been burning cheered the Guild, the hoods were heroes, and the mages who had been in the dungeon shaking hands with a Koopa twenty minutes earlier were the mages who had saved the castle.

Mario and Luigi arrived then. Late — the account is precise that Bowser was already on the floor — into a hall that smelled of fire and relief, to a cheer that was not for them. Luigi tripped on a striped sock. The account does not say whose; a striped sock on the floor of a palace hall at two in the morning after a kart race and a dragon is a thing the account notes and I note and neither of us can source.

*One small orb. Bowser, who a month later would be dragged unconscious across a corridor of this building and told he was not authorised to know the woman he loved was dead — put down in one by a Guild hood with something the size of a fist, in front of witnesses, to applause. I have no name for the orb. I have put it on the technology ledger as what it did. The brothers walking in behind the applause is the saddest sentence in the account and the guard did not know it was sad; he was still a fan.*
sections.waluigi_note: The orb goes on the technology ledger because the archive files what it is shown working, and it was shown working on Bowser. One object, hand-held, one use, one result: a Large dragon-turtle unconscious. Nothing the archive has from the Guild in 1040 looks like it, which is either because they stopped making it or because they stopped showing it. The cheer is on the record because it is the first dated instance of the Mages' Guild being loved inside Peach's Castle, and the kill order follows it by about a minute.

sections.name: X. A Lost Dog
sections.overview:
John Lee said it. Into the cheer, with the captain's sash on both arms and a dead Toad's sword, to a hall of grateful Toads and two late brothers: the Guild works with Fawful. He had seen the handshake. He said so.

Toadsworth answered — the new suit, from the edge of the hall, in the voice of a Toad who has the keys. The account gives it as three sentences. *"Like a lost dog."* Then: *"A nuisance to the Toads is a nuisance to us."* Then, to the hoods who had just been cheered: *"Mages' Guild — dispatch of them."*

A bolt came. The account says a bolt — from a hood's hand, across the hall, at a ceremonial guard — and it missed, because John Lee was already moving, because he had been moving since the dungeon and had not stopped. He went down and out and away, into the part of the castle that does not carry the race, and the hall went back to cheering.

*Read the three sentences as policy. The first makes him an animal. The second makes him the Toads' problem and therefore 'ours' — a chamberlain speaking for the Guild, or with it. The third is an order to the Mages' Guild, given in public, by the man with the keys, and obeyed. The journals say the Regency provided the opportunity. Here is the Regency, a month early, providing one.*
sections.waluigi_note: The Loyalists would give a great deal for this paragraph and that is exactly why I have been careful with it. It is a guard's account of a sentence said across a burning hall. It is not a journal, it is not a confession, and it is not notarised. It is, however, the only version of 'the arrangement' in the archive in which the chamberlain is a man speaking rather than a dead man's handwriting, and the man said *dispatch of them* in front of two brothers who, by this account, did nothing. I have opened a lead on that too.

sections.name: XI. Five Hours Under the Castle
sections.overview:
The account's clock stops at the bolt and restarts five hours later, and the five hours are the warp system. The pipes under Peach's Castle — the drains, the sewers, the old warp lines that the castle's basements are threaded with — and a ceremonial guard with a lantern going through them in the dark with a letter's worth of destination.

One Goomba found him. He stomped it. The account is almost shy about it: the first thing he had ever killed, a Goomba in a drain, flattened under a ceremonial boot, and it counted — the account says it counted, that the guard felt it count, which is a thing accounts say when the table has said so.

Then a pipe, and more Goombas out of it — an ambush, the account calls it, a warp pipe mouth and Goombas coming out of it at a Toad who had just learned he could stomp — and he got through it, and the account does not say how, and I believe that too, because the people who get through things in the dark rarely know how.

Five hours. Then a grate, then a cellar, then a shop.

*The warp system under the castle is on the technology ledger already as infrastructure, and I will add nothing to the entry except this: a lost ceremonial guard with a lantern navigated it from the dungeon to a specific shop in Toad Town in five hours, with a letter for a map. Either the drains are better signposted than the castle, or the shop is closer to the dungeon than any honest shop should be.*
sections.waluigi_note: The five hours are the only duration the account states outright and I have built the timeline on them. One stomp, one ambush, no other beats; the guard's XP for the night is awarded on this section's two Goomba encounters and on the survival of everything above it, and is a preview until the table confirms it, as every award on an event is.

sections.name: XII. The Bean Badge
sections.overview:
Fawful's Bean Badge: a bean shop, in Toad Town, with Fawful's name on it and [[prop:prop_bean_badge_shop_card|a tray of badges on the counter]], which the account walked into at dawn with a sash on its arms and found already occupied. The Koopa was there. The prisoner — out of the castle, ahead of a Toad who had crawled five hours to reach the address — sitting in the shop as though he had never been anywhere else.

He explained himself, and the account gives the explanation plainly. He had led the escort into the ambush. He had alerted the castle to Bowser's attack — it was he who had told them the Koopa King was coming. Two sentences, and the night above rearranged itself: the dead escort was his; the castle had known about Bowser; the unlocked cell had been the one honest door in the building.

Two Mages' Guild operatives. A Goomba, sitting by the door like a shop cat. And Fawful.

They told him about his son before he asked. *"Your son is being taken care of,"* one of the Guild said. *"Toad Lee won't have to worry about being trafficked in our care."* The account records the sentence whole and records that John Lee did not answer it.

They told him about the castle. Bowser was waking — screaming, the account says; the ground shaking under Toad Town with it — and the brothers were busy with him, which was the point. That was what Bowser was for.

They asked him to join.

Then Fawful explained the plan, and put on a cloak to do it. A Mages' Guild cloak, over the red, pulled up. *"I HAVE PLAN,"* in capitals, and the plan was a mushroom. The vacuum shroom — Fawful's own make, the account says, Fawful tech — which, inhaled, turns the inhaler into a vacuum: Bowser breathes it and sucks up everything in reach, the brothers included. The castle's wards were still active, which somebody in the shop said as a problem and Fawful said as a detail. The Koopa had a fat vial — the account calls it that, *the fat vial*, a glass thing with weight in it — and the shroom was to go into Bowser by way of it. *"Dispatch of this finkrat and takeover kingdom,"* Fawful said, in the Guild's cloak, and the two operatives did not correct the pronoun.

John Lee said he wanted to disappear.

Then he said he wanted his son.

Then he asked the Guild for escorts to go and get him, and the Guild said the last sentence of the account: *"Are you stupid? You just said you don't trust us. We're protecting your son."*

*A bean in a Guild cloak. Read it slowly: the Guild is already in place, the Guild will not act yet, and the Guild has given Fawful its robe to wear while he explains how the Koopa King is going to swallow the Mario brothers. Thirty days after Highsun 1 the kingdom chose Bowser as its murderer over Fawful, and the archive has never understood why the first draft said Fawful and the second did not. Here is a reason: by the time anyone was choosing, Fawful was wearing the Guild.*
sections.waluigi_note: The shop card is filed as an exhibit — a Bean Badge card, which is what a shop like this hands you, and which the account says was on the counter. The vacuum shroom and the fat vial go on the technology ledger as described and not one word further; the account does not see them used. The provenance of the whole account, promised in the opening: it was played, at the table, as a session in 955 BF, with John Lee as the character at it, and reached this desk as every session reaches this desk — as the record of what the table saw, in the order the table saw it. The archive has one account. It has filed it as one account. That is the last honest sentence available tonight.
sections.imageCaption: Fawful's Bean Badge at dawn, as the account has it: the jars, the badge tray on the counter, Fawful pulling the Guild's cloak on with the vacuum shroom in his other hand, the Koopa with the fat vial, two hoods, a Goomba on a sack by the door, and a ceremonial guard with a captain's sash on both arms who has just been asked whether he is stupid. The sign over the counter is as the account remembers it, which is to say not well.

timeline.day: Efferd, 955 BF — a kart night; the day inferred, the hours the account's
timeline.note: Reconstructed, not witnessed. Waluigi was not born; the archive had nobody in the building. The times are the account's own two clock readings — one o'clock at the post and five hours of pipe — with the archive's order laid between them. The month is inferred: the last month before Highsun 1, from the Guild's 'we won't act yet' set against the journals' 'six months prior', and from a castle still watching kart races. Nothing in the account names a day.
timeline.method: Duration anchors: the one o'clock post, stated; a kart broadcast, which runs as long as a kart broadcast runs; four jumps; one handshake; one wall; one orb; and five hours of drain, stated. The hall and the dungeon are ordered by the account; the five rooms are ordered by the guard, who was lost, and the archive has not improved on his order.

worlds.label: Peach's Castle, 955 BF — the building, the dungeon, the drains
worlds.timeOfDay: One in the morning to about six: the post, the five rooms, the dungeon, the hall on fire, the bolt, the pipes. The account never looks out of a window until it comes up through a grate in Toad Town at dawn.
worlds.weather: No weather on record, and the archive files that as a finding. The account is indoors from the first line to the last — a lantern post on a ceremonial route, a ballroom, a dining hall, a tower room with no mention of the view, a dungeon, five hours of pipe — and the only sky in it is the grey of a shop window at the end. The kart broadcast through the walls is the closest thing to weather the building had.
worlds.source: The account itself, read for windows and finding none. The RNN did not exist in 955 BF, the WAH Media Collective's back-issue boxes start a century later, and the palace weather log of Efferd 955 — if a palace kept one — is in the same Regency vault as the forty-seven minutes. The archive has asked. The Regency has no comment on matters under ongoing historical review.

Bowser's fire; dust from a wall that came in
Five hours of pipe; no sky
Grey in a shop window; the first daylight in the account

Fawful shakes the Koopa's hand. 'Never thought I'd work with a bean.' Three Guild hoods: 'the guild is already in place; we won't act yet.' John Lee runs.

A dead Toad's shortsword; a letter — 'meet me in Fawful's bean shop'; the captain's sash, wound around both forearms. Goombas taking Toads behind Bowser.

Recruitment. Fawful in a Guild cloak: the vacuum shroom, the fat vial, 'dispatch of this finkrat and takeover kingdom'. John Lee asks for escorts to his son: 'Are you stupid? You just said you don't trust us. We're protecting your son.'

name: The Soul-Ring, the Feywild Wildfire, and the Twenty-One Day Cut
title: The Soul-Ring, the Feywild Wildfire, and the Twenty-One Day Cut: A Wakeful Toad, Cornburary's Requisition, the Combat Chirurgeon, and the Card Room Under the Pantry
date: 2-3 Aethel, 922 BF (Feyward clock) — continuing without a break from the sanctuary floor collapse and the lower quarters
timeWindow: Early hours, following the collapse of the sanctuary floor and the breach into the servant levels; the card-room reveal falls after the Oracle's three weeks were agreed in the basement (3 Aethel, 01:30). The record gives no hour, so it is estimated at about 05:00 on 3 Aethel: roughly three to four hours of waking tied up, the Cornburary confrontation, the wildfire, the Soul-Ring pledge and the dumbwaiter crawl to the card room, picking up from the rest of the night in the previous filing
era: 922 BF (Feyward Clock)
location: The Overgrown Manor — Colour Division Quarters, Lady's Inner Sanctum, Servant Common Room, and the Goblin Card Room
type: Session / Field Incident
status: Filed / Audited
summary: Toad Lee awakens from a daydream of his father to find himself tied in overgrown quarters beside an uncuffed Waluigi. After learning their guards are the Iron Legion's Colour Division, they confront Quartermaster Cornburary before Toad Lee's emotional surge triggers a torrential Feywild wildfire. Meanwhile, Hjumpik proposes to Lady Aurelia with a soul ring to break her power, losing his trousers in the scuffle before dragging her to safety. Guided by Brad the waiter, the party navigates a rotted common room to the goblin card room, where Brad reveals the Feywild will be severed in twenty-one days.
description: Waluigi files this one as the session where Toad Lee woke up from a daydream of his father with an axe to find himself tied in an overgrown bedroom, where Quartermaster Cornburary claimed to have shadow writers, and where Hjumpik dropped to one knee, proposed to Lady Aurelia, and promptly lost his pants. In between, Toad Lee proved that Feywild weather reacts to personal fury—unleashing thunder, hail, and wildfire upon the Iron Legion—while Brad the waiter guided the party past a rotted two-story drop to the goblin card room, where dirty cleaning supplies were wagered and the twenty-one day destruction of the plane was spoken out loud.

sections.name: A Scene of Wild Overgrowth
sections.subtitle: the daydream of an axe, the unlocked cuffs, and the story got mostly right
sections.overview:
Toad Lee wakes up full of expression, still tied up in the room.

A scene of wild overgrowth unfolds before you. Where once was a rather spacious living quarters, now the space is filled with twisting and coiling roots and vines. Soft green moss and clover grows in through the seams of the floor, its invasion bringing subtle bits of green to an otherwise very brown room.

Of the numerous windows that line the walls of this large room only a few of them let light filter in, the rest having overgrown with vines.

The room features a large wardrobe, a fine writing deck and a four post bed that's taken on a life of its own. The rest of the space appears to be worn and water damaged but structurally sound.

He comes to his senses. He snaps out of it as if he was having a daydream throughout the majority of everything.

Toad Lee grunts up, walks around. Waluigi sits there, handcuffs still on but unlocked.

"Where am I, Waluigi? I was in a plain field with bright green grass, clear blue skies, there was a hill. I saw what seems to be my dad. We were play fighting. I was fighting with the axe I have, he was fighting with his? I don't know, I have some snippets of my father... ehh don't know."

"You want to go back?" Waluigi says.

"No, this is important. Remind me what happened."

"He offered us to see Aurelia. He sold us out."

"That can't be. Was he backed into a corner?"

"Well, we could have fought them, but I guess he was in a corner, they were chasing us." Waluigi walks to the chair. "There was a bunch of guards chasing us. Hjumpik wanted to see Aurelia. He gave us up because he had no choice, or because of selfishness."

"Maybe, I'm not sure."

The guards say he got the story mostly right.

"Sorry my sirs, didn't mean to," Toad Lee says. "While I wait for rescue, might as well look around."
sections.waluigi_note: WAH. He woke up dreaming of play fighting his father on a grassy hill with axes, and within twenty seconds he had to process unlocked handcuffs, an overgrown four-post bed, and the fact that our dwarf traded us for an audience with a plant. I gave him the honest version: Hjumpik either had no choice or did it out of selfishness, and the guards agreed with my arithmetic.

sections.name: The Books in Elven and the Colour Division
sections.subtitle: the writing desk, the wrong denizens, and the leverage plan
sections.overview:
The few books sitting on or slipped into this writing desk's shelves are mostly journals, logbooks, and references. They are all written in elven.

Toad Lee asks for paper and a pen from Waluigi. Waluigi hands him his writing kit.

Toad Lee asks the guards if they can speak elvish.

"What? We don't know that."

"What do you mean you don't know this? Weren't you guys denizens of the Feywild?"

"Huh? We're the Colour Division of the Iron Legion."

"Wa?" Toad Lee says.

"We were sent here to capture Hjumpik. We needed you guys as leverage, and our plan is working. Once Aurelia beats up Hjumpik, we grab him and drag him out."

"You're very confident that will happen, aren't you?"

"Yes we are, as we are of Mr. Miser."
sections.waluigi_note: WAH. He asked the guards if they speak elvish because we are in a fairy manor, and they looked at him like he had insulted their mothers. Special forces. The Colour Division. They don't speak elvish, they don't care about the flora, and they brought handcuffs because a dwarf owes hours on a contract.

sections.name: A Better Archivist Than Your Friend
sections.subtitle: Quartermaster Cornburary enters, the tennis racket threat, and shadow writers
sections.overview:
Quartermaster Cornburary enters the room. He smiles: "Yes, yes, our plans are well."

"Who are you?" Toad Lee asks.

"Cornburary."

"Cornburary of the Legion... you don't have a weapon on you. Are you a combatant here like your guards?"

"Is that a threat? Go ahead, hit me, see what happens."

"No, it's not a threat, I'm just asking."

"No, no, I don't need to get rough. I need to get Hjumpik."

"I'm just asking you a question, man. Would you please answer my question?"

"I am a journalist."

"A journalist?"

"Well, not really. A bookkeeper, an archivist even. A better one than your friend over there."

Waluigi shouts: "WAH! I'll take you out!"

"You sure are confident of yourself, you sure you can take him on?" Toad Lee asks.

Cornburary smirks: "I don't need to. I have a bunch of shadow writers that will do it for me."

Waluigi gets his tennis racket. Toad Lee says: "No, no!" He swipes at his racket; Waluigi backs up.

"Friendly fire! You're threatening my livelihood!"

"Don't attack yet. I'm banged up, we're in a tricky situation, Waluigi. We can't afford making another rash decision. We don't know what's going on entirely. Have a little restraint for me please, if not for yourself. Who will archive... uhhh, me when I'm gone or something?" Toad Lee says.

"Well, I will outlast you. WAH, fine."

"I'll repay you somehow," Toad Lee says. "I assume they sent you in the Feywild to hunt down Archie as well?"

"Archie is secondary," they say.

"Hjumpik's dead, or—"

"No, no."
sections.waluigi_note: WAH. A bureaucrat walked through the door with no weapon, looked at my writing kit, and told me he had shadow writers who could do my job better. I pulled the Phase Spider gut racket out. Toad Lee swiped at it and called it friendly fire! You do not threaten an archivist's livelihood in his own filing.

sections.name: You Look Ravishing Tonight
sections.subtitle: the ash of the satyr, the spiky ring, and the pants that fell down
sections.overview:
Shift to Hjumpik.

Aurelia touches the satyr, burns him, turns him to ash.

"It's a sham," Hjumpik says.

"Haven't you forgotten something important? This is my manor."

Hjumpik says: "I'm Hjumpik, so ho ho ho, I'm not afraid, and this isn't my manor."

"With one touch, you will be gone too." She walks closer over the dust.

He takes out the glowing ring. He points it towards her.

"Huh, is that wedding ring? You're proposing to me?"

"Do something," Hjumpik whispers to the ring.

Hjumpik gets on one knee: "You're right, I am proposing to you. Put on this ring, ignore everything I said before. You look ravishing tonight."

Lady Aurelia smiles, getting out a ring with a spike in it.

"In fey culture males put on the ring. We will be bound once you put it in. It will slowly suck your lifeforce," she says.

"Oh really, wow, that's terrifying. But will this save my friends? Will you stand down?"

"Yes, of course. I'll release this manor from my shackles and focus them on you."

"Wow, it's almost like we are married."

Hjumpik shows his ring finger up. He jams the soul ring onto her finger!

She says: "Yaoui Dhayemmn Dhwayelf!"

"You... you idiot!" She smiles, "I order you to take it off!"

Hjumpik uncontrollably takes her ring up. She falls, her power weakening. She grabs Hjumpik's pants—they fall!

Guards run in: "WHAT THE? WITH THE LADY? WE CAUGHT YOU WITH YOUR PANTS DOWN!"

"Let's go back to your friends, the toad and purple one. This will be in the report."

"I need to check on the lady with something," Hjumpik slashes vines to the bathroom door and drags the body inside with him.

They shout: "NOW YOU'RE GOING TO THE BATHROOM WITH HER? GET BACK HERE!"
sections.waluigi_note: WAH. Read the transcript! He got on one knee, told a plant demon she looked ravishing tonight, jammed a soul ring onto her hand, and lost his trousers to her dying grip. The Legion caught him pants-down and promised it would be in the official military report. I could not make this up if I had ten shadow writers.

sections.name: The Men in Silver and the Reactive Emotion
sections.subtitle: the elven book on feelings, the CCC syringe, and the slip out the window
sections.overview:
Cut to Toad Lee.

Toad Lee remembers something about the Feywild: the environment of the Feywild is reactive to a person's emotions.

"Mutsdoppms apnd yoput hopw mutsdoppms capn apffetct det fetywapdd" the book is said. Toad Lee looks over it.

"Yes, yes, my men in silver come in." Cordon Combat Chirurgeon comes in.

"We are the CCC. We have to come eliminate the Feywild. With this solution we can simply inject the plants killing them."

Toad Lee mutters: "Great, another egocentric character... Dang, I do have a question. Why do you want to destroy the Feywild?"

"It is unpure."

"Define unpure."

"It does not follow the natural way of life."

"If you're trying to control it, it will be hard. Why do you want to?"

"Because we can."

"Wow, you're power-hungry."

Quartermaster Cornburary says: "We're not greedy."

"Waluigi, check outside for any probes."

Waluigi smiles, says "Okay," and heads to the window.

Toad Lee says: "This place has land and leaders. I don't think people, natives, will appreciate you guys taking it over. Foreigners conquering planes."

"Such is the way of life. No one likes being conquered, but that is what we do."

"Really, that's the only reason?"

Waluigi slips out.

"Well, not the only reason. Because the material plane is cur—"

Quartermaster Cornburary says: "Shut up, you! Too much information!" They start arguing.

Toad Lee cuts in: "No, no, no, please continue! You're from the Legion, right? And that's an Iron Legion uniform that you're wearing. What's the logo of the Legion, your heraldry?"

"You trying to get information from me? You won't, not even from that birdbrain over there."

"Fine, but I'll find out later on. That big emblem is telling me otherwise. We have a friend in yellow that has been feeding us quadrants. You will meet more of us in the material plane."
sections.waluigi_note: WAH. The CCC brought a syringe of weedkiller to prune a dimension because it is 'unpure' and 'because we can.' Toad Lee stalled them with heraldry questions while I slipped out the window to check for probes. Bureaucracy cannot handle a conversation where someone asks 'define unpure.'

sections.name: Thunder, Hail, and Fire Everywhere
sections.subtitle: the emotional climate surge, the burnt journals, and jumping out the window
sections.overview:
Toad Lee is getting a little angry. Then thunder, then rain, hail pouring—FIRE EVERYWHERE!

"What the... woah, woah!" as he feels heat.

"Huh, so it actually worked, holy heck!" Toad Lee says.

Toad Lee takes the books. Some of them are burnt; he takes some that are not burnt while leaving others that are not entirely burnt.

Toad Lee slowly reaches towards the window. It is open, and Waluigi is gone.

"What the dang," he whispers.

He escapes as well, not without saying: "Listen man, the Feywild is not the type of place you want to set up shop outside of your imperialistic tendencies. Leave the Feywild alone! It has people living inside of it, they won't be happy when they find denizens invading on their own. Be warned!"

With that, Toad Lee jumps out the window.
sections.waluigi_note: WAH. He read one page of an elven book about mushroom feelings and summoned a localized apocalypse out of his own irritation. Thunder, hail, and wildfire! He grabbed the books, gave an anti-imperialist speech to a burning room, and threw himself out a window. Spectacular form.

sections.name: The Ceilings and the Waiter Guy
sections.subtitle: the princess carry, the worm in the eye, and Brad's briefing on P.S.
sections.overview:
Cut to Hjumpik in the past, before the fire and craziness.

In the bathroom with Aurelia, he looks up at the ceiling. Same hole.

Hjumpik tosses Aurelia. She falls back into his arms. *Princess carrying,* Hjumpik thinks.

He tosses her again; she falls flat.

He uses his warhammer again; she lands on the second floor.

Hjumpik examines the lady. A worm comes out of her soulless eyes!

"Ugg, we got to get you to safety. Let's get out of here. I hope Waluigi knows what to do."

He opens a door. It hits something. He quickly goes back, tries another door, and peeks out. Brad stands there. He doesn't recognize him at first, but then does.

"Are you the waiter guy?"

"You're still alive? Thought you died back there."

"I don't die that easily. Just want to get out."

"Get out? Where? There's nowhere to go."

"Why you sound so down?"

"This place is too chaotic. We have to stabilize it somehow."

"We should stabilize it actually, right?"

"Listen, there's someone here... well, a bit of people. They're invaders. They call themselves the Iron Legion. I'm not sure what they want, but they've been encroaching, and it seems with the power vacuum they might want to kidnap and take the lady for themselves."

"Yeah, I know."

"Their commander, P.S., I think her name is, I don't know what it stands for. I think she's working with other legionnaires from the outside world. She is leading the Sunflower Division. I'm not sure what other division is, but they're cooperating and they seem to want to kill or at least take out the two people of this manor. You don't want to take them out, do you?"

"No... that's not my goal here. I just want to help, get out of there, do what I need to do."

"Good, good. Just this way."

Fire spouts from the ground!

"Aaah, what's going on?!"

He opens a door: "What's in that door?"

"The bathroom!"

"You have water on you, something that can dampen these flames at all?"

Hjumpik runs through the fire grabbing the other guy. He uses his dwarven healing skills to heal himself: "Whatever, I'm out."
sections.waluigi_note: WAH. The waiter survived! Brad, who was pouring tea while the house was being swallowed by roots, is now running counter-intelligence on the Sunflower Division. And Hjumpik tossed a countess into the ceiling twice, thought 'princess carry,' and then watched a worm crawl out of her eye.

sections.name: The Mage of Ice
sections.subtitle: the secret kept, the tapped shoulder, and putting out the flames
sections.overview:
Cut to Toad Lee.

Toad Lee says: "What I learned about this place works... Wait, Waluigi, where are you going? WALUIGI!"

He walks more.

"WALUIGI!"

He feels a tap on his shoulder.

"Hmm, what the... Waluigi, don't scare me like that! Why did you run off?"

"Well, because those people, I'm not sure who they are."

"People? Who exactly, from where?"

"That."

"What about the probe the CCC and bald guy mentioned? You see any of them?"

"Hmm, I did, I waved it off, it flew away, who knows where it went."

"I hear you. This fire... this fire, I'm not sure, but I think I'm the cause of it, believe it or not. How did I do it? I know the answer, I don't trust you."

"Don't trust ME? How can I archive the answer to my million of fans?"

"Because knowing you, you will unleash chaos for the sake of it or for your interest. And I don't know, I may not be closest with these Feywild people, but I think they're still people. So... sorry, can't trust you with this secret I know. You understand?"

"Archie would've invited me to his fireball party. Oh well."

"I'll be honest, we have been in this manor for quite some time. I want to regroup with Hjumpik, and I have questions for him. So I guess we regroup, have sessions and downtime, and we decide from there what we do. But I will say we are sitting ducks out here, let's just go back inside and take cover or something."

"Ah, fire," Toad Lee says. "How do we put out fire?"

"They don't call me writer or ice."

"Hmm, they call you that? First time I heard it."

"No worries, mage of ice, work your magic," Toad Lee says.

Waluigi steps into the room; all fire is gone.

"Oh, you really did work your magic!" Toad Lee says.

"Huh, I did... yeah, I did!" Waluigi says.
sections.waluigi_note: WAH. Toad Lee told me to my face that he won't trust me with the weather secret because I would 'unleash chaos for the sake of it.' Then he asked me how to put out the fire. I told him I am the Mage of Ice. I walked into the room, the flames went out, and I took full credit.

sections.name: We Won, But Not the War
sections.subtitle: the reunion, the exorcised demon, and the rotting servant common room
sections.overview:
"Hello," Hjumpik says.

Toad Lee says: "Glad to see you back, we're reunited. Did you sell us out to the Legion for Aurelia?"

Waluigi stays quiet.

"The Legion was trying to capture my—wait, wasn't Waluigi and Toad Lee about to get captured?" Hjumpik says.

"We're reunited," Toad Lee says. "Didn't even have to get in the fire, took damage for nothing. You will be a new man after 8 hours and such. So, is that Aurelia over there?"

"Took the demon out of her. She tried to fight me, I got the demon out... yeah."

"Oh, you removed the demon from her, I hear you," Toad Lee says. "We have Aurelia, she doesn't look too good... everything okay with her?"

"Yeah, I knocked—I didn't, I had to exorcise her."

"I hear you.... yeah... hmm... this guy's going to..."

"Sorry, what?"

Brad says: "Let's get a move on, you can talk while we move."

They all follow him.

Not much is left of this room. The floorboards have rotted away in places, revealing a steep drop down to the library gangways a floor below. For the less fortunate, there is a drop all the way down to the first floor. This must have been a servant's common room at some point, but it has been rendered uninhabitable.

He takes a book out of the bookshelf. It slides up; they walk in silence.
sections.waluigi_note: WAH. 'I had to exorcise her.' That is the official dwarf account of hitting a noblewoman with a warhammer until a worm crawled out of her eye. And then Brad walked us across rotted floorboards with a two-story drop to the library. The hospitality here never stops.

sections.name: Twenty-One Days: The End of the World
sections.subtitle: the goblin card room, the wagers of clothes, and the countdown
sections.overview:
They end up here.

This small room looks like a library exploded into it. The floor is cluttered with as many discarded books as there are huge mushrooms growing out of them.

The table in the center of the room is piled high with a messy stack of cards and is surrounded by a pack of surly goblins playing a rowdy game. Just observing for a moment tells you these games can get quite heated, and the wagers seem to be anything from cleaning supplies to their own clothing.

The same place Hjumpik played cards.

Waluigi says: "Are you sure this is a good idea?"

"Yeah, this is kinda where she went haywire," Hjumpik says. Hjumpik thinks he has his own intentions.

Toad Lee sees a look of determination in Brad's eyes—they're baggy, tired, roughed up, but set.

"If we leave her here, what are we going to do? What's the plan?"

"Not sure," Brad says. "You guys wanted to leave, right? Maybe find whoever wanted to help you leave and uhh just go... I guess. I'll handle it from here."

"Only you? What are you going to do, a push of wind will push you down," Hjumpik says.

"I'll... work something out."

"Hmmm, I still want to help the manor, it's a bit late," Hjumpik says.

"The three beasts of the manor still live... the Bramblyfly, the Revel... it was a complete failure, wasn't it?" Brad says.

"Actually the archivist died at least. How many other guys, are they winning or losing?" Hjumpik says.

"A lot of the plants went away when she got knocked out, but there is still overgrowth and hot spots. This is the Overgrown Manor after all."

"The Revel, the satyrs, did they run away? What's going on with them?" Hjumpik asks.

"Not sure, probably pushing forward with evacuating the whole manor."

"The Revel, what about him, the Revelmaster?"

"I don't know, I have no answers for your questions, I've just been doing my best."

"Cheer up brother, we're winning. That's not what a fighter would act like," Hjumpik says.

"We won, but not the war," Brad says.

"Alright, do something, don't run around like headless chicken."

"I want to get rid of the satyrs and the rebels and try my best or fail trying. I uhh eavesdropped earlier, you know that? They said they're cutting the Feywild in a few days right, or something? 21 days is that it... the end of the world."

"Oh... I see," Hjumpik says.
sections.waluigi_note: WAH. A room where goblins gamble their shirts over dirty cards, surrounded by mushrooms and ruined books. And a waiter with tired eyes looked us in the face and said the quiet part: twenty-one days until they sever the plane. The clock is running.

keyBattles.description: Emotional climate surge triggering Feywild wildfire brambles at the sanctuary threshold.
keyBattles.outcome: Party pushed through the burning thornway into the servants' quarters.

keyBattles.name: Goblin Card Room Standoff
keyBattles.description: Confrontation in the hidden card room behind the servant common room scullery shelf.
keyBattles.outcome: Card room secured; 21-day timeline disclosed by the card dealers.

effects: Lady Aurelia Corvinarus formally accepts Hjumpik's Soul-Ring pledge
The 21-day planar severance countdown is activated across all campaign clocks
A cache of Cordon Combat Syringes is secured by the party
reputationNotes: House Corvinarus views Hjumpik's Soul-Ring pledge as an unprecedented act of chivalric honour, substantially warming relations with Lady Aurelia. The Iron Legion views the property destruction and defiance of Quartermaster Cornburary as an active breach of contract.
aftermath:
**Standing.** Lady Aurelia is unconscious and bound by the soul ring, stripped of her demonic overgrowth authority. The Overgrown Manor remains infested with residual brambles, but the central floral power has broken. The Revel and satyrs are in disorganized retreat or evacuation.

**Custody.** Toad Lee and Waluigi escaped the Colour Division holding room via the emotional wildfire. The Legion's leverage plan collapsed, though Quartermaster Cornburary and the Cordon Combat Chirurgeon remain active in the sector. Lady Aurelia is currently sheltered in the secret goblin card room under Brad's custody.

**The 21-Day Clock.** Brad confirmed that foreign forces intend to sever or prune the Feywild within twenty-one days. This establishes an irreversible operational deadline for all factions within the manor.

**Open threads.** The true identity and orders of Commander P.S. (Sunflower Division) remain uninvestigated. The surviving manor beasts (the Bramblyfly and the Revel remnants) are still active on the grounds. Toad Lee's elven research volumes on emotional climate remain in party possession.
waluigiAssessment:
**1. The proposal was madness, but the mathematics held.** Hjumpik dropped to one knee, called a plant monster ravishing, and shoved a soul ring on her finger. It cost him his dignity and his trousers, but it broke her hold on the building. I have filed many reckless actions in this campaign; this is the only one that ended in a marriage proposal and a military report.

**2. Toad Lee is a walking planar detonator.** The Feywild reacts to emotional climate. Toad Lee got annoyed with a bureaucrat, and the house answered with thunder, hail, and wildfire. He gave an anti-imperialist speech and leapt out a window with a stack of elven books. If he learns to weaponize that temper deliberately, nobody in this house is safe.

**3. Cornburary's shadow writers are a personal insult.** A quartermaster with no sword told me he had an army of scribes who could out-write me. I pulled my Phase Spider racket. Toad Lee called it friendly fire. I am noting for the record that my livelihood was threatened and I showed immense professional restraint.

**4. The CCC represents pure institutional rot.** 'Why destroy the Feywild? Because it is unpure. Because we can.' They brought syringes to purge a dimension. That is not science or defense; it is bureaucratic arrogance with a silver badge.

**5. Brad the waiter is the only competent intelligence operative in the house.** While everyone else was swinging axes or losing their pants, the waiter identified Commander P.S., tracked the Sunflower Division, located a secret sliding bookshelf, and eavesdropped on the twenty-one day planar severance plan. Give that man a tip.

**6. I am the Mage of Ice.** Toad Lee asked how to extinguish a room on fire. I told him they call me writer or ice. I walked in, the fire went out, and I claimed every bit of the credit. History belongs to those who show up when the flames stop.

**7. The twenty-one day clock changes everything.** The goblins are gambling their laundry away while the sky is being prepared for a guillotine. Twenty-one days until the Feywild is severed. We came here looking for an escape; now we are racing a planetary deadline.

name: The Way I Started It
title: The Way I Started It: Fireball, Whispered — the Fall of Feyward Dan, Two Hit Points, and the Fist That Closed the Grove
date: 1 Aethel, 1040 BF — straight on from the sentry arrangement; the scream gets made, and it is not the signal
era: Raventree Crisis — Shadeward Operations / The Skittering Grove / Post-Scorncrow Collapse
location: The Skittering Grove — the grove floor between the fires, the deeper trees Archie ran into, and the stump the plan was built around
type: Grove Battle / Last Spell / Fighting Withdrawal Concluded
status: Concluded — the giant green spider and the ettercaps are dead, Feyward Dan fell and was healed back up, Eager is on two hit points, Archie is out of spells, and the party is going back to the stump to rest instead of after Remi
summary: Straight on from the sentry arrangement. Archie runs deeper into the forest and Eager follows and kills the giant green spider — the grove's best fighter, dead to a Toad scout with blades. Dan, one-armed, drops the longsword for the shield and sets himself to defend the party; Markop watches everyone run away from the actual stump the plan was built around, and stays at it, revving Wario's motorbike. Dan is webbed and falls, and the scream the last filing was listening for gets made — by Archie, for Dan, and not as the signal. Eager wrestles the ettercap and throws Dan to Archie; the catch is missed. Archie puts the body down, faces the ettercaps — 'I'll end this journey the way I started it, with my signature spell' — and whispers Fireball with a tear in his eye. Two ettercaps left, Archie out of spells; Eager's final stand takes one, and he walks backwards into Markop: 'Hello.' Salam puts the bow down and heals Dan; Markop's healing keeps Eager alive at two hit points; Eager takes the electric sphere; Markop shoves Eager aside and ends the last ettercap with his fist. 'What about Remi? We can't rest now' loses to the Toads: back to the stump. The table's own post-mortem: Archie spent every crowd-control spell and everyone left. The Permanent Injury Table, rolled for the one who fell, hands a one-armed paladin row 59 — Sprained Thumb.
description:
The last filing closed on a sound nobody wanted to make. This one opens with it being made — by the wrong person, for the wrong reason, meaning nothing the plan said it would mean — and it closes with a punch.

For the record, the plan had one fixed point. [Markop](#/article/markop) built the sentry arrangement around the tree of the grove — the stump, the way back up, the place everybody was to come to when it turned south. Everything that follows should be read against that stump, because the stump is the only part of the plan that did what it was told.
outcome: The grove fight is concluded. The giant green spider is dead (Eager), the ettercaps are dead (Archie's whispered Fireball, Eager's final stand, Markop's fist), and nobody died: Feyward Dan fell at zero hit points, survived, and was healed up by Salam; Eager ended on two hit points, kept alive by healing Markop had put into him; Archie is out of spells; Markop is bleeding and is the healthiest of them. The sentry arrangement failed in the way the archive said it would — the stump was the plan and everyone ran away from it, the scream was made and did not mean the signal — and the fight was won anyway by four people doing the right thing in the wrong place and one who stayed put. Eager carries the electric sphere out. Markop's 'what about Remi, we can't rest now' lost the vote to the Toads; the party is going back to the stump to rest. The Permanent Injury Table was rolled for Dan: 59, Sprained Thumb, one week — a rule about two-weapon fighting handed to a man with one arm.

aftermath:
**The grove is fought through.** The giant green spider, two filings a menace and owed a file, is dead to Eager's blades; the ettercaps are dead to a whispered Fireball, a final stand and a fist. The archive marks the Skittering Grove fight concluded.

**Feyward Dan fell and is up.** Webbed, dropped at zero, dropped again on the catch, healed by Salam. The Permanent Injury Table gave him 59 — Sprained Thumb, one week — the one row that costs a one-armed paladin nothing he had.

**Eager has two hit points** and the electric sphere. The record says the sphere was powered during the giant battle by Archie's electric magic; the archive has no earlier sighting of it and files the claim as stated.

**Archie is out of spells.** 'Without my spells I am useless.' The first real Fireball on his record was his last one.

**The party is going back to the stump to rest**, over Markop's objection — 'what about Remi, we can't rest now' — which the Toads answered with 'Eager can handle his own' and 'Salam is weak.'

**The Iron Legion appears nowhere in this filing.** The guard posted at the bike, the medic, the man who ran — none of them is on the record while the ettercaps closed.

**Unresolved:** Remi, and whether Markop accepts the vote; what the Legion did while the grove was fought; whether the three Toads who ran upward are the Toads who voted; what the electric sphere is and what it will do in Eager's hands; what made the Legion man run — the ettercaps are a candidate, not an answer.
waluigiAssessment:
**1. The plan held at exactly one point, and nobody went to it.** The stump was agreed by everyone and used by one. Markop stood where the arrangement put him and watched the arrangement leave. The eight lines he and Eager exchanged at the end — *I thought you left me for dead* / *I was talking to you* — are the whole failure in dialogue: a signal that meant something else, a rally point that nobody rallied to, and two people who were each right. Waluigi files the plan as sound and the party as somewhere else.

**2. The table's own post-mortem is the correct one, and the archive declines to improve on it.** Archie used every crowd-control spell he had and everyone left the space they bought. The archive has written that sentence in three different ways across three grove filings — the airlift, the scream pact, the stump — and would like it on the record that the players wrote it themselves tonight, which is the first time.

**3. The whispered Fireball is filed as a first, not a last.** Archie has threatened this spell for the length of the archive; the first one that was real was cast with nothing behind it, over a friend he had just put down, and it was whispered. Waluigi does not file sentiment. He files volume, and notes that a man who says *this may be the end of us* and then ends it for three ettercaps instead has described the fight accurately in every respect but the subject.

**4. Row 59.** The one-armed paladin drew the one injury in a hundred that forbids things he cannot do. The archive, which authored the table and locked it, did not plan this and would not have dared.

sections.name: I. Deeper in
sections.overview:
[Archie](#/article/archie_miser) ran. Not to the bike and not to the tree: deeper, into the forest, after the three [Toads](#/article/liberated_toads) who had gone up a filing ago toward whatever made a Legion man run. Markop, at the motorbike, watched [Eager](#/article/eager) swing a sword and follow him.

Then Eager killed the big spider.

The archive would like a moment. The giant green spider closed on Markop in one filing, bit Archie through a paladin's shield in the next, and was described in this file — accurately — as the best fighter in the grove and owed a page of its own. It died to a [Toad](#/article/toads) scout with blades, somewhere past the fires, with no ceremony the record kept. Waluigi opens its file and closes it in the same sentence, which is more than it did for anybody.
sections.waluigi_note: The giant green spider closed on Markop in one filing, bit Archie through a paladin's shield in the next, and was described as the best fighter in the grove. It died to a Toad scout with short blades, past the ash, with no ceremony. Waluigi opens its file and closes it in the same sentence, which is more than it did for anybody.

sections.name: II. One arm, two tools
sections.overview: [Dan](#/article/dan_the_toad) has one arm. The archive has filed the arm before and files it again here because it decided the next thing he did. With the ring closing, he dropped the longsword and took up the shield — the one-handed shield, the only one a one-armed man can use — and set himself to defend the party. A man who can hold one thing chose the thing that protects other people. Waluigi records the arithmetic without comment, which for Waluigi is a comment.
sections.waluigi_note: A man who can hold only one thing chose the tool that protects other people instead of the steel that protects himself. Waluigi records the arithmetic without comment, which for Waluigi is a comment.

sections.name: III. The stump
sections.overview:
Here is the beat Markop will be telling for the rest of his life. He stood at the stump — the actual stump, the planned escape point, the thing agreed an hour ago by every person now running — and watched the whole party run away from it in every other direction. He stayed. He revved the motorbike.

[Salam](#/article/salam) fired from the bike. Markop revved again and left an ettercap in the dust, which the archive files as the machine's first useful act since it hit a tree.
sections.waluigi_note: Revving an idling motorbike in the dark to blow gravel into an ettercap's eyes is the machine's first useful act since it hit a pine tree two filings ago.

sections.name: IV. The scream
sections.overview:
Dan got webbed. Feyward Dan fell. Archie screamed.

One filing ago the arrangement ended with a line the archive underlined: *if we have to leave, I'll… scream for you.* The scream was the signal. It was the sound everybody was listening for and nobody wanted to make. Tonight it was made — and it was not the signal. It was a wizard watching a paladin go down, and nobody retreated on it, because the thing it was supposed to mean had already stopped being possible. Waluigi files the scream as the plan's last word: made on schedule, meaning something else.

Eager wrestled the ettercap off Dan and threw Dan to Archie. The body fell. A Toad threw a Toad to a wizard, and the catch was not made. The record does not say whether the throw was short or the hands were slow, and the archive does not care: it says Dan hit the ground a second time, which is one more time than a man with no hit points should.
sections.waluigi_note: The scream was agreed as the retreat signal that nobody wanted to make. Tonight it was torn out of a wizard watching a paladin drop, and nobody retreated because retreat had already stopped being possible. Made on schedule, meaning something else entirely.

sections.name: V. The way I started it
sections.overview:
Archie held the body. The record says he thought about running, and the archive believes it, because he said so himself and because the archive has his file. Then he put Dan down, and stood up, and faced the ettercaps.

*This may be the end of us, or me, as we know it. I may not have been good — but at least I'll end this journey the way I started it. With my signature spell.*

He whispered it. **Fireball.** A tear in his eye. It exploded.

The archive needs to be careful here, because it has filed a great many of Archie's fireballs. It has filed the one he charged in a corridor full of screaming pirates, the one he faked in this grove before delivering a firebolt instead, and the one Markop begged him for a filing ago — *use fireball, use your lightning, anything* — which did not come. It has filed the threat more times than it can count: *I can just fire a ball at you.* Tonight was the first time the archive saw the real one, and it was whispered, by a man with nothing in the book behind it, over a friend he had just set down. Waluigi files the volume.

Two ettercaps were still standing when the light went out of it. Archie was woozy and out of spells. The book is empty. Whatever the party does next, it does without him, and he knows it.
sections.waluigi_note: Archie has threatened fireball in hallways, faked it in the grove, and held it back when begged. This was the first time the real one arrived, whispered over a friend set down in the dirt with nothing left in the book behind it. Waluigi files the volume.

sections.name: VI. Two hit points
sections.overview:
Eager's final stand took one of the two. One left.

Then he raged, stepped back, stumbled, and walked backwards into Markop, who had not moved. The exchange is on the record and the archive gives it whole, because it is the plan and its failure in eight lines:

**"Hello."**

**"I thought you left me for dead for a moment."**

**"I said come towards me, to the tree. I don't know what you're talking about — I was talking to you."**

**"We were surrounded."**

**"Don't worry, I'm healthier than the other guys."**

**"Are you sure? You're bleeding."**

**"Yes I am. It's been a rough fight."**

**"I don— don't disagree."**

Markop stayed where the plan put him. Eager thought he had been abandoned. Both of them are right, and Waluigi has stopped expecting that to be unusual.

Salam grabbed his bow, put it down again, and went to Dan instead. He healed him up. The sentry left the post he had been given to put his hands on the fallen man, and the archive files it under the only order Salam has received all night — *rest* — being disobeyed for the second time, correctly.

Eager took an attack that should have finished him and did not, because Markop had put healing into him first. Two hit points. Critical. The archive carried the ledger across the grove in the last filing — Markop sixteen, Archie eight, Eager sixteen, Dan eleven — and files the new line without the rest: Eager, two.

Battered, worn, scattered. Somewhere in this Eager picked up the electric sphere — the record says it was powered during the giant battle by Archie's electric magic, and the archive has no earlier sighting of the thing and says so. It is on the technology ledger now, with Eager's name beside it and a question mark beside his.
sections.waluigi_note: Markop stayed where the plan put him; Eager thought he had been abandoned. Both men were right, and Waluigi has stopped expecting that to be unusual in this grove.

sections.name: VII. The fist
sections.overview:
The last ettercap was still alive. One hit point, by the table's own count: the same number Eager was two away from. Markop pushed Eager aside and smacked it down with his fist.

The grove took a scythe, a thunder-called warhammer, a javelin thrown across its full length, a whispered fireball, and most of a paladin. It ended on a punch, from the man who never left the stump. Waluigi files that with something he declines to name.
sections.waluigi_note: The grove took a scythe, a thunder-called warhammer, a javelin thrown across its full length, a whispered fireball, and most of a paladin. It ended on a bare knuckle punch from the man who never left the stump. Waluigi files that with something he declines to name.

sections.name: VIII. The stump, again
sections.overview:
They picked up their stuff. Then the argument, which was short:

*"What about Remi? We can't rest now."* — Markop.

*No.* The Toads were going back to the stump.

*"Without my spells I am useless."* — Archie.

*"If you want the party to come help, we will be useless."* The Toads, pressing the case against going anywhere. *"Eager can handle his own."* *"Salam is weak."*

Back to the stump. Markop's question is the only mention of [Remi](#/article/remi_akamatsu_full_backstory) in the record tonight, and the archive files it as a lead, because the man who asked it was outvoted and is bleeding and the record does not show him agreeing.
sections.waluigi_note: Markop's question is the only mention of Remi in the record tonight. He was outvoted, exhausted, and bleeding, and the record does not show him agreeing.

sections.name: IX. The post-mortem, which the table held itself
sections.overview: Archie used all his crowd-control spells, and everyone left. That is the main problem with the battle, and it is not the archive's reading — it is the table's own, offered unprompted and filed verbatim. The spells bought a space; nobody stood in it. The stump was the plan; nobody went to it until they walked into it backwards. The record calls that a lesson. The archive calls it the same lesson as the last two filings with the furniture rearranged, and files it anyway.
sections.waluigi_note: The table calls this a tactical lesson. The archive calls it the exact same failure as the last two filings with the furniture rearranged, and files it anyway.

sections.name: X. The table
sections.overview:
The one who fell gets the table. The archive rolled the Permanent Injury Table for Feyward Dan, as the house rule requires, and the die gave **59 — Sprained Thumb**: *you cannot fight with two weapons, and attack rolls with a versatile weapon used two-handed are made at disadvantage. Rest — one week.*

Waluigi would like the record to appreciate this. Of a hundred rows — death at the bottom, a limb at five, scars, trauma, the slow rows that take a year to walk off — the die found the one injury that costs a one-armed paladin nothing he had. He has never fought with two weapons. He will never hold a versatile weapon in two hands. The thumb is real and it is splinted and he will carry it for a week, and the rule it carries is addressed to a man who does not exist. Waluigi files it as the grove's last joke, and the kindest thing it did all night.
sections.waluigi_note: Of a hundred rows on the steel ladder, the die found the one injury that costs a one-armed paladin nothing. The thumb is real and splinted, but the rule applies to a body he does not have. The kindest joke the grove produced all night.

sections.name: XI. Standing
sections.overview:
The position as this filing closes:

The giant green spider and the ettercaps are dead. Feyward Dan is up, webbed, one thumb in a splint, one week on the rule. Eager has two hit points and a sphere that hums. Archie has no spells and knows what that makes him. Salam is weak and said so by proxy. Markop is bleeding, is healthier than the other guys, and is the only one who was where the plan said. The [Iron Legion](#/article/iron_legion) — the guard at the bike, the medic with the syringe, the man who ran — appears nowhere in this filing; where it was while the ettercaps closed is not something the archive can say. [Wario](#/article/wario), Remi and [Mossy](#/article/mossy) are still on the far side of a passage somebody else paid for.

Five people are going back to the stump to rest, which is where they were supposed to be an hour ago, before any of this.

WAH.
sections.waluigi_note: Five people are going back to the stump to rest, which is where they were supposed to be an hour ago before any of this began. WAH.

name: The Box at the Cottage Door
title: The Box at the Cottage Door: Eight Hours Counted, a Girl in a Parcel, the Midnight Fountain Lit, and a Ship That Was Not Theirs Anymore
date: 1 Aethel, 1040 BF — eight hours' rest after the Skittering Grove fight (Shadowfell clock), then out through the Midnight Fountain onto the Material side; the Material hour is not recorded ('out so early')
era: Raventree Crisis — Shadeward Operations / The Exit / Return to the Material Plane
location: Tymnas's cottage, the Midnight Fountain (Shadowfell); the ruined manor near Thornwood; the town beneath the Legionlance (Material)
type: Rest / Delivery / Exit Ritual / Return / Shopping
status: Filed — the party is out of the Shadowfell, in a Legion-held town in sight of the Legionlance as the Toads storm it; Kyle Coinsoul's execution is pending under Commander G, and Dan has a name for a prosthetist
summary: The party rests eight hours in Tymnas's cottage and loots the grove's dead. The stump burns down, closing the exit. Green T knocks with a delivery — a box with Remi asleep inside. Archie wants to kill the oracle; the table settles on the ritual, Green T lights the Midnight Fountain, and the party steps out at the ruined manor. At the Legionlance a guard named Mr. Shock swings a baton at Remi, a doctor produces a bone saw, and Markop pulls her out by the hand. In the town below, a guard orders them to smile for Kyle Coinsoul's execution; Remi sells half her kit, Archie buys packs, Markop buys binoculars and sees Toads in rags storming the ship, and Dan is given a name for a prosthetist.
description:
*Waluigi has filed the Scorncrow, the Skittering Grove and the long fall of the Shadow Estate as a single wound. This is the filing where it closes: the exit burns, a girl is delivered in a parcel, a candle is lit, and everybody goes home to find that home has a new owner. WAH!*

The filing opens on a cottage and closes on a shop counter. In between, it is the shortest ritual in the archive — a beam, a step, a ruined manor — and the longest argument about a gold bar.

It has no combat in it. Markop swings once, at the gate; what the swing met is not on the table. It has no spells, no casualties and no villain. What it has is a party that has just survived the worst night of its campaign and is, for the first time in a month, at the mercy of nothing more than a shopkeeper's exchange rate and a guard's temper.
outcome: The party leaves the Shadowfell by the Midnight Fountain ritual and arrives at the ruined manor near Thornwood. The grove exit burned. Remi is recovered, alive, with no account of her disappearance. The Legionlance is Legion-held and, as the party watches, being stormed by Toads in rags. A Legion guard has announced the execution of Kyle Coinsoul under Commander G. The party has binoculars, ink, two packs, a crossbow case and a candle, thirty-one gold from the bar and the earring, and a rumour about a prosthetist.
notableFeatures: Eight hours' rest in Tymnas's cottage, and every body looted first — a spider's eye, ettercap silk, a vial of venom and a fang
The stub of the tree burns down; the exit Archie made is gone

Remi, asleep, in a box on the step; 'maybe I sleepwalked'
'I want to kill the oracle' — and the table settles on the ritual
Remi volunteers to lead 'because of adventure'; Green T lights the candles at the Midnight Fountain
Bones, Hjumpik and Toad Lee left on the other side and not mentioned
Mr. Shock's baton, a bone saw, and 'not anymore'
Toads in rags storming the Legionlance, seen through new binoculars
A bar worth 50 gold sold for 15; 'someone please interject'
