gallery.caption: Remi among the gold toads, and Speaker Rivers above them with his tea.

sections.name: I. For Free
sections.overview:
The gold bar was gone, and the coins it had been turned into were in a pocket, and [Remi](#/article/remi_akamatsu_full_backstory) was in the mood to spend the rest of the afternoon on something other than a shop.

"Now that I sold money to that guy," she said, "we can go on an adventure."

The shopkeeper, the same one who had paid a third of what the bar was worth, came out from behind the counter. "I have an adventure mask for you," he said, "and it's free."

"For free?" Remi said. "It does sound interesting. For free."

He put it in her hands. It was gloomy. She looked at it for as long as it took to decide. "I won't wear it," she said. "Maybe the toads will."

Then she and the others went out of the door. [Green T](#/article/green_t) went after them. "I'd better supervise them," he said.

The toads in the party sang as they walked, and the song was short:

**"We are the toads."**

*WAH! A counter that pays a third gives away a mask. The archive has priced a great many free things and would like it noted that the shop only ever gave anything away after it had finished taking.*
sections.waluigi_note: Nothing in the account says what the mask does, who it was made for, or why a shopkeeper who offers a third on everything lets a gloomy one go for nothing. The archive has the mask on the sheet and has not been told what it is. WAH.

sections.name: II. Whose Airship
sections.overview:
[the old Vigilance](#/article/vigilance) was where they had left it, and the gangway had a toad on it.

"Who goes there?" the toad said.

"Us," said the party. "The owners of the airship."

"That's not right," the toad said.

"What do you mean it's ours?"

"No, no, no, no. This is the TOADS' airship. The TOADALNAEC. It belongs to [Speaker Rivers](#/article/speaker_rivers)."

"No, no, it may be the same layout," came the answer, "but I assure you it's ours."

The toad on the gangway looked at them, and then over his shoulder, and then he made the decision of every gate guard in every archive: he sent for someone else. "Come on out, Hudston," he called. "We have a problem."

*WAH! The Legion renamed this ship and got it wrong. The Toads have renamed it back and got it wronger. TOADALNAEC. Waluigi has said it forty times to himself and has not yet found where the stress goes.*
sections.waluigi_note: The ship on the gangway is the Vigilance. Both sides in the argument say the layout is the same, because it is. Neither side, at any point in the account, says the other is wrong about the layout. Only about whose it is.

sections.name: III. Gold or Gold-Plated
sections.overview:
[Hudston](#/article/hudston) came out on deck and stopped when he saw [Remi](#/article/remi_akamatsu_full_backstory).

"Wow," he said. "Are you gold, or gold-plated?"

"Come and find out for yourself," said Remi, and she shook his hand.

The gold started at the palm. It ran up his arm and across his shoulders and out to his feet, and when it had stopped he looked at himself for a moment and turned to the gangway.

"Hey, guys," Hudston said. "Check it out. I'm gold now."

"You want to test it out?" Remi asked.

[Green T](#/article/green_t) told him to stand against the wall, and Hudston stood against the wall, and Green T shot him. The bullet rang off the gold and went somewhere else.

"Wow," Hudston said. "How can I ever repay you? It kind of stung, but it's really fun."

Green T shot again, with the same result.

The other toads on the gangway said the sentence the afternoon was about to be built on.

**"You're one of the toads now."**
sections.waluigi_note: The account does not say that the mask caused the gold. It does not say that the mask didn't. It says a girl was handed a thing for free, would not put it on, and was shaking hands with metal within the hour. The archive is not going to settle that and would like the room to stop looking at Waluigi.

sections.name: IV. The New Toad
sections.overview:
Remi started singing. It was not a good song, and she did not stop.

*Oh, I'm the new toad, listen to me, I'll sing a song in the air or the sea,* she sang, and the toads sang it back.

They picked her up. The new toad, the crowd sang, will be **very small, nimble and happy.** "What a fun game," they said. "We will see."

They carried her through the ship, singing, all the way along.

*Oh, I'm a new toad, listen to me, I'll sing you a song, the air and the sea.*

Behind them, the others had worked out what they were looking at. The toads from Disaster Inc. went after Remi to try to save the rest of the party, and caught up with the song in time to see the toads set Remi down.
sections.waluigi_note: Waluigi would like the record to show that nobody sang her a lullaby by accident. The verse is a recruitment drive with a tune, and the tune worked on a girl who had been given a mask for free an hour earlier. It has been a day.

sections.name: V. Speaker Rivers Receives
sections.overview:
[Speaker Rivers](#/article/speaker_rivers) came out into the hall like a man arriving at his own party.

"Oh, good," he said. "New recruits."

The hall was full of toads, and the party was in the middle of them. "You guys with our toads," [Dan](#/article/dan_the_toad) asked, "or...?"

"They're with me," said Speaker Rivers.

He looked at the party for a moment and nodded to himself. "Hmm. I don't know. So you're the Liberated Toads, right?"

"I feel kind of independent," Dan said. "I got back with Rodger. Is anyone here from the Pond Patrol? I have to report to them."

"Oh, don't worry about them," said Rivers. "You report to me now. I took over Speaker L's job while you were handling the whole manor situation."

Then [Archie](#/article/archie_miser) walked into the hall, and everybody saw him.

**"IT'S HIM! THE MAN WHO BREATHES FIRE! ARREST HIM FOR CRIMES AGAINST THE TOADS!"**

"What's going on here?" Archie asked. [Markop](#/article/markop) had already taken a step forward.

"Is this legal?" he asked. "The Legion arrested [Speaker L](#/article/speaker_l)."

"No," said a toad. "We got him back. And we put him in jail."

"Isn't this a coup d'état?" Markop said. "Let me duel you. You're unfit to rule."

"Fine," said Speaker Rivers.

*WAH! Speaker L was arrested by the Legion, rescued by the Toads and put in a Toad cell by the rescuers. That is a single sentence, and everybody in the room said it with a straight face.*
sections.waluigi_note: Rivers took Speaker L's job 'while you guys handled the whole manor situation.' The 'manor situation' is the party's whole last month, and Rivers uses the phrase the way a man uses it who was not at the manor. The archive has no date for when Speaker L's post changed hands and nobody in the hall offered one.

sections.name: VI. The Three Lies
sections.overview:
Markop walked out onto the floor to meet him and dodged a trapdoor on the way. Archie fell into a barrel. The account does not say how.

"I saved you from slavery!" Archie said from inside it.

The toads picked up the barrel. It went up on shoulders. Markop started to argue with them and was told that Archie was an arsonist, and Markop said they had been saved by him, and Archie Miser fell into a barrel, which the account says twice, so the archive does too.

[Gentlepad](#/article/toad_gentlepad) came up to Markop. "Stand still," Gentlepad said, "while we get these Archie germs off of you."

"What have they been telling you?" Archie asked from the barrel.

"The three lies of Archie Miser," the toads told him, and they took him through them one at a time, each with its correction.

**"1. He saved the toads."** "No. He didn't save them. He put them back in their place, to be cogs in the machine."

**"2. Archie Miser is a sane individual."** "False. Archie Miser is INSANE. He burnt down a village full of orphans."

"That ain't true," Archie said. "I do have flaws, but the village never happened. On remembering it was someone else."

**"3. Anything Archie says is a lie."**

"That's it," a toad said. "Those are the three Miserly principles."

"Okay," Markop said, "so if that was true, why isn't he fireballing us right now?"

"Because he's scared of me," said Speaker Rivers.

"Archie fought an evil tree," said Markop.

*WAH! Three lies, recited by toads, ending in the fact that the third one covers the first two. The archive would call it a logical trick if the ship were not holding the logician in a barrel.*
sections.waluigi_note: The second lie is a charge of burning a village of orphans, and Archie answers that the village never happened and that he remembers it being someone else. The archive has nothing to put under either half of that. It files the charge and the reply side by side and declines to pick.

sections.name: VII. Why
sections.overview:
From the barrel, Archie spoke to Rivers, and it was the longest thing he said all day.

"This is the first time I've met you," he said. "You don't scare me at all. If I wanted to, I would do what Markop did. But I'm nice, and so I need to understand why you hate me. I saved you guys, all hundred and fifty of you. So why?"

Nobody in the hall answered it. "Well," Archie said, "take it away, Remi."

[Remi](#/article/remi_akamatsu_full_backstory) had been listening with her head on one side. "I'm not sure why Archie is evil," she said, "but why not?"

She went for a high five, up high. [Speaker Rivers](#/article/speaker_rivers) dodged it.

"Get away from me, you filth animal!" he said, and then, to the toads, "Surround her. Oh, oopsie."

He had caught himself. It was too late. The whole hall of toads said the same thing together.

**"Huh?"**

"You guys want to be called that?" Markop asked, into the quiet. The toads paused, and the pause went round the hall.

*WAH! A recruiter's slip is the one thing a crowd always hears, and Rivers had just told his own followers what he called them when he thought they weren't listening. Waluigi has been bitten by that dog before.*
sections.waluigi_note: 'All hundred and fifty of you' is Archie's number, given from a barrel. The archive has no other count and files this one as his.

sections.name: VIII. Show Me Your Hands
sections.overview:
Markop turned to the hall.

"Did anyone actually see Speaker Rivers fight?"

"Yeah," Rivers said. "I fought. Killed them with my bare hands." He put his hands in his pockets.

"Let me see your hands," said Markop. "They should be bruised and bloodied."

The hands stayed where they were. "Out of your pockets," Markop said. Rivers made a fake stumble and tripped on the floor, and when he came up he held both hands out.

"See?" he said. "My hands are dirty. Dirt and dust."

"I said bruised and bloodied," said Markop. "See? He's lying to you."

"I personally unchained you guys," said Rivers, "and freed you."

Markop asked the hall whether anyone remembered being unchained by Rivers.

"The metaphorical chains," Rivers said.

"Makes sense," said a toad.

"Wasn't Speaker L the savior?" Markop asked.

"No," said Rivers. "He was a vigilante criminal."

Markop was about to say something, and then he saw [Green T](#/article/green_t) on the far side of the room, pulling the barrel back. He gave him a look. Green T nodded back.

Over by the wall, [Remi](#/article/remi_akamatsu_full_backstory) spun round to watch. Another toad had turned gold.
sections.waluigi_note: The hands are the whole case. A toad who says he killed with them has to show them, and Rivers was asked for his hands and produced the floor. The chains turned out to be metaphorical, and the Toads took that without a murmur.

sections.name: IX. Tea, and the Truth Spell
sections.overview:
[Speaker Rivers](#/article/speaker_rivers) said he was a bit too tired and asked whether anyone could carry him, and the toads carried him.

"Your tea's ready, sir," one of them said, and he drank it.

"That's not a potion, is it?" Markop asked.

"No, no. Just tea."

Markop looked down at his spellbook and smiled. "We don't have to fight," he said. "You just have to tell the truth, and I'll go. I have a spell that will make it so you can't lie. I ask you questions."

[Remi](#/article/remi_akamatsu_full_backstory) had gotten bored. She leaned on a toad, and the toad went gold. She yawned and hit another, and he went gold. She kicked her legs back, and a third.

The tea came. Rivers sipped.

"Of course," he said, "I'd never lie to anyone."

Markop pointed at him. "Now say the truth spell didn't work."

"Maybe you're a bad magician," said Rivers.

Markop lost his temper. "You want me to beam you?"

"No," Rivers said, quickly.

Markop turned to the toad next to him, who was in range of the spell. "Tell me your secret."

"I like lifting up people," the toad said, "and I also stole something from Archi—"

Rivers forced the tea down the toad's throat, and the toad threw up.

"Hey," said Markop. "What did he steal?"

"Into the dungeon with him," said Speaker Rivers. They dragged the toad away. He drank another one, a blue one this time, a coffee.

*WAH! A speaker accused of lying asked for his tea and then used it to stop another man talking. The account has the whole interrogation in two cups.*
sections.waluigi_note: The toad was inside the spell and the spell did not misfire. It said a true thing, and a second later someone silenced the speaker with the contents of a teapot. Whatever the toad stole from Archie is not on file, because the end of the sentence is a tea cup.

sections.name: X. The Pen and the Axe
sections.overview:
Markop turned back to Rivers. "You're lying. We need to duel. The spell clearly didn't work."

"I am the best," said Speaker Rivers. "It's not a lie."

Archie was still in his barrel.

Rivers attacked Markop with a pen. The pen, he said, is mightier than the sword.

They duelled. Markop attacked and set Rivers on fire, and Rivers screamed. The battleaxe swung and set him on fire again, and he screamed again. Another swing missed. Someone grabbed for the battleaxe and was too weak to take it.

Then the toads began to walk away.

"Lame," some of them said as they went. "He's losing his crowd."

Markop smiled, and got ready for another strike. The account ends there.
sections.waluigi_note: The account never says whose hands the burning battleaxe was in, or which man was too weak to take it. The archive files the hall emptying out as the only clear outcome of the fight. WAH.

name: The Archive Hall and the Song 'Alone'
title: The Archive Hall and the Song 'Alone': Two Songs, Ten Thousand Missing Gold, the Third Haunting, and the Courier Who Cleans the Laundry
date: 3 Aethel, 1035 BF — evening into late night, the day after the Star Hill crash (inferred from 'sent over this morning' and the empty-hours clinic corridor)
timeWindow: 3 Aethel, 1035 BF — one continuous evening into night: the 'Wawario' sheet slid across the Archive Hall table, Waluigi's exit into the rain, an unmeasured sleep under the leaking vault, three hours after Wario began checking the morning ledgers, the third haunting of the week, and the corridor exit
era: 1035 BF — Mario disappearance file
type: Audit / Haunting / Song Record / Mario Arc
location: the_archive_hall
status: Filed — genuine backup ledgers reclaimed by Wario, Treasury of Wonders tampering confirmed on the shelves, Beta Luigi departed alone with one archive volume, and Wario pursuing the Feywild contract down the corridor
summary: Twenty-four hours after losing his working notebook at Star Hill, Waluigi meets courier-auditor Mr. T in the unguarded Archive Hall and is handed the full 'Mario, Luigi, Wario, Waluigi, Bowser, and Wario Bowser / Wawario' lyric sheet, scoring out his own name before storming into the rain. While Mr. T sleeps beneath a freshly leaking stone vault, Wario arrives to expose a ten-thousand-gold discrepancy and a forged five-thousand-gold Treasury of Wonders entry swapped over his genuine shelf backups — right above Mr. T's unread 'AUDIT REQUIRED - WARIO' warning. Footsteps from the empty clinic corridors then herald the hall's third haunting of the week: Beta Luigi crushes a live Fire Flower underfoot and weeps through every verse of 'Alone' under a fifteen-foot crimson phantom while Mario's voice answers in Italian ('Ti perdono. Vai avanti'), before pulling a book off the shelf and walking out alone — driving Wario to slam the stone wall and declare gold does not bring dead men back.
description: *I am putting both songs into the permanent record word for word — the idiotic one with six names that insulted my mustache on page one, and the one that tore the air open behind a green cap two hours later — because anybody who cuts a single line out of tonight will claim tomorrow that half of it was a dream. It was not a dream. My name is still blacked out on the first sheet, Wario's backup ledgers are missing five thousand gold from a fund he is terrified to say out loud, a dead man spoke Italian in a room with no radio, and a ghost walked out of a locked archive carrying a real book under his arm.*
outcome:
Filed as settled: Wario reclaimed both authentic backup volumes of *The Complete Ledger of Wario's Enterprise* from the Archive Hall shelves, proving that someone with inside access planted falsified schedules over intact originals — including a fabricated 10,000-gold variance across columns seven and nine, a client deposit backdated by two weeks, and an altered 5,000-gold withdrawal and one-month re-deposit touching the Treasury of Wonders. Mr. T proved from the bottom-left margin ('AUDIT REQUIRED - WARIO') that he had warned Wario months earlier in his daily reports. Beta Luigi entered during the storm as the hall's third haunting of the week, crushed a working Fire Flower on the flags, sang and wept through 'Alone' beneath a fifteen-foot crimson phantom while Mario's voice answered in English and Italian, pulled one unnamed book from the shelf, and walked out alone.

Filed as open: which volume Beta Luigi took from the shelf and where he went with it. Who holds clearance to swap ledgers inside an Archive Hall left unguarded for months, and whether the motive targets Wario's Enterprise, Waluigi's debts, or the Treasury of Wonders itself. What burned the edges of Waluigi's second notebook during his twenty-minute absence outside. What exact terms sit inside the Feywild Contract of Accord that keep Wario from walking away even after declaring gold cannot bring dead people back.

sections.name: I. 'Mario, Luigi, Wario, Waluigi, Bowser, and Wario Bowser'
sections.imageCaption: Mr. T slides the transcribed sheet across the oak reading table; Waluigi cracks the paper under his palm on the first pass.
sections.overview:
Rain was already coming down outside the stone lancets when **Mr. T** sat across the reading table in **The Archive Hall**, slid [[prop:prop_wawario_affiliations_sheet|a heavily annotated sheet of paper]] across the wood toward **Waluigi**, and said, **"I got what you wanted."**

What was written on the page — music cues left right where the transcription hand had put them — ran in full:

> *MARIO,*

> *WARIO, WALUIGI,*  
> *BOWSER,*

> *same game series, but you don't often*  
> *see*  
> *Wario [music] Bowser*  
> *and Waluigi*  
> *in any Mario games [music] like Mario*  
> *Kart 64,*  
> *on the great Nintendo 64,*  
> *and New Super Mario [music] Bros. Wii on*  
> *the white Nintendo Wii, and there is*  
> *something that you need to know that in*  
> *Mario Kart 64 [music]*  
> *and in Super Smash Bros., there is*  
> *Mario, Luigi, and Wario, but no Waluigi,*  
> *and there is Bowser, [music] but there's*  
> *no Wario Bowser who's not in any Mario*  
> *game to ever*  
> *exist. [music]*  
>   
> *There is Mario, Luigi,*  
> *and Waluigi, and they say that [music]*  
> *Wario and Waluigi are meant to beat*  
> *them, and Mario and Luigi are brothers,*  
> *[music] and Wario is their cousin, but*  
> *nobody knows if Waluigi is*  
> *>> [music]*  
> *[music]*  
> *>> Nintendo, [music] please make this into*  
> *a reality of how many evil clones are*  
> *there and if there is [music] any more*

> *know.*  
>

> *[music]*

> *been a villain for long and see him*  
> *introduce*  
> *>> [music]*

> *would be much better than seeing Bowser*  
> *kidnap the princess again.*  
> *Mario, [music] Luigi, Wario and Waluigi*  
> *must all work together to stop Bowser.*  
> *Mario, [music] Luigi, Wario and Waluigi*  
> *team up with Bowser*  
> *to stop*  
> *Wart Bowser.*  
> *>> [music]*  
> *>> Now [music] let's end this*  
> *song now.*  
> *M A R I O W A L U I G I Bowser*  
>   
> *Mario, [music]*  
> *Luigi, Wario, Waluigi, Bowser*  
> *and Waluigi*  
> *have the three*  
> *evil clones [music] and I don't think we*  
> *know if there is any more characters*  
> *with evil clones and*  
> *Mario says wow.*  
> *Luigi says wee.*  
> *Wario [music] says*  
> *WAH. WALUIGI SAYS WAH.*  
> *WAWARIO SAYS WAH.*  
> *WAWARIO SAYS WAH.*

> *Wario, Waluigi, Bowser,*  
> *>> [music]*  
> *>> and Wawario.*  
> *Mario, Luigi, Wario, Waluigi, [music]*  
> *Bowser, and Wawario.*  
> *Wawario. [music]*  
> *>> [music]*

**"What do you think?"** Mr. T asked.

Waluigi's eyes narrowed with every line until his jaw locked. The scrap of notebook paper surviving from the thorn bush the night before burned cold against his ribs with enough red annotations to glow in the dark. He let out a bitter laugh and slumped back against the stone wall.

**"Evil clones?"** he spat. **"Wario's *cousin*? You think Nintendo just... forgot about me?"** His pen hovered over the sheet without touching it. Then his palm came down flat on the page hard enough to crack the paper. **"The thing you need to know is this — there's no Wario Bowser because *Wario* already IS Bowser for most games! Do they not pay attention in their offices?!"**

He slashed violently through a line in his open grimoire. **"The Waluigi that exists is EVIL enough to Wario, thank you very much! Mario's had three lives in one game while I've been stuck with two for years now, and somehow they're still considered heroes! You want to know about Nintendo? Ask them when their next press conference is. And stop asking me questions that make my notebook burn hotter."**

*WAH! Read that mustache verse again if you want to understand why my blood pressure requires its own ledger column! Mario has a zigzag mustache? Luigi has an L-shaped mustache? And whoever wrote this musical abomination looked me dead in the face on paper and called me an optional sixth wheel next to 'Wario Bowser' and 'Wart Bowser'! I kept every single word in the record so posterity can see what I have to work with!*
sections.waluigi_note: Every word on that sheet is preserved verbatim — right down to 'Wawario says wah' three times in a row. Nobody gets to accuse this desk of editing evidence to protect its own dignity.

sections.name: II. 'The Name Is WAWALUGI': The Blacked-Out Line and the Leaking Vault
sections.imageCaption: Mr. T asleep across the Archive Hall desk beside the open red-stained grimoire and the scored sheet while water drips from the uncracked vault overhead and Waluigi leaves into the rain.
sections.overview:
Mr. T stopped him at the doorway with the obvious question: **"Wario already IS Bowser for most games? What do you mean by that?"**

Waluigi turned with one hand still on the frame, walked back, and dropped into his chair like a man deflating. **"Look at it logically! Mario and Luigi are brothers. Wario is their cousin. He's ALREADY the rival version of Mario. Do they really think just because he has a Koopa shell that makes him an entirely different franchise?! And then there's me — the one who gets left out! The 'W' in Waluigi is RIGHT THERE, people are supposed to see it, but nooo—"**

He held his working notebook up like a shield. Mr. T tilted his head: **"I thought it was like Wa Wario and Wa Wa Luigi, no? The evil-evil version of you two."**

Waluigi's eye twitched. **"Wa Wario?"** He said the words like sour milk. **"And Wa Luigi? Don't you DARE get those two names confused with mine! I'm Waluigi. Singular. Unique. The only one of my kind in existence!"**

**"No, no,"** Mr. T corrected calmly. **"Wawaluigi. Two Wa's."**

All the color drained out of Waluigi's face. His mouth opened twice before any sound came out: **"W-Wawal... ugi?"** His chair tipped back hard enough to nearly throw him. **"Do they seriously have a Wa Waluigi character? And they put him right next to me?! To Wario?!"** His pen flew across the Archive Hall, missed the target wall by several feet, and hit the plaster with a dull *thunk*. He buried his face in both hands over the fluttering pages of his grimoire and whispered it to the wood: **"Wawalugi... The name is WAWALUGI. WA WALUGI!"**

**"I guess you want to scrap this, then,"** Mr. T said.

At the word *scrap*, Waluigi's head snapped up. Slowly he retrieved his pen — nib still wet with ledger ink — and drove a hard, jagged black line straight through **'Waluigi'** on the sheet until nothing white showed underneath. **"Scrap this whole mess. No more confusion. No more evil versions. This isn't about the Wa characters. This is about ME. And if anyone else thinks they can just erase me like this again..."**

He stood, pulled his rain-damp cloak across his shoulders, and walked for the door. **"I need to clear my head. Get out of here."** Halfway across the threshold he glanced back for one flickered beat, muttered **"Don't wait up,"** and clicked the door shut behind him.

Alone in the quiet hall, Mr. T read back over his own notes — Waluigi's clenched jaw, the six names, the half-finished line where he had stopped himself — and saw a drop slide down the glass. Looking ten feet straight up into the vaulted stone ceiling, he murmured, **"Is the ceiling leaking?"** A fresh dark stain was spreading across uncracked stone, dropping irregular beads of water onto the flags: *pitter-patter... pitter-patter...* Thinking to himself that it sounded *like music*, Mr. T lowered his head into his hands beside the open red-stained grimoire and fell asleep.

*WAH! Yes, I threw the pen, and yes, it missed by four feet — the nib was weighted wrong and my cheekbone was already throbbing from twenty-four hours earlier! Try hearing somebody calmly explain that there is now a 'Wawaluigi' with two Wa's while your real notebook is sitting in a stranger's satchel and tell me you keep your pen on the blotter!*
sections.waluigi_note: Note the fresh water stain directly above the table. No crack in the stone, dry when I walked out, dripping within minutes. Remember that when Wario starts complaining about the building.

sections.name: III. 'Wake Up, Sleepyhead': Wario, the Brass Key, and Ten Thousand Missing Gold
sections.overview:
Measured footsteps crossed the cold stone while Mr. T slept — circling the table once in the dark, stopping directly behind his chair, waiting through two steady drips from the vault overhead. Something cool touched the back of his neck, then tapped his shoulder a second time right beside his ear:

**"Wake up, sleepyhead."**

Mr. T raised his head with a groggy **"Uggu"** to find **Wario** leaning beside the chair, his red cap sitting slightly askew, golden eyes glinting above a crooked grin. **"Ugh? Really? After all that groaning and complaining about being tired..."** Wario clapped the back of his head roughly, glanced with open disgust at the scattered inventory sheets — **"useless busywork if I ever saw it"** — and when Mr. T stared back blankly without moving, jabbed both thumbs at his own chest.

**"I am Wario! The Explosive Accountant! And you're just... what exactly are you supposed to be?"**

Mr. T pushed himself out of the chair. **"Alright... what is on the agenda?"**

Wario's whole posture snapped straight to business. From the inside pocket of his coat he pulled a thick sheaf of financial schedules that Waluigi had sent over that morning. **"The numbers don't add up. Not even close. I've been checking my own grimoire against these figures for three hours now, and I can tell you right now — this is either a mistake or someone's trying to pull some kind of fast one over on us."**

Stepping shoulder to shoulder with Mr. T, Wario dragged one gloved finger down [[prop:prop_warios_enterprise_ledger_discrepancy|the open ledger columns]]:

**"Look here — column seven versus column nine. See how they're different by almost ten thousand gold? That's not accounting error; that's fraud or incompetence. Either Waluigi's been cooking books again and hasn't told us about it, or someone else is playing games with our ledgers."** He flipped hard to a quarterly client deposit and tapped the timestamp. **"This was logged almost two weeks before any actual business transaction would have occurred that makes sense."**

When Mr. T asked who stood to gain by faking them, Wario lowered his voice — **"this isn't just about money anymore — this is politics"** — and produced a **small brass key** from his coat pocket, admitting he had already used it on locked filing cabinets earlier and found *"interesting things."* Mr. T asked flatly whether Waluigi owed him coin. Wario looked away toward the rain-streaked glass before his jaw set: **"We're family... He owes me money. Big time. And then he has the audacity to send me paperwork that might be fake?"**
sections.waluigi_note: 'The Explosive Accountant.' He gave himself that title at full volume in an empty vault while holding a brass key to cabinets he swears nobody can get into. Keep count of how many things Wario calls impossible right before doing them himself.

sections.name: IV. The Shelf Backups, the Treasury of Wonders, and 'AUDIT REQUIRED - WARIO'
sections.imageCaption: Wario slams open *The Complete Ledger of Wario's Enterprise* beside his brass cabinet key as Mr. T points to 'AUDIT REQUIRED' in the bottom-left corner and a bruised Waluigi comes through the glass door clutching a scorched notebook.
sections.overview:
Mr. T glanced past Wario's shoulder toward the entrance — where **Waluigi** was standing directly behind the Archive Hall door with his ears pressed flat against the glass.

The door swung open and Waluigi strode in rumpled and furious, a fresh bruise darkening his cheekbone and **a badly scorched notebook** clutched tight against his chest. **"I got here about twenty minutes ago,"** he snapped when Wario moved closer to check his face. **"I was just dealing with some... complications. That's none of your concern right now. What matters is that I'm here and we can finally start figuring out what the hell is going on with these fake ledgers."** Outside in the distant hallway, running boots and urgent voices briefly shouted something about an emergency before fading.

While the two of them bristled over who in the kingdom wanted Waluigi ruined, Mr. T turned to the oak shelves, pulled a bound volume down at random, and held its cover up to Wario.

Wario froze, then lunged forward to snatch it out of his hands. **"You've got to be kidding me — *The Complete Ledger of Wario's Enterprise*... this is actually the real thing!"** Seconds later Mr. T pulled down a second volume beside it; Wario pried that one free too, stacking both authentic backup ledgers together. **"Public? You think THIS Archive Hall is just some public library where anyone can wander in off the street?! This place houses the most sensitive financial records in all of civilization! There are supposed to be guards on duty at all times!"**

Mr. T looked across at Waluigi: **"When you first brought me in here, I don't remember there being anyone on guard."**

**"I— I didn't either,"** Waluigi admitted quietly, tugging at his coat collar. **"I've been coming here for months now, and I always assumed there would be someone watching. Turns out that trust was misplaced."**

Wario's trembling fingers raced down the genuine backup columns until his palm slammed flat on the page: **"There! That's not right! This transaction here... it shows that I withdrew 5,000 gold coins from the Treasury of Wonders three months ago. But according to these records, those same funds should have been deposited into my account exactly one month after that date! Someone's been cooking the books!"**

At the words *Treasury of Wonders*, Mr. T asked whether the Toads controlled it — and joked straight-faced: **"Yeah, this is definitely fraud. Should I contact the TPF — Toad Police Force?"**

Both men went rigid at once. **"WAIT!"** Wario barked, going pale under his tan. **"Do NOT contact them! Do not tell a single soul about this!"**

**"It was a joke, calm down,"** Mr. T said dryly. **"I should know — I am the one who cleans the dirty laundry. In fact, I told you about it a few months ago in your daily reports, Wario. Let's pull out the paper with the discrepancy and check the bottom."**

They turned the sheet over to its bottom-left corner. Jabbed into the margin in tiny, unmistakable ink sat four words:

> **`AUDIT REQUIRED - WARIO`**

**"Of COURSE you told me. I'm a fool,"** Wario groaned, dragging both hands down his face. **"This changes everything."**

*WAH! Months! MONTHS! Mr. T wrote WARIO'S OWN NAME after a hyphen at the bottom of the exact discrepancy page, filed it in the daily packet, and 'The Explosive Accountant' filed it straight into oblivion while lecturing the rest of us about competence! Frame that margin corner in gold!*
sections.waluigi_note: Read the sequence carefully: genuine backups sitting openly on unguarded shelves, forged morning schedules swapped into circulation, and a 5,000-gold Treasury of Wonders loop sitting unread under Wario's own thumb.

sections.name: V. The Third Haunting This Week: Footsteps in the Clinic and the Crushed Flower
sections.imageCaption: Beta Luigi drives his heavy boot through a live Fire Flower on the wet Archive Hall stones as lightning breaks outside and pale phantoms coil around the door; Wario and Waluigi watch from between the stacks.
sections.overview:
Before anyone could turn another page, muffled footsteps broke the silence from the connected clinic hallways — multiple sets of boots moving fast where nobody belonged at that hour.

**"Shit,"** Waluigi whispered, tucking the ledger tight under one arm and backing into the shadow of the stacks. **"The hallways are supposed to be empty this time of—"** A distant door slammed open, followed by raised voices. Wario clapped one hand over his coat pocket — right over the hidden **Contract of Accord** — pulled Mr. T down into deep cover between two massive oak bookcases, and breathed directly into his ear: **"Stay completely silent. If we move even an inch, they'll hear us."**

The Archive Hall door creaked slowly inward.

Work boots scraped across the floorboards. Out from behind the stacks stepped **Beta Luigi** — dressed in stained green overalls with a heavy leather tool belt pulled high over one shoulder, his dark green cap tugged low enough to swallow his upper face.

Phantoms materialized around him in the doorway and sang together as thunder cracked outside the windows:

> *Fell up high to rock bottom, the guilt in your stomach feels uneasy —*  
> *now he is lost, yet not forgotten.*  
> *Look at him now, look what you have done, Luigi.*

The ghostly chorus vanished like smoke. Behind the shelves Wario sagged against the wood, pulling out the worn parchment of [[prop:prop_archive_hall_haunting_docket|the Contract of Accord]] to squint at it in the lantern spill. **"That was the third haunting this week,"** he muttered bitterly when Mr. T whispered that the man looked familiar. **"First Boo's ghost, then that giant moth thing from last week... Now THIS? I'm starting to think the Archive Hall has a grudge against Wario's Enterprise."**

Then the figure in green walked slowly back across the threshold, humming softly under his breath as the memories of Mario trapped behind **King Boo's** chasm closed over him:

> *How can I call myself a hero?*  
> *When I couldn't even save the one — my big bro.*

Clenching a live, glowing **Fire Flower** between both hands, his face drooping and his eyes barely open beneath the cap brim, Beta Luigi shuffled straight toward Wario:

> *Lost his life, I face, so why strife, so why still loom?*  
> *He's already lost to his doom.*

**"What the hell are you doing?!"** Wario blurted, jabbing a finger at his chest. **"You look like death warmed over! I don't need another person falling apart on me right now, Luigi! Maybe this whole Feywild breach was a mistake that's going to cost us everything — so are you going to stand there holding flowers like some kind of funeral bouquet, or tell me what's going on?!"**

Pale apparitions drifted closer around the green overalls, searching for red that was nowhere in the room. Without answering a word, Beta Luigi plucked the working Fire Flower, dropped it onto the wet stones, and **crushed it flat beneath his boot**.

*WAH! A LIVE FIRE FLOWER! Working petals, actual heat still in the stem, stepped on like a cigarette butt in a gutter! I pulled my pen straight out of my coat before my brain caught up with my arm — do you have ANY idea what a live flower goes for on the open market?!*
sections.waluigi_note: Wario blurted two things in panic that belong underlined in red: 'the third haunting this week' and 'this whole Feywild breach.' Neither one slipped out by accident.

sections.name: VI. 'Alone': The Crimson Phantom and the Voice in Italian
sections.imageCaption: A fifteen-foot crimson phantom towers over weeping Beta Luigi on the Archive Hall stones while Mario's faint apparition answers from the mist and a ghostly wall holds Wario and Waluigi back.
sections.overview:
**"WHAT THE— Don't you DARE!"** Waluigi lurched out with his pen shaking in his fist. **"That was a perfect flower! A WORKING flower with actual power and you just CRUSHED IT!"**

Beta Luigi raised his head without looking at either of them, the cap brim still hiding his eyes as he broke open into tears:

> *I'm trying, bro, I swear I'm trying!*  
> *Oh Mario, I'm sorry, there's no use defying!*  
> *The guilt in my heart tears me apart!*  
> *Why'd you depart?!*  
> *All I've ever wanted was to restart!*

Waluigi went white to the lips and slammed both palms against the bookcase hard enough to knock his own cap onto the stones. **"Brother! Do NOT stand there weeping about Mario! You think King Boo cared about your feelings when he trapped him?!"**

Ghosts surged forward between them like an unseen wall, throwing Wario stumble- footed backward when he tried to grab Beta Luigi's shoulders. Beneath the cap, dreadful dark bags hung under Beta Luigi's eyes as he stared through the barrier:

> *You were my number one, bro — now the guilt takes number two whole!*  
> *My cowardice cost your life, yet you can't move on to the afterlife!*  
> *Oh Mario, oh Mario, where did you go?*  
> *I am sorry, bro, you must be so lost and alone.*  
> *After all the wasted years, I still can't face my own fears —*  
> *now I stay sitting here, forced to wipe my own tears.*

A loud crash echoed somewhere in the lower vaults. Then the temperature dropped and **a giant angry crimson ghost** rose fifteen feet into the vault — arms thick as tree trunks, skin burning red — as Beta Luigi crumpled beneath it:

> *This was my only chance, the only time I saw the ball in my court,*  
> *and yet I missed the shot even with all of his support...*  
> *Oh what a failure I have become, how could I let someone down so wholesome.*  
>   
> *YOU WERE THEIR EVERYTHING, THE HAPPINESS YOU'D BRING TO THE LAND —*  
> *NOW ALL OF YOUR BLOOD IS ON MY HANDS.*  
> *OH. GOD. NO.*  
> *Why did I let you go? Please come back home.*

Wario crossed his arms with dead-eyed stubbornness, raising his ledger chart between himself and the crimson giant while the spectral ring closed tighter from every aisle:

> *He would always tell me there is another tomorrow!*  
> *I cannot see! I cannot breathe — I'm suffocating.*  
> *I hear their calls, I hear them all, the ghosts are waiting.*  
> *I face the wrath of reality — my brother is never gonna come back home to me.*

Waluigi's knees gave way on the cold stone floor. His scorched notebook fell open across the flags — pages on *"spectral barriers"* and *"quantum entanglement"* fluttering around his boots — as tears cut clean tracks through the soot on his face. **"Brother! BROTHER! I'm sorry! I'm SO sorry!"**

Beta Luigi whispered on through the closing dark:

> *No matter how much I try to restore it, no matter how much I pray for it,*  
> *life will never be the same without him — life lost to a fate so grim.*  
> *I left in the final hour — why did Luigi sit and cower?!*  
> *Couldn't face the fear of the ghost, left when he needed me the most!*  
> *What kind of brother am I, who would leave their bro to die?*  
> *I am simply not worthy, a hero for sure not me —*  
> *wish I was home back in bed, I hear his voice in my head.*

Then another voice answered — faint at first, unmistakable, coming from nowhere in the stone hall:

> **Mario's voice:** *"Luigi, where did you go? I'm stranded, lost and alone."*  
> **Beta Luigi:** *"Oh, Mario, where do I go? The kingdom's lost and alone."*  
>   
> **Mario's voice** *(clearer now)*: *"Luigi, where did you go? Ti perdono. Vai avanti."*  
> **Beta Luigi** *(sobbing harder)*: *"Oh... Mario... I TRY, BUT I JUST CAN'T MOVE ON!"*  
>   
> **Mario's voice:** *"Tocca a te salvarli."*  
> **Beta Luigi:** *"WASN'T READY — STILL HAD MUCH TO IMPROVE ON!"*  
>   
> **Mario's voice:** *"Mario non c'è più — non farmi morire invano."*  
> **Beta Luigi:** *"We still had so much left to do—"*  
>   
> **Mario's voice:** *"Mostra loro che sei il fratello..."*  
> **Beta Luigi:** *"—still had so much to prove to you!"*  
>   
> **Mario's voice:** *"...di Mario! Sei Luigi!"*

Every ghost in the Archive Hall went silent at once. Beta Luigi dropped to the stone floor. For three breaths nothing moved except the ceiling drip. Then he murmured into the flags:

> *Every last story has its end, no matter how much I try to pretend.*  
> *Now Luigi's fate left unknown — they laugh at me, but I'll make them atone,*  
> *and this time I'll be sure to do it alone.*

Beta Luigi pushed himself upright, **reached onto the nearest Archive Hall shelf, pulled down a single bound book**, and walked straight out the door alone.
sections.waluigi_note: For the record's translation line: 'Ti perdono. Vai avanti' — I forgive you, go on. 'Tocca a te salvarli' — it is up to you to save them. 'Mario non c'è più — non farmi morire invano' — Mario is no more, do not let me die in vain. 'Mostra loro che sei il fratello di Mario! Sei Luigi!' — show them you are Mario's brother; you are Luigi. And then he walked out with physical paper under his arm.

sections.name: VII. 'Gold Doesn't Bring Dead People Back': The Corridor and the Feywild Contract
sections.imageCaption: Outside in the dim stone corridor, Wario scars the plaster with his fist and thrusts the worn Contract of Accord at a speechless Mr. T.
sections.overview:
Waluigi stared at the empty doorway with his worn grimoire pressed tight against his chest. **"Sometimes you don't get second chances because there weren't any first chances to begin with,"** he said flatly, walking to the threshold without looking back. **"And this time when Luigi tries to do something heroic, he's going to have to do it alone."**

Inside the quiet hall, **Mr. T** turned to Wario: **"He said Mario, right? That means the Mario disappearance case — it was a side thing, I know, but Wario, think of the gold we can get if we bring Mario back!"**

Wario stared at the empty doorway for three full seconds before his head snapped sideways.

**"Gold?"** His voice came out razored. **"You think I care about gold right now?"** He yanked the **Contract of Accord** out of his coat pocket so hard the worn parchment cracked under his grip, jabbed a finger into Mr. T's chest, and when Mr. T muttered in shock that *Wario not caring about gold meant this must be serious*, drove his fist straight into the stone wall hard enough to scar the plaster.

**"Enough!"** Wario's voice cracked open. **"Mario's gone and I'm standing here talking about bringing him back like some kind of miracle worker?! I don't care if there's gold involved, Mr. T! Gold doesn't bring dead people back!"**

He burst out of the Archive Hall into the dimly lit corridor with Mr. T trailing behind him in stunned silence. **"Get moving! And Mr. T? You're coming with us whether you like it or not! I don't care about your debts, I don't care about Waluigi's gambling problems, and I sure as hell don't care about whatever skeletons are rattling around in Luigi's closet right now! What matters is fixing this before more people get hurt. Before someone else dies because we couldn't do our jobs properly."**

**"What is that book — the Contract of Accord?"** Mr. T asked at his heels.

Wario spun dead in his tracks, white-knuckled fingers crushing the bent corners and torn edges of the parchment between them.

**"This isn't a book. It's a contract. And right now it's the only thing keeping me from walking away from all of this because I know damn well that if I don't fix this somehow, there won't be any coming back — not for anyone. So either you start explaining what goes on in these Feywild contracts or you can just turn around and get out of my way. Because I've got better things to do than stand here arguing about paperwork with a courier who knows too much about gambling debts."**

*WAH! Read that sentence twice and carve it into granite: WARIO SAID HE DOES NOT CARE ABOUT GOLD. In front of a witness! Sober! While holding a Feywild contract by its torn corners! Either the sky is coming down before Darkmoon or the fat man finally read the penalty clause at the bottom!*
sections.waluigi_note: He called it 'these Feywild contracts' to Mr. T's face in the corridor, after calling the sixty-thirty sheet 'the Contract of Accord' at my outpost the night before. Either Wario carries two contracts under one name or the paper in his coat is older and uglier than he told me on the balcony.

aftermath:
Three doors closed on different people within five minutes: Beta Luigi went out first with an unidentified volume off the Archive Hall shelves; Waluigi walked out second with a scorched notebook and three worn grimoire pages; Wario stormed out third with *The Complete Ledger of Wario's Enterprise*, a brass cabinet key, the worn Contract of Accord, and Mr. T drafted behind him into the clinic corridor.

Behind them, the Archive Hall remains unguarded, leaking clean rainwater through an uncracked stone ceiling over a crushed Fire Flower, red ink stains, and [[prop:prop_wawario_affiliations_sheet|one song sheet with Waluigi's name blacked out]].
waluigiAssessment:
**1. Two songs went into this record and neither gets cut.** The first one — *'Mario, Luigi, Wario, Waluigi, Bowser, and Wario Bowser'* — is thirty lines of slander about mustaches and evil clones that accidentally asked the one real question nobody in this kingdom will answer: *how many copies are walking around right now?* Between Promo Mario's studio, GB Mario's gold road, Mr. L in three copies on the street, and Beta Luigi weeping over a crushed Fire Flower inside the stacks, the idiot who wrote that song was closer to the headcount than the Toad ministries.

**2. Somebody inside the building cooked Wario's books — and left the real ones on the shelf.** Column seven against column nine misses by ten thousand gold, a client deposit is stamped two weeks early, and five thousand gold moves out of and back into the **Treasury of Wonders** across thirty days. Mr. T caught it months ago and wrote `AUDIT REQUIRED - WARIO` in the bottom-left corner. Wario never read down that far.

**3. Mr. T clears up yesterday's street mystery without even knowing it.** When Paulo looked at Mr. L outside the clinic last night and said *'I didn't know skinny T wore green,'* we had no courier on file with that handle. Tonight Wario stood in the next corridor over and called Mr. T *'a courier who knows too much about gambling debts.'* Same hill, twenty-four hours apart.

**4. Ghosts do not carry bound books out the door.** Phantoms vanish when the thunder stops. Beta Luigi crushed a real flower on real stone and took a real volume off the shelf before walking out alone. Check every gap on that bookcase before morning.

**5. Watch Wario's coat pocket.** A man who screams *'Gold doesn't bring dead people back!'* and asks a courier how **Feywild contracts** work is not protecting a sixty-thirty publishing split. He is terrified of what happens if defaults trigger.

name: The Feywild House and the Open Door
title: The Feywild House, the Contract of Accord, and the Open Door
date: 3 Aethel, 1035 BF — direct continuation from the Archive Hall corridor into the Feywild; no clock time or local Feyward-clock reading is stated
timeWindow: Begins immediately after Wario and Mr. T leave the Archive Hall corridor with the Contract of Accord; the party then travels through the Feywild to an unnamed house. No duration, hour, or local Feyward-clock reading is given.

status: Filed — the group reaches an ominous Feywild house and the door opens with Beta Luigi at the threshold; Mario is not seen and his location remains unconfirmed
summary: Continuing directly from the Archive Hall, Wario and Mr. T carry the Contract of Accord into the next leg of the Mario search, and the party travels through the Feywild to a sinister, unnamed house. Waluigi cannot establish whether Mario is inside; Wario argues for an explosive entry while Waluigi and the others dispute the plan and even what to call the group. Beta Luigi appears at the opened threshold and admits he wants to help rescue Mario but is afraid. The scene ends at the open doorway: no one confirms that Mario is inside, and the transcript does not show what lies beyond it.
description:
The corridor argument did not end at the Archive Hall door. Wario kept the worn Contract of Accord with him, and Mr. T went along as the group continued the search that Wario had said mattered more than the gold. Their route carried them into the Feywild. The transcript gives no travel interval, no hour, and no reading from the Feyward pocket clock; the date is therefore chained to the Material-clock corridor scene immediately before it, without pretending the transition had a measured duration.

They eventually reached a house that looked wrong even by Feywild standards: dark, ominous, and isolated enough to make the group stop and argue before trying the entrance. Waluigi consulted his grimoire and floated the name “Feywild Cavern of Despair,” but that is his description, not a verified place-name. He suspected the house might be connected to Mario’s disappearance, yet nobody had seen Mario there. His presence inside remained a possibility, not a discovery.

The locked entrance turned the rescue into a dispute over method. Wario pressed for explosives; Waluigi objected and pushed for a less destructive way in. Jory Dobbs and Mr. T were part of the discussion as the group weighed the risk, the lock, and who should take the next action. Waluigi tried to work the problem with his grimoire while the argument kept circling back to Wario’s preferred solution. Nobody established that an explosive had been used.

The argument expanded from the door to the group itself: Wario tried to frame the search as a party, and the companions traded possible names. Waluigi had opinions, naturally, but the transcript does not establish a settled name for the group. The talk did not make the house any less ominous or prove that the missing Mario was inside.

At the threshold, Beta Luigi was revealed as the figure connected to the door. The scene records him speaking to himself and then engaging with the others. Wario challenged him to act with courage; Beta Luigi acknowledged that he wanted to help rescue Mario but did not feel brave. Wario urged him to come with them. The transcript also uses “Luigi” in a way that is not fully reconciled with its explicit identification of Beta Luigi, so this record does not infer a second identity or silently resolve the wording.

The door finally opened, but the account does not settle exactly whose action released it: Waluigi reports a click during the attempt, while the final beat identifies Beta Luigi opening the door. The group reaches the threshold. The record stops there. No interior search is described, Mario is not located, and nothing beyond the doorway is confirmed.
outcome: Filed as an open lead in the ongoing Mario search. The party reaches an unnamed house in the Feywild; the entrance opens and Beta Luigi is at the threshold. The transcript does not confirm that Mario is in the house, show anyone searching inside, or establish what lies past the doorway. The exact mechanism that opened the door is also unresolved.

waluigiAssessment:
1. Wario leaves the Archive Hall saying gold does not bring dead people back, then brings a contract with him and proposes explosives at the first locked door. I am not calling that a contradiction until I see the clause. I am calling it a pattern.

2. “Mario may be in there” is a lead, not a location. A dark house, a spooky grimoire label, and Wario’s confidence do not add up to a witness. Nobody sees Mario. Nobody says they have searched the rooms.

3. The group argued about what to call itself before it had even crossed the threshold. I would like the archive to record that the name remains unsettled, so no one can later claim I approved a title I was still improving.

4. Beta Luigi admits he wants to help and is afraid. That is more useful than pretending the fear is not there. Wario can push; the door still has to open.

5. The door does open. Who opened it, exactly, is less clear than the people outside would like. The record ends at the threshold. I refuse to let anybody turn an open door into a successful rescue by grammatical optimism.

name: The Locked Cottage, the Hypno-Helmet, and the Dragon at the Goblin Camp
title: The Locked Cottage, the Hypno-Helmet, and the Dragon at the Goblin Camp: A Bonding Ritual, a Borrowed Bean Disguise, and the Hour-Long Map
date: 2 Aethel, 1040 BF — estimated next-day continuation from Bones's tree-rest on 1 Aethel; the final map beat may cross midnight, but no hour or boundary is recorded
timeWindow: Begins at an unknown hour on 2 Aethel and continues through the night to the goblin camp; the map is measured for one hour. No exact clock reading or midnight crossing is supplied.
era: Mushroom Civil War
type: Session Event / Escape, Ritual, and Unresolved Dragon Summons
location: Unnamed Material-plane cottage, Fawful-aligned compound, woodland, and goblin camp; no route between them or canonical site name is established
status: Bones escapes and ends in the trees still disguised; Fawful's ritual remains unresolved, and a dragon leaves with an Archie-like camp figure whose identity is not confirmed
summary: After the previous Bones filing leaves him sleeping in trees beyond the Legion wall, this account opens in a locked cottage far from it, with two armed Toad guards calling his confinement a ‘bonding ritual.’ A failed key swipe gives way to an emergency-release button that unlocks every door. Outside, a green-cloaked figure and a figure called Mimbus appear near Fawful’s declaration, ‘I HAVE DRAGONS.’ A Fawful hypno-helmet drone attacks an unidentified person; its vines lash Bones before an older woman and a fox-eared Toad help remove the helmet. The conversation invokes the Emerald Enclave, a closed door to new members, and a plan to stop Fawful’s forces from completing a dragon-linked ritual. The possible dragon connection to Bowser’s Castle before 1035 is not proven. Bones accepts a recorded 20-gold payment, takes a Bean guard’s outer disguise but leaves the shorts, escapes through a broken window, and later slips away from Fawful’s sacrifice preparations and a mustard-spraying clockwork drone. A camp-side fart-spray gag is also recorded, though its user and target are unclear. At an unnamed goblin camp, an Archie-like bot douses the fire with ‘WATERBALL!’ and wins a place among the goblins. A dragon then arrives asking for Archie and leaves with an Archie-like figure after an offer of training; neither figure is reconciled with Archie Miser. Bones declines, sleeps in the trees still disguised, and spends one hour measuring a map whose route and scale are not recorded.
description: The previous Bones filing closes with him under the trees, beyond the Legion wall but not beyond anyone else's reach. This account begins after a gap the notes do not bridge: Bones wakes in a cottage with two armed Toad guards and locked doors. The route from the tree to the room is not supplied, and the archive will not invent one. What follows is a chain of escapes under Fawful's pursuit, an offered ‘bonding ritual,’ a threatened sacrifice, and a dragon who comes looking for an Archie. The record keeps the green-cloaked figure, the older woman, the guards, the drone's victim, and the camp's Archie-like figure at the level of identification the notes support. It also keeps the dragon separate from the Bowser's Castle record until someone can prove the match.
outcome: Bones escapes the cottage and Fawful's ritual site, survives the drone pursuit, and reaches a goblin camp. The camp's Archie-like figure leaves with a dragon; the dragon's identity, the passenger's identity, and the ritual's outcome remain unresolved. Bones ends in the trees wearing the borrowed Bean disguise, with a map he measured for one hour.

sections.name: I. A Cottage Far from the Legion Wall
sections.imageCaption: The distance from the wall is certain; the route from Bones's tree-rest to this cottage is not recorded.
sections.overview:
The previous Bones filing left him asleep in the trees after turning away from the Legion wall. This one opens somewhere else: Bones wakes in a cottage, far from the wall he had just left. The record never explains the transfer. There is no marked road, no named guide, no time spent traveling. The gap stays a gap.

Two armed Toad guards hold the room. Both doors are locked. When Bones asks what is happening, the explanation he receives is a **‘bonding ritual.’** The phrase is preserved because it is the explanation the guards gave, not because it explains the locks, the distance, or the weapons. Their names and their reason for holding him are not recorded. Neither guard is promoted to a known character by standing near a door.
sections.waluigi_note: A locked cottage and two armed guards are confinement. Calling it a ‘bonding ritual’ does not make the hinges less honest.

sections.name: II. The Failed Swipe and the Button That Opened Every Door
sections.overview:
Bones tried the key swipe. It failed; the door stayed locked. The account does not say whether the swipe was a card, a borrowed credential, or some other access gesture, so the archive records the failed attempt and leaves the object unnamed.

Then Bones found the emergency-release button. The cottage's own explanation was unusually clear on that point: it released all the doors from being locked. He pressed it. The locks opened. Not just the one in front of him—all the doors.

The button was not a key, and it did not tell him who had brought him there. It did give him a way out. Bones took it, and the story moved from a room with two armed guards to the ground outside without furnishing a map of the route between them.
sections.waluigi_note: The swipe did nothing. The button did everything. Waluigi would like the builders of the cottage to explain why the emergency release was easier to reach than the exit.

sections.name: III. The Green Cloak, Mimbus, and Fawful's Claim
sections.overview:
At the tree line, Bones saw an unnamed figure in a green cloak. Mimbus was named near that sighting, but the account does not describe the cloaked figure's face, allegiance, or relation to the other person. It also does not say whether this Mimbus is the historical operative from the 1035 false-heir scheme or another figure using the same name.

Fawful's words arrive as a claim: **‘I HAVE DRAGONS.’** The shout marks the threat that hangs over the next scenes. It does not, on its own, prove the ritual has worked, that the speaker has a dragon under control, or that the cloaked figure is part of his force. Bones does not stop to solve the cast list while the compound is active around him.
sections.waluigi_note: A boast is evidence that someone made a boast. It is not a custody chain for a dragon.

sections.name: IV. The Hypno-Helmet Drone
sections.imageCaption: Bones moves toward the helmeted victim as the fox-eared companion and an older woman reach the room; neither companion's identity is settled.
sections.overview:
A **Fawful hypno-helmet drone tackled an unnamed person.** The machine forced its helmet down over the victim's head. The notes describe the drone as eating the person's brain; no name, anatomy, or medical outcome follows that line, and the archive adds none.

Bones ran in. The device sent vines out and slashed at him: **the drone's vines lashed at Bones.** The older woman and the fox-eared Toad also moved into the room. Between them, the helmet was pulled off the victim. The drone scurried away before Bones could establish what happened to the person underneath it.

This machine is not filed as the Fawthful drone first seen in Bowser's Castle in 1035. That older record describes a small surveillance drone; it says nothing about hypnosis, helmets, brain-feeding, or vines. The new device gets its own entry, and its current location remains unknown.
sections.waluigi_note: A helmet removed is not the same thing as a victim recovered. The drone escaped, the person is unidentified, and nobody filed a medical report.

sections.name: V. The Emerald Enclave and the Dragon-Summoning Stakes
sections.overview:
The woman and the fox-eared companion spoke of the **Emerald Enclave**. Their account says the group had stopped letting new people in. The notes do not establish the Enclave's leadership, its full territory, or whether these two had formal authority to speak for it. The woman and the fox-eared Toad are not given names that the archive can safely assign. ‘Konathin’ enters the exchange, as does an unclear phrase about ‘Toad ie Fox’; who said which name and whom it referred to remain unresolved.

The stakes were clearer than the introductions. The pair said Fawful's Beans were preparing to summon a dragon and that the ritual involved a sacrifice. They were there to stop it. The conversation then reached backward toward Bowser's Castle: the dragon might be the one used there before 1035. The recollection moves from uncertainty to confidence, but no identifying feature or record is produced. This is a lead, not a match.

Bones offered to help for money. The notes record a **20-gold payment** from the woman. That is an event transaction, not a reconciled purse total. The camp-side gold exchange later in the account has no reliable amount or recipient, so Waluigi does not add a second invented number to it.
sections.waluigi_note: The name ‘Emerald Enclave’ is enough to open a file. It is not enough to invent a leader, a map, or an admission policy beyond the one the witnesses described.

sections.name: VI. The Borrowed Bean Disguise and the Broken Window
sections.imageCaption: Bones leaves the shorts behind while wearing the rest of an unnamed guard's outer clothing; the broken window is the recorded exit.
sections.overview:
Bones took the clothes from an unnamed man and copied the man's outward look. The exception is singled out in the notes: **everything but the shorts.** The shorts stayed behind. Bones wore the rest as a Bean guard disguise; no name, rank, or unit was attached to the person whose clothes he borrowed.

He saw two hooded figures and a Magikoopa shape. The account does not identify either hooded person or say whether the Magikoopa was a guard, a prisoner, or a witness. Bones took the broken window as an exit and jumped through it.

The woman and the fox-eared Toad were later taken by guards. A fight broke out among the people in that arrest, but the notes do not assign a victor or say whether anyone was freed. Bones did not stay to settle it. He had a disguise, a gap, and more of the compound between him and the doors than he had a moment earlier.
sections.waluigi_note: A disguise is only as good as the clothes you keep. The shorts were not part of the plan. Waluigi will not ask for further clarification.

sections.name: VII. Fawful's Sacrifice and the Mustard-Drone Pursuit
sections.imageCaption: Fawful directs the pursuit while Bones turns from a hulking Bean and a separate clockwork drone vents mustard into the passage.
sections.overview:
Fawful announced that the preparations were ready and that he had a sacrifice. A hulking Bean grabbed Bones. Bones drove his shortsword into the Bean's chest, hoping the poison would take effect. The notes give no saving throw, reaction, or confirmed result; the attack is recorded, and the poison's outcome is not.

**Fawful wound up a separate clockwork drone.** It spat mustard across the passage and across Bones. Fawful's pursuit widened: Bean forces closed in, the drone kept spraying, and Bones was grabbed again from behind. He slashed for room, bore through the hold, and bolted. The machine is not the hypno-helmet drone; the record treats them as separate devices because it describes separate attacks and does not say they are one chassis.

Fawful then brought the older woman and the fox-eared Toad out as backup. The two were held against a wall and hit with the mustard spray while the pursuit continued. Bones saw the scene, judged that the pair could manage themselves, and left while the guards were occupied. That judgment is his, not proof that either one escaped.

He ran into the trees, climbed, and got out of the immediate chase. No ritual completion is observed. No sacrifice is confirmed. Fawful's declared preparation and the dragon that appears later remain adjacent facts, not a proven cause-and-effect chain.
sections.waluigi_note: Poison hoped for is not poison proven. A dragon appearing later is not proof that the ritual summoned it. The file keeps both distinctions, even if Fawful does not.

sections.name: VIII. Goblin Fire, Waterball, and an Archie Bot's Recruitment
sections.overview:
Bones reached an unnamed goblin camp. He stayed apart from the goblins and waited as the light went; the notes do not name the camp or establish a route back to Arunedeal. A fart-spray gag appears in this camp-side sequence, but the source does not make its user, target, or effect clear. The filing keeps the beat without assigning it to Bones, the goblins, or the Archie-like figure, and does not treat it as a separate weapon or held item. When the goblins lit a fire, a figure they called an **Archie bot** stood near it.

The bot used a water trick to put out the fire. The shout is filed as heard: **‘WATERBALL!’** The goblins asked for Archie Miser's blessing, and the bot answered with the kind of pitch that turns a camp into a job interview: it said that having a bandit on their team mattered, that they needed it to win, and that they should keep paying it. The goblins accepted the pitch and showered the figure with bones and gold. The account does not count the coins or say whether any of that payment went to Bones.

The machine is filed as an ‘Archie bot’ because that is what the camp called it. Nothing in this scene proves that it is Archie Miser, that Archie Miser was inside it, or that the dragon's passenger is the same person. The separate Shadowfell/TOADALNAEC account dated 1 Aethel stays where it is.
sections.waluigi_note: The fart-spray gag is on the record; its target is not. Waluigi will not guess which camp member had the can, or what the can did.

sections.name: IX. The Dragon Comes for Archie
sections.imageCaption: A dragon arrives at the goblin fire; the portrait reference is a possible visual comparison to the Bowser's Castle record, not an identity finding.
sections.overview:
The trees shook. A roar followed, and a dragon crossed overhead before landing beside the camp. It asked, **‘WHERE IS ARCHIE? I WAS SUMMONED.’** The dragon also claimed, **‘I BETRAYED THE BEANS FOR THE TOAD GOD.’** The account does not name the summoner or establish that the dragon was the one Fawful had promised.

The camp's Archie-like figure went with it. The dragon offered training and an ‘Omega Fireball’; the exchange mentions that Archie had failed a mission in Feyward. The figure began to object that it used water, then let the objection go. The dragon invited Bones to come too. Bones said he had no quarrel and declined. The dragon ended the exchange with **‘Green D to you,’** then left with the Archie-like passenger.

The departure is clear. The identities are not. The report's possible Bowser's Castle connection is added to the castle succession file as a question to verify, not as a finding that this is The Supplied Dragon. The passenger is not folded into Archie Miser's existing status, and the dragon's allegiance to the Toad God is recorded as its claim, not a permanent contract.
sections.waluigi_note: The dragon left with an Archie. The archive still does not know which Archie, who summoned the dragon, or whether ‘betrayed the Beans’ is a confession, a boast, or a new contract.

sections.name: X. An Hour with the Map, Then Another Tree
sections.overview:
Bones did not take the dragon's invitation. He slept in the trees, still wearing the borrowed Bean disguise. At the final beat, he had a map and spent one hour measuring it. The notes do not name the route, the map's origin, its scale, or its destination. The archive records the object without drawing a road it never saw: [[prop:prop_bones_one_hour_map|the one-hour map docket]].

This is where the session stops. Bones is alive, outside the compound, disguised, and not on the Legion wall's doorstep anymore. The woman and her companion have no confirmed outcome; the victim of the hypno-helmet has no confirmed outcome; Fawful's ritual has no confirmed outcome; the dragon's identity and the passenger's identity remain open. The map is measured. The next direction is not.
sections.waluigi_note: One hour was measured. The route was not transcribed. Waluigi will not draw a shortcut because the blank page looks lonely.

aftermath: Bones exits the session in a Bean guard disguise and sleeps in trees with a map he measured for one hour. The current position of the woman and fox-eared companion, the hypno-drone victim, the ritual site, and the two drones is unknown. The dragon leaves with a figure called Archie, but the file does not equate that figure with Archie Miser or the dragon with The Supplied Dragon. The 20-gold cottage payment is recorded; the camp-side gold exchange is unquantified and unattributed, so the wallet is not reconciled.
waluigiAssessment:
**1. A ritual is not consent.** Two armed guards, locked doors and an explanation called ‘bonding’ do not turn a holding room into a voluntary event. The archive records their phrase and the physical locks; it does not accept the phrase as an answer.

**2. The machines are not one machine.** The 1035 Castle drone is a surveillance device. The hypno-helmet drone and the mustard-spraying clockwork drone are described here doing different things. They get separate entries, and neither is silently attached to the older drone.

**3. The Enclave is a name with a witness, not a full dossier.** The older woman invokes the Emerald Enclave and a closed admission policy. The record does not supply leadership, headquarters or an official roster. The possible fox-eared match to Toad ie Foxx remains a possibility; roster #73 stays unseen until the identity is actually established.

**4. The dragon's claim has two missing links.** The account ties a dragon to a later goblin-camp departure and recalls one at Bowser's Castle before 1035. It does not establish that they are the same dragon, nor that Fawful's ritual summoned this one. The Supplied Dragon file remains historical, and the Bowser Castle board gets a lead rather than a retcon.

**5. ‘Archie’ is not yet a person match.** The camp calls a figure an Archie bot; the dragon takes an Archie-like passenger. The existing Archie Miser record is a Shadowfell/TOADALNAEC account dated 1 Aethel. Waluigi will not teleport that person into the Material Plane by adjective.

**6. Bones's money is not 20 gold.** The woman pays 20 gold. Bones already had 17 gold on the last recorded wallet, but the camp-side gold exchange is not quantified or assigned cleanly. The wallet records the old reconciled amount and a warning; it does not pretend that the final balance is known.

**7. The last frame is the one to carry forward.** Bones has the borrowed outer clothes, not the shorts; he is in the trees, and he has spent an hour measuring a map whose route the archive cannot see. That is enough for continuity. It is not enough to name the next place.

name: The Intake Drone and the Unfinished Escape
title: The Intake Drone, the Blackout, and the Escape That Did Not Finish
date: 1 Aethel, 1040 BF — continuation aboard the TOADALNAEC after the afternoon takeover; no clock or elapsed interval is recorded
timeWindow: A same-day continuation of the 1 Aethel TOADALNAEC account. The scene remains aboard the ship after the takeover, but neither a clock time nor an interval between the two accounts is stated. The archive does not place it past midnight.
era: 1040 BF — Toad Liberation file / the TOADALNAEC
location: Aboard the old Vigilance, now the TOADALNAEC (Material Plane), including the engine room and interior passages
type: Interrogation / Escape Attempt / Shipboard Confrontation
status: Filed — Eager is released after questioning; Remi escapes the intake drone by cutting power to the ship's field, then fights the Toads and ends surrounded but invisible, feeling along a wall. Archie leaves after attempting to stabilize Perot. The escape, Perot's condition, and the ship's power state remain unresolved.
imageCaption: The engine room is dark after Remi removes X.O.'s staff. Masked Toads search for the escaped prisoner; Remi has gone invisible, but the wall ahead has not yet become an exit.
image_alt: In a dark airship engine passage, an almost invisible red-haired girl with a staff is surrounded by masked Toad guards with colored caps; a barrel lies nearby, and a small spell-light catches the searchers' masks.
summary: Aboard the TOADALNAEC, Remi offers a porcupine Toad a high five before the Toads demand the stolen technology and trap her inside an intake drone. Eager is questioned about the missing Pond Patrol and released; Salam explains that he was separated from Rodger and Toad Lee. The drone carries Remi to the engine room, where the Toads say her power will drain over a week and set Perot to watch her. Remi removes X.O.'s staff from the field and the ship's power immediately fails. In the darkness she shoots Perot, escapes during the search, and reunites with Archie as he crawls out of a barrel. Archie later treats Perot instead of fleeing with Remi. Lulu Green and other Toads block her route; a fight leaves Remi surrounded, blinded, and invisible, still searching along a wall when the record ends.
description:
The last filing left the old Vigilance in Toad hands, a hall in uproar, and Archie inside a barrel. This one stays aboard the same ship. It does not begin with a new map or a clean report of the duel's end. It begins with Remi trying to pick up where she left off.

She offers a high five to a porcupine Toad. Then the Toads demand the stolen technology. An intake drone opens, takes her in, and shuts its bars. Eager is brought over to answer questions about the Pond Patrol. He says he was sent without a detachment, went on a misadventure that took longer than expected, and believes Toad Lee and Rodger were sent too. He cannot say where either is. Salam is there; the whereabouts of the other two remain unknown. Eager is told his answer is sufficient and that he is free. Remi is not. The Toads say she trespassed and turned people gold.

They carry the drone to the engine room. There, an unnamed Toad explains that the field will drain Remi's power over a week, with Perot assigned to overwatch. Remi wonders whether the ship has taken off. She takes X.O.'s staff out of the field. The power immediately goes out.

The blackout does not end the confinement. It changes the room in which the search begins. Remi casts light, finds the assembled Toad Rangers, presses her musket to a Toad's head and fires. The bullet bounces off the Toad's squishy body; the Toad falls bleeding. The other Toads run with Archie's barrel. Remi disguises herself and moves with an escort, while the barrel is carried toward an electrical port it was not meant to enter. Archie is shocked, stays silent, then crawls out through the bottom.

The ship keeps making claims about who owns it, who betrayed whom, and which prisoners deserve a way out. Remi and Archie do not agree on what to do. Archie chooses to help the Toad she shot. Remi stays. The fight grows from one bleeding guard to a masked search party, and the filing stops while she is still trying to find a way around a wall. WAH.
outcome: Eager is released after questioning. Remi gets out of the intake drone when she removes X.O.'s staff from the engine-room field, causing the ship's power to fail; whether the vessel itself stops, lands, or remains in flight is not recorded. Perot is shot and left bleeding, and Archie attempts to stabilize him, but the result is unknown. Archie leaves through a doorway while Remi remains in conflict with Lulu Green and other Toads. Their fight is unfinished: Remi ends surrounded, unable to see, and invisible, feeling for a route around a wall. The status of the missing Pond Patrol members, the intake drone, the staff, and the ship's systems is unresolved.
notableFeatures: Remi's attempted high five to a porcupine Toad is interrupted by a demand for stolen technology; the result of the high five is not recorded.
The intake drone closes its bars around Remi; Eager answers the Toads' questions and is released.
Eager says he was sent without a detachment and cannot locate Rodger or Toad Lee; the Toads' claim that the Pond Patrol has been missing three weeks is not independently verified.
Salam says he failed the mission and became separated from Rodger and Toad Lee; the Toads invoke his past association with Speaker L.
Perot is assigned to overwatch Remi in a field that is said to drain her power over a week.
Remi removes X.O.'s staff from the field; the ship's power immediately goes out, but the record does not say whether the ship stops moving.
Remi's bullet bounces off the Toad she shoots; he falls bleeding and is later identified by Lulu Green as Perot. Archie makes an uncertain attempt to stabilize him.
Archie escapes the barrel after it is carried toward an electrical port and shocked; the Toads' account of Speaker Rivers and Speaker L is relayed during the disguise walk.
Lulu Green pardons Archie but calls Remi the Toads' number-one target; he leaves while she stays behind.
Remi is blinded and surrounded by masked Toads who can see in the dark. She turns invisible and chooses to go around a solid wall; no exit is shown.
